title: Benchmark and validation case registry (cavity, backward step, channel, flat plate, NACA0012, heated cavity)
acceptance: cases/ folder with case definitions plus reference data from public literature; runner lists them
note: Reference tables (Ghia 1982, de Vahl Davis 1983) were first typed from memory and have since been cross-checked against independent published copies (wave 6a, docs/reference-data.md): every tabulated value matches. The Ghia v-centreline is checked at Re=100 only and the 0.9766 u rows of Re=100/400 only via one source. NACA0012 case has no mesh generator yet. WAVE 30C: the de Vahl Davis reference values are now checked against the primary source (Table V of the 1983 paper read from a page scan, all eleven quantities at Ra 1e3 to 1e6 plus the locations of the maxima, cases/heated_cavity/reference/devahldavis1983_tableV.csv); every earlier value matched. NACA0012 still has no mesh generator (not attempted). WAVE 30B (ADR 0060): incompressible benchmarks re-validated against data actually read, limits registered before running (docs/reference-data.md, wave 30B section). Status unchanged (done). Passing: cavity Re 100/400/1000 vs Ghia and Botella (max u error 4.5e-3, 1.8e-3, 4.4e-3/5.4e-3); backward step Re_D 800 x_r/h 11.80 (published 11.48 to 12.20, GCI 0.5 percent); Blasius with an upstream shear-free belt (Cf error 0.2 to 0.7 percent, profile 2.3e-3, delta* +0.01 percent, GCI 0.16 percent); wall-resolved SST channel Re_tau 178 vs MKM DNS (U_b+ +1.7 percent); k-epsilon wall functions on two of three meshes; cylinder Re 100 C_D within 2.4 percent. Known misses (ignored known-miss tests, limits intact): cavity Re 1000 GCI; Blasius plate abutting the inlet (set-up defect); SST channel observed order 0.63; k-epsilon y+ sensitivity; cylinder St -3.8 percent and GCI. See the ADR addendum. Not obtained: Armaly, Gartling and Ghia originals, Moody/Colebrook. WAVE 31C (ADR 0064): discrepancies are listed in docs/reference-data.md (wave 31C), nothing silently changed. Ghia u (Re 100/400/1000, incl. y 0.9766) and v (Re 100) now checked against three secondary copies cell by cell (the in-repo tables equal them). Ghia v Re 400/1000 read with two cell disagreements between copies (not used by any test). Gartling Re 800 step lengths 12.20/9.70/20.96 h seen in two secondary sources (one conflicting row 11.9/9.5/20.6). Armaly paper read but its reattachment lengths exist only in figures (data not obtained). Williamson 1989 St-Re fit read in the primary paper (St(100) 0.1643). WAVE 31A (ADR 0062): The Ra 1e6 cavity miss of wave 30C is an unstable iteration, not a discretisation or limiter effect. The SIMPLEC iteration at alpha_u 0.8 with energy relax 0.9 stalls (residual 1.3e-2) on the 32 x 32 mesh with every convection scheme. A steady state exists (PISO march reaches it, rate 5e-10; alpha_u 0.5, 0.3, energy relax 0.7 or classic SIMPLE converge to Nu 8.8727 to 8.8732), and the steady iteration started from it leaves it. The corrected ignored test a_ra_1e6_alpha05 (alpha_u 0.5, all limits unchanged) passes: Nu +0.33 percent, GCI 0.05 percent. The Sod Van Albada miss is fixed (the limiter overflowed to NaN above 1.34e154). Cylinder Re 100 St miss of wave 30B: a time-discretisation error (first-order PISO step, order 0.85 in dt, second order in h). With the common dt 0.025 the registered K1 to K4 pass (St 0.16175, -1.97 percent; GCI 1.6 percent), extrapolated St 0.1669, C_D 1.357. The 181 x 141 mesh at dt 0.05 diverges.

Cylinder Re=100 (O-grid 128x100, R=20D, linear-upwind, dt=0.05 Co~2.6, 160 time units, AMG pressure) gives St=0.1588 vs ~0.165 (-3.8 percent, passes the 5 percent gate; heavy test: cargo test --release -p rcfd-fv --test cylinder -- --ignored, ~5 min). Reference St=0.165 at Re=100 verified (Williamson Annu. Rev. Fluid Mech. 1996 as tabulated in arXiv:2303.09262; converged 2D computations 0.164); the earlier Williamson 1989 / Henderson 1995 attributions are unconfirmed. Also fixed the periodic-patch HbyA flux (boundary_hby_a), which broke periodic flows. Caveat: central + deferred correction with a single outer iteration is unstable at high cell Peclet number. Audit 2026-10-14: the cylinder Strouhal gate (0.1588 vs 0.165, -3.8 percent) is an ignored test; only Taylor-Green runs in the default suite. WAVE 31A (ADR 0062): the St -3.8 percent of the 128 x 100 dt 0.05 run is mainly time-discretisation error of the first-order PISO step (observed order 0.82 to 0.87 in dt, 2.3 to 2.5 in h); at dt 0.025 St 0.16175 (-1.97 percent) and on 181 x 141 0.16255, extrapolation 0.1669; C_D 1.357 extrapolated. title: Porous media, momentum sources, MRF (rotating frame) source terms
acceptance: Packed-bed Ergun pressure drop and rotating channel tests pass
note: Wave 9. Acceptance met, scope partial. Delivered: rcfd-fv sources.rs (Darcy-Forchheimer porous sink in the superficial-velocity form, Ergun coefficients 1/K = 150 (1-e)^2/(e^3 d^2), C2 = 3.5 (1-e)/(e^3 d); relative-velocity rotating frame with analytic centrifugal and lagged Coriolis accelerations as balanced-force BodyForce terms; constant acceleration), rcfd-api sources.rs and settings sources.<name> (type porous | rotating_frame | acceleration; zone all | box | cell_zone; steady simple/simplec only, other algorithms are a located diagnostic; docs/case-schema.md; cases/packed_bed, cases/rotating_channel). Ergun constants checked against a secondary source (neutrium.net, Manchester packed-bed page; Ergun 1952 itself not accessed). Checks fixed before running (rcfd-api tests/sources.rs, nu = 1.5e-5, bed e = 0.4, d = 5 mm, U = 0.15 m/s, 40x8 cells): packed-bed kinematic pressure gradient between 30 % and 70 % of the bed 149.7666 vs Ergun 149.7656 (+0.001 %, limit 1 %; the viscous and inertial terms are 51 %/49 % of it); direct Darcy-Forchheimer input gives the same field to 1e-9; a porous box zone over the middle half gives 149.7965 inside (+0.02 %) and -0.041 outside (0.03 % of Ergun, limit 1 %). Spanwise-rotating laminar channel (Omega = 2, nu = 0.1, g = 1, 4x40 cells, Coriolis only): profile error 0.062 % of the centre-line velocity (limit 1 %), transverse pressure difference -3.3371 vs -2 Omega times the integral of the parabola -3.3302 (+0.21 %, limit 1 %). NOT met: fluid at rest in a rotating frame (closed 1 m box, Coriolis + centrifugal, nu = 0.05, Omega = 3): the pre-fixed criterion was spurious speed < 1e-3 Omega R_max and pressure error < 1 % of the range; measured 5.2e-3 and 1.62 % on 24x24, 1.3e-3 and 0.80 % on 48x48 (speed falls with order 2.0, pressure with order 1.0). Cause: next to walls the Green-Gauss cell gradient of a curved pressure field differs from the cell-centre force by O(h), the same wall effect as the rest state of F-050 (an attempt to change the wall pressure extrapolation did not help and was reverted). The cross-stream velocity of the rotating channel is 1.4e-5 of the centre-line speed for the same reason. The normalised momentum residual cannot be used as a stop criterion for these uniform or linear solutions (its normalisation vanishes); the tests check stationarity instead. Not done (reason for partial): MRF zone interface (frozen-rotor absolute/relative velocity conversion between a rotating and a stationary zone needs the non-conformal interface of F-114), transient PISO/PIMPLE support, porosity-weighted (physical-velocity) formulation, anisotropic/directional resistance, porous jump (F-113). Update (wave 10): the rest-state criterion is now MET on the original 24x24 mesh (criterion text unchanged: spurious speed < 1e-3 Omega R_max, pressure error < 1 % of the range): speed 5.3e-12 Omega R and pressure error 0.000 % (round-off; 48x48 2.5e-11 and 0.000 %), previously 5.2e-3 and 1.62 %. Cause and fix: the wall value that enters the Green-Gauss gradient of a wall cell was extrapolated with the face body force, but the gradient of a curved pressure with linearly interpolated opposite faces is O(h) off whatever the wall value of that kind (the earlier extrapolation attempts could not help). The wall value is now chosen so that the wall-normal gradient of the wall cell equals the cell-centre body force exactly, and with SIMPLEC the lagged (rAU - rAtU) correction is applied to the wall pressure gradient of the flux balance so that the wall gradient converges to the same value as the interior faces. Scope: SimpleSolver::wall_pressure_trapezoid, switched on only when a rotating-frame/acceleration source supplies a body force (rcfd-api); all other baseline runs are bit-identical (hash check), only the rotating_channel case changed numerically. Its pre-registered limits still hold: profile error 0.062 % (limit 1 %), transverse pressure difference +0.203 % (was +0.21 %, limit 1 %), cross-stream velocity 1.39e-5 of the centre line (was 1.4e-5). Caveat: for flows with other wall-normal momentum terms the construction imposes the body-force balance on the wall-normal gradient of wall cells (the usual fixed-flux wall treatment); only the cases above were checked. The stationarity check of the test helper uses a speed-scale floor of 1e-3 for the rest state only (a relative change of round-off speeds is meaningless). The remaining scope gaps for partial are unchanged. Update (MRF, ADR 0008, rcfd-api tests/mrf.rs; criteria registered in the ADR before the code ran, never changed): new source type mrf = absolute-velocity frozen-rotor zone (momentum convected with phi - (Omega x r).S on faces inside the zone, lagged -Omega x u through the balanced-force BodyForce path, interface/boundary faces get no offset so absolute momentum crosses the interface; zone boundary must be a surface of revolution, else a located error), mesh generators annulus_3d and annulus_3d_interface (planar non-conformal join of F-114 perpendicular to the axis). Measured against analytic flows only (no pump or turbine benchmark is claimed): M1 solid body across the interface velocity 7.84e-3 W r_o (limit 2e-2) pass, pressure 7.55e-2 of the range (limit 5e-2) MISS. M2 Taylor-Couette in one MRF zone velocity 6.76e-3 V_i (1.5e-2) pass. M3 frame invariance Omega 0/0.5/1/2 W_i velocity 6.76e-3 V_i and difference to the stationary frame <= 1.7e-3 V_i (1e-2) pass. M4 across the non-conformal interface velocity 7.92e-3 V_i (2e-2) pass. M5 continuity 5e-12, net interface flux 3e-14, sum |flux| 8.9e-4 (limits 1e-8, 1e-8, 1e-3) pass. M6 axial through-flow with a swirl-free MRF half (Omega 5): in/out and interface flux agree to 1e-10, max swirl 2.0e-4 (2e-2), max axial-velocity deviation 9.8e-3 (2e-2) pass. Registered misses (ignored *_known_miss tests): Torque from the moment report: before the wave-11 fix it was 37.8 percent below the registered full-stress value in M2/M3/M4 (the report integrated nu du/dn without the transpose term). The report now integrates the full viscous stress nu (grad u + grad u^T) . n (rcfd-post wall_force_and_moment, analytic tests: rigid rotation gives zero force and moment, simple shear gives the transpose traction) and reads -3.41 percent (M2), -3.41 to -3.42 percent (M3), -4.12 percent (M4) against the registered 4 pi nu W_i r_i^2 r_o^2/(r_o^2 - r_i^2) lz, still outside the registered 3 percent, so the ignored m2_m3_m4_torque_known_miss test stays (criterion unchanged). The open-end variants M2b/M3b/M4b, whose report-consistent target (nu du/dn, 0.2618 lz) is obsolete, now compare with the registered target too and read -3.59, -3.59, -4.36 percent (ignored m2b_m3b_m4b_torque_known_miss; their velocity and pairwise limits still pass). The M3 stationary frame exactly as registered (no source, kernel without the H correction): velocity 3.06e-2 V_i, spurious 1.39e-3 V_i, difference to the MRF frames 2.57e-2 V_i, all missed (the passing M3 test uses an MRF source at Omega 0). Spurious axial/radial speed in that Omega 0 frame 1.41e-3 V_i (limit 1e-3; the MRF frames 9.7e-4 to 3.2e-4 pass). Open-end variants: spurious speed 8.5e-3 V_i and interface net flux 3.2e-5 V_i A (axial flow through the fixed-pressure ends). M1 pressure. Kernel change: the first runs missed badly (3.06 percent of V_i in the stationary frame) because the H operator uses the component-averaged diagonal while a symmetry plane adds its Dirichlet term to the normal component only, scaling tangential end-cell velocity by a_k/a_p. SimpleSolver::component_diag_correction repairs H per component, enabled only for MRF cases so shipped constant-density results stay bit-identical (baseline hashes unchanged); wall_pressure_trapezoid is not switched on by MRF-only sources. Still not done (status stays partial): transient/PISO/PIMPLE and sliding-mesh MRF, curved (cylindrical) and non-perpendicular interfaces, porosity-weighted formulation, anisotropic resistance, porous jump (F-113), turbulence/energy with MRF unvalidated. ADR 0010: the component-consistent diagonal is also available for non-MRF cases as the opt-in solver.component_diagonal = "corrected" (it changes the packed_bed baseline hash, so it is not the default). The registered stationary frame without any source (M3a) then meets its velocity (6.8e-3 against 1.5e-2 V_i) and pairwise (1.7e-3 against 1e-2 V_i) limits and still misses spurious speed (1.41e-3 against 1e-3 V_i). SCOPE (merged review): add directional (Cartesian, conical, curvilinear) resistances, a power-law porous model, porosity and relative-viscosity inputs, and a non-equilibrium thermal porous option; source terms for other equations are tracked in F-201. DONE (audit 2026-10-21, docs/audit/partials-group-*.md): acceptance text as written is met by passing tests; scope beyond the acceptance text, and the caveats in the audit file, are not claimed.

title: Coupled pressure-velocity solver (block-coupled) with AMG
acceptance: Cavity converges in fewer outer iterations than SIMPLE; documented
note: Block-coupled solver (rcfd-fv coupled.rs, solver.algorithm = "coupled"): (u,v[,w],p) in one system per Picard iteration, implicit Green-Gauss pressure gradient, implicit Rhie-Chow continuity rows, GMRES(40) with ILU(0) momentum blocks and one AMG V-cycle on the approximate pressure Schur complement (AMG is used on the pressure block only, not on the full interleaved system). Measured (checks fixed beforehand: F-028 cavity Re 100, 40x40, linearUpwind; shared measure = first outer iteration after which the velocity stays within 1e-5 U_lid of the solver's own converged state, same function for both solvers; coupled must pass the unchanged Ghia gate 0.02 U_lid for u and v): coupled alpha_u 0.9 settles at 165 outer iterations (270 total, 3060 GMRES iterations), SIMPLEC alpha_u 0.9 at 167 (273), classic SIMPLE alpha_u 0.7 at 610 (917); Ghia max error u 0.00277, v 0.00855 (SIMPLEC identical, limit 0.02). Acceptance (fewer outer iterations than SIMPLE) met against SIMPLE (165 vs 610), but at equal relaxation the coupled solver needs the same number of Picard iterations as SIMPLEC (the count is set by the momentum under-relaxation, not the coupling). Its advantage is stability at stronger relaxation: alpha_u 0.95 settles at 83, 0.98 at 38 outer iterations versus SIMPLEC best 97 (0.95; 249 at 0.98). Wall time is worse: 1.9 s at 0.98 versus 0.6 s for SIMPLEC at 0.95 (ILU/AMG rebuilt each iteration, unoptimised). The AMG-less Jacobi Schur block needs 2 to 5 times more GMRES iterations (e.g. 14181 vs 3060 at alpha_u 0.9). Wave 19A (ADR 0029, still partial): open boundaries (zero-gradient velocity with fixed pressure), uniform body force with a balanced-force term, Boussinesq buoyancy, the energy equation and solid cells excluded from the pressure-velocity system were added (settings tree; located errors). Measured (checks registered beforehand): Couette exact to 1.5e-11; pressure-driven channel equals the discrete closed form to 9e-10 U_max with observed order 2.000 (the segregated SIMPLEC misses the same limits: 1.3e-2, order 1.4, relaxation-dependent converged solution; kept as ignored known-miss tests); hydrostatic rest 4e-12; de Vahl Davis cavity Ra 1e3 and 1e4 within 0.74 percent of the secondary-source values (reference-data.md: printed 1983 tables not reachable). title: Wall distance calculation and standard wall functions
acceptance: y+ and wall distance verified on channel mesh; log law recovered in developed flow
note: Wave 5 added wall distance, standard wall functions and a mixing-length closure to rcfd-turb. Caveats: the log-law is recovered with a mixing-length interior closure, not yet with k-epsilon (F-042); a comparison with DNS is left to F-042. wall_distance: exact Euclidean distance from each cell centre to the nearest wall face (faces split into triangle fans, closest-point test per Ericson, bounding-box pruning; no Poisson/PDE method). WallConstants: kappa 0.41, E 9.8, Cmu 0.09; Launder and Spalding 1974 equilibrium log law with the viscous-sublayer switch at the y+ intersection, 11.5 for these constants. u_tau comes from the first-cell velocity by Newton iteration. Wall eddy viscosity comes from velocity (nu_t,w = u_tau^2 y/u_P - nu) and from k (nu_t,w = nu (y* kappa / ln(E y*) - 1), y* = Cmu^1/4 sqrt(k) y / nu). wall_y_plus and effective_viscosity (face viscosity for SimpleSolver.nu_face with wall-function values on wall faces). Prandtl mixing-length closure (l = kappa d) with the log-law value kappa y u_tau in wall cells. Verification (rcfd-turb tests): wall distance equals min(y, 2h-y) to 1e-13 on uniform and graded channel meshes and equals x for a side wall; triangle distance covers face/edge/vertex regions. Periodic channel at Re_tau = 395 (h = 1, u_tau = 1 imposed through the body force, nu = 1/395), mixing-length interior plus wall functions, ny = 8/12/16 (first-cell y+ = 49.4/32.9/24.7): Reported y+ equals y u_tau/nu within 0.5%. Wall shear from the wall function equals the imposed 1 within 2e-3 (momentum balance). First-cell u+ is on the log law. Interior profile vs the exact solution of the mixing-length stress balance (nu + l^2 S) S = 1 - y/h: max deviation 2.1% / 2.3% / 2.4%, test tolerance 3%. The offset is the second-order stencil error across the log layer between the first two cells of a uniform mesh (centre distances 1:3) and does not shrink with ny. Convergence of this stiff diffusion-dominated flow needed the new opt-in SimpleSettings.h_from_solution (H operator from the solved predictor as in classic SIMPLE; default off, ~6x faster here). The default Jacobi-like H needed >8000 iterations. The normalised momentum residual is meaningless for the identically zero v component (round-off noise), so the test converges on max velocity update < 1e-10. Wave 6b: the wall functions are reachable from the case schema through turbulence.model = k_epsilon (turbulence.wall_function = standard, kappa, e_wall), with the y_plus field/boundary value/report (type y_plus, statistic average|min|max) and the k, epsilon, nut, wall_distance fields in VTU output. The mixing-length closure is not selectable from the schema. Scalable wall functions and rough walls are not included.

title: Spalart-Allmaras one-equation model

note: Wave 8, PARTIAL: model and settings-tree wiring done, but the registered power-law check misses (ADR 0014). NOT DONE: no mesh study, no other validation case (BFS, airfoil). Constants/limits registered before running in docs/adr/0014-sa-and-turbulence-interface.md. Model (rcfd-turb sa.rs, SpalartAllmaras): SA-noft2 of the NASA TMR page, with the Allmaras 2012 S~ limiter and SA-neg. Constants sigma 2/3, cb1 0.1355, cb2 0.622, kappa 0.41, cw2 0.3, cw3 2, cv1 7.1 verified by web fetch. Convection is first-order upwind. Wall modes: auto (Spalding law of the wall, wall-cell nuTilda matched for y+ > 5; works from y+ ~1 to the log layer) and resolved. Settings: turbulence.model = spalart_allmaras with turbulence.sa.*, nutilde_ratio, boundaries.<patch>.nutilde_value, nuTilda field. FLAT PLATE (tests/flat_plate_sa.rs, ignored, release; TMR set-up Re 5e6/m, nuTilda_inf = 3 nu, 140x110 cells, 70 layers, y+ 0.5, converged 2204 iterations): Cf(0.97) = 0.002786: +2.97% vs TMR CFL3D SA 2.70565e-3 (PASS, limit 5%; the grid behind that file value is unverified). vs TMR theory curves +2.29/-3.36/-3.08% (PASS). vs White -4.1/-3.6/-3.1/-3.0% at x 0.4/0.6/0.97/1.0 (PASS). vs power law 0.0576 Re_x^-0.2 +0.8/+2.7/+5.29% at x 0.4/0.6/1.0 (MISS at x = 1.0, limit 5%; ignored test sa_flat_plate_cf_vs_power_law_known_miss; +7.2/+9.2% at x 1.4/1.99 reported only). title: k-epsilon family (standard, realizable, RNG) with scalable wall functions
acceptance: Channel Re_tau=395 mean profile within 10 percent of DNS; backward-facing-step reattachment within literature scatter
note: PARTIAL. Last recorded results: the channel criterion is met (the 10 percent assertions all pass; Realizable bulk U+ +9.0%, close to the limit). On the step, the 'within literature scatter' criterion is met by RNG/Realizable only, and all three variants miss the registered window 6.26±0.10. On the corrected set-up BFS-C (medium mesh, window 6.16 to 6.36), Standard and Realizable MISS and RNG passes, marginally; Realizable with A0 = 4.0 passes, marginally, but is NOT grid-converged (ADR 0017). Scalable wall functions are in the library but not wired to the settings tree, and the energy / moving-wall sub-criteria and low-Re variants are not addressed (ADR 0015). Wave 5, PARTIAL: channel criterion met, backward-facing-step criterion NOT attempted. rcfd-turb kepsilon.rs: KEpsilon with variants Standard (Launder-Spalding 1974), RNG (Yakhot-Orszag; C2* strain correction) and Realizable (Shih et al. 1995; variable Cmu, C1 = max(0.43, eta/(eta+5)), eps sink C2 eps^2/(k+sqrt(nu eps))). Implicit-sink k and epsilon transport on the SIMPLE flux (rcfd-fv convection/laplacian), nu_t under-relaxed. Standard wall functions from F-040 (wall-cell epsilon fixed to Cmu^3/4 k^3/2/(kappa y), wall-shear production, wall-face nu_t from k). Library API only (nu_face() feeds SimpleSolver.nu_face; run with SimpleSettings.h_from_solution = true). Test tests/channel_kepsilon.rs: periodic channel Re_tau = 395 (h = 1, u_tau = 1 via body force, nu = 1/395), 4 x 14 uniform cells (first-cell y+ 28), converged (max update < 1e-9, nu_t change < 1e-8) in about 4500-4800 iterations. Centre-line U+ / bulk U+: Standard 20.69 (+2.9%) / 18.39 (+5.7%), RNG 21.14 (+5.2%) / 18.65 (+7.2%), Realizable 21.59 (+7.4%) / 18.93 (+8.8%) against DNS (Moser, Kim and Mansour 1999) 20.1 / 17.4, all within the 10% criterion. Log-layer profile (20 < y+ < 150) within 10% of Reichardt's law (test asserts it; Standard 13.91 vs 13.37 at y+ 28, 16.63 vs 16.52 at y+ 85). CAVEATS: DNS numbers verified in wave 6a against the published MKM chan395.means (actual Re_tau 392.24: U_c+ = 20.13, U_b+ = 17.54, Re_b = 13764) and the RNG/realizable/standard constants cross-checked against published documentation (realizable A0 appears as 4.04 in some references and 4.0 in others). Only the 14-cell mesh was run (no mesh study). The profile comparison beyond the log layer is only through the centre-line and bulk values. All three variants overpredict the velocity, Realizable the most. NOT DONE: backward-facing-step reattachment: the available step mesh generator has uniform spacing only and expansion ratio 2 does not match Driver and Seegmiller (1985, ER 1.125, xr/H about 6.26), the second-order BFS convergence problem found in F-106 at Re_h >= 200 is undiagnosed, and no reference-consistent case was set up, so no reattachment number is claimed. Wave 6b: wired into the case schema (rcfd-api turb.rs). Keys: turbulence.model = laminar | k_epsilon, turbulence.variant = standard | rng | realizable, wall_function, kappa, e_wall, convection, relax, relax_nut, k_initial/epsilon_initial or initial_intensity/initial_viscosity_ratio. Inlet helpers per boundary (turbulence_spec = intensity_length | intensity_viscosity_ratio | values: k = 3/2 (I U)^2, epsilon = Cmu^3/4 k^3/2 / l or Cmu k^2/(ratio nu), checked in a test against the area average of the boundary k/epsilon). Outputs: k, epsilon, nut, y_plus, res_nut monitor. Validation errors with line numbers: transient algorithm, no wall patch, moving wall, energy equation, missing turbulence_length, inconsistent k/epsilon initial values, y_plus report on a non-wall patch. Tests (rcfd-api tests/physics_schema.rs): the periodic Re_tau 395 channel run through the settings tree equals the library run after 60 iterations to 1e-12 (u, k, nut; standard, RNG, realizable). The converged run (4508 iterations in cases/channel/kepsilon_channel.toml, stopped by a y+ plateau because the relative momentum residual stalls near 5e-4) gives bulk U+ 18.389 (the library test value 18.39, +5.7% vs DNS 17.4), wall-cell y+ 27.733. The case cases/channel/kepsilon_inlet.toml runs through rcfd run and the service. Still no scalable wall functions, k-epsilon is steady-only, incompressible, without heat transfer, and the backward-facing step is still not attempted; multiple wall faces per cell use the nearest only. WAVE 6 UPDATE (supersedes the 'NOT DONE: backward-facing-step' item above; status stays PARTIAL because scalable wall functions and schema wiring are still missing). Step case: tests/step_kepsilon.rs (rcfd-turb, #[ignore], run in release), Driver and Seegmiller geometry via StepSpec::from_expansion_ratio(1.125) (inlet channel 8 h, step 1 h, l_in 5, l_out 40), graded mesh (backward_step_graded), standard wall functions, SIMPLEC alpha_u 0.8 linearUpwind momentum, upwind k/epsilon, Re_h = 37500. Measured reattachment x_r/h (last negative-to-positive sign change of u in the first cell row above the floor; 4000-5000 iterations), three meshes (5.1k / 10.6k / 23.8k cells; 3000 iterations on the coarse and fine meshes, 5000 on the medium one): Standard 5.20 / 5.36 / 5.46, RNG 6.32 / 6.37 / 6.38, Realizable (medium mesh) 6.40. Reference: Driver and Seegmiller 6.26 +- 0.10 (value from cases/backward_step/case.json) and the 5.5-7 RANS scatter band in that file. Secondary sources checked this wave (NASA NPARC validation archive and the OpenFOAM verification docs built on the NASA Turbulence Modeling Resource case) give 6.26 +- 0.10 for the zero-degree top wall, quoted there at Re_h = 36000, while case.json and the runs use 37500. RNG and Realizable are inside the scatter band, 0.06-0.14 above the nominal 6.26 (RNG 6.32 on the coarsest mesh is inside the +-0.10 window, the finer meshes are 0.01-0.04 above it). Standard is 13-17 percent LOW, below the band on the two coarser meshes and 0.04 below it on the finest. So the 'within literature scatter' criterion is met by RNG/Realizable only. CAVEATS: The inlet is an approximation (1/7 power-law boundary layer thickness 1.5 h on both inlet-channel walls, 1 percent free-stream intensity, k and eps from a mixing-length estimate), not the measured D&S profile. The top wall is straight, which matches the zero-degree reference configuration. Fixed outlet pressure at x/h = 40. The nu_t of the wall-adjacent cells on the viscous/log switch oscillates O(1) between iterations (max velocity update stalls at 3e-4 - 4e-3, 'nut change < 1e-6' never reached) although x_r is constant to 1e-5 on the medium and fine meshes (fine RNG: 6.37817 from iteration 1500 to 3000). k-epsilon constants/RNG/realizable forms still from memory. No schema wiring. Details: docs/bfs-convergence-findings.md. WAVE 7 UPDATE (status stays PARTIAL: scalable wall functions are still not implemented and only RNG/Realizable are inside the step scatter band). The wall-cell oscillation reported above is DIAGNOSED AND FIXED. Diagnosis: a top-N listing of the changing nu_t cells showed all of them wall-adjacent (step face and floor), i.e. the hard viscous/log switch of the wall function (epsilon jumps about 4x, production 0 to log-law). Fix: rcfd-turb now has WallTreatment { Switch (old), Hysteresis{band} (+-10 percent dead band, band 0.1), Smooth (default: epsilon_w = sqrt(eps_vis^2 + eps_log^2), compound form after Popovac and Hanjalic 2007, and log-law production times r^6/(1+r^6), r = y*/y*_lam) }, selectable as turbulence.wall_treatment = smooth | hysteresis | switch in the case schema. Convergence with the UNCHANGED criterion (max velocity update < 1e-7 and nu_t change < 1e-6): tests/step_kepsilon.rs now asserts convergence (hysteresis and smooth). The medium mesh (24+160 x 40+20 cells) converges in 800-920 iterations (du 1e-8, dnut 1e-6) for Standard, RNG and Realizable; Switch never does (du 2e-4 - 1.7e-3, dnut 0.4 - 1.1). Measured x_r/H (target 6.26 +- 0.10 and the tolerances are unchanged), as Standard / RNG / Realizable: Medium mesh: Switch 5.3583 / 6.3726 / 6.4042, Hysteresis 5.3581 / 6.3724 / 6.4043, Smooth 5.3594 / 6.3729 / 6.4015. Fine mesh (36+240 x 60+30, Smooth, converged at about 1540-1570 iterations): 5.4599 / 6.3797 / 6.5063. The treatment moves x_r by less than 0.003, so the earlier numbers stand: RNG and Realizable are inside the 5.5-7 scatter band (0.11-0.25 above the nominal 6.26; RNG medium/fine 6.37/6.38 are 0.01-0.02 outside the +-0.10 window, Realizable 6.40-6.51 is 0.04-0.15 outside), Standard (5.36-5.46) is outside the band. Channel (tests/channel_kepsilon.rs, 10 percent assertions unchanged, all pass) shifts slightly with the smooth default: centre-line / bulk U+ Standard 20.742 (+3.2%) / 18.441 (+6.0%), RNG 21.193 (+5.4%) / 18.702 (+7.5%), Realizable 21.630 (+7.6%) / 18.973 (+9.0%, close to the 10 percent limit); U+ at y+ 28.2 13.957 vs Reichardt 13.372. Details: docs/bfs-convergence-findings.md. AUDIT FOLLOW-UP (ca78589): the registered reattachment window 6.26±0.10 is now asserted in ignored *_known_miss tests; measured Realizable 6.402, RNG 6.373, Standard 5.359 (all converged); all three miss. SCOPE (merged review): add combination with the energy equation and moving walls as sub-criteria; low-Re and differential-viscosity variants stay here; wall treatments move to F-203. ADR 0015 (turbulence finishing), STILL PARTIAL: corrected step set-up BFS-C (Re_h 36000, inlet x/h = -4, measured Driver-Seegmiller profile) with three meshes. Medium-mesh x_r/h (window 6.16 to 6.36): Standard 5.350 (MISS, fine 5.452). RNG 6.334 (PASS, grid-converged: coarse 6.255, fine 6.348; marginal, 0.026 inside the upper edge on medium and 0.012 on fine, smaller than the 0.107 convection-scheme sensitivity, so not credited to any single factor). Realizable 6.413 (MISS, fine 6.520, not grid-converged). Inlet plane, free-stream k and Re_h each move x_r by < 0.01. The only factor >= 0.10 is the first-order k/epsilon convection for RNG and Realizable (second order: -0.11 to -0.16; the Standard second-order runs did not converge and decide nothing). No defect in the variants found; Standard under-prediction (-14.5 percent) and the Realizable excess are model/discretisation limits (ignored step_c_reattachment_*_known_miss tests; the old tests stay). component_diagonal corrected is a bitwise no-op on the step mesh. Scalable wall functions added (WallFunction::Scalable; flat plate average Cf within 4.6 percent of Prandtl-Schlichting at y+ 30 and y+ 1), so the title piece is in the library but not wired to the settings tree (turb.rs hook missing). Energy / moving-wall sub-criteria and low-Re variants not addressed. ADR 0017 (Realizable A0): the original report prints A0 = 4.0 (verified in the report text). The library default 4.04 is a commercial-code variant and stays the default. A0 is now selectable (KEpsilon::a0, turbulence.realizable_a0, default bit-identical, baseline hashes unchanged). With A0 = 4.0 the BFS-C Realizable medium-mesh x_r/h is 6.349 (window 6.16 to 6.36: PASS, marginal, 0.011 inside the edge) against 6.413 with 4.04. Coarse/medium/fine 6.174/6.349/6.453, abs(fine - medium) = 0.105 > 0.10 so NOT grid-converged (ignored step_c_realizable_a0_4_grid_study_known_miss), and the fine value is outside the window. The pass is marginal and mesh-dependent, smaller than the 0.14 convection-scheme sensitivity, and is not proof of correctness. The default was not changed (user decision). Status stays partial. WAVE 31B (ADR 0063, diagnosis only): the mesh dependence of Standard k-epsilon with the standard wall function in the Re_tau 178 channel is the validity limit of the log-law function, not a coding defect. The bump at y+ ~ 15 is the wall cell entering the viscous branch (y* < 11.06): G -> 0, eps -> 2 nu k/y^2, the wall-cell k collapses from ~3.05 to ~0.8 u_tau^2 (positive feedback through y* = Cmu^1/4 sqrt(k) y/nu: y* 7.45 at y+ 14.8) and U_b+ then falls to -29 percent at y+ 5.6. Switch/Hysteresis show the same at y+ 17.8. WallFunction::Scalable is mesh independent to 2.8 percent (U_b+ +4.9 to +7.9 percent) over ny 4..32. A common standard wall-function formulation (no published source is cited for it here) uses equilibrium G and eps in every wall cell (rcfd drops to a viscous branch below y*_lam). An opt-in Equilibrium treatment with those forms was tried and removed the bump (+4.1 to +4.4 percent for y+ >= 12.7) but still falls for y* < 11 (-8.7 to -22 percent), so it missed its registered limits and was not kept. Probe: crates/rcfd-turb/tests/diag_w31b_channel_wf.rs.

title: k-omega SST (and BSL) with low-Re wall treatment
acceptance: Flat plate / BFS / NACA0012 validation passes; y+~1 meshes stable
note: PARTIAL. Last recorded results: the flat plate passes against the TMR CFL3D values (ADR 0015) but misses White's 5 percent band (audit follow-up known miss), the TMR theory curves (ADR 0015) and the registered 5 percent against Karman-Schoenherr at three stations (wave 30C known miss; wave 31B: NOT a proven implementation defect). The wall-resolved backward-facing step misses the window 6.16 to 6.36 (y+ 2 runs did not converge) and the y+ stability spread misses 3 percent (ADR 0015). NACA0012 is NOT done. Wall-resolved (y+~1) meshes come from boundary-layer inflation (F-108); pseudo-transient (F-106) is the robustness fallback. Wave 6: dependency F-106 is now diagnosed (second-order step convergence fixed, see F-106 note) and the BFS case is available as a k-epsilon validation geometry (F-042 note, x_r/h 6.3-6.4 with RNG/Realizable), but F-108 (wall-resolved boundary-layer meshes) is still todo, so SST stays todo. Model: rcfd-turb sst.rs KOmegaSst (Menter 2003 form of the NASA TMR page). BSL is not a separate option. Constants and blending functions verified against https://tmbwg.github.io/turbmodels/sst.html by web fetch: beta* 0.09, a1 0.31, set 1 sigma_k 0.85 sigma_w 0.5 beta 0.075 gamma 5/9, set 2 1.0 / 0.856 / 0.0828 / 0.44, production limiter 10 beta* omega k, CDkw floor 1e-10, F1 tanh(arg1^4), F2 tanh(arg2^2), nu_t = a1 k / max(a1 omega, S F2), wall omega 10 * 6 nu/(beta1 d^2). Wall treatment (automatic across y+): Spalding law of the wall (wall.rs SpaldingLaw, bisection for u_tau) gives the wall shear and the wall-cell strain and production; omega Dirichlet on wall faces = 10 * 6 nu / (beta1 y_c^2); for cells with y+ > 5 the cell omega is fixed to sqrt(w_vis^2 + w_log^2), w_log = u_tau / (sqrt(beta*) kappa y); k zero gradient. Convection of k and omega is first-order upwind (linearUpwind diverged). A first version that fixed the wall-cell omega itself had a strongly arbitrary Cf dependence on its factor and was replaced. CHANNEL Re_tau = 395 vs MKM DNS (tests/channel_sst.rs, default tests, about 10 s, converged to 1e-9/1e-8): Wall-resolved (first-cell y+ 1.00, WallLayers first 2/395, growth 1.1, 16 layers, 60 cells): U_c+ 20.457 (+1.6% vs 20.13), U_b+ 18.167 (+4.4% vs 17.4), profile within 10 percent of DNS at y+ 5, 10, 20, 30, 50, 100, 150, 200, 300 (assertion; DNS samples interpolated from chan395.means). Coarse 14 uniform cells (y+ 28.2): U_c+ 18.774 (-6.7%), U_b+ 16.920 (-2.8%), both inside 10 percent. Sensitivity to the first-cell y+ (caveat): channel U_b+ error +5.4 / +4.4 / +2.7 / +1.4 percent at y+ 2 / 1 / 0.5 / 0.25. FLAT PLATE (tests/flat_plate_sst.rs, ignored, about 100 s release, converged about 2000 iterations; TMR set-up Re_L 5e6, plate 0..2 with Re 5e6 per m, k_inf 2.25e-7 U^2, omega_inf 125 U/L, target y+ 0.5, growth 1.1, 70 layers, 140 x 110 cells): Cf(x = 0.97) = 0.002663 vs the TMR CFL3D SST value 0.00268299 (-0.7%; the TMR page does not print a grid-converged number, the 273 x 193 grid value is used). Against the power law 0.0576 Re_x^-0.2: -3.8 / -1.9 / +0.6 / +2.6 / +4.6 percent at Re_x 2e6 / 3e6 / 5e6 / 7e6 / 1e7 (asserted within 5 percent for x <= 1.0). Against White 0.455/ln^2(0.06 Re_x): -8.5 / -7.9 / -7.3 / -6.9 / -6.6 percent (printed, NOT within 5 percent: White's formula is itself 8.7 percent above the power law at Re_x = 5e6 and SST lies between the two). Cf rises as the first-cell y+ falls (y+ 2 / 1 / 0.5 / 0.25 / 0.1: White deviation at x = 1 -10.5 / -9.2 / -7.3 / -5.9 / -4.8 percent). It is insensitive to the freestream k (1e-6 to 1e-4 of the TMR value), to NX (140 to 280) and to the growth ratio (1.1 to 1.06). NOT DONE: backward-facing step and NACA0012 validation, BSL variant, transition/low-Re damping beyond the wall treatment, linearUpwind convection of k/omega. Schema (rcfd-api): turbulence.model = k_omega_sst (steady algorithms, wall required, no energy), turbulence.omega_initial, boundaries.<patch>.omega_value (turbulence_spec = values), field omega. Documented in docs/case-schema.md and docs/reference-data.md (Spalding 1961 and Popovac-Hanjalic 2007 / Menter-Esch 2001 are cited from memory and not re-fetched). SCOPE (merged review): add generalised k-omega with calibratable coefficients, explicit algebraic stress variants and low-Re/shear-correction toggles (see F-206); wall-omega options move to F-203. ADR 0015 (turbulence finishing), STILL PARTIAL: BSL variant (SstVariant::Bsl) and low_re wall condition (SstWallMode::LowRe) added to the library. Flat plate at x = 0.5, 0.97, 1.5: SST within 1.2 percent of the TMR CFL3D SST-V values (PASS), BSL within 1.6 percent of CFL3D and 2.4 percent of SST (PASS). WAVE 30C (ADR 0061 D, crates/rcfd-turb/tests/validation_flat_plate_wall_law.rs): against the Karman-Schoenherr law at equal Re_theta (TMR data) the wall-resolved SST on a 3-mesh sequence (y+ 1, 0.5, 0.25) is low by 8.7, 6.4, 5.2, 4.4 percent at Re_theta 5000, 7500, 10000, 12500 (finest). Status unchanged (partial). A registered 5 percent miss at three stations (d1 known miss). The mesh sequence converges slowly (order 0.55, 1.94 percent between the two finest, d3 known miss). The log-law slope fit over y+ 50 to 300 misses (kappa_eff 0.36, d2 fit known miss). The pointwise u+ comparison with the Coles curve is within 3 percent. Streamwise resolution and the convection scheme of k and omega were excluded by a diagnostic; the dependence is wall-normal. Not changed in the solver. WAVE 31B (ADR 0063, diagnosis only, no solver change): the wall-resolved flat-plate deficit against Karman-Schoenherr is NOT a proven implementation defect. Term-by-term comparison with the NASA TMR SST page (https://tmbwg.github.io/turbmodels/sst.html, fetched 2026-10-18): equations, F1, F2, CD floor 1e-10, limiter 10 beta* k omega, nu_t with S, all constants and the wall condition omega_w = 10 * 6 nu/(beta1 d1^2), k_w = 0 agree. The rcfd-only extras (Automatic Spalding overrides, k zero gradient, omega fixing for y+ > 5, nu_t cap 1e5 nu, first-order k/omega convection) change Cf by < 0.2 percent at y+ < 5. Findings: (1) The Re_theta of ADR 0061 addendum 4 is biased low (negative near the leading edge, 25 percent below int Cf/2 dx at x ~ 1). With the momentum integral or an nu_t-edge profile the finest-mesh deviation from K-S is -2.4/-2.2/-1.9/-1.8 percent (momentum integral) and -3.4/-3.0/-2.7/-2.5 percent (edge profile) at Re_theta 5000/7500/10000/12500, inside 5 percent (the registered D1 measurement and its known-miss test are unchanged). (2) The remaining y+ dependence is the slowly decaying (first order) sensitivity to the wall-face omega value. Factor 1 instead of the published 10 changes Cf(Re_theta 10000) by 5.0 percent on the medium mesh, the channel U_b+ becomes mesh independent to 0.2 percent (ny 24..160) and the factor-10 sequence extrapolates to the same value. This is not a defect (10 is the published factor), no fix made. (3) Not influential (< 0.2 percent): LowRe versus Automatic, plain wall strain, k = 0 at the wall, limiter off, least-squares strain, wall-distance accuracy (exact). Cross-diffusion off moves Cf by 3.9 percent (a published term). (4) The log-law fit slope 2.78 (kappa_eff 0.36) is not explained (2.76 with factor 1). Probe: crates/rcfd-turb/tests/diag_w31b_sst_probe.rs.

title: Energy equation (T / enthalpy), Boussinesq buoyancy, ideal-gas density
acceptance: Differentially heated cavity Nu matches de Vahl Davis for Ra=1e4..1e6 within 2 percent
note: Wave 5. Acceptance met, scope partial. In WAVE 30C, Ra 1e6 misses two convergence checks (a_ra_1e6_known_miss) and the acceptance stays met. The audit of 2026-10-21 marks the item DONE on the acceptance text as written; scope beyond it, and the caveats in the audit file, are not claimed. Implemented in rcfd-fv energy.rs: EnergySolver: steady T transport with the momentum convection/diffusion operators, thermal diffusivity k/(rho cp), optional turbulent diffusivity and volumetric source. Wall gradient and conductive heat flow per patch. BuoyantSimple: SIMPLE/SIMPLEC coupled with the Boussinesq body force -beta (T - T_ref) g, balanced-force on faces. To make buoyancy balance at walls, the SIMPLE pressure condition on prescribed-velocity boundaries now extrapolates the wall pressure with the gradient that balances the body force (fixed-flux pressure). This only changes runs with a body force acting normal to a wall. Effect, measured on the de Vahl Davis cavity: Ra=1e4 n=40 Nu error +1.77% -> +0.02%, Ra=1e5 n=64 +2.98% -> +0.07%; stably stratified fluid at rest: spurious face flux 0.54 -> 8e-4 (forcing ~3e3). Case wiring (steady simple/simplec only; piso/pimple with energy is a validation error): energy.enabled/buoyancy/relax, initial.temperature. boundaries.<patch>.temperature = zero_gradient | fixed | heat_flux with temperature_value / heat_flux_value (W/m^2 into the domain) or the expression forms (F-104). physics cp/conductivity/reference_temperature/thermal_expansion/gravity. field T (probe/average/min/max reports, VTU output), heat_flow reports (conductive, out of the domain, W), res_T monitor and convergence. mesh.grading now applies to box_2d (symmetric clustering). Validation (tests/natural_convection.rs, nondimensional H=1, alpha=1, Pr=0.71, vanLeer momentum+energy, SIMPLEC, residual < 1e-9, hot/cold wall flux balance < 1e-12) vs de Vahl Davis 1983 [REFERENCE VALUES TRANSCRIBED FROM MEMORY, see cases/heated_cavity/reference; the very close agreement at all four Ra suggests they are right but they were not checked against the paper]: Ra=1e3 32x32 graded 4:1: Nu 1.1167 (-0.11%), u_max 3.622 (-0.73%), v_max 3.678 (-0.52%). Ra=1e4 40x40 graded 4:1: Nu 2.2434 (+0.02%), u_max 16.163 (-0.09%), v_max 19.517 (-0.51%). Ra=1e5 48x48 graded 6:1: Nu 4.5228 (+0.08%), u_max 34.834 (+0.30%), v_max 68.187 (-0.59%). Ra=1e6 64x64 graded 8:1: Nu 8.8383 (+0.44%), u_max 64.834 (+0.32%), v_max 220.365 (+0.46%). Mesh refinement at Ra=1e5 (48/64/96): Nu 4.5228/4.5224/4.5220. The same Ra=1e3 case runs through the settings tree (rcfd-api test): 1087 iterations, Nu 1.1167. Not done (reason for partial): ideal-gas density and a total-enthalpy formulation (constant-cp temperature formulation only, no compressible coupling), buoyancy in the transient PISO/PIMPLE algorithms, viscous heating, radiation, temperature-dependent properties. The reconstructed cell-centre velocity of a fluid at rest still shows an O(h) error next to non-wall boundaries (not measured further). Update: transient energy (implicit Euler/BDF2) and Boussinesq buoyancy with PISO/PIMPLE are done (BuoyantPimple; energy now accepted with piso/pimple in the case file; temperature advanced first on the previous flux, so the coupling is first order in dt). Checks fixed before running: Slab conduction vs erfc (Euler error 1.78e-4 and 1.09e-4 for dt 2e-5 and 1e-5, ratio 1.63; BDF2 4.4e-5). Ra=1e4 cavity marched to steady state: Nu 2.2434 (de Vahl Davis 2.243), u_max 16.162 (16.178), v_max 19.516 (19.617), all within 2 percent, Nu equal to the steady SIMPLEC value. Stratified fluid at rest max |phi| 7e-15. Ra=1e3 case-file run with piso Nu 1.1167, wall flows balanced to 1e-6. Still not done: ideal-gas density and total enthalpy (the SIMPLE/PISO kernel is kinematic with no density anywhere, so variable density is a core rewrite), viscous heating, radiation, temperature-dependent properties and scalars with transient runs. Update (wave 10, ADR 0005): ideal-gas density and the total-enthalpy energy equation are done in the steady pressure-based variable-density SIMPLE/SIMPLEC kernel (rcfd-fv varden.rs; case switch fluid.density = ideal_gas, fluid.mode compressible | low_mach, constant or Sutherland viscosity, conductivity from Pr, stagnation inlets, nozzle_2d generator, docs/case-schema.md, rcfd-api tests/variable_density.rs; unsupported combinations are located diagnostics). The constant-density code path is untouched (baseline hashes of the existing solver runs identical). Checks written into the ADR before any run, all met: Differentially heated cavity with large dT against Le Quere et al. 2005 (ESAIM M2AN 39, DOI 10.1051/m2an:2005027, Table 1 verified from the author's postprint), 96x96 graded 8, Ra=1e6, eps=0.6: constant properties Nu 8.8678 vs 8.85978 (+0.09 %, limit 1 %), P/P0 0.856023 vs 0.856338 (-0.037 %, limit 0.3 %); Sutherland Nu 8.7034 vs 8.6866 (+0.19 %), P/P0 0.924353 vs 0.924487 (-0.014 %); hot/cold heat flow imbalance below 1e-8 (limit 1e-6). Hydrostatic ideal-gas column H=8000 m: density error 3.8e-5 (isothermal, limit 1e-3) and 2.1e-5 (linear T, limit 2e-3), speed 2e-14, mass drift 1e-16. Constant-density limit: lid cavity max |u-u_old|/U 5.6e-12 (low_mach, limit 1e-4) and 1.3e-6 (compressible, limit 1e-3); Boussinesq limit Nu +0.045 % (limit 1 %). Disclosed: the hydrostatic tests use mu = 10 Pa s and k = 100 W/m/K (air values leave the conduction-driven column below round-off of the balanced face terms); the ADR Rayleigh-number formula had a g^2 typo, corrected before any validation run. Still not done: viscous heating, radiation, transient variable density, turbulence, species with variable density, non-orthogonal pressure correctors in the variable-density kernel. Update (wave 12, ADR 0009, checks and limits registered in the ADR before any transient code; never changed): Transient variable density (implicit Euler and variable-step BDF2, Euler first step, SIMPLE-inner iterations per step, density time derivative in continuity, momentum and energy, transient Rhie-Chow defect, exact discrete mass balance) in the pressure-based kernel for the ideal gas (compressible and low_mach) and the real gas. Viscous heating (viscous work div(tau.u) in the total enthalpy, dissipation in low_mach, switch energy.viscous_heating) and a volumetric heat_source. Case file solver.algorithm = pimple, fluid.inner_iterations / inner_tolerance, energy.viscous_heating / heat_source, initial.velocity_expression_x/y/z (docs/case-schema.md, located validation errors). Steady results bit-identical (ideal nozzle hash, varden_* and baseline_hashes unchanged). Measured (release): T1 closed-box heating p error 2.9e-10 / 1.7e-10 (compressible Euler / BDF2) and 3.3e-12 / 4.8e-12 (low-Mach), mass 2e-15, |u| 4e-10 (limits 1e-6, 1e-11, 1e-8) PASS. T1r CO2 Peng-Robinson energy balance 1.2e-10 / 2.1e-10 (1e-6) PASS. T2 temporal order Euler 1.019 [0.90, 1.10], BDF2 1.989 [1.85, 2.15] PASS. T3 standing acoustic wave frequency error -0.13 % (1 %) and BDF2 amplitude ratio 0.99157 [0.98, 1.001] PASS, Euler order 0.922 [0.85, 1.15] PASS, BDF2 order 1.34 [1.80, 2.20] MISS (ignored t3c_order_bdf2_known_miss; post-hoc cause: a_P is the mean of the component diagonals and the one-cell-high symmetric strip inflates it, order 2.07 on a taller strip; not a gate). T4 differentially heated cavity (Le Quere Ra 1e6, eps 0.6, BDF2 dt 0.02 s, 20 s) Nu 8.8676 / 8.8681 vs 8.85978 (+0.09 %, limit 1 %), P/P0 0.856036 vs 0.856338 (-0.035 %, 0.3 %), heat-flow imbalance 5.3e-5 (2e-3), stationarity 4.8e-5 (1e-3) PASS (heavy, 590 s). T5 steady limit of the transient ADR 0005 a1 duct vs the steady kernel max dMach 6.0e-4 (2e-3) and dp/p0 1.9e-4 (5e-4) PASS, mass flow vs steady 1.64e-3 / 1.62e-3 (1e-3) and in/out 1.6e-5 (1e-6) MISS at 400 steps (ignored t5_..._mass_flow_known_miss; post-hoc 1200 steps would pass, in/out 5e-10). T6 Couette flow with viscous heating, compressible and low-Mach, both-isothermal and one-adiabatic wall: profile error 1.6e-4 of mu U^2/(2k) (limit 1 %), wall heat flow 1.00000 of the analytic value (1 %), switch-off dT 1e-10 K (1e-6 K) PASS. T7 case-file closed box p error 1.3e-10 (1e-6) and Couette 1.6e-4 (1 %) PASS. Kernel faults found by the checks and fixed: real-gas closed-domain mass shift (Newton with the true EOS); lagged boundary density of prescribed-velocity faces diverged for flow Courant number > 1 (now implicit upwind, transient compressible runs only); adiabatic-wall energy BC (steady kernel keeps its limitation unless viscous heating is on). Disclosed: tightened linear-solver tolerances in the kernel tests, compressible inner change floors near 1e-11, T6 first steps stop at the inner cap, the transient solver diverges from a start that contradicts an imposed velocity profile (T7 uses initial.velocity_expression). No shock-tube or choked transient benchmark is claimed. Still not done: radiation, turbulence and species with variable density, time-varying boundary expressions in variable-density runs, non-orthogonal pressure correctors in the variable-density kernel, adaptive time step. ADR 0010: the component-consistent diagonal (opt-in solver.component_diagonal = "corrected") brings the T3c BDF2 order on the one-cell-high acoustic strip to 2.08 (registered [1.80, 2.20]; 1.34 with the averaged diagonal, which stays the default). The T5 mass-flow limits then pass (9.3e-4, 9.2e-4 against 1e-3) but the in/out equality at 400 steps still misses (1.56e-5 against 1e-6). SCOPE (merged review): make viscous dissipation, pressure work, kinetic-energy and inlet-diffusion switches explicit sub-criteria. WAVE 30C (ADR 0061 A, crates/rcfd-fv/tests/validation_natural_convection.rs): three-mesh sequences per Rayleigh number against Table V of the 1983 paper (primary). Finest-mesh Nu_avg errors -0.04, +0.07, +0.07, +0.33 percent at Ra 1e3, 1e4, 1e5, 1e6; u_max and v_max within 0.6 percent; Nu_max within 2 percent; observed order about 1 to 3, GCI(Nu) at most 0.13 percent. Ra 1e3 to 1e5 meet every registered check; Ra 1e6 misses two convergence checks (a non-converged 32 x 32 coarse mesh and a 0.04 percent non-monotone v_max), recorded as a_ra_1e6_known_miss. The acceptance (Nu within 2 percent for Ra 1e4 to 1e6) stays met with the status still partial for scope reasons. title: Passive scalar and multicomponent species transport; temperature-dependent properties (polynomial, Sutherland)
acceptance: Mixing layer species mass conserved to machine precision
note: Done. Caveats: constant density (no ideal-gas density), constant per-species diffusivity (no multicomponent diffusion), no reactions, steady algorithms only; the Sutherland constants are user inputs, no data shipped (see F-111). rcfd-fv scalar.rs: one shared implicit scalar sweep (EnergySolver::iterate now calls it, no duplicated assembly), ScalarTransport, SpeciesSet (N-1 transported mass fractions, balance species by difference), exact discrete boundary_flux per patch. rcfd-core materials.rs: PropertyLaw (constant, polynomial, Sutherland). api: scalars.<name>, species.<name> (diffusivity or Schmidt number, source, per-patch fixed/gradient with expression profiles). properties.viscosity/conductivity/specific_heat (T-dependent via the nu_face and alpha_face paths; conflicts with rheology, UDF viscosity, turbulence, missing energy, non-steady algorithms diagnosed). reports scalar_flux/scalar_average, res_<name> monitors, VTU fields, solver.pressure_abs_tol. Validation (checks fixed beforehand): Mixing layer of two streams, 3 species with different diffusivities (one via Schmidt number), 100x50: net boundary outflow per species relative to summed boundary fluxes A -3.7e-16, B -3.5e-16, balance species C -8.7e-17 (limit 1e-12), mass fractions sum to 1 within 1.1e-16 (limit 1e-14), similarity-solution profile error 0.66 percent of the jump (limit 2); fv-level run on the frozen uniform flux 3e-15 and 0.11 percent. Couette flow with polynomial viscosity (b=2): max |u - ln(1+by)/ln(1+b)| 2.8e-4 U (limit 1 percent), Sc=1 scalar equals u to 1.9e-9 (limit 1e-6). Conduction with k(T) vs Kirchhoff transform: T error 1.7e-4 of range (limit 0.2 percent), heat flow 0.374967 vs 0.375 (limit 0.5 percent). Sod (gamma 1.4, t=0.2, HLLC+vanLeer+RK3) density L1 vs exact: 5.30e-3, 2.82e-3, 1.57e-3 at n=100/200/400 (order 0.91, 0.84); n=200 density L1 for Rusanov 3.65e-3, Roe 2.64e-3, HLLC 2.82e-3, AUSM+ 2.44e-3, first-order HLLC 1.33e-2; mass/energy conserved to 1e-12. Oblique shock (M=2, 10 deg ramp, 100x35 cells, steady drift 8e-8): measured wave angle 39.324 deg vs theta-beta-M 39.314 deg (0.025 percent), post-shock pressure within 1e-4 of the theoretical ratio. Reference star-state values (p*=0.30313, u*=0.92745) verified in wave 6a against a published analytic Sod solution (arXiv:2108.01709) and beta=39.31 deg against an independent theta-beta-M solve (39.314 deg). The Toro Table 4.3 attribution is unconfirmed. The tests also check Rankine-Hugoniot consistency independently. NOT done: implicit time-integration option. Wave 6b: selectable from the case schema and service: solver.algorithm = compressible; compressible.flux, reconstruction, rk_order, cfl, gamma, gas_constant, mode transient|steady, steady_tolerance, initial uniform|riemann with left/right states. boundaries compressible_bc = slip|extrapolate|fixed with density_value/pressure_value/velocity_value. mesh generator wedge_2d with ramp_start/ramp_angle. fields rho, p, T, mach, ux.. examples cases/sod/sod.toml and cases/wedge/wedge.toml. Sod through the settings tree reproduces the library run to 1e-13 (172 steps at n=100) and gives density L1 5.302e-3 against the exact solution. The 60x20 wedge example peaks at p = 1.2496 (free stream 0.714) and conserves the inflow mass flux to 1e-9. Unsupported combinations are validate errors with line numbers (forward Euler with a limiter, turbulence, energy, pseudo-transient, periodic meshes, force/moment/heat-flow/y+ reports, bad fixed state). Residual semantics: res_u = max relative density change per step, res_p = relative pressure change, continuity = relative mass drift; transient runs do not converge to zero. WAVE 31A (ADR 0062): TvdLimiter::VanAlbada overflowed to NaN for gradient ratios above 1.34e154 (HLLC + Van Albada + RK3 aborted at step 1); fixed (r > 1e150 uses the algebraically identical (r + 1)/(r + 1/r), bit-identical below). Choked converging-diverging nozzle (240x12, exit Mach 1.854, supersonic branch, p_e/p0 = 0.1602): Mach error 9.2e-4 (limit 3e-2), p/p0 1.3e-3 (2e-2), choked mass flow vs A* p0 sqrt(gamma/(R T0)) (2/(gamma+1))^((gamma+1)/(2(gamma-1))) -4.05e-4 at inlet and outlet (acceptance limit 1 percent), in/out 2e-14. Deviation: the choked case needs under-relaxation 0.7/0.5/0.7 (defaults 0.9/1.0/0.9 diverged when the supersonic region forms) and a back-pressure continuation start-up (0.98 p0 to p_e in 40 stages of 100 iterations, then 6000 iterations at p_e); starting at the mean pressure diverged. These start-up choices were not registered; the tolerances were not changed. Isentropic and area-Mach relations are standard textbook formulae. The choked test is heavy (about 80 s release, #[ignore]). Caveats: steady and laminar only, no shock capturing beyond what the first/second-order upwind density gives (not tested), residual res_u floors at about 1e-5..1e-6 for the cavity and nozzle cases. API wiring test (nozzle_2d case file): mass flow in/out within 1e-6 and throat Mach 0.2997 vs 0.3 met; the registered residual target 1e-8 was NOT met (res_u 2.6e-5, res_p 6e-13 at 3000 iterations), so such runs stop at max_iterations unless convergence conditions are used. AUDIT FOLLOW-UP (ca78589): the 1e-8 residual target of the API nozzle case is recorded as subsonic_nozzle_residual_target_1e8_known_miss (res_u 2.6e-5 after 3000 iterations, not converged). REAL GAS (ADR 0007, checks and limits written before any code): fluid.density = real_gas (fluid.eos peng_robinson|redlich_kwong, fluid.species from a built-in critical-data table N2/O2/Ar/CO2/CH4/H2/H2O or explicit critical_temperature/critical_pressure/acentric_factor/molar_mass, fluid.specific_heat = constant ideal-gas cp0) in the same varden kernel. rcfd-fv realgas.rs gives rho(p,T) (vapour root), psi = d rho/dp|T analytic for the transonic pressure equation, enthalpy and entropy departures (h = cp0 T + h_dep), cp, cv, real sound speed (Mach), T from h by Newton, and the stagnation inlet follows the real-gas isentrope. Schema keys with precise located validation errors (unknown species, missing constants, low_mach, gas_constant, keys without real_gas), docs/case-schema.md, JSON schema from the same Rust schema, CLI/API/assistant validate through Case. The ideal-gas path is bit-identical (new fixed-iteration hash test recorded before the edits, baseline_hashes and all varden tests unchanged). Measured, CO2, p0 5 MPa, T0 400 K, cp0 940, against an independent real-gas isentropic reference integrated in the test (RK4 in p, dT/dp|s = T (dv/dT)_p/cp, energy balance to 3.5e-9, sonic state at the mass-flux maximum M = 1.0000): Subsonic duct (R5, throat M 0.3, A_t/A* 2.0495 vs 2.0351 ideal) Mach 7.7e-4 (limit 1.5e-2), p 4.1e-5 (5e-3), T 8.4e-6 (3e-3), mass flow -2.7e-4 (limit 1e-2), in/out 3.2e-13. Choked nozzle (R6, 240x12, exit M 1.78 branch, ACCEPTANCE) choked mass flow -2.8e-4 at inlet and outlet (limit 1 percent), Mach 9.2e-4 (3e-2), p 1.3e-3 (2e-2). The real-gas choked flux G* is 5.73 percent above the ideal-gas formula, so the EOS is active (the API case differs 5.5 percent from the ideal-gas case at 5 MPa). Ideal-gas limit through the solver (R3): CO2 at 2 kPa real vs ideal solver mass flow 2.1e-5 (limit 1e-3), Mach 2.3e-7, p 5.6e-8, T 5.8e-7; through the case file 1.2e-5. Solver tuning disclosed: the choked real-gas case used the same start-up as the ideal one (under-relaxation 0.7/0.5/0.7, back-pressure continuation 0.98 p0 to p_e in 40 stages of 100 iterations, then 6000 iterations); the subsonic cases used the defaults; nothing else was tuned. EOS-level KNOWN MISSES against NIST (limits registered beforehand, not changed; tests ignored, named *_known_miss): (R1) PR density within 1 percent where |Z-1| <= 0.05 missed for N2 at 300 K and 5.1/10.1/15.1 MPa (+1.03, +1.68, +2.24 percent); the other 20 of the 23 points with a tolerance pass (CO2 350 K errors +0.04 to +2.1 percent, 310 K up to +2.9 percent, N2 140 K 3.1 MPa +4.0 percent; the dense points with Z_NIST < 0.5 are reported only: CO2 310 K 9.1 MPa -11.4 percent, N2 140 K 6.1 and 9.1 MPa -1.3 and +1.8 percent, CO2 310 K 8.1 MPa +0.1 percent). (R2) Enthalpy difference within 10 percent missed for N2 at 300 K (+18.8, +15.7, +12.3 percent at 5.1/10.1/20.1 MPa; CO2 passes at +9.3/+8.5/+7.8 percent at 350 K), entropy differences within 0.7 percent (limit 2), sound speeds within 0.23 percent for CO2 and 1.55 percent for N2 at 10.1 MPa (limits 0.5 to 5), dcp -7.5 percent (limit 20). (R3) The 1 Pa ideal-gas limit of the enthalpy and entropy departures (limit 1e-8) missed for CO2: 3.1e-8 / 2.1e-8 (PR), 2.6e-8 / 1.7e-8 (RK), the limit was mis-estimated because the departures scale with p. Density, psi and sound speed pass at 5e-8 to 1e-7 (limit 1e-6). The NIST reference values were retrieved through a summarising page fetcher and critical constants are from memory: both marked unverified in docs/reference-data.md. Approximations: energy diffusivity k/cp0 and zero-gradient enthalpy for adiabatic walls (cp0 dT/dn), mu and k are user inputs, no liquid root or phase change (a state without a vapour root falls back to the ideal gas), compressible mode only, no van der Waals, mixtures or transient. Update (ADR 0009): the transient variable-density solver also runs with the real gas (Peng-Robinson CO2, 8 MPa, 330 K, closed box with a volumetric heat source, Euler and BDF2): energy balance rho0 (u(p,T) - u0) = q t to 1.2e-10 / 2.1e-10 (limit 1e-6), pressure equals the EOS at the fixed density to 1e-15 (1e-6), mass 1.7e-15 (1e-11), which also required the Newton mass shift with the true EOS. No transient real-gas nozzle or choked benchmark is claimed. The registered API residual target of the ideal-gas nozzle case (1e-8) remains the known miss recorded above.

title: Compressible BCs: total pressure/temperature, characteristic far-field, non-reflecting
acceptance: NACA0012 transonic Cp within published scatter; no spurious reflection test
note: Wave 11, PARTIAL. Check D, NACA 0012 transonic Cp within published scatter, is NOT ATTEMPTED. One part of check B MISSED: registered sigma = 0.02 limit R <= 0.05, measured 0.461. Built: rcfd-fv compressible_bc.rs (ADR 0006); boundary face states use the physical flux. CompBc::TotalInlet (p0, T0, direction; outgoing invariant from the interior). PressureOutlet (subsonic/supersonic switching). NonReflecting (relaxation weight sigma). FarField (Riemann invariants, free-stream Mach/angle). Case schema: compressible_bc = total_inlet | pressure_outlet | farfield | nonreflecting with total_pressure_value, temperature_value, flow_direction, pressure_value, mach_value, flow_angle, reflection_value; located validate errors, docs/case-schema.md, JSON schema (generated), assistant BC-suggestion note. Checks were registered in the ADR before any run. A: algebraic face-state checks and A5 free-stream preservation (5.6e-16): PASS. B: no spurious reflection (1-D Gaussian pulse, 400 cells, reflected/incident amplitude): Fixed-pressure outlet 0.941 (registered 0.8..1.2) PASS. Outlet with sigma = 0: 0.0000 (limit 0.02) PASS. Registered sigma = 0.02 limit R <= 0.05 MISSED: measured 0.461 (kept as ignored test b_non_reflecting_sigma_002_known_miss). Cause: the stateless relaxation reflects waves slower than dx/(sigma a); post-hoc, disclosed, not a gate: sigma 0.002 -> 0.078, 0.005 -> 0.172, 0.01 -> 0.293, 0.05 -> 0.709, 1 -> 0.941. Only normal incidence is treated; sigma = 0 imposes no pressure so it cannot hold a back pressure. C: total-pressure inlet reproduces the F-061 isentropic nozzle (200x10, same geometry and limits, density-based HLLC/MUSCL/RK3, marched 136934 steps to a 1e-9 density change): Mach 5.4e-3 (1.5e-2), p/p0 5.7e-4 (5e-3), T/T0 1.8e-4 (3e-3), inlet mass flow -4.9e-3 vs A*-formula (1e-2), in/out 3.3e-7 (1e-3): PASS (heavy, ignored, 220 s release). D: NACA 0012 transonic Cp within published scatter: NOT ATTEMPTED. The kernel could run an Euler airfoil (cylinder_ogrid + warp), but no quantitative published reference (AGARD AR-211 scatter, Vassberg-Jameson Euler values) was accessible, so no gate was invented; ignored placeholder naca0012_transonic_cp_known_miss. No solver parameter was tuned (defaults HLLC, van Leer, RK3, CFL 0.4). Not done: airfoil validation, oblique/multi-dimensional non-reflecting (Giles), vortex far-field correction, pressure-based (varden) kernel BCs. Status stays partial. SCOPE (merged review): outlet pressure-averaging options, mass-flow update strategies and flow-regime options move to F-200; impedance-type conditions to F-243.

title: Expression language for setup and post (named expressions with units, arithmetic/functions, field and report references)

title: Pseudo-transient (local time-stepping) steady solver option with automatic timescale selection
acceptance: Lid-driven cavity at Re 1000 and a backward-facing step converge with pseudo-transient where plain SIMPLE needs lower relaxation; timescale factor and auto/local/physical modes selectable in the settings tree
note: P1. Gap: pseudo-transient convergence control (physical, local and automatic timescales) is standard practice; improves robustness for phases 3-5. Partial. The acceptance (cavity and a step converge with pseudo-transient where plain SIMPLE needs lower relaxation) is only partly met: both converge with pseudo-transient, but plain SIMPLEC now also converges and the Re_h = 400 step still needs a specific scheme/coupling combination. The automatic pseudo-step controllers of WAVE 17A (ADR 0023) do NOT converge the registered cavity/step cases (known misses), so they are not validated and the status stays partial. Partial (wave 5). Done: the SIMPLE/SIMPLEC pseudo-transient term (V/dt added to the momentum diagonal with explicit old-iterate source, before relaxation) was already in rcfd-fv simple.rs but untested and not exposed; now selectable in the settings tree: solver.pseudo_mode = off | auto (one global step factor*L/U_max) | local (per-cell dt = cfl*V/sum(0.5|phi|+nu*lap)) | physical (fixed dt). solver.pseudo_cfl, solver.pseudo_dt and the timescale factor solver.pseudo_factor. Tests: rcfd-api case test runs all modes from the tree; rcfd-fv factor test (factor 0.4 on cfl 5 equals cfl 2). Measured, lid-driven cavity Re=1000, 32x32, linearUpwind (tests/pseudo.rs, release): Plain SIMPLEC alpha_u 0.9/0.95/1.0 diverge (no convergence in 5296/4154/3298 iterations, residual ~0.7, then non-finite). SIMPLE 0.7/0.3 converges in 1900 iterations. Pseudo-transient with alpha_u = 1 (no momentum relaxation) converges to residual 1e-6 for local cfl 2 (1798), cfl 5 (1364), physical dt 0.05 (1918), 0.2 (1515) and auto (1532 iterations), all to the same steady state. Larger pseudo steps fail: local cfl >= 10 and physical dt 1 do not converge (residual ~0.6-0.7). 64x64 vanLeer: SIMPLEC 0.95 does not converge in 6000 its (residual 3.7e-2), pseudo local cfl 5 converges in 3996, SIMPLE 0.7/0.3 in 4552 (wave-5 exploration run, not a kept test). NOT met: the backward-facing step. With the project backward_step mesh (uniform inlet, expansion ratio 2, 16+80 x 8+8 cells; Re_h=400 vanLeer also 32+160 x 16+16): Re_h=100 converges with every variant (SIMPLE 646 its, pseudo cfl 5 571; kept as a light test). Re_h=200/400 with second-order schemes (vanLeer, linearUpwind) does not converge with ANY variant, including plain SIMPLE 0.7/0.3, SIMPLEC 0.9 and all pseudo modes tried (residual stalls 0.05-0.5 or diverges). With first-order upwind Re_h=200 converges for all, Re_h=400 only for SIMPLE 0.7/0.3 (1395 its). So the step case shows no pseudo-transient advantage and points to an unresolved robustness issue of second-order schemes on the step (corner/outlet) that was not diagnosed. Note: an earlier exploration table with 'res 0.00e0' entries was invalid (NaN fields); the test harness now treats non-finite fields as failure. Next: diagnose the step (outlet backflow treatment, limiter chatter at the corner, deferred-correction under-relaxation), then re-run the BFS comparison. Wave 6b: remaining solver settings of the library are now in the schema: solver.h_operator (default | from_solution | previous_iterate), p_ref_cell/p_ref_value, bulk_velocity/bulk_direction (mean-velocity driver), physics.body_force, momentum/pressure linear-solver tolerances and iteration caps, ddt_correction, and res_T/res_nut/res_rho are accepted convergence monitors. The pseudo-transient and energy settings were already exposed (see above) and are unchanged. Documented in rcfd/docs/case-schema.md. WAVE 6 UPDATE: the step failure is DIAGNOSED AND FIXED. Root cause: SimpleSettings.h_from_solution defaulted to false, i.e. H (and the Rhie-Chow flux) used the previous iterate instead of the solved momentum predictor, a Jacobi-like lagged iteration that is marginally unstable with second-order deferred correction (wave of O(1) amplitude, wavelength ~10 cells, growing toward the outlet; l_out 10 converged, l_out 14-20 did not; dx 0.5 and 0.125 converged, 0.25 did not; alpha 0.5/0.2 converged). Now default true (still false while a MeanVelocityDriver is active, whose gain assumes the lagged response). Evidence and tables: docs/bfs-convergence-findings.md. Measured after the fix: Step (uniform inlet, ER 2, 16+80 x 8+8) Re_h = 200 linearUpwind SIMPLE 0.7/0.3 646 its. Cavity Re = 1000 32x32 linearUpwind plain SIMPLEC alpha_u 0.95 WITHOUT pseudo-transient now converges (442 its; SIMPLE 0.7/0.3 660 its), so the wave-5 premise that plain SIMPLE needs lower relaxation than pseudo-transient came from this defect (test now asserts both the legacy failure with h_from_solution = false and the new convergence). Laminar step, parabolic inlet (tests/step_laminar.rs): Re_h = 200 vanLeer SIMPLEC alpha_u 1 + local pseudo cfl 5 converges (607 its); plain SIMPLE/SIMPLEC, linearUpwind and vanLeer converge for Re_h <= 200. STILL NOT MET at Re_h = 400: vanLeer SIMPLE 0.7/0.3 (and 0.5/0.2, 0.3/0.1) limit-cycles (residual 0.02-0.2). linearUpwind SIMPLEC 0.95 does not converge (0.4). Pseudo local cfl 5 (alpha_u 1) does not converge with vanLeer (4.9e-2) or linearUpwind (4.4e-2) in 3000-4000 its. Converging recipes: vanLeer + SIMPLEC alpha_u 0.9 (696 its on 120x16, 1404-2359 its on 320x32 - 480x48) and linearUpwind + SIMPLE 0.7/0.3 (2795 its). So the acceptance (cavity and a step converge with pseudo-transient where plain SIMPLE needs lower relaxation) is only partly met: both converge with pseudo-transient, but plain SIMPLEC now also converges and the Re_h = 400 step still needs a specific scheme/coupling combination. No auto setting beyond the h_from_solution default was added. Laminar reattachment x_r/h (ER 2, parabolic inlet, vanLeer; Re_Armaly = 2 Re_h): Re_h 100: 4.95; 200: 8.19; 389: 11.54; 400: 11.24 / 11.67 / 11.75 on three meshes (not yet mesh independent). Remembered literature (NOT verified, from memory): Gartling 1990 Re 800 about 12.2, Armaly 1983 about 12 (3D); lower Re values not citable. Graded step mesh: gen::backward_step_graded (StepGrading, StepSpec::from_expansion_ratio) agrees with the uniform mesh of the same size to 0.2 percent at Re_h 400 (11.70 vs 11.67). Convention warning: Re_h = 389 was run as asked (Re_Armaly 778); Armaly's own '389' would be Re_h about 195, for which Re_h 200 (8.19) is the nearer point. SCOPE (merged review): local timescale factor, automatic/physical timescale and nonlinear acceleration are tracked in F-209. WAVE 17A UPDATE (ADR 0023): automatic pseudo-step controllers solver.pseudo_control = ser | ser2 (cap solver.pseudo_scale_max) added and tested; they do NOT converge the registered cavity/step cases (known misses; fixed cfl 5-50 converges on the cavity, 100 fails), so they are not validated and the status stays partial. Also solver.residual_norm = reference | backward | scaled; the stalls of the F-200 C2/D1/D2/E2 residuals were diagnosed as a normalisation artefact and pass with scaled.

note: P1. Gap: boundary-layer (prism) mesh generation with growth and shell controls; needed for wall-resolved turbulence validation. Still PARTIAL (WAVE 39C, ADR 0094). Remaining: the unstructured-wall-patch clause (inflate_patch builds an outward shell not merged into a fluid domain; waits on F-234). Wave 6: not started. Tests (rcfd-mesh, 4 new, 24 pass): layer heights and growth ratio equal the request to 1e-5/1e-6, mirror symmetry, impossible stacks rejected, y+ round trip (generated first cell centre has y+ 1.0 to 1e-5), volume conserved to 1e-12, check_mesh ok and max aspect ratio = dx/h1 with no warnings. Schema (box_2d and channel_2d y direction): mesh.wall_layers, first_layer_height, target_y_plus, layer_growth (1.2), layer_walls both | lower, layer_reference_velocity, layer_reference_length, layer_u_tau, located diagnostics (rcfd-api tests/sst_schema.rs); example cases/channel/sst_channel.toml. Solved check of the acceptance 'flat-plate mesh built from a target y+ meets it within 10 percent': TMR-like flat plate (Re 5e6 per m, 0..2 m) with target y+ 0.5 at x = 2 gives a solved first-cell y+ of 0.48-0.54 along the plate (within 10 percent of the target; tests/flat_plate_sst.rs, ignored). SCOPE (merged review): add uniform, aspect-ratio and last-ratio offset types; volume-fill integration in F-234. WAVE 15B (ADR 0020), still PARTIAL. New rcfd-mesh inflate::inflate_patch(mesh, patch, LayerSizing) (layer 1 of the sizing lies against the far cap, which is the new wall; a first version had this reversed and was corrected after review, see ADR 0020 addendum 1) adds prismatic/hex layers on the outward side of ANY boundary patch (triangles, quads, curved) with uniform, first-height + growth, aspect-ratio (first height = local surface size / aspect) and last-ratio sizing, and returns an InflateReport (first/last height, thickness, growth min/max, QualityReport). Checks (inflate.rs, all at first run): box patch volume, layer planes, side area to 1e-15 relative; 72-triangle prism patch volume error 1.5e-14; O-grid inner wall added volume matches the polygon closed form to 2.3e-15; sizing-type heights to 1e-12; wall-adjacent cell height 3.2e-4 and y+ 0.8 recovered to 1e-9 (i6c); max aspect ratio 100.0 as derived.
