title: Report definitions, convergence conditions and automatic stopping criteria
acceptance: A report definition (e.g. drag coefficient) can drive a monitor and a stop condition (window range / change tolerance / residual); the run stops automatically and records why
note: P1. Gap: report definitions, convergence conditions, monitors and interrupt conditions. Done (wave 5). Caveat: conditions are evaluated on recorded monitor samples (once per iteration/step), not on sub-iteration values. rcfd-post::convergence (Condition kinds window_range / change / below / above on any monitor series, any/all combination). Settings tree: top-level convergence.<name> {monitor, type, tolerance, window, relative}; solver.stop_when (any|all), solver.min_iterations. Any monitor can be used: residuals (res_u, res_p, res_T, continuity, courant, dt) or any report (drag coefficient, heat flow, expression report). Reports already feed monitors each iteration/step (F-082); above conditions act as interrupt conditions (run ends with converged=false). The run records why it stopped (Simulation::stop_reason(), status JSON stop_reason, HTML summary row 'Stopped because', CLI prints 'stopped: ...'); built-in reasons: residual targets met, iteration limit, end time. Unknown monitor names are rejected at validation. Measured: lid-driven cavity 12x12 with a lid_drag report, window_range relative tolerance 1e-5 over 10 samples stops after 112 iterations ('range 9.352e-6 <= 1.000e-5'); the window one step earlier did not satisfy it. Tests: 3 unit tests in rcfd-post (window, change/below/above/non-finite, any/all) and 3 case-level tests in rcfd-api (report-driven stop with recorded reason, interrupt + built-in reasons, all-combination).

title: Non-Newtonian and temperature-dependent viscosity laws (power, Carreau, Carreau-Yasuda, Cross, Herschel-Bulkley, Bingham; Arrhenius/WLF shift)
acceptance: Power-law channel flow matches the analytic profile; Carreau recovers Newtonian limits at low and high shear; laws exposed in the settings tree with units
note: Done. Law forms are from memory of the literature and marked unverified in docs/reference-data.md. rcfd-api `rheology`: settings group `rheology` (docs/case-schema.md) with power_law, carreau, carreau_yasuda, cross, herschel_bulkley (Papanastasiou-regularised yield stress) and bingham, viscosity clamps, face-wise relaxation, and temperature dependence by time-temperature superposition mu(g,T) = a_T mu_ref(a_T g) with Arrhenius, WLF or a lookup table a_T(T) (F-105 tables; needs the energy equation). Dynamic viscosities in Pa s, times in s, stress in Pa, declared with units in the schema. The solver uses mu(shear rate sqrt(2 S:S))/rho on the momentum-diffusion faces in steady SIMPLE/SIMPLEC (with or without the energy equation) and transient PISO/PIMPLE runs (PimpleSolver gained nu_face). Measured (tests/rheology.rs, checks fixed first, 60x20 plane channel, H=1, U=1, K=0.1): Power law n=0.6: profile error 0.77% of centreline (limit 2%), dp/dx +0.26% (limit 3%); n=1.4: 1.15%, -0.86%. Bingham (mu_p 0.1, tau0 0.2, regularisation 200 s) vs Buckingham-Reiner: profile 1.6% of the plug velocity 1.349 (limit 5%), dp/dx +1.04% (limit 5%), 1783 iterations. Carreau, Carreau-Yasuda, Cross and power law (n=1) in their Newtonian limits reproduce the plain run to below 1e-6 (steady and PISO). Unit tests: Carreau within 1e-6 of mu_0 at lambda*g=2e-4 and within 3e-3 of mu_inf at 1e14, closed forms, Yasuda a=2 equals Carreau. Arrhenius and table shifts at uniform T equal a Newtonian run with scaled viscosity (1e-6). A temperature outside the shift table stops the run with a message; bad parameters are diagnostics. Not done: the transposed-gradient viscous term of a variable viscosity, yield-stress laws with a temperature shift (diagnostic), combination with turbulence models, the compressible solver or a UDF viscosity (diagnostics), restart checkpoints carrying the viscosity relaxation history.

title: Material property library: temperature-dependent polynomials, Sutherland, ideal-mixture rules and open real-gas EOS (ideal, Peng-Robinson, Redlich-Kwong, IAPWS-IF97 from public papers)
acceptance: Air/water properties within 1 percent of published tables; mixture rules unit-tested; no third-party licensed data (no REFPROP files) is shipped
note: Partial. Audit 2026-10-14: the 1 percent air-viscosity criterion is NOT met by the Sutherland law. The follow-up records it as sutherland_air_viscosity_within_1pct_300_to_500_k_known_miss (-1.08% at 400 K, -1.46% at 500 K). rcfd-core fluids.rs: NASA TM-4513 species polynomials (N2, O2, Ar, H2O, CO2, CH4, H2), mole/mass fractions, mass-weighted and ideal-volume mixing, Wilke gas-mixture rule, air mixture, Sutherland air laws and 200-600 K cubic fit laws, Redlich-Kwong and Peng-Robinson EOS (roots, density, fugacity, residual enthalpy, saturation pressure). iapws.rs: IAPWS-IF97 regions 1 and 2, B23, saturation pressure, IAPWS R12-08 viscosity and R15-11 conductivity (no critical enhancement). Water: all IF97 verification points (Tables 5, 15, 35) and the viscosity/conductivity verification tables reproduced to 1e-8 / 1e-7 relative. Air check pre-registered at 1 percent for 300-500 K against the CRC/NIST gas tables (Huber) and NASA TN D-5452: cp -0.01/+0.12/-0.01 percent and Sutherland conductivity -0.64/+0.26/+0.69 percent met. Sutherland VISCOSITY NOT met (-0.22 at 300 K, -1.08 at 400 K, -1.46 at 500 K; -2.07 at 600 K). Cubic fit laws for 200-600 K are within 0.11 percent but are in-sample fits to the same 3-digit table (leave-one-out 400 K row -0.22 percent). Not done: IF97 region 3 and 5, backward equations, critical enhancements, species transport coefficients per species, case-schema keys for the library (laws are pasted through properties.*; no variable-density coupling, that is F-050). Mixture-rule formulas, PR/RK constants and atomic weights are from memory and listed as unverified in docs/reference-data.md. No NIST WebBook or REFPROP data used. Audit 2026-10-14: The 1 percent air-viscosity criterion is NOT met by the Sutherland law (asserted at 1.5 percent in fluids.rs); the 1 percent assertion passes only for the cubic fit laws, which are in-sample fits to the same 3-digit table, and the test name still says 'within_one_percent'. The IAPWS viscosity/conductivity tolerance was widened from 1e-8 to 1e-7 after a miss (disclosed in docs/reference-data.md). AUDIT FOLLOW-UP (ca78589): the 1% Sutherland viscosity criterion is recorded as sutherland_air_viscosity_within_1pct_300_to_500_k_known_miss (-1.08% at 400 K, -1.46% at 500 K). SCOPE (merged review): remaining forms (piecewise-linear and piecewise-polynomial tables, nine-coefficient heat capacity, compressible-liquid density, orthotropic conductivity) are tracked in F-220; database-file import of reference fluids is not planned.

title: 0D reactor toolkit: constant-volume/pressure ignition delay, PSR, equilibrium and 1D flame speed using the mechanism reader
acceptance: H2/air and CH4/air ignition delay agree with published GRI-Mech 3.0 based results within 5 percent; PSR blowout temperature trend matches literature
note: Partial (ADR 0013, crates/rcfd-reactor, `rcfd reactor`, docs/reactor-and-acoustics.md; criteria registered before running and unchanged). The acceptance comparison with PUBLISHED GRI-Mech 3.0 ignition delays within 5 percent could not be made because no published number could be verified from an accessible source. 1D flame speed (in the title) is not implemented. Delivered: CHEMKIN-II mechanism reader with NASA-7 thermo (elementary, three-body, Lindemann/Troe falloff, REV, DUP; unsupported keywords diagnosed with line numbers). In-repo stiff adaptive implicit integrator (3-stage Radau IIA order 5, written here). Constant-pressure and constant-volume batch reactors with ignition delay (max dT/dt and temperature-rise definitions). Perfectly stirred reactor with continuation to blowout. Constant-area plug flow. Gordon-McBride equilibrium at TP/HP/UV. JSON case file with located validation errors. No mechanism is committed; GRI-Mech 3.0 is read from the git-ignored F-125 fetch (53 species, 325 reactions, zero element imbalance). Measured: Prothero-Robinson lambda 1e6 error 1.2e-9 (limit 1e-6). Robertson t=40 relative 2.7e-11/6.1e-11/1.6e-10 (limit 1e-5/1e-4/1e-5; reference digits from memory, reproduced to 1e-10). Toy equilibrium vs analytic 1.3e-15. Adiabatic energy drift 1.5e-13/2.8e-12 (limit 1e-8). GRI H2/air phi=1 1 atm ignition delay CV 3.05e-4/8.62e-5/4.42e-5 s at 1000/1100/1200 K (CP 3.12e-4/8.86e-5/4.53e-5 s), strictly decreasing, element drift 2e-15. CH4/air HP T_ad 2225.5 K (reference 2225 K from memory). 1 s limits equal UV/HP equilibrium to 2e-11. PSR blowout tau bracket 2.6 percent, shorter with 600 K preheat (1.03e-5 vs 1.49e-5 s) and longer for phi 0.5 (4.3e-5 s) as expected. NOT met / not done (reason for partial): The acceptance comparison with PUBLISHED GRI-Mech 3.0 ignition delays within 5 percent could not be made because no published number could be verified from an accessible source (the ignition delays above are this code's own results). The PSR blowout check is a qualitative trend, no literature number. 1D flame speed (in the title) is not implemented. The GRI thermo polynomials miss the registered 1e-3 continuity limit at 1000 K (5.1e-3 in h, property of the data file, ignored r3_gri_nasa_continuity_known_miss). No CFD coupling (F-054 stays todo). Falloff SRI, PLOG, FORD and Landau-Teller unsupported. Development note: the first integrator (extrapolated linearly implicit Euler) needed 4e4+ steps on GRI and was replaced by Radau5; a pivoting defect in the dense LU solver, found along the way, was fixed. SCOPE (merged review): plug-flow reactor, shock tube and network composition are tracked in F-225. Wave 18B: the cell chemistry of F-054 reuses this toolkit (mech.rs `rates_of_progress` split out without changing arithmetic; `cell.rs`, `toy.rs`); F-112 itself stays partial and the CFD coupling now exists in F-054 (partial).

title: Lumped zone components: fan curves, porous jump, radiator/heat-exchanger macro and 1D network boundaries
acceptance: Fan curve BC reproduces the specified operating point in a duct; porous-jump pressure drop matches a Darcy-Forchheimer sheet; radiator heat duty balance within 1 percent
note: The audit of 2026-10-21 marks the item DONE on the acceptance text as written; scope beyond it, and the caveats in the audit file, are not claimed. Registered misses (ignored known_miss tests): network patch pressure vs R(Q) 8.5e-4 against 1e-4, and effectiveness duty vs nominal-inlet formula 1.45e-6 against 1e-6. Acceptance met, scope partial (wave 12, ADR 0012, rcfd-api tests/lumped.rs, criteria registered in the ADR before running and unchanged). Delivered: components.<name> of type: fan (piecewise-linear fan curve). porous_jump (Darcy-Forchheimer jump). heat_exchanger (fixed duty or effectiveness, K/s energy source over a zone). network_outlet (lumped R1 Q + R2 Q|Q| outlet pressure). Fan and jump are realised as pressure-jump planes in the SIMPLE kernel (rcfd-fv lumped.rs FaceJump, opt-in field, baseline hashes bit-identical), reusing the sources.rs zone selection. Measured: Porous jump vs Darcy-Forchheimer sheet worst 1.0e-6 (limit 1e-3). Fan plus jump operating point Q +0.061 percent (limit 0.5), fan rise +0.091 percent (limit 0.1), jump drop +0.030 percent (0.1). Network Q -0.032 percent (0.5). Heat-exchanger stream enthalpy balance 3e-12 and 1e-12 (limit 1e-6; acceptance 1 percent). Registered misses (ignored known_miss tests, criteria unchanged): Network patch pressure vs R(Q) 8.5e-4 against 1e-4 (a small persistent flow two-cycle). Effectiveness duty vs nominal-inlet formula 1.45e-6 against 1e-6 (axial conduction warms the inlet by 7e-5 K). First design (cell-based sink) missed Z1 by 17 percent and was replaced; fan and network relaxations are tuning (network test relax 0.02). Not done (reason for partial): general 1D network coupling beyond the lumped outlet relation, shell-and-tube and porous exchanger domains, exhaust-fan boundary types, transient and compressible runs. SCOPE (merged review): list fan, intake-fan, exhaust-fan, vent, porous-jump, radiator and network boundary types as sub-criteria; exchanger domain model in F-217. DONE (audit 2026-10-21, docs/audit/partials-group-*.md): acceptance text as written is met by passing tests; scope beyond the acceptance text, and the caveats in the audit file, are not claimed.

title: Non-conformal mesh interfaces (general grid interface / mortar) with flux conservation
acceptance: Two non-matching blocks give the same channel solution as one conformal block within discretization error; fluxes conserved to round-off across the interface
note: Done (first version, mesh-level). Partially overlapping and conical interfaces remain (Wave 43B, ADR 0109). New rcfd-mesh module non_conformal: join_non_conformal(A, patchA, B, patchB, tol) intersects two planar, coplanar, opposed interface patches (Sutherland-Hodgman clipping of convex faces in plane coordinates), emits one ordinary internal face per overlap (owner on the A cell, neighbour on the B cell, area vector = overlap area x normal, centre at the overlap centroid), deletes the original interface faces, merges coincident points and inserts hanging nodes into the in-plane edges of neighbouring faces so every cell stays closed under Mesh::validate. The solver is untouched; flux conservation holds by construction. Case file: mesh.generator = channel_2d_interface (nx/ny, nx_right/ny_right). Checks fixed before running: (1) face overlaps tile each original face and every cell's area vectors close: 20|27 interface 46 overlaps, tiling error 2.8e-15, worst closure 2.9e-17 relative; 3-D 3x4x5 vs 2x7x3 blocks 70 overlaps, tiling 1.0e-15, volume conserved. (2) Poiseuille channel (nu 0.1, interface perpendicular to flow, 20 vs 27 cells across, linear upwind, 2 non-orthogonal correctors): L2 error of u vs exact relative to 1.5: non-conformal 1.93e-3 against conformal 20 cells 2.28e-3 and 27 cells 1.76e-3 (criterion <= 1.5 x the larger, met), max error 6.18e-3 vs 8.08e-3 and 6.18e-3 (met); interface flux 0.100125000000 equals inlet and outlet flux to 2e-16 relative (limit 1e-12); dp/dx -1.2061 vs -1.2 (0.5 percent, limit 2). (3) linear temperature patch test across the interface: max error 7.8e-12 (limit 1e-8). Kernel fix found on the way (affects every case with non-orthogonal correctors): the pressure solve discarded the explicit non-orthogonal term in its first pass and the reported pressure residual excluded it, so res_p stalled at 2e-4 on non-orthogonal meshes; the first pass now uses the gradient of the current pressure and the residual includes the term (converges to 1e-10 in 223 iterations). Not done: non-planar/curved interfaces (rotating-frame sliding/AMI, F-063), partially overlapping interfaces (patches must cover each other), face zones are dropped by the join, transient motion. Update (MRF, ADR 0008): the planar join is now used by the mrf source (annulus_3d_interface, 48x16 and 48x11 radial blocks): Taylor-Couette across the interface velocity error 7.9e-3 V_i, solid-body rotation velocity 7.8e-3 W r_o, through-flow interface flux equals the inflow to 1e-10; the symmetry-end set-up keeps continuity 5e-12 and net interface flux 3e-14 V_i A. Status unchanged (curved and partially overlapping interfaces remain). Pointer only (no scope change): interface physics extensions are tracked in F-215. Wave 43B (ADR 0109): Cylindrical interfaces added (join_non_conformal_cylindrical: patches on one cylinder about an axis, any counts around and axially, full annulus or sector, seam at theta = +-pi handled); tiling 3.1e-15, closure 1.2e-16, closed-form volume 1.4e-15. A sector stays rotationally periodic through it. The solver needs interface cells that are not much thinner radially than they are wide (79 deg overlap faces diverged, 49 deg converged). Partially overlapping and conical interfaces remain.

title: Interpolate a previous solution onto a new mesh and restart from it
acceptance: Solution from a coarse cavity interpolated to a fine mesh starts at a lower initial residual than uniform init; conservative and non-conservative modes selectable
note: Partial. USER DECISION 2026-10-21: accept the negative result, stays partial. The iteration count to tolerance 1e-6 did not drop (103 interpolated vs 89 uniform), and on a common scale the interpolated start does not have a lower pressure residual (0.149 vs 0.126, ignored known miss f1). Not queued unless interpolated starts matter for the fan workflow. Partial (acceptance met; scope limited). Delivered: rcfd-post interpolate module (nearest source cell by bucket search + least-squares gradient, clipped to the neighbour range; modes nonconservative and conservative). SimpleSolver::set_fields (rebuilds the face flux). Simulation::interpolate_from(source case, checkpoint, mode). rcfd run --interpolate-case/--interpolate-checkpoint/--interpolate-mode. run.headless interpolate_* parameters and matching MCP run_headless fields (docs/run-control.md, docs/service-protocol.md). Measured (checks fixed up front), 12x12 cavity solution onto 24x24: First-iteration normalised residual res_u 0.1656 and res_p 0.1091 versus 1.0 and 1.0 for the uniform start (conservative: 0.1656 and 0.1086). Relative L2 distance of the start from the converged speed 0.171 versus 1.000. A linear field is reproduced to 1e-12 inside the source cell-centre hull; conservative mode matches the source volume average of p, ux, uy to 1e-10 (non-conservative differs: ux average 1.43e-3 vs 3.25e-3). Negative finding: the iteration count to tolerance 1e-6 did not drop (103 interpolated vs 89 uniform) because the normalised residual is relative to the solution's own variation; the hypothesis that it would drop is recorded, not an acceptance gate. Not done: Conservative here means a uniform shift that matches the volume average, not a geometric cell-overlap remap (sub-regions are not conserved). The donor cell is the nearest centre, not a point-in-cell search. Steady laminar SIMPLE/SIMPLEC only (transient, compressible and turbulence-model state are not interpolated). The source is a checkpoint plus its case, VTU/result files cannot be read back. No GUI control. Audit 2026-10-14: the asserted check (first-iteration normalised residual below the uniform start) is near-vacuous because the uniform start gives 1.0 by construction (residual normalised by the solution's own variation), and the practical benefit was measured negative (103 iterations vs 89 uniform). The acceptance text is unchanged; the evidence does not show a faster start. WAVE 19C (ADR 0031, still partial): New rcfd-post `remap` module with six methods (nearest, inverse_distance, least_squares, gradient, conservative, conservative_overlap = axis-aligned box cell-overlap remap with a linear reconstruction), selectable by `restart.method` and `--method`. Restart files now embed the mesh and carry transient state (time, step counter, BDF2 history), so `rcfd restart <case> --from f [--mesh m]`, `rcfd run --restart-from`, the `restart` case section and chain stages restart on the same mesh exactly or transfer onto another one; a steady file starts a transient run. Measured (checks registered first in ADR 0031): Linear field exact to 1.6e-15 for least_squares, conservative_overlap and gradient. conservative_overlap integral mismatch 8.9e-16 (refine) and 1.4e-15 (coarsen). Identical meshes bit-exact. Same-mesh steady and transient restarts (PISO Euler, PISO BDF2, PIMPLE BDF2) bit-identical to the uninterrupted run. MISSES, reported not tuned: Convergence-order bands I2 (least_squares 2.01/2.14 and nearest 1.00 pass; gradient 2.09/2.75, conservative_overlap 2.63/3.77 and inverse_distance 1.58/1.64 exceed their registered upper bounds, i.e. are more accurate than assumed). One clause of I5 inconsistent with I1 (ADR defect). S5a: iterations to tolerance on 24x24 are 103 (gradient), 96 (least_squares), 103 (overlap) versus 89 cold, still negative. S5b (iterations to within 1e-2 of the converged speed) passes, 10 versus 23. Not done: unstructured conservative remap, divergence-free/flux-conservative projection (rebuilt flux imbalance 0.18 after a 12 to 24 transfer), BDF2 history across a mesh change, transient restart with energy/scalars/statistics/turbulence/compressible, reading a solution back from VTU results, service run.headless support for restart.from. WAVE 40C (ADR 0099, still partial): F1 measures the first-iteration residual numerators of both starts against fixed denominators, the reference norms of the converged uniform 24x24 solution (D_ux 0.0765, D_uy 0.0371, D_p 0.0377). Momentum passes: R_u 0.155 interpolated (both modes) vs 0.261 uniform (ratio 0.59). Pressure MISSES: R_p 0.149 non-conservative and 0.148 conservative vs 0.126 uniform (ratio 1.18), so on a common scale the interpolated start does not have a lower pressure residual; ignored known-miss test f1_fixed_normalisation_initial_residual_known_miss in crates/rcfd-api/tests/interpolate.rs, limit unchanged. Likely cause (not tested): the rebuilt face flux is not divergence-free (imbalance 0.18). S5b and the negative iteration-count result (103 interpolated vs 89 uniform to 1e-6) stand as recorded above. USER DECISION 2026-10-21: accept the negative result, stays partial. Wave 40C (ADR 0099): fixed-normalisation first-iteration residual, momentum 0.155 interpolated vs 0.261 uniform (passes), pressure 0.149 vs 0.126 (misses, ignored known miss f1); likely cause an interpolated face flux that is not divergence-free (imbalance 0.18), untested. Not queued unless interpolated starts matter for the fan workflow.

title: Run-time statistics and output policy: transient mean/min/max/RMS/std fields, selected-variable result files, backup retention, elapsed-time and interrupt limits
acceptance: Time-averaged field over a vortex-shedding run matches the post-computed average; the run honors a max-elapsed-time and a stop-file; retained backups limited to the configured count
note: Done. Audit 2026-10-14: the vortex-shedding part is an ignored test, and the averaging check verifies bookkeeping, not an independent average. rcfd-api `stats` plus run-control changes: statistics.enabled/start_time/fields collect time-weighted mean, rms, std, min and max of ux, uy, uz, speed and p in transient piso/pimple runs (fields <name>_mean etc. in solution.vtu, snapshots, probes and reports; weighted Welford update, definition in the module header). output.write_interval now writes numbered snapshots (snapshots/snapshot_<step>.vtu, `snapshot` status event) with output.retain_snapshots keeping the newest N. output.retain_checkpoints keeps the newest N periodic restart files (<checkpoint>.<step>) while the end-of-run checkpoint stays at the requested path. output.fields selects the variables written. The wall-clock limit and stop file are the F-121 controls, verified here on a transient run (stop file -> interrupted/exit 7, --max-elapsed 0 -> time_limit/exit 8). Measured (tests/statistics.rs, checks fixed first): Adaptive-step transient cavity, mean/rms/std/min/max of four fields equal the post-computed moments from stored per-step fields to a worst relative difference of 1.2e-15 (limit 1e-12). Ignored long test, cylinder Re=100 128x100 mesh, 3200 PISO steps to t=160, statistics from t=100 (averaging time 60): mean ux and p fields equal the post-computed average to 4.9e-15 and 3.6e-15 relative, 12 sign changes of the wake probe velocity (shedding present, limit 4; an earlier 96x64 run to t=100 had only 2 sign changes because shedding had not set in yet, so the run was lengthened and the criterion kept). Snapshot retention leaves exactly the newest 3 of the multiples of 10, checkpoint retention the newest 2 periodic files plus the final one. Not done: statistics for steady and compressible runs, statistics inside checkpoints (transient runs cannot be checkpointed), time-based write interval, retention for transient restart files (none exist). title: User-function plugin API with sandboxed (WASM) execution for sources, BCs, properties and monitors
acceptance: A user-defined momentum source loaded as a WASM module changes the solution as expected; the module cannot access the filesystem or network; the ABI is versioned
note: Done. Audit 2026-10-14: the original position-dependent source check (max|u| < 1e-6) was replaced by a weaker refinement-ratio check. The acceptance text is unchanged and its other clauses (constant source, sandbox, ABI version) are covered by tests. Sandboxed user functions in rcfd-api `udf` (wasmi 0.31, pure-Rust interpreter; ABI version 1, docs/udf-abi.md): a WebAssembly module must export rcfd_abi_version() and may export momentum_source, velocity_profile, kinematic_viscosity and monitor. Case settings udf.<name> (file, fuel_per_call, momentum_source/viscosity/monitor roles) and boundaries.<patch>.velocity_udf. Isolation: Any import (so no WASI, file, network, clock) is refused at load. Per-call fuel is renewed on every call and exhaustion traps. Linear memory capped at 16 MiB. Results must be finite, viscosity positive. Failures stop the run with state failed (exit 1), never a panic. Module files stay inside the service sandbox root. Measured (tests/udf.rs, checks fixed first): Constant momentum_source module equals physics.body_force to below 1e-9 relative and differs from a run without it. kinematic_viscosity module and velocity_profile module reproduce the plain physics.nu / expression runs to below 1e-9. Monitor equals the independent sum(ux*V) to 1e-12. Infinite loop, memory growth past the cap, NaN, negative viscosity, wrong ABI, wrong signature, missing ABI export and imports (wasi fd_write) are all rejected. 20000 calls under a 1000-fuel budget succeed. Position-dependent source a=(3x,0,0) in a closed 10x10 box: first check (max|u|<1e-6) measured 4.4e-2 because the wall pressure extrapolation uses the owner-cell force (first order for non-uniform forces), so it was replaced, not loosened, by a convergence check written before the 20x20 run: spurious velocity 4.44e-2 -> 1.09e-2 (ratio 4.1), pressure error 3.86e-2 -> 1.94e-2 (ratio 2.0), both above the 1.7 floor. Not done: momentum source and viscosity in transient runs (refused), anything in the compressible solver (refused), viscosity together with a turbulence model (refused), scalar/energy sources, host functions, batch interface (every cell is one interpreted call), no MCP or assistant tool wrapper for udf settings (settings are available through the generic case tools and schema). Audit 2026-10-14: the original position-dependent source check (max|u| < 1e-6) was replaced by a weaker refinement-ratio check (floor 1.7; pressure ratio 2.0 clears it narrowly; remaining spurious velocity 1.1e-2 on 20x20). The acceptance text is unchanged and its other clauses (constant source, sandbox, ABI version) are covered by tests. Pointer only (no scope change): the wider hook catalogue is tracked in F-239.

title: Cell registers / regions (value-threshold, box, boundary-adjacent) for patching, source zones and adaption
acceptance: A region defined by a field threshold can be patched with a value and used to restrict a source term; registers are named objects in the settings tree
note: The acceptance is met (WAVE 39D, ADR 0095). Outside the acceptance and not done: re-evaluation during a run, thresholds on restarted fields, mesh adaption (marks only), case reports of register statistics. Partial (ADR 0011, gap A). Delivered: rcfd_post::registers: Box, value threshold on a cell field with inclusive limits, expression of the cell centre, boundary-adjacent with layers, mesh cell zone. Union, intersection, difference, complement, grow and shrink by face or point neighbours. Per-register statistics count/volume/min/max/volume mean/integral incl. vector components, None for empty. patch_field; interface area; face-jump indicator and tolerance marks restricted to a register with count and volume fraction. The settings tree: registers.<name> (type box|expression|boundary_adjacent|cell_zone|combine, grow/shrink), sources.<n>.zone = "register" and initial.patches.<n> (velocity, pressure, temperature). Measured on the 20^3 cube: Box 1000 cells volume 8.9e-16 rel err. The x>=0.5 threshold 4000 cells with mean 0.75, integral 0.5, min/max 0.525/0.975 (1e-12). Sphere r 0.3 on 40^3 4.2e-3 volume error (limit 3e-2). Boundary layers 400/800/2168 and interface area 1.0. Step-field marks 800 cells and linear-field marks 0. On a 20x20 case a porous sink is non-zero on exactly the 100 register cells and bit-exact zero elsewhere and initial patches change exactly those cells. Every error names its setting path. Measured (rcfd-api --test registers G1, G2) on the 20 x 20 box with initial ux = 4y(1-y): The threshold |u| >= 0.75 selects exactly 200 cells (analytic 200) and equals the library threshold. A pressure patch changes exactly those 200 cells. A porous sink is non-zero on exactly those cells and bit-zero elsewhere. 5 SIMPLEC iterations are bit-identical to a box register on the same cells (the source moves ux by up to 0.164). Located errors pass. The acceptance is met. Outside the acceptance and not done: re-evaluation during a run, thresholds on restarted fields, mesh adaption (marks only), case reports of register statistics.

title: Turbomachinery rotating interfaces: frozen-rotor and stage (mixing-plane) interfaces with sector periodicity
acceptance: A public low-speed compressor/rotor case reproduces overall pressure ratio and efficiency within published scatter; mass conserved across the interface
note: P3 (stretch). Gap: turbomachinery interfaces and stage-average constraints (including a downstream velocity constraint). Public rotor reference data via the validation pack (F-125). PARTIAL: the acceptance (a public compressor case reproducing pressure ratio and efficiency within published scatter) is NOT MET and NOT ATTEMPTED. WAVE 45B (ADR 0116) does not open MRF on the bladed FAN-01 passage, whose blade wall is still refused by the revolution check. SCOPE (merged review): add circumferential averaging as a frame-change option, flow-regime options and a downstream-velocity constraint for stage interfaces; outlet averaging per F-200. WAVE 29A (ADR 0055), PARTIAL; acceptance (a public compressor case reproducing pressure ratio and efficiency within published scatter) NOT MET and NOT ATTEMPTED (no Rotor 37 or Hannover run, no comparison to any published turbomachine). Delivered: rcfd-fv rotor_interface.rs (RotorFrame: frame velocity, absolute/relative conversion and frame change, exact for rigid rotation to 1.7e-15 (limit 1e-14); FrozenRotorInterface: internal faces between two cell zones from the F-114 join with frame-flux jump, non-axisymmetry check and flux closure in absolute and relative form; located errors). mixing_plane.rs (MixingPlane: radial bands, circumferential/band averages, flux-weighted band reduction and pass-back conserving mass (u_n = Q/A'_b on the receiver), angular momentum (u_theta = Gamma_b/r, exact for a free vortex), normal momentum with mixed-out pressure, and a flux-weighted scalar such as total enthalpy; mixing loss as the non-conserved mechanical energy flux, shown non-negative; constant density; cancelling-flux, empty-band, out-of-band and orientation errors are located). The solver's frozen rotor is the absolute-velocity MRF zone of ADR 0008 (identity frame change at the interface). New solver checks: Plug flow through a stationary/rotating pair 1.5e-14 (1e-6). Flux closure 4.7e-15 (1e-9). Taylor-Couette across the interface with lower-zone frame 0, 0.5, 1 W_i: analytic error 7.6e-3 V_i (2e-2), mutual difference <= 9.1e-4 V_i (1e-2). Library checks (limits registered in ADR 0055 before running): Band average vs closed form 1.7e-15 (1e-13). Mass across a mismatched receiver 4.3e-16 (1e-13). Angular momentum flux 6.3e-16 per band (1e-12). Two-jet mixed-out pressure rise and mixing loss to 2e-16 and 3.3e-15 (1e-13, 1e-12). MISSES (ignored known-miss tests, limits intact): X3 uniform flow through the mismatched mesh pair deviates by 3.7e-1 (limit 1e-13) because donor and receiver band areas differ by up to 27 % (sharp face-to-band assignment by face centre and different polygon areas; exact mass conservation then scales the velocity by the area ratio); corrected checks X3b (equal band areas, 4.8e-15) and X3c (identity) added. R5 interface-flux limits 1e-8/1e-3 registered for the open-end Taylor-Couette missed (3.2e-5 to 3.7e-5 and 1.0e-3) as already known for M4b in ADR 0008. Not delivered: solver-coupled mixing plane and any case-tree keys for it (needs a per-iteration boundary hook; no natural place in the case tree), area-fraction splitting of faces across band edges, compressible mixed-out state, rothalpy, curved/cylindrical interfaces, sector periodicity of a stage, downstream-velocity constraint, flow-regime options. WAVE 30A (ADR 0059): the mixing plane is now WIRED into the steady SIMPLE/SIMPLEC loop: Case section mixing_plane (enabled, upstream_patch, downstream_patch, axis, origin, bands, r_min, r_max, relax, every, tolerance; all additive, inert when off, located errors). Mesh generator annulus_3d_stage (two unjoined annulus blocks, patches plane_out and plane_in). Monitor res_mixing. Per iteration the upstream outlet is circumferentially averaged in radial bands (MixingPlane) and installed as a relaxed per-face fixed velocity on the downstream inlet, the band pressure is returned as a relaxed per-face fixed pressure on the upstream outlet. Free-vortex plus uniform axial flow through the frozen-rotor/stationary plane (exact solution, no published data): Exchange change 4.2e-14 after 189 iterations. Mass and angular momentum per band conserved to 2.5e-14 and 2.4e-14. Velocity error 6.0e-3 of V_ref (limit 2e-2), plane_in face velocity 2.9e-3. Relaxation 0.3 vs 0.7 agree to 2.6e-13. Circumferential distortion mixed out (polar spread 6.7e-16, mixing loss 11.8 percent of the energy flux, non-negative). 48 vs 36 cells around 6.1e-3. Known miss: pressure error 6.85e-2 P against 5e-2 P (near-hub-wall pressure discretisation, not the plane: the plane-free control gives 1.13e-1, 6.62e-2, 4.24e-2 for 4, 8, 16 radial layers). Baselines bit-identical when the section is off. Acceptance (published compressor case) still NOT MET and NOT ATTEMPTED. Still not delivered: transient and coupled solvers, compressible mixed-out state, rothalpy, curved or non-aligned interfaces, sector periodicity, turbulence transfer. WAVE 43B (ADR 0109): cylindrical frozen-rotor interface. New rcfd_mesh::non_conformal::join_non_conformal_cylindrical joins a rotor block and a stator block across a cylinder about the axis (chart (r theta, z), overlap faces are planar chord rectangles with radial normal, frame flux 1.8e-14 of |S|); planar joins bit-identical. Full annulus 48 vs 35 around: 328 overlaps, tiling 3.1e-15, closure 1.2e-16, closed-form volume 1.4e-15. Solver checks (mesh read as a file, MRF on cell zone rotor): On the registered mesh (uniform, dr = 1/32, overlap faces 79 deg non-orthogonal) every run DIVERGED (known misses). The face_flux correction alone or with 3 correctors did not converge. The amended mesh K2 (96 vs 70 around, radial cells growing towards the interface, 48.7 deg) converges: solid body 1.6e-3 W r_o and pressure 1.4 % of range, Taylor-Couette 3.8e-3 V_i (conformal controls 3.0e-3 and 3.9e-3), frame invariance 4.2e-4 V_i, radial source flow through the cylinder: interface flux equals inflow to 1.5e-14, velocity 4.8e-3. Sector periodicity through the cylinder (60-degree sector, inertial and rotating frame): error within 1.5 x the conformal controls, net interface flux 3e-17 / 5e-11, seam balance 0 / 4e-10. MISS (ignored, limits intact): the sum of absolute interface fluxes 5.8e-3 / 2.1e-2 / 1.2e-3 V_i A against 1e-3 (azimuthal velocity interpolated between cells at different angles; first order: halves with doubled counts). Acceptance (published compressor case) NOT attempted. Still not delivered: MRF zones with cyclic seams (needed for a rotor passage with this interface), a case-tree generator or keys, conical/partial/transient interfaces, the mixing plane on a cylinder, plus the items above. WAVE 44B (ADR 0112): Case-tree generator mesh.generator = annulus_3d_cylindrical_interface (rotor block r_in..r_interface with cell zone rotor, stator block r_interface..r_out, counts around/axially may differ; keys r_interface, isotropic_interface; located errors) with a non-orthogonality pre-flight. rcfd_mesh::non_conformal::interface_non_orthogonality reports the worst overlap-face angle, the centre offsets and the factor by which the radial spacing must grow; the case is rejected above 70 deg (ADR 0109 runs diverged at 72.7 deg and above; largest converged 48.75 deg). It reproduces the ADR 0109 angles (M 79.19, 75.71, 72.68, K2 48.74, conformal 0.0 deg; equal to the quality-module angle to 1e-9). Opt-in near-isotropic interface layer (cylindrical_interface_layer_size at a 45 deg bound plus gen::expansion_for_end_cell): sized meshes 36.6-37.7 deg. The ADR 0109 60-degree sector tests on the sized sector pass (inertial: converged, error 1.353e-2 V_i within 1.5 x controls 1.960e-2, net interface flux 6e-18, seam 0; rotating frame: error 1.058e-2 within 1.917e-2, net 1.8e-10, seam 8.2e-10, but the continuity floor 1.18e-9 misses the 1e-9 convergence criterion: ignored known miss). The option in the full annulus (K2 counts) converges in 238 iterations, Taylor-Couette error 6.2e-3 V_i (2e-2). The tree mesh equals the library join (content hash) and the tree run equals the library run exactly (0 difference, 272 iterations); a case without the keys is bit-identical. Uniform 60-degree sector G2 measures 70.5 deg (above the limit, although its rcfd-fv runs converge). Not changed: the first-order sum of absolute interface fluxes (2.0e-3 / 1.8e-2 V_i A on the sized sector), MRF on cyclic seams, sector periodicity in the case tree. Acceptance (published compressor case) NOT attempted; stays partial. WAVE 44C (ADR 0113): MRF zones with rotationally cyclic seams, opt-in key sources.<name>.cyclic_seams (mrf only, default false, located error otherwise). A seam pair is an internal face cut in two: with the cyclic rotation about the MRF axis F_g = -F_f, so both faces get the frame flux (Omega x r).S when both owners are in the zone; the revolution check counts the pair mismatch instead (misaligned axis or one-sided zone refused). Found and fixed on the way (same opt-in): the SIMPLEC h1 of a cyclic cell lacked the lagged partner coefficients, so rAU/rAtU of seam cells differed from the unsplit mesh; this moved the fixed-velocity wall pressure gradient in seam-wall corner cells under a body force (K1 sector-annulus pressure 5.9e-4 of the range) and gives 4.6e-3 U spurious swirl in an inertial sector through-flow (2.2e-12 with the fix; the default path keeps the defect, bit-identical). Checks, sector = exact sixth of the annulus (library level, rcfd-fv tests/mrf_cyclic_seams_w44c.rs): Seam pair mismatch 2.3e-15 (1e-12), per-cell frame-flux closure 4.4e-16 (1e-12). Solid body sector-annulus 3.6e-9 W r_o / 6.6e-9 of the pressure range (4.3e-4, the smallest ADR 0008 M3 frame difference), analytic 7.9e-4 / 3.7e-3 (2e-2 / 5e-2). Taylor-Couette sector-annulus 1.2e-10 V_i (4.3e-4), analytic 6.76e-3 V_i (1.5e-2). Axial through-flow with an Omega 5 rotor band: sector-annulus 1.8e-11 U, swirl 1.1e-10 U (2e-2), band effect sector against annulus 1.8e-11 U (4.3e-4). Empty passage rotating as a whole stays at the exact state u = (0,0,U) to 1.1e-15 U (1e-8; without seam frame flux 2.6 U). ADR 0109 sector joined on the cylinder with the inner block as MRF zone: error 1.27e-2 V_i (2e-2, 0.76 of 1.5 x controls), net interface flux 2e-17, seam balance 8e-12. Positive path verified at library level only. Case tree: key checked, refusals located (the message now names the patch), default bit-identical (key absent/false/true on the M2 annulus), baseline hashes untouched; the sim.rs wiring of F1 is unexercised because no case-tree mesh reaches it. NOT unblocked for the fan: the axial_fan_sector hub and shroud faces are not surfaces of revolution (frame flux 1.8e-2 / 4.5e-3 of Omega r |S|, 4.2e-3 even unsheared; limit 1e-6), so the fan passage is now refused at the hub instead of the seams; at library level the same empty passage leaves the exact state by 7.4e-4 U (limit 1e-8, ignored known miss, worst cell on hub/shroud, seam pair mismatch 5.4e-14); a sector read from a mesh file loses its cyclic rotation (OpenFOAM writer stores neighbourPatch only). Acceptance NOT attempted; stays partial. WAVE 45B (ADR 0116): the case-tree generator annulus_3d_sector (an empty annular sector with planar faces and the cyclic pair theta_min / theta_max) runs an mrf zone with cyclic_seams = true through the case tree (exact empty passage 5.6e-13 U, limit 1e-8; sector against the full annulus 1.4e-11 W r_out, limit 4.3e-4), which is verification infrastructure only: it does not open MRF on the bladed FAN-01 passage, whose blade wall is still refused by the revolution check.

title: Eulerian-Eulerian and mixture multiphase with interphase forces, plus cavitation mass transfer
acceptance: Bubble-column void-fraction profile and a cavitating hydrofoil/venturi sheet-length trend match literature
note: PARTIAL (wave 29B, ADR 0056). No published cavitation data and no bubble-column profile were compared (NOT ATTEMPTED); the acceptance of this item is therefore not met. All references UNVERIFIED (docs/reference-data.md). DELIVERED: (1) mixture model with drift-flux algebraic slip (Stokes and Schiller-Naumann closure) on the VOF host: slip flux in the alpha transport, drift mass flux and stress in the momentum (rcfd-fv mixture.rs, vof.rs; case keys multiphase.mixture.*). (2) ONE cavitation model, Schnerr-Sauer with bubble-number density, coupled IMPLICITLY to the pressure equation (chord linearisation on the pressure-matrix diagonal, advective alpha transport; rcfd-fv cavitation.rs, vof.rs; keys multiphase.cavitation.*). (3) a 2-D cavitating venturi test. Passing: C1-C4, D1-D6 (corrected set-ups), M1-M3, M4b, N1, N2, N6, W1-W3 (tree equals library to 1e-9). Misses (limits intact, ignored known_miss tests): N3 end-of-run, N4, N4-prime, N5 global balance 1.96e-5 vs 1e-6, bitwise tree equality; the registered dt for the venturi exceeds the flow Courant limit at cavity collapse (corrected dt 5e-5). NOT DELIVERED: Full multi-fluid Euler-Euler with per-phase momentum, lift, wall lubrication, virtual mass, turbulent dispersion, granular kinetic theory, wall boiling, free-surface damping. No published cavitation data and no bubble-column profile were compared (NOT ATTEMPTED); the acceptance of this item is therefore not met. All references UNVERIFIED (docs/reference-data.md). Previous scope text: P3 (stretch). Gap: the roadmap has only VOF and one-way Lagrangian; typical multiphase solvers also offer drag/lift/virtual-mass/turbulent-dispersion closure sets and cavitation models. SCOPE (merged review): make the closure taxonomy the criteria set: drag, lift, wall lubrication, turbulent dispersion, virtual mass, granular kinetic theory, wall-boiling closures, algebraic slip and free-surface damping; population balance in F-228, interfacial transfer in F-226.

title: Lagrangian extensions: two-way coupling, turbulent dispersion, injection distributions, breakup, wall film, erosion
acceptance: A two-way coupled particle-laden jet conserves total momentum; a Rosin-Rammler injection distribution is reproduced statistically
note: DONE (decision 2026-10-21): acceptance field met, first-principles references only; no published particle-laden jet attempted. The unmet scope (breakup, wall film, erosion, evaporation, track files, spray-penetration and falling-film additions) moved to F-245. PARTIAL (wave 29C, ADR 0057). Delivered: Two-way exchange record (drag impulse and total-energy gain per cell, optional Ranz-Marshall heat transfer; conservative to round-off: momentum residual 3.6e-16 and 6.3e-17 with wall hits, energy 2.7e-16 against a 1e-12 limit; observation-only for the particles). Single-cell coupled closed form (relative velocity decay exp(-(1+phi) t/tau), explicit-coupling error 1.0 percent at dt = tau/100, first order). Dilute limit (two-way minus one-way = 0.262 phi). Discrete random walk dispersion (eddy lifetime and crossing time; particle variance within 0.31, 0.31, 0.15 percent of the derived closed form sigma^2 T_L/(T_L+tau) for tau/T_L = 0.1, 1, 5 with 40000 particles, tracker level 1.0 percent). Uniform and Rosin-Rammler equal-mass parcels from a mass flow (Kolmogorov distance 0.0049 to 0.0053 against 0.0138; total mass to 3e-13). Cone and hollow-cone injection. Case keys particles.dispersion*, injection.*.mass_flow, cone_*, distribution = uniform. Acceptance NOT fully met: the two-way sources are NOT applied by Simulation::step (no particle-laden jet in the solver; momentum conservation is shown in a closed particle/carrier loop), no published comparison. NOT delivered: solver-loop feedback, dispersion from turbulence-model fields, evaporation, breakup, wall film, erosion, particle reactions, group and file injections. One set-up defect (gravity impulse over the full time for stuck parcels) kept as an ignored test with a corrected one. P3 (stretch). Gap: particle injection, breakup, wall-film and erosion options; discrete-phase models. SCOPE (merged review): split into injections with breakup, heat and mass transfer, and dense flow; add diameter distributions, first-stage and secondary breakup, rough-wall interaction and track-file output. Acceptance additions: constant-volume vaporising spray liquid and vapour penetration within 10 percent of public data; falling-film thickness within 5 percent of the Nusselt solution. Discrete-element coupling is not planned. WAVE 30A (ADR 0059): two-way coupling is now WIRED into the solver loops: The Coupling record is applied as a momentum source (and a temperature source with heat_transfer, which requires two_way) with the sign that conserves momentum, under-relaxed and lagged in the steady loop (re-tracking every two_way_every iterations, monitor res_particles, converged only when the change is below two_way_tolerance), per time step on the old-level field in piso/pimple. Keys: particles.two_way, two_way_relax, two_way_every, two_way_start, two_way_tolerance, heat_transfer, particle_cp, injection temperature; located errors; bit-identical when unset. First-principles checks (no published data read): Closed-form plug with parcels in a uniform stream, force equals parcel momentum flux 9.7e-8 and 1.8e-5 (PLUG-B, corrected set-up; a miss of the registered 1e-6), pressure drop within 7.6e-4, transient piso/pimple record identity 4e-14. Particle-laden jet momentum balance residual 3.9e-11 (limit 2e-2), momentum delivered equals exchanged 5.7e-16, cross-stream force 3.4e-13, force linear in loading with D(0.1)/D(0.01) = 9.57. Heat: outlet rise 7.5e-4 off the closed form, delivered heat equals particle loss to 4.7e-10. Known misses (limits intact): PL2 1.64e-3, PL3 1.5e-2, PL4 144 updates, uniformity, PL1b. A published particle-laden jet is NOT ATTEMPTED; the acceptance wording (total momentum conserved) is met on the first-principles jet only. DONE (decision 2026-10-21): acceptance field met (two-way jet momentum residual 3.9e-11 vs 2e-2, cross-stream 2.1e-13, record vs particle sum 5.7e-16; Rosin-Rammler KS 0.0049 vs 0.0138, mass flow 3e-13), first-principles references only; no published particle-laden jet attempted. The unmet scope above (breakup, wall film, erosion, evaporation, track files, spray-penetration and falling-film additions) moved to F-245.

title: Combustion extensions: non-premixed flamelet/mixture-fraction PDF and premixed progress-variable models
acceptance: A methane jet flame temperature profile and lift-off trend compare with a public benchmark (e.g. Sandia flames); the flamelet library reader is documented
note: PARTIAL (wave 28B, ADR 0053). Delivered as libraries (no case keys). NOT ATTEMPTED: any comparison with a published flame (Sandia etc.). Delivered as libraries (no case keys): Mixture fraction with an HP equilibrium table and exact beta-PDF integration over the piecewise-linear table (mixfrac.rs), Burke-Schumann closed-form check (table within 2.6e-6 K of the closed form). Steady laminar flamelet equations with chi_st continuation table and extinction trend (flamelet.rs). Premixed progress variable with a phase-plane front speed (Zeldovich cubic within 3.0e-5 of the closed form) and a tabulated-source beta-PDF mean (progress.rs). NOT ATTEMPTED: any comparison with a published flame (Sandia etc.), a GRI flamelet table, G-equation, BML or thickened flame, coherent-flame, spark and ignition models, wiring of Z or the flamelet library into the case tree. Known miss: the temperature-based progress variable is not monotone for H2/air (induction period slightly endothermic); Y_H2O is used instead. P3 (stretch). Gap: flamelet-with-PDF, burning-velocity and extended coherent flame models; non-premixed and premixed combustion. SCOPE (merged review): add progress-variable and flamelet-generated manifold models, G-equation with reinitialisation, burning-velocity and coherent-flame models, spark kernels and ignition-delay models as sub-criteria; pollutants in F-222.

title: Radiation extensions: Monte Carlo, Rosseland, spectral bands/WSGG, scattering and solar load
acceptance: A participating-medium benchmark between plates matches the analytic result; the non-grey band model reproduces tabulated emissivity
note: Partial (wave 12, ADR 0012). Not done (acceptance part 2 and scope): non-grey band model and tabulated emissivity, WSGG (no verifiable coefficient table), Monte Carlo, six-flux, solar load. Delivered: Rosseland diffusion approximation (radiation.model = rosseland: Kirchhoff variable linear to 2.4e-5 and wall flux -0.003 percent against the closed form) and P1 with scattering. Participating-medium plates benchmark: P1 matches the analytic P1 result to 2.6e-9 and the Milne transport asymptote to 0.41 percent at tau = 20 (the Milne constant 0.7104 and its equivalence to the plate problem are not verified against a primary source, see docs/reference-data.md). SCOPE (merged review): add discrete transfer, six-flux, non-gray spectral models, radiometers and interphase radiation; solar acceptance: sun azimuth and elevation from the published open algorithm to 0.1 degree and flat-plate absorbed flux equals the cosine-law value.

title: Surface sizing and surface-mesh generation from STL/faceted geometry (size fields, feature capture, connect/seal)
acceptance: A closed STL of a cylinder in a box meshes with curvature-based sizing; the result passes watertightness and quality checks
note: USER DECISION 2026-10-22: accepted done with the opt-in quality_sweeps pass (Wave 41D, ADR 0104). The default mesher still misses the ADR 0030 T5 limits (1.84 deg, 0.936), and Wave 42C (ADR 0107) evaluated the pass as the DEFAULT and did NOT switch it (default stays quality_sweeps = 0). Partial (wave 19B, ADR 0030, docs/meshing.md): library rcfd_mesh::surface_remesh with uniform, curvature, proximity and box size fields (gradient-limited), feature-preserving split/collapse/flip/smooth remeshing projected on the input surface. Checks pass on: A sphere (Hausdorff 0.0147 vs limit 0.025, 99 percent edges within 0.7-1.4 of target, min angle 44.5 deg). A cube (features and area exact). A torus (chi 0, 98.8 percent edges in band). A tagged cylinder in a box. One registered check missed and is an ignored known_miss test: torus volume change 4.18 percent vs 3 percent (limit under-derived: the inscribed-polygon angle allows about 5.9 percent; post-hoc bound test passes). Pipeline remesh then tetrahedralize of a cylinder in a box passes watertightness and check_mesh. NOT done: hard/soft controls, geodesic and volumetric fields, body-of-influence beyond a box, connect/seal and wrapping, anisotropic sizes, brute-force closest point (small surfaces only), CLI and case hooks. Literature attributions unverified. P3 (stretch). Gap: mesh size controls and fields, surface remeshing, connection and wrapping tools. Do not link AGPL/GPL meshers (TetGen, Gmsh) into rcfd; external-process use only. SCOPE (merged review): add curvature, proximity, hard/soft and body-of-influence size controls and geometric, volumetric and geodesic size fields; quality measures in F-233; diagnostics and wrapping in F-232. Wave 39B (ADR 0093, crates/rcfd-io/tests/stl_cylinder_in_box.rs): The cylinder in a box is now written as a two-solid ASCII STL file, read back and welded: S1 passes (closed manifold, Euler 4, 2 components, area and volume within 1e-12). The curvature-sized remesh and tetrahedralization of the STL surface are watertight (volume within 1e-10, 2 patches, positive volumes, check_mesh ok; s2b). Registered quality limits (ADR 0030 T5) MISSED, kept as ignored known-miss tests: minimum dihedral 1.84 deg vs 3.0 (the in-code surface, re-measured, gives 3.34 with the same coordinates; the difference is consistent with the remesh depending on the STL vertex numbering, cause not isolated) and radius-edge fraction 0.936 vs 0.99. Still partial on the quality clause: needs sliver removal and quality refinement in the tetrahedral mesher (F-132 scope). USER DECISION 2026-10-21: quality work queued: closing needs sliver removal and quality refinement in the tetrahedral mesher (F-132 scope), then re-run the ignored S2/S3 known misses. Wave 41D (ADR 0104, crates/rcfd-io/tests/w41d_tet_quality.rs): DONE with the opt-in tetrahedral quality pass (TetOptions::quality_sweeps = 10; constrained circumcentre insertion, interior-vertex smoothing, flips; default output bit-identical, 9 fingerprints checked). Same STL file, curvature remesh and ADR 0030 T5 limits: minimum dihedral 17.66 deg (limit 3.0), radius-edge fraction 1.0 (limit 0.99), watertight (volume 1e-10, 2 patches, check_mesh ok, patch areas 1e-10, boundary faces on same-tag input triangles, Euler 2), all non-ignored and passing; in-code surface 16.33 deg and 0.997. Numbering dependence isolated (D0-D2): the remesher depends on the vertex numbering (equal-length edges split in id order), the tetrahedral mesher does not. The ADR 0093 S2/S3 records stay ignored known misses because they run the default mesher, which still misses (1.84 deg, 0.936). USER DECISION 2026-10-22: accepted done with the opt-in quality_sweeps pass. Queued: evaluate making the pass the default, only if every existing baseline hash stays identical. Wave 42C (ADR 0107, crates/rcfd-io/tests/w42c_tet_default_eval.rs): pass evaluated as the DEFAULT and NOT switched (default stays quality_sweeps = 0). With the default at 10 in a scratch tree the whole workspace passes (1961 / 0 / 578) and the rcfd-api baseline hashes are unchanged (no API/CLI path reaches tetrahedralize), but the registered rule blocks: the ignored ADR 0030 record t5_torus_known_miss changes (0.634 -> 1.000) and the cost limits miss (tetrahedralize time factor 3.05 on this mesh, marginal, and 4.81 on a 10614-cell mesh, limit 3.0; added time per cell grows 2.79x, limit 2.0). 7 of the 9 W0 fingerprints would change (not re-recorded). Safety holds with the pass (no inverted cell, volume error 8e-16, check_mesh ok on 1k and 10k cells; the 10k mesh meets T5: 14.2 deg, 1.0). Switching needs a user decision on the t5 torus record and a cheaper (non-superlinear) pass or acceptance of about 3-5x cost. stl_cylinder_in_box.rs now writes one temp STL per call.

title: Tet/polyhedral volume mesh generation from a closed surface mesh, with polyhedral dual conversion
acceptance: Meshes closed STL geometry with boundary layers; cell quality within thresholds; polyhedral conversion preserves volume
note: Partial. No boundary layers on a tetrahedral mesh of STL geometry are tested; the pass is a bounded heuristic without guarantees (no sliver exudation). USER DECISION 2026-10-22: the tet quality pass (quality_sweeps) stays default 0. Partial (wave 19B, ADR 0030, docs/meshing.md): library rcfd_mesh::tetmesh with exact predicates; Delaunay tetrahedralization of a closed surface with boundary recovery, radius-edge refinement, size control, bistellar sliver improvement, conversion to rcfd Mesh with tag patches. Cube, sphere (volume to 1e-10), torus and cylinder-in-box meshes pass euler/volume/check_mesh, determinism and located error messages. Laplace smoke test on the generated sphere mesh gives relative L2 error 1.1e-2 (limit 0.05). One registered check missed and is an ignored known_miss test: radius-edge fraction on the coarse anisotropic torus 0.634 vs 0.99 (boundary splitting off by default because it does not terminate on small-angle surfaces); after surface remeshing the fraction is 1.0. Slivers remain (cylinder in box: min dihedral 3.3 deg). NOT done: boundary layers, polyhedral dual conversion (F-102 stays todo), hexcore (F-234), sliver optimisation, CLI and case hooks. Literature attributions unverified. P4 (long-term). Gap: volume fill (tet, poly, hexcore). Implement from public algorithms; no GPL/AGPL linkage. SCOPE (merged review): Cartesian-core fill and prism integration are tracked in F-234. Wave 41D (ADR 0104): Opt-in quality pass added to tetrahedralize (TetOptions::quality_sweeps, default 0 = unchanged output): constrained circumcentre insertion for radius-edge failures, interior-vertex smoothing checked with exact orient3d, flips. Cylinder in a box from the STL file: minimum dihedral 17.66 deg and radius-edge fraction 1.0 (default 1.84 deg, 0.936); held-out cube, sphere and remeshed torus meet the T5 limits with the pass (torus 16.73 deg, 1.0). The polydual remark above is stale: polyhedral dual conversion exists (rcfd_mesh::polydual, ADR 0054). Still partial: no boundary layers on a tetrahedral mesh of STL geometry are tested; the pass is a bounded heuristic without guarantees (no sliver exudation). Wave 42C (ADR 0107): the pass stays opt-in (cost 3.05x at 1k cells, 4.81x at 10k cells, superlinear; see F-131); with the pass a 10614-cell STL cylinder-in-box mesh meets T5 (14.2 deg, fraction 1.0) with no inverted cell. Boundary layers still untested. USER DECISION 2026-10-22: the tet quality pass (quality_sweeps) stays default 0 (wave 42C, ADR 0107: t5 torus record and cost limits block). Enable it explicitly where the case-level STL meshing step is wired; fixing the superlinear cost is a backlog item.

title: Blade-passage mesher for turbomachinery (template topologies from hub/shroud/profile curves)
acceptance: A public blade geometry (e.g. NASA Rotor 37) yields a structured passage mesh with acceptable angle/expansion ratios
note: P4 (long-term). Gap: turbomachinery blade-passage topology templates and curve-file inputs. WAVE 32A (ADR 0065): PARTIAL, a lower-fidelity route that is NOT the template-topology mesher and does NOT meet the acceptance (no public blade such as Rotor 37, no acceptable angle/expansion ratios). SCOPE (merged review): add partial and conformal tip-clearance modes, splitter and tandem blades, y+-based first offset, secondary passages, curve-file inputs and spanwise distribution control. WAVE 32A (ADR 0065, rcfd-mesh fan.rs and fan_mesh.rs, case generator axial_fan_sector, cases/axial_fan_sector): PARTIAL, a lower-fidelity route that is NOT the template-topology mesher and does NOT meet the acceptance (no public blade such as Rotor 37, no acceptable angle/expansion ratios). Delivered: Parametric axial-fan geometry with located validation errors (hub/tip radius, tip clearance, blade count, axial extent, per-station chord, stagger, camber, thickness, sweep, lean; NACA 4-digit and circular-arc sections). A watertight blade surface triangulation (area and volume order 2.0). A hex-only periodic single-passage mesh (H-grid with a slit, blunt axially truncated blade edges) with inlet/outlet/hub/shroud/blade/seam patches accepted by the rotational-periodic machinery (node rotation mismatch 1.1e-16 m), exact y+-based first-cell and growth stacks (4.5e-13 relative), cell zone rotor and volume conservation to 1.8e-16. Measured misses (ignored known_miss tests, limits unchanged): Quality gates, set-up A non-orthogonality 73.4 deg (limit 70), skewness 7.57 (2.0), aspect 810 (300), set-up B 89.8 deg, 66, 19123 (3000). First-cell exactness at y+ 1 reads 9.9e-12 against 1e-12 (f64 coordinate resolution, the corrected test uses that bound). G1 400-point polygon area 1.03e-5 against 1e-5 (the corrected 1000-point test passes). S2 thin-blade L2 0.094 at nu 1e-3 against 0.08 (corrected nu 1e-4 gives 0.057, 0.053, 0.051, monotone, residuals not at tolerance after 1500 iterations). S3 m_in + m_out 4.4e-5 of m_in against 1e-6 because the mass flows of the two seam patches do not cancel exactly (the balance over all patches is 7e-16). Limits: the absolute-formulation mrf source is refused on the sector, the relative-frame rotating_frame source is used; no fan performance prediction and no comparison with published fan data. Not done: O-grid or C-grid topology that removes the sheared columns, rounded or sharp edges, splitter blades, partial tip clearance, curve-file input, y+ check of a converged solution.

title: Overset (chimera) mesh coupling
acceptance: A cylinder moving through a background mesh conserves mass and gives drag within 5 percent of a body-fitted run
note: P4 (long-term). Gap: overset boundary type and methods; extends F-063. ADR 0219 (registration of F-134, 2026-11-07, branch f134-overset, not merged): PARTIAL, library only. Built: a component mesh moving rigidly over a static background mesh, joined into one composite mesh with the hole cut by a user function, one fringe layer, donor search and weights exact for linear fields (rcfd_mesh::overset), and an implicit overset PISO step (rcfd_fv::overset::OversetSolver) whose one offset of the background fringe pressures makes the mass of the domain exact. Met (acceptance): a cylinder at Re 40 moving 7.5 diameters through a Cartesian background keeps the continuity of every calculated cell to 8.1e-17 and the mass of the domain to 7.5e-15 of U D L (limits 1e-9); its drag is within 0.62 % of a body-fitted run of the same motion at every step from t = 2 to t = 8 (limit 5 %; mean C_D 1.788 against 1.793). Without the offset the domain loses 2.7e-3 of U D L. Also met: with every cell calculated the overset step gives the library's ALE step bit for bit; a uniform flow through a moving, turning component stays uniform to 1.4e-14; the Taylor-Green error stays within 1.82 times that of the background alone. Known misses, diagnosed by ADR 0232 (F-314): the Taylor-Green observed order, 0.75 as registered and the fine-level ratio 3.31 (limit 2): a first-order time error of the library's moving-mesh PISO step (the lagged convecting flux; 5.99e-4 at the registered step on level 2), not of the overset coupling; with three outer iterations, an opt-in since F-335 (ADR 0238), the fine-level ratio is 1.86 and holds and the order as registered is 1.61; with BDF2 as well, an opt-in since F-338 (ADR 0241), the time error is 2.1e-5 in the difference of 200 and 800 steps, the fine-level ratio is 1.63 and the order as registered is 1.67 (still missed: what is left is spatial); and 1.62 with dt proportional to h^2 (limit 1.7), 1.66 with BDF2 and three outer iterations: the truncation of the linear donor interpolation at one component fringe cell, a second-order error sampled at one pose (the root mean square converges at 1.99 and 1.96 on three levels), free of time error with BDF2. Found there and traced by ADR 0246 (F-334) to the truncation of the linear donor interpolation: with the component at rest the root mean square of the calculated component cells converges at 1.277, 1.166, 1.626 on levels 1 to 4 and at 1.922, 1.935, 1.950 with a third-order interpolation supplied by the test; the mechanism is open. With the opt-in quadratic donor interpolation of F-336 (ADR 0251) the Taylor-Green order with dt proportional to h^2 is 1.993 and 2.000 on levels 1 to 3 and the calculated component cells at rest converge at 1.916, 1.924, 1.952 on levels 1 to 4; T1c stays a recorded miss of the default linear stencils (1.618). Found by ADR 0251: the donor search (ADR 0219 M3) finds no donor for a point in the sliver between two cells that share a non-planar face. Not delivered: the case-tree, CLI and Studio wiring (ADR 0219 Q1); several components, a moving background, hole cutting from the wall geometry, non-orthogonal correctors, turbulence (Q2 to Q5).

title: Aeroacoustic far-field via Ffowcs Williams-Hawkings integral post-processing
acceptance: Rotating-dipole and monopole analytic far-field pressure reproduced; works from sampled surface data files
note: Done against the acceptance (Wave 40A, ADR 0097). Still not done: volume quadrupole, convective FW-H (F-243 known misses), solver-side surface sampling, a measured CFD case. Partial (ADR 0013, crates/rcfd-post/src/fwh.rs, `rcfd acoustics`, docs/reactor-and-acoustics.md; criteria registered before running, all met on the first run). Delivered: Farassat/Brentner formulation 1A on a permeable (or impermeable) data surface in a uniform medium at rest. Surfaces moving on a prescribed subsonic path. Retarded time by Newton iteration. Thickness and loading terms. Valid-window and subsonic guards. Sampled-surface JSON file format (rcfd-fwh-surface v1) with located errors. CLI observer time series to CSV. Measured against exact fields (rho0 1.2, c0 340, 64 samples per period, limit 1e-3 RMS-relative each): Stationary non-compact monopole r=3/10/50 m 4.1e-6/4.4e-6/4.5e-6. 1/r decay spread 2.7e-8. Retarded-time phase error 8.8e-9 rad. Dipole directivity error 2.0e-9, series 4.9e-6. Rotating monopole (tip Mach 0.3) 4.6e-6 in plane and out of plane. Rotating dipole realised as a rotating pair of opposite monopoles 1.0e-5. CLI equals library on a sampled file to 0 relative difference (limit 1e-12). Not done (reason for partial): the rotating dipole is a monopole pair, not a rotating point force with an exact non-compact velocity field; no volume quadrupole term; no uniform-flow (convective) formulation; no sampling of a running CFD solution into surface files (the file format is the interface, the F-029/F-071 solver side is not wired); no measured comparison with a CFD case. The formulas are from memory of the published papers and are validated only by the analytic checks. SCOPE (merged review): add on-the-fly versus post-process evaluation, convective effects, moving receivers, source-surface pruning, band output; acoustic boundary options in F-243. Wave 40A (ADR 0097): The rotating dipole is now a rotating point force (W3, ADR 0066) checked against an independent first-principles reference, the direct retarded-time solution p' = -d/dx_i[F_i/(4 pi r (1 - M_r))]_ret with its own Newton retarded time and an 8th-order observer-space difference (no FW-H or rotor code). FW-H series error 1.9e-8 to 3.4e-8 for B = 1 and 3 at r = 2000 m (45/90/135 degrees) and r = 15 m (limit 1e-3), harmonics to 2.3e-7 (limit 1e-3); reference self-check 1.1e-13, step study <= 4.2e-10. The in-repo Gutin-type formula matches the same reference to 4.0e-5 (limit 1e-2); its attribution to Gutin/Lowson stays UNVERIFIED. Done against the acceptance (the 'monopole pair' wording above is superseded). Still not done: volume quadrupole, convective FW-H (F-243 known misses), solver-side surface sampling, a measured CFD case.

title: Adjoint-based sensitivities and shape morphing for gradient-based design
acceptance: Drag sensitivity of a 2D duct with respect to a few shape parameters matches finite differences within 5 percent
note: P4 (long-term). Gap: gradient-based (adjoint) optimisation and geometry-parameter design tools. USER DECISION 2026-10-21: set to partial: the title promises shape morphing for gradient-based design and RBF morphing is not delivered, although the written acceptance (adjoint drag vs finite differences) is met. SCOPE (merged review): add observables (forces, moments, centre of pressure, cumulative), RBF morphing, and shape, topology and turbulence-coefficient optimiser types with multi-objective support. WAVE 38D (ADR 0091, done): `rcfd_api::design::adjoint` computes shape sensitivities of converged steady laminar SIMPLE/SIMPLEC solutions by a fixed-point discrete adjoint with a finite-difference-assembled dense Jacobian of one outer iteration ((I - G_X)^T lambda = J_X^T, dJ/da = J_a + lambda^T G_a). At a converged fixed point this is the sensitivity of the discrete residual root, independent of relaxation. A registered comparison chose it over a continuous adjoint (inconsistent with the discrete primal at O(h)) and a hand-transposed SIMPLE adjoint (too large). It comes with free-form-deformation morphing (`Ffd`, Bernstein lattice, interior nodes follow) and `optim::projected_gradient` (bound-constrained steepest descent, Armijo) as the gradient option of the design loop. Measured on a 2D duct (40 x 10, Re 20, SIMPLEC upwind, three FFD bump parameters): Adjoint derivatives of the pressure drop and the wall x-drag match central differences of converged solutions (h 1e-3; step study against 2e-3 agrees to 2.3e-6, noise floor 3.5e-10 relative) to 1.1e-6 relative at worst against the 5 percent limit. State-step sensitivity 2.4e-7. Three projected-gradient iterations lower the pressure drop from 2.684 to 2.294. Accurate for the discrete objective on the given mesh and settings, not the mesh-converged quantity. Cost: one gradient (N = 2050) 6.1 s against 0.33 s per primal, so it pays off beyond about 9 parameters; dense, so small meshes only (max_state 4000). NOT delivered: RBF morphing, observables beyond pressure drop and wall force (moments, centre of pressure, cumulative), turbulent gradients (refused; no frozen-turbulence variant), body-force, driver, pseudo-controller and face-jump cases (refused), large meshes (sparse or matrix-free transposed solve), gradients through studies, case files, service or MCP tools, topology, turbulence-coefficient and multi-objective gradient optimisers; only one solver configuration verified. USER DECISION 2026-10-21: set to partial: the title promises shape morphing for gradient-based design and RBF morphing is not delivered, although the written acceptance (adjoint drag vs finite differences) is met.

title: Multiphysics co-simulation participant interface (data transfer, coupling time steps) for external structural solvers
acceptance: A mock structural participant exchanges wall displacement/force with rcfd and converges a coupled iteration; the protocol is documented
note: P4 (long-term). DONE pending acceptance (ADR 0256, 2026-11-12; registered before the code, one amendment before any run). In-process library interface rcfd_fv::cosim, opt-in, nothing calls it; no transport, case key, CLI or MCP tool. Protocol (docs/cosimulation-protocol.md): a fluid and a structural participant answer describe, time, checkpoint, restore, forces and advance with plain arrays in SI units (face forces of the fluid on the wall in newtons, displacements from the reference configuration in metres); the coupler owns the mapping (weights from structural nodes to wall points, rows summing to 1, consistent; forces back by the transpose through the face means, conservative in resultant and work) and iterates within a coupling step on the nodal force with a fixed or an Aitken factor until the force residual is below tolerance times max(force, floor); at the cap it restores and stops, or keeps the iterate by a setting; a failing participant (error, wrong length, non-finite value, wrong time) stops the step with an error naming participant, time and iteration, both restored bit for bit. Fluid participant FlowWall (moving-mesh PISO step, per-face loads from the new sixdof::patch_face_forces, wall pressure from the prescribed gradient of ADR 0252); mock structural participant SprungWall (lumped sprung nodes, RK4). Model problem: a sprung wall of six nodes closing a channel of 20 x 8 x 2 cells whose 16 wall faces do not match the nodes, cosine modes with omega_j^2 = k/(m + rho tanh(kappa_j L)/kappa_j), mass ratios 4 and 0.51. Measured: every one of 650 steps converged, 7 to 10 iterations (mean 8.8, tolerance 1e-8); omega_m/omega 0.998618 (mode 0, limit 0.5 %) and 1.011453 (mode 1, limit 3 %), within 7e-6 and 2e-5 of the discrete model computed before the code (the 1.1 % of mode 1 is the six-node structure); turning points never grow (0.926, 0.950 per period); resultant and work equal on the two meshes to 1e-16, in the run to 5e-16, swept volume to 2e-14; a repeated step restores both participants and repeats bit for bit; with one rigid node the result equals fsi::strong_step_with to 1e-16; controls: the plain fixed point multiplies the residual by 2.0 per iteration (511 in 10), the loose coupling passes 10 X at step 27, the fixed added-mass factor 1/3 takes 30 iterations, an averaging force map loses 85 % of the resultant. Defaults bit-identical (patch_force_moment sums the same face loads in the same order; sixdof, sixdof_coupled, sixdof_flow_f244, strong_fsi_f251, added_mass_f351, f237_heat_rate, w27c_structural pass unedited; baseline hashes 3 passed). Eleven mutations each failed their tests. Amendment 1: the registered set-up had zero-gradient side walls, which leave the side flux free for a transverse flow; Symmetry on the two sides replaced it before any run (the record: mode 1 at 0.977). Not delivered, from the merged-review scope: a transport, a real structural solver, geometric or radial-basis mapping, unmapped-value policy, ramping, quasi-Newton stabilisation, extrapolated step initialisation, several participants; functional-mock-up import stays in F-242. Open: ADR 0256 Q1 to Q5. Follow-ups (ADR 0256 questions 1 to 3, recommendation taken on the maintainer's standing instruction of 2026-11-11): F-360, F-361, F-362. To correct: docs/dynamic-mesh.md still says there is no strong coupling (stale since F-251) and lacks a sentence on zero-gradient side walls (ADR 0256 Q4, Q5). Geometric and radial-basis mapping with an unmapped-point policy: F-362 (ADR 0263, 2026-11-12).

The 40 x 40 viewport raster (one cell per pixel) centreline ux matches Ghia Re 100 within 0.0028 (limit 0.02 of lid speed).
