title: Boundary-condition catalogue completion: mass-flow inlets/outlets, total-pressure inlet with direction and swirl, outflow with flow-rate weights, vents with loss coefficients, outlet-to-inlet recirculation pair, backflow direction and pressure options, target-mass-flow and radial-equilibrium pressure outlets, reverse-flow prevention, opening/entrainment-type boundaries, outlet pressure averaging and mass-flow update options
acceptance: Hagen-Poiseuille pipe and channel with prescribed mass flow reproduce the analytic pressure drop within 1 percent; a swirling pipe with a radial-equilibrium outlet matches the closed-form pressure profile dp/dr = rho w^2 / r; mass is conserved to solver tolerance for every boundary kind
note: Status stays partial. Not delivered after WAVE 29A: compressible/coupled support, time-varying mass flow, lid-pipe mesh, recirculated-stream temperature. Wave 16B recorded three MISSES as ignored tests: F1 secant, C3 reversed K = 0, and registered residual convergence for C2, C3, D1, D2 and E2. Wave 16B, PARTIAL (ADR 0022, commits fed2628 and 52bfe09). Built: boundaries.<patch>.bc_kind values: mass_flow (exact flux, profile expression, direction, swirl, outlet or inlet, outlet-to-inlet recirculation pair). outflow (flow-rate weights, reverse-flow prevention). pressure_outlet (backflow direction and static/total pressure options, reverse-flow prevention, area pressure averaging). opening (entrainment). vent (loss coefficient, both directions). total_pressure_inlet (direction, swirl). radial_equilibrium_outlet (hub or area-mean reference). target_mass_flow_outlet (bernoulli update). rcfd-fv Directed and Switched conditions and outlet helpers. Located validation (V1-V14), turbulence role and inlet speed for the new kinds. docs/case-schema.md. Constant-density segregated kernels only (simple, simplec, piso, pimple). Checks were registered in the ADR before any run. PASS: L1-L6 library (<= 2.2e-16 except the 1.58e-5 free-vortex trapezoid, limit 1e-4). A1 flux exact 1.4e-16 (1e-12). A2/A2b plane Poiseuille dp/dx error 0.498 % (limit 1 %) and profile 2.5e-3 (1.5e-2). A3 annular Hagen-Poiseuille error 0.398 % (1 %). A4-A7 swirl, direction, recirculation pair (4e-13 against 1e-8) and turbulence inlet values. A8 located errors. B1-B4 outflow shares to 4.4e-16 (1e-10). C1, C4, C5 (C5 trivially at rest), D3. Accuracy of C2, C3, D1, D2 (<= 1.4e-9 against 1e-5, pressure <= 7.3e-11) and E2 (outlet pressure 0.41 % of range (3 %), u_theta 0.03 % (3 %), mid-length pressure 2.67 % (3 %, tightest), discrete balance 2.3e-15 (1e-8)) under a POST-HOC settled-field criterion and, for C2, C3, D1, D2, pseudo-time stepping. F1 bernoulli m_out error 1.4e-15 (1e-3) and F2 slope 0.498 % (1 %). T1 pimple 5.6e-16 (1e-12). Mass conservation <= 1.2e-12 (1e-9) for every listed case. Baseline hashes unchanged. MISSES (three): (1) F1 secant (registered 1e-4 in 6000 iterations) diverges, ignored test f1_f2_target_mass_flow_outlet_secant_known_miss; cause: the secant slope is taken from iterates while the flow still spins up and the registered 1000x clip turns one spurious slope into an overshoot. (2) C3 reversed K = 0 does not settle within the registered 6000 iterations (settles after 23174, post-hoc observation), ignored test c3_vent_reversed_k0_known_miss. (3) registered residual convergence (plain simplec, residual targets 1e-12) is NOT MET for C2, C3, D1, D2 and E2, ignored tests *_as_registered_known_miss. No parameter tuned to hide any of them. Deviations disclosed in the ADR addendum: C2, C3, D1, D2 and E2 use a post-hoc settled-field criterion (change <= 1e-10, threshold loosened from 1e-12 once) instead of residual targets, and C2, C3, D1, D2 pseudo-time stepping because plain SIMPLEC from rest diverges (an existing-condition control shows the same residual floor for the uniform duct; the E2 stall is undiagnosed). C5 is trivially at rest. The Hagen-Poiseuille pipe is an annular duct (no solid-pipe mesh). R3 asserts roles, not the model wall set. Not delivered: solid circular-pipe mesh, compressible/variable-density/coupled support, recirculated-stream temperature and per-boundary thermal conditions (F-051), time-varying mass flow, pressure averaging on other kinds, a guarded secant update. Closed forms are textbook relations from memory (docs/reference-data.md wave 16B). Status stays partial. Priority P1. Size L. Area: fv,api. Extends the boundary vocabulary beyond the current field-level and compressible kinds; each new kind is a schema enum value with unit-tested closed-form cases. WAVE 29A (ADR 0055 D5, G1, G2): New pressure_update = guarded_secant for target_mass_flow_outlet (secant slope accepted only when |dm| <= 0.5 |e| and the slope lies within 0.1 to 10 times the dynamic-head slope, else the dynamic-head slope). The registered F1 case (secant limit 1e-4 in 6000 iterations) reaches m_out error 4.2e-16 in 1880 iterations, F2 slope error 0.498 % (1 %), imbalance 9.2e-13 (1e-9). The plain secant known miss is unchanged. Audit: mass-flow flux exactness, total-pressure inlet direction and backflow options already had closed-form checks in ADR 0022 (A1, A5, D2, C2, C5); no new BC kind was added in this wave. Status stays partial; the remaining not-delivered list is unchanged (compressible/coupled support, time-varying mass flow, lid-pipe mesh, recirculated-stream temperature).

title: Near-wall treatment catalogue: enhanced and blended wall treatments, scalable and non-equilibrium wall functions, wall-omega options, equivalent-sand-grain roughness with velocity-shift law

note: Priority P1. Size M. Area: turb,api. The audit of 2026-10-21 marks the item DONE on the acceptance text as written; scope beyond it, and the caveats in the audit file, are not claimed. Non-equilibrium wall functions are still absent. The Enhanced treatment is implemented but NOT converging on the flat plate, unvalidated. Measured misses: SST automatic at y+ 1 and Standard at y+ 30 on the smooth plate, SST + roughness on the rough plate (cause not established). The schema currently accepts a single wall-function value; this adds the other treatments and roughness as enum values. ADR 0015 (turbulence finishing), PARTIAL in the library: Scalable wall functions (Grotjans-Menter form). Equivalent-sand-grain roughness with the Cebeci-Bradshaw velocity shift (k-epsilon and SST automatic). SST low_re wall-omega option and BSL variant. An Enhanced treatment (two-layer scales + Kader law; implemented but NOT converging on the flat plate, unvalidated). Non-equilibrium wall functions NOT attempted. Measured: Smooth plate average Cf vs Prandtl-Schlichting (5 percent): SST automatic y+ 30 -0.5 / -0.7 percent PASS, y+ 1 -8.4 / -7.8 MISS. Scalable y+ 30 -4.0 / -3.1 and y+ 1 -4.6 / -3.1 PASS. Standard y+ 30 -6.2 MISS. Rough plate (10 percent): k-epsilon Standard + roughness -1.0 / +0.3 / +6.3 PASS. SST + roughness -22 to -17 MISS (field stationary, deficit specific to the SST rough path, cause not established). Schema keys turbulence.wall_function {standard, scalable, enhanced}, roughness_height, roughness_constant, wall_omega, sst_variant exist with located validation (rcfd-api wall_opts.rs) but non-default values are rejected until turb.rs / model.rs apply them (hook described in ADR 0015); the tree-equals-library check is unmet. Non-equilibrium wall functions still absent, so partial. DONE (audit 2026-10-21, docs/audit/partials-group-*.md): acceptance text as written is met by passing tests; scope beyond the acceptance text, and the caveats in the audit file, are not claimed.

title: Wall motion and shear conditions: translating and counter-rotating walls, specified shear, partial slip (specularity), Marangoni stress
acceptance: Plane Couette flow and a thermocapillary layer match closed-form profiles; Taylor-Couette torque agrees with the analytic value within 1 percent
note: DONE: all three acceptance checks met by non-ignored tests (D1, D4, D5d). Outside the acceptance and still open: turbulence with the new kinds, MRF Taylor-Couette, the D5b velocity known miss, D2 still reporting converged false. ADR 0016 wave 13. New velocity kinds: moving_wall (translation and rotation). shear. partial_slip (slip length or Maxwell specularity with mean free path). marangoni (thermocapillary stress from the temperature gradient). MET: Plane Couette 1e-13 (limit 1e-8). Specified-shear and slip layers to 1e-11 or better (with solver.component_diagonal = corrected; the averaged diagonal stalls on shear-driven layers, a known ADR 0010 issue). Thermocapillary layer 3.25e-5 (limit 7.5e-4). Taylor-Couette torque -0.43 percent at 128 radial cells (limit 1 percent; first order). Rigid-rotation torque 1.5e-5. MISS: rigid-rotation velocity error 1.4e-5 at 32 radial cells against the registered 1e-6 (9.9e-7 at 64), in an ignored known-miss test. Not delivered: turbulence combined with these kinds (located error), MRF Taylor-Couette. Statused partial because of those gaps, although the three acceptance checks are met. WAVE 40B (ADR 0098): D5d re-runs the n_r = 128 Taylor-Couette case with the iteration cap raised 6000 -> 20000 (registered set-up change, tolerances 1e-11 unchanged) and asserts convergence: converged after 6206 iterations (res_u 9.965e-12, res_p 9.971e-12), torque relative error -4.307e-3 (limit 1e-2). DONE: all three acceptance checks met by non-ignored tests (D1, D4, D5d). Outside the acceptance and still open: turbulence with the new kinds, MRF Taylor-Couette, the D5b velocity known miss, D2 still reporting converged false.

title: Initialisation methods: potential-flow initial solve, coarse-level pre-solve, region patching by registers, localised turbulence initialisation

note: Priority P2. Size M. Area: fv. WAVE 39C (ADR 0094), done: the step clause is met by a coarse-level start (the acceptance asks for an initialised case, not a potential one). Cylinder potential flow within 3 percent (surface 9.7e-4 of 2A on the fine mesh, order 2.0) and the 40x40 cavity coarse start (112 against 165 iterations) met. The backward-facing-step check MISSED (potential 258 iterations against 253 uniform and 258 zero; kept as ignored known-miss test, diagnosis in the ADR), so the item stays partial. title: Numerics robustness options for poor meshes: warped-face gradient correction, secondary gradient limiting, boundary-gradient treatments, pressure-interpolation variants, solution limits
acceptance: Manufactured-solution order-of-accuracy test on skewed, warped and stretched meshes recovers the design order and the options do not degrade it on good meshes
note: DONE: acceptance met by non-ignored tests (m1_m4, m5). Outside the acceptance and still open: pressure-interpolation variants, a separate warped-face correction, case-tree wiring of GradientOptions. ADR 0016 wave 13. Library: GradientOptions (face-gradient correction, secondary limiter, boundary-gradient treatment) in rcfd-fv; case-level solution limits limits.temperature/scalar with clipped-cell count. MET: MMS order on skewed, warped and stretched meshes (>= 1.7 with the options off and with correction, >= 1.5 with the limiter; measured 1.76 to 2.04 except stretched 1.74 at n=32, all in limit). Options cost <= 4.6 percent error on near-orthogonal meshes. Limits clip to the band to 1e-14. On the affine skewed mesh the correction raises the error constant (2.1x) while keeping the order: no benefit is claimed. Registered mild mesh missed its non-orthogonality precondition (13.96 deg) and was replaced by a 0.015 amplitude mesh (disclosed). NOT delivered: pressure-interpolation variants, a warped-face correction separate from the face correction, case-tree wiring of the gradient options. WAVE 40B (ADR 0098): M5 adds n = 64 on the stretched mesh; all runs converge under the unchanged rule (change <= 1e-13 of the range, 600 sweeps) and the 32 -> 64 L2 order is 1.908 for C0, C1 and C2 (limit 1.7; the options are inert on this orthogonal mesh), so the asymptotic range is reached. DONE: acceptance met by non-ignored tests (m1_m4, m5). Outside the acceptance and still open: pressure-interpolation variants, a separate warped-face correction, case-tree wiring of GradientOptions. F-256 (ADR 0190, branch f256-gradient-wiring, not merged): the gradient options are wired into the case tree as solver.gradient_*. F-246 (ADR 0193, branch f246-pressure-interp, not merged): pressure-interpolation variants of the steady kernel, solver.pressure_interpolation; partial.

title: Adaptive time stepping and convergence accelerators: error-estimator steps, period-based steps, RMS/MAX Courant criteria, local timescale factors, residual smoothing, extrapolated step initialisation, nonlinear (Aitken-type) acceleration, stretched-mesh pseudo-time acceleration
acceptance: Error-controlled stepping (step doubling, `solver.error_tolerance`) on a two-timescale linear decay (rates differing by at least 100, both modes of unit initial amplitude) reaches its requested error without a user-chosen step: the final error E satisfies E / (tol T) within [0.3, 3] for two tolerances a factor 4 apart; on the Taylor-Green vortex the error-controlled global error scales with the tolerance (E / (tol T) within [0.3, 3]); a high-aspect-ratio flat-plate boundary-layer mesh converges to Blasius and turbulent skin-friction values within the unaccelerated tolerance
note: Priority P3. Size M. Area: fv,linalg. Still PARTIAL: the flat-plate clause is open (residual smoothing, local timescale factors, stretched-mesh acceleration, Aitken in the outer loop also not delivered). WAVE 42A (ADR 0105) meets the first clause as worded on 2026-10-22; e2 shows the library controller, not the case path free of a chosen step. The Taylor-Green clause is met by S4 (E/(tol T) 0.87-0.90). The acceptance was reworded twice by USER DECISION (2026-10-21 and 2026-10-22), each after a check MISSED; those misses are kept as the ignored tests t1_..._known_miss and e1_..._known_miss. Depends on the pseudo-transient option being finished. WAVE 17A (ADR 0023): Only a library building block, ddt::ErrorController, exists (not wired to the tree). Linear-decay acceptance missed (81 vs 76 steps relative scale, 46 vs 36 absolute reference), recorded as ignored known-miss tests. Taylor-Green, flat-plate acceleration, residual smoothing and Aitken acceleration not delivered; status then todo. WAVE 27B (ADR 0050): rcfd_fv::stepctl and the case keys solver.max_courant_rms, dt_safety/growth/shrink, min_dt/max_dt, error_tolerance (step doubling, implicit Euler), period/steps_per_period, extrapolate_initial, output.write_times/write_time_interval (exact landing, restart-safe). Taylor-Green: Courant control needs 74 steps vs 113 fixed (limit 0.75x) at 1.7 percent L2 difference. Error control E/(tol T) 0.87-0.90 with halving ratio 1.93-2.00. Variable-step BDF2 order 1.95. Extrapolated start halves the initial residual (median ratio 0.14). NAMED GAPS: Aitken relaxation is a library building block only (not in the PIMPLE outer loop or the tree). Local timescale factors, residual smoothing, the stretched-mesh pseudo-time acceleration and the flat-plate acceptance are not delivered. Step control excludes energy/scalar/turbulence/dynamic-mesh runs. Error control is implicit Euler only. Compressible solver not covered. WAVE 39C (ADR 0094), still PARTIAL: the fixed-step side of the Taylor-Green comparison is now measured. Uniform implicit-Euler step counts N = 1, 2, ... were run against the same BDF2 reference: the smallest N with L2 error <= 0.02 is 64 (error 1.97e-2), and the smallest with error <= the Courant-controlled run's 1.69e-2 is 72; the Courant-controlled run takes 74 steps. The registered limit (74 < 64) is MISSED, kept as the ignored test t1_..._known_miss in rcfd-fv tests/adaptive_step.rs. For a single decaying mode a Courant controller (itself fixed-CFL stepping) cannot beat the best uniform step; ADR 0094 proposes (not applied) rewording the first clause to a two-timescale linear decay under error control plus the already measured Taylor-Green tolerance scaling (S4). Linear-decay misses, the flat-plate clause, residual smoothing, local timescale factors and stretched-mesh acceleration remain open. USER DECISION 2026-10-21: acceptance reworded to the two-timescale form proposed in ADR 0094 (Courant control cannot beat the best uniform step on a single mode). Still partial: the two-timescale test does not exist yet; S4 covers the Taylor-Green scaling; flat-plate clause open. WAVE 41A (ADR 0101, rcfd-fv tests/adaptive_step.rs e1): the reworded two-timescale clause was tested and MISSED, as predicted in the ADR before the run. Shear wave u_x = sin y + sin 12y on a periodic 4 x 64 box (rates 0.999 and 128.1, ratio 128; one PISO step equals the implicit-Euler factors to 1.7e-15), T = 1, S4 controller settings: tol 1e-2 takes 1913 controlled steps (E 7.84e-3) against 64 uniform steps at equal error; tol 2.5e-3 takes 3149 against 240. Kept as the ignored e1_..._known_miss with the limit unchanged. Reason (derived in ADR 0101): an error-per-unit-time controller spends about lambda_fast/(4 tol) steps resolving the fast transient, which L-stable uniform implicit Euler damps without resolving; it can only win once the slow mode has decayed by about e^-(rate ratio). So the clause as reworded is not expected to be met by local error control on a decaying linear system; this is for the user to decide. The Taylor-Green clause is met by S4 (E/(tol T) 0.87-0.90). The flat-plate clause is still open. Stays partial. USER DECISION 2026-10-22: acceptance reworded a second time. Wave 41A (ADR 0101) showed error control cannot beat the best uniform step count on a linear decay (1913 steps vs 64 at tol 1e-2): per-unit-time control resolves the fast transient that implicit Euler merely damps. New first clause: error control hits the requested error with no hand-picked step. The step-count test e1 stays as an ignored known miss. Flat-plate clause still open. WAVE 42A (ADR 0105, rcfd-fv tests/adaptive_step.rs e2, non-ignored): the first clause as worded on 2026-10-22 is MET. Same shear wave as E1 (rates 0.999 and 128.1, unit amplitudes), T = 1, error = relative L2 time error against the exact semi-discrete solution. No step chosen by the user: library controller defaults (no min_dt / max_dt), only error_tol set, first proposal = T. tol 1e-2: 2502 steps (18 rejected), E 7.917e-3, E/(tol T) 0.792; tol 2.5e-3: 9989 steps (20 rejected), E 2.080e-3, 0.832 (limit [0.3, 3]). Limitation recorded: through the case keys the run still needs solver.dt (timectl takes the first proposal and max_dt from it and min_dt = 1e-3 solver.dt by default), so e2 shows the library controller, not the case path free of a chosen step; not changed (default change). e1 stays ignored. Still PARTIAL: the flat-plate clause is open (residual smoothing, local timescale factors, stretched-mesh acceleration, Aitken in the outer loop also not delivered).

title: Non-iterative time advancement (fractional-step) option for transient flow
acceptance: Taylor-Green vortex decay matches the analytic solution within 2 percent; transient lid-driven cavity agrees with published data
note: Priority P3. Size M. Area: fv. The audit of 2026-10-21 marks the item DONE on the acceptance text as written; scope beyond it, and the caveats in the audit file, are not claimed. Three registered checks MISSED and are ignored known-miss tests: BDF2 temporal order, spatial ratio (met after the wave 25A fix) and the Kim-Moin boundary treatment. Alternative to the iterated PISO/PIMPLE loop for large steps and low cost. PARTIAL (wave 21C, ADR 0037). Delivered: solver.time_advance = fractional_step for the transient piso algorithm (Euler and BDF2). solver.fractional_form incremental or chorin. solver.fractional_boundary kim_moin or plain. One momentum predictor and ONE pressure Poisson solve per step (library PimpleSettings.fractional, module rcfd-fv pimple/fractional.rs) with a case-tree option and located errors. Measured: Taylor-Green kinetic-energy error 2.3e-3 (limit 0.02). Euler temporal order 1.034. Divergence 1.8e-11 default and 2.8e-15 tight solver tolerance. Difference to PISO 3.0e-3 (limit 5e-3). Lid-driven cavity Re 100 Ghia centreline error 3.0e-3 and 9.0e-3 (limit 0.02) and difference to SIMPLEC 4.7e-4 (limit 0.01). Tree equals library bit for bit. The roadmap acceptance is met by these checks, but three registered checks MISSED and are ignored known-miss tests: BDF2 temporal order 1.04 on the periodic Taylor-Green (band 1.7 to 2.3; wave 25A, ADR 0043: the lagged periodic partner value was a defect and is now extrapolated, order 1.51, the rest is the O(dt h^2) collocated pressure-smoothing term; a wall-bounded mode gives 2.07). Spatial ratio 2.48 (limit 3.0; met after the wave 25A fix, 3.95). The Kim-Moin boundary treatment shows no benefit in the Chorin form (ratio 1.13 against 0.5; the incremental form is insensitive to it). NOT delivered: rotational pressure correction, Crank-Nicolson, Choi-type transient Rhie-Chow, body force and buoyancy, turbulence, energy, rheology, pimple outer loops, moving meshes, restart of fractional runs, verification of the Kim-Moin and Zang et al. references (see docs/reference-data.md). title: Advection and transient scheme additions: high-resolution (bounded blended), compressive, specified blend factor, bounded central differencing, bounded second-order time scheme

note: The audit of 2026-10-21 marks the item DONE on the acceptance text as written; scope beyond it, and the caveats in the audit file, are not claimed. Flow-rate reduction error 1.2e-3, 8.6e-4, 4.1e-4 (limit 1e-2). Insulated walls Ha 10 the same. Lorentz integral, work identity and momentum balance at round-off. Electrode current within 1.5e-3. title: Heat-exchanger domain model: shell-and-tube and dual-cell macro models, with fan, vent, porous-jump and network boundary types as sub-criteria
acceptance: Counterflow exchanger reproduces the effectiveness-NTU analytic result within 2 percent; fan and vent boundaries reproduce their prescribed pressure-flow curves
note: The acceptance is met (WAVE 39D, ADR 0095). The exchanger checks still verify the algebraic macro model, not a resolved exchanger, and shell-and-tube stays UNVERIFIED. Plain SIMPLEC with a velocity inlet and a forward vent diverges from the first iteration; this robustness defect is not fixed. Not delivered: segmented/resolved exchanger, multi-branch network, two-phase, fan total pressure with dynamic head. PARTIAL (wave 23A, ADR 0039). Delivered: rcfd_fv::hx (eps-NTU counter, parallel, crossflow with one stream mixed, shell and tube, both-unmixed fit; pressure-loss closure). Components heat_exchanger mode ntu (arrangement, UA, constant or dual-cell secondary, loss_coefficient/loss_linear on the downstream plane) and type fan_boundary (curve-driven pressure patch). Measured: Counterflow/parallel against eps-NTU and an independent marched solution to 1e-14 (limit 2e-2). Dual-cell energy exchange to 1e-8. Loss closure exact to 1e-14. Fan boundary flow within 6.3e-4 of the analytic operating point and patch pressure on the curve (limit 2e-3). The macro cell is algebraic, so these checks verify wiring, not a resolved exchanger. Misses (ignored known_miss tests, limits unchanged): The both-unmixed crossflow curve fit deviates up to 3.3 percent from the exact solution and breaks the small-N slope and parallel <= cross ordering. Shell and tube is UNVERIFIED against a published table. Vent and porous jump reuse ADR 0012/0022 evidence (no new CFD vent test); the fan test needs a distributed bed because a lossless pressure-pressure duct diverges in SIMPLEC. Not delivered: segmented/resolved exchanger, multi-branch network, two-phase, fan total pressure with dynamic head. WAVE 25C (ADR 0045): fan, porous jump, loss closure, fan_boundary and the NTU exchanger now also run in transient PISO/PIMPLE (pimple, 3 outer iterations). Fixed-point source check 9.0e-6. Fan flow 1.5e-5 and jump drop 2.2e-6. Loss closure 6e-14. fan_boundary flow 1.9e-13 and patch pressure 5e-15. NTU duty equal to the steady SIMPLEC duty to 1.4e-14 relative. Coupled and compressible algorithms give located errors and are not delivered. WAVE 25B (ADR 0044): the both-unmixed crossflow fit is replaced by the exact Poisson-tail series (worst deviation 7.7e-6 from a Richardson-extrapolated marched 2-D reference, limit 1e-4); the three H2/H3 known-miss tests now pass under --ignored and stay ignored with limits intact. WAVE 39D (ADR 0095): X6 fan boundary at three operating points (bed permeability 3e-7, 1e-6, 1e-5 on the X4 set-up): Q = 1.929e-2, 3.052e-2, 3.621e-2 against the analytic operating points within 1.13e-3, 6.35e-4, 8.6e-5 (limit 5e-3), one point on each curve segment; the patch pressure lies on the curve to 1.8e-13 (by construction). X7 vent on its own set-up (periodic duct, velocity inlet, vent with K = 2.5 at xmax) at u = 0.5, 1, 2, -0.5, -1, -2: the outlet pressure equals 0.5 K u|u| within 3.9e-13 (limit 1e-6), which separates the quadratic law from a linear one by a factor of 2. X7 uses pseudo-time at Courant number 1 (pseudo_dt = 0.02/|u|, ADR 0095 amendment 1). The registered fixed pseudo_dt 0.02 gives NaN at u = 2 (ignored test x7_vent_at_fixed_pseudo_dt_known_miss). Plain SIMPLEC with a velocity inlet and a forward vent diverges from the first iteration (max |ux| 6.06, 1.8e2, 1.8e5 at K = 2.5; stable at K = 0); this robustness defect is not fixed. The acceptance is met. The exchanger checks still verify the algebraic macro model, not a resolved exchanger, and shell-and-tube stays UNVERIFIED.

note: PARTIAL (wave 23B library, ADR 0040; wave 28A wiring into the VOF host and case tree, ADR 0052). The 1D Stefan evaporation acceptance and the CFD-level film condensation within 10 percent of Nusselt are missing. There is no energy equation in the multiphase path, so the temperature is a PRESCRIBED field. Lee, ZGB factor values, Schrage factor and Rohsenow 0.68 are from knowledge and UNVERIFIED (docs/reference-data.md). WAVE 28A: Lee and Hertz-Knudsen-Schrage mass transfer is wired into the VOF host (rcfd-fv vof.rs) and the case tree (multiphase.mass_transfer). Source in the alpha equation (exponential integrator of the frozen-temperature relaxation for Lee, alpha stays in [0, 1]) and the continuity volume source mdot (1/rho_v - 1/rho_l) in the pressure equation (solve_pressure_src); the same delivered rate feeds both. Checks M1-M5 pass: closed form 1.4e-14, per-cell phase balance 2.2e-16, coupled volume identity 9.2e-16, continuity 2.1e-13, zero transfer at saturation bit-identical, Hertz-Knudsen 1.1e-15; tree equals library. LIMITATIONS: there is no energy equation in the multiphase path, so the temperature is a PRESCRIBED field (uniform plus constant gradient), the latent heat only enters p_sat and a reported power, there is no latent-heat feedback, no 1D Stefan problem or boiling run, and no phase-change term in the momentum rho phi; a pressure patch is required; the rate is clipped to the phase available in the cell. Library delivered in wave 23B: rcfd-fv masstransfer.rs, per-cell source evaluators taking phase fractions, temperatures and pressures: Lee temperature-driven and Hertz-Knudsen-Schrage kinetic evaporation-condensation. A pressure-driven bubble-dynamics form derived from Rayleigh-Plesset (Zwart-Gerber-Belamri structure). Raoult bubble/dew pressures and Henry's law with van 't Hoff temperature dependence. Species transfer rate. Nusselt laminar-film wall condensation (film thickness, wall mass flux, mean coefficient 0.943 form). A 0-D Lee relaxation cell. Checked against hand values and closed forms (to 1e-13 and better), exact phase-source conservation (liquid + vapour == 0, energy == -mdot h_fg), zero at saturation, sign logic, kinetic-theory maximum flux, Nusselt mass-flow identity, and the frozen-mass relaxation analytic solution (6e-11 relative); located errors for bad inputs. All M1-M9 checks pass, no misses. Missing (why partial): An Euler-Euler host. title: Free-surface wave generation and absorption: linear and Stokes wave inlets, irregular spectrum waves, numerical beach damping
acceptance: Linear dispersion relation and Stokes wave elevation reproduced; reflected-wave fraction below 5 percent with the beach
note: PARTIAL (wave 23B library, ADR 0040; wave 28A wiring into the VOF host and case tree, ADR 0052). The full tank acceptance beyond the coarse 2-D checks of wave 28A is missing. WAVE 28A did not deliver a refinement study, Stokes-2 or irregular waves in a tank run, 3-D tanks or a comparison with published tank data. WAVE 28A: a wave-inlet boundary (per-face velocity and alpha from Airy / Stokes-2 kinematics with a ramp) and a relaxation-zone beach (still-water target, exponential or polynomial weights) are wired into the VOF host and the case tree (multiphase.waves, multiphase.reference_point). Coarse 2-D tank (depth 0.30 m, T 1 s, H 0.06 m, lambda/32): Wave height -10.5 percent at 0.5 lambda and -18.0 percent at 1.5 lambda (limits 12 and 25, numerical damping stated in the ADR before the runs), periods within 0.5 percent. Beach K_r 0.014 against the control wall 0.524 (20 periods; Goda-Suzuki two-gauge method; limits 0.15 and 0.5). Volume identity 6e-14, level drift 1.4e-3 m (limit 6e-3), alpha bounded. Inlet values reproduce the wave to 1e-16 m. KNOWN MISSES (ignored tests, limits intact): The 10-period control (set-up defect, window before the reflected group returns; corrected 20-period tests pass). Still water with the zone and 3 PISO correctors (max|U| 1.3e-8 against 1e-10: base PISO splitting error of the thin air layer, identical without the zone; with 4 correctors 8e-12 passes). Not delivered: a refinement study, Stokes-2 or irregular waves in a tank run, 3-D tanks, comparison with published tank data, relaxation to a wave target in the tree. Library delivered in wave 23B: rcfd-fv waves.rs: Finite-depth dispersion solved to 2e-15 residual. Airy and second-order Stokes kinematics (elevation, velocity, potential, pressure) usable as wave-inlet values with a start-up ramp and an exact liquid-volume-fraction helper. Irregular waves from Pierson-Moskowitz and JONSWAP spectra with a seeded reproducible phase set (recovered Hs within 4.8e-4 and 3.3e-4 of target, moments m1 and m2 within 2e-5 and 8e-4 of closed forms). Relaxation-zone blending weights (exponential and polynomial, exact endpoints, monotone) and sponge profiles. A 1-D linear shallow-water tank for reflection estimates. Linear dispersion limits, energy equipartition and mean flux, continuity and Laplace pass; the Stokes formulas satisfy both free-surface conditions through second order (the residual is third order: ratio 8.00 for halved amplitude). 1-D toy tank: rigid wall R = 1.00000, exponential relaxation beach of 2 wavelengths R = 2.6e-4 (limit 0.05, acceptance statement met only in this toy, not in a free-surface solver). KNOWN MISSES (ignored tests, limits not changed): The registered W3 residual-scaling statement divided by the amplitude and so cannot pass (corrected test w3b passes). The registered 'abrupt zone reflects at least 0.5' check measured 0.214 (wrong premise; a post-hoc corrected comparison is labelled as such in the ADR addendum). Missing (why partial): The full tank acceptance beyond the coarse 2-D checks of wave 28A. Third and higher order Stokes, cnoidal and stream-function waves. Directional spectra. Piston/flap wave makers. Any 2-D/3-D reflection measurement. Second-order Stokes, JONSWAP and the blending formula citations are UNVERIFIED (docs/reference-data.md); the formulas are validated by the tests. Previous scope text: Priority P3. Size M. Area: fv. Wave boundary conditions for the free-surface solver. WAVE 25B (ADR 0044): damping diagnosed as per-step multiplication; the sponge R=0.135 is exp(-2 int sigma dx/c); the W7(d) premise (abrupt zone reflects >= 0.5) is ill-posed for the registered blend (R=0.214); w7d stays ignored, continuum estimate misses its 25 percent limit (ignored w8_4 known miss).

Delivered in rcfd-api `rules` with the data file crates/rcfd-api/rules/setup_rules.json (format rcfd-setup-rules v1): A strict declarative engine (conditions all/any/not, path and count tests with where, 13 operators, each-iteration, mesh context, located paths, sorted deterministic output of id/severity/category/path/message and optional fix). 21 registered rules (13 errors, 5 warnings, 3 infos; categories mesh, boundaries, materials, models, solver, output, setup). Wired into `rcfd check`, `rcfd validate`, `rcfd run` (error-level rule: exit 3 before solving; warnings: stderr and `warning` events with the rule id) and the `check` event (`rules` array). Measured (checks registered first in ADR 0031): E1 every one of the 21 rules fires with its id, severity, category and path on a seeded setup and no other error-level rule fires. E3 deterministic bytes. E4 strict loader rejects unknown keys/operators/severities/categories/versions, a rule written only as data works. E2 PARTIAL: on 66 distinct case texts (8 cases/**/*.toml, 1 documentation block, 57 extracted from the test sources) no error-level diagnostic, but one warning, SV103 (aspect ratio above the library's own threshold of 1000) on the wall-resolved mesh of a turbulence test case; the registered assertion lives in an ignored known-miss test, thresholds not changed. Limits: 12 of the 13 error rules restate checks the loaders already enforce (SV004 the turbulence initial-k derivation, SV009 the chain sequence check) and SV011 overlaps the mesh quality error, so through the binary no error-level rule was observed to fire on its own. The new diagnostics are SV101-SV105 and SV201-SV203. No auto-fix is applied (suggestions only). The acceptance wording 'accepts the benchmark registry cases' is evaluated on the TOML setups under cases/ because the registry case.json files are descriptors that do not load. User-function and component checks are not in the rule set. WAVE 39A (ADR 0092, done): the 'accepts the benchmark registry cases' and 'published validation cases' clauses are now measured by crates/rcfd-api/tests/registry_setups_w39a.rs V1: case-tree set-ups of the five registry descriptors (cavity Re 100 n 32; backward_step with the descriptor mesh built by gen::backward_step and read as a polyMesh file; flat_plate laminar Re_L 1e5 with wall layers; heated_cavity Ra 1e3; naca0012 on an O-grid warped onto the NACA 0012 thickness formula, Re 6e6, SST) plus cylinder Re 100, channel Re_tau 178.12 (SST), the wall-function channel and Sod, each through runctl::check_only (the library body of rcfd check). Limit exit 0 and 0 error-level rule diagnostics on all nine: met (0 errors; one warning, SV101 on the NACA O-grid, max non-orthogonality 80.3 deg). Reading registered in ADR 0092: 'published validation cases' = the five registry benchmarks plus the validation-test cases the case tree can express. ADR 0092 amendments 1-2 add V2b, the parallel-plate Graetz set-up on a prescribed parabolic flow (solver.frozen_flow): exit 0, 0 rule diagnostics (the first Graetz set-up, V2, had a zero inlet velocity and is kept as an ignored known miss). Not covered: the FAN-01 case (a format! template in fan01_validation.rs, F-126) and the w33c SST plate/wall-layer library-only set-ups. The NACA O-grid is a rule-check set-up, not a lift-prediction mesh; the registry descriptors still carry no shipped case file. USER DECISION 2026-10-21: accepted as done on the definition in ADR 0092 (five registry cases plus validation cases a case file can express). Outside that definition: FAN-01 (code template, tracked under F-126) and the library-only SST plate tests. Registry folders still hold no case files; the set-ups live inside the test. KNOWN ISSUE (ADR 0191 addendum 1, observation): SV202 (info, when no boundary condition is set) says every patch takes the default "a fixed no-slip wall"; for the compressible solver a patch without a condition is a slip wall (an outlet patch extrapolates; docs/case-schema.md), so the message is wrong there. USER DECISION 2026-11-06: the message becomes solver-aware; the change is made separately.

title: Chained run configurations: sequenced steady-then-transient restart, interpolating initial values onto a new mesh
acceptance: Two chained configurations (steady then transient restart) on the lid-driven cavity reach the same final state as a single run
note: Done under the user's reading (chain equals an uninterrupted run); the steady-then-transient chain stays covered by C1/C2. A split whose stage end clips a step by a few ulp (e.g. 0.3) is not bitwise equal and is not tested. Partial (acceptance met; scope limited). Delivered in rcfd-api `chain` and `rcfd run`: The `chain` section (sequence plus named stages with `set` overrides that accumulate, `restart` mode, transfer `method`, `allow_unconverged`). Per-stage output directories with restart files. Restart from the previous stage through the F-115 machinery (same mesh exact or steady-to-transient initialisation, changed mesh transferred). Failure propagation by exit code. Status events stage_start/restart/stage_finish/chain_finish with a `stage` field. Located static checks. Measured (checks registered first in ADR 0031): The chain's final transient state equals the manual two-run procedure bit for bit (and the CLI solution.vtu is byte-identical to `rcfd run` then `rcfd restart`). Acceptance case, 16x16 cavity steady (1e-8) then PISO dt 0.05 to t = 1: speed relative L2 distance to the single steady run 2.08e-3 and pressure (mean removed) 8.35e-3 against the registered 2e-2. 12 to 24 mesh change between stages converges (147 iterations). Failure of stage 1 gives exit 5 with stage 2 never started. Seven kinds of malformed stage definitions rejected at their located path. Threads 1 versus 3 byte-identical. Not done: operating-point sweeps (parametric-study item), chains through the service run.headless and MCP, stage-specific rule checks before the chain starts (each stage is checked as it starts), restart of transient runs with energy/scalars/turbulence, parallel or branching chains. Wave 40A (ADR 0097, test c7 in crates/rcfd-api/tests/chain_w19c.rs): two chained transient stages (PISO dt 0.05, 0 to 0.5 then exact restart to 1.0) equal one transient run from rest to t = 1 bit for bit in ux, uy, p, face flux and time (registered tolerance 0). The split at 0.5 takes ten full steps; a split whose stage end clips a step by a few ulp (e.g. 0.3) is not bitwise equal and is not tested. Done under the user's reading (chain equals an uninterrupted run); the steady-then-transient chain stays covered by C1/C2.

title: Acoustic boundary and source options: impedance boundary, non-reflecting forcing, broadband-noise estimates, wave-equation solver with sponge layers, modal export
acceptance: Impedance-tube reflection coefficient matches the closed form; a quiet boundary reflects a pulse by less than 1 percent
note: Priority P3. Size M. Area: fv,post. WAVE 32B (ADR 0066) and the job of 2026-11-12 (ADR 0233). The acceptance text is MET IN THE LIBRARY, not from a case file. Built in ADR 0233: `CompBc::Impedance { p, z }` (rcfd-fv compressible_bc.rs `impedance_wall`), a locally reacting wall with a real specific impedance on the outgoing Riemann invariant, also on moving faces; the quiet boundaries are the matched impedance `z = rho c` (holds the ambient pressure) and the existing `NonReflecting` with `sigma = 0` (holds nothing). Registered checks, all met at the first run: impedance tube with a pulse for z/(rho c) = 0, 1/3, 1, 3, 19: R within 1.13e-3 of (z - rho c)/(z + rho c) (limit 1e-2); the quiet boundaries reflect 2.1e-5 (matched) and 5.8e-8 (Thompson) of a pulse (limit 1e-2); standing-wave ratio of a tone 3.006 and 3.004 against 3 (limit 2 percent); a uniform overpressure decays to 5.4e-5 with matched walls and stays with Thompson boundaries; oblique plane pulses at 30 and 45 degrees within 1.5e-2 of (z cos - rho c)/(z cos + rho c) and of (1 - cos)/(1 + cos) (limit 3e-2). Five mutations caught. Not done: case-schema wiring (a new key needs an approved edit of case_hashes_w48u.rs; this is why the status is partial). Limits: real, frequency-independent impedance only; both quiet boundaries reflect 7 percent at 30 degrees and 17 percent at 45 degrees; gas at rest, Cartesian grids, verification against closed forms only. Unchanged from wave 32B: FW-H 1A (fwh.rs), Gutin rotor tones (rotor.rs), metrics (acoustics.rs), surface-series reader, `rcfd fwh`, non-validated broadband proxies (noise_proxies.rs), docs/acoustics.md; W5a/W5b known misses (7.7e-2 and 6.7e-2 against 1e-2 and 1e-3). Not built: quadrupole volume term, comparison with a measured fan, calibration of the proxy constants, on-the-fly sampling. The wave-equation solver with sponge layers and the modal export were built under F-333 (ADR 0351, 2026-11-12, library only). Follow-ups (ADR 0233 questions 1, 2 and 4, recommendations taken on the maintainer's standing instruction of 2026-11-11): F-330 (wiring), F-331 (sponge layer), F-332 (frequency-dependent impedance), F-333 (wave solver and modal export). Open: question 3 (the reflection_value default reflects 46 percent of a short pulse; changing it changes a default).

title: Flow-coupled six-DOF validation: body falling through a fluid and spring-mounted body in a flow
acceptance: Laminar incompressible PISO/PIMPLE on a moving mesh, existing loose coupling (ADR 0033 D7), added-mass-to-body-mass ratio <= 0.2 (from the ADR closed form, not the displaced-fluid mass), no cyclic faces carrying a moving-wall velocity. (a) Falling body: a rigid block falling under gravity minus buoyancy along a closed 2-D channel, the displaced fluid returning through the two side gaps (falling-piston viscometer), reaches the terminal velocity of the lubrication closed form derived in the ADR within 2 percent after an approach of at least 5 time constants that fits inside the F-063 smoothing compression limit; the ADR bounds the neglected end-effect, finite-Reynolds and finite-length terms to <= 0.5 percent before the run. (b) Spring-mounted body: free decay of a spring-mounted piston driving a fluid column (the C2 geometry plus a spring, amplitude <= 1 percent of L0) oscillates at omega = sqrt(k/(M + rho A L0)) within 2 percent, with parameters chosen so the fluid lowers the frequency by at least 4 times the tolerance (mass ratio 0.2 gives 8.7 percent), so the check fails with fluid forces off. Both: halving dt changes the measured quantity by <= 0.5 percent; per-step continuity <= 1e-10 and the uniform-flow GCL to round-off are asserted (not only printed); in (b) the amplitude at successive same-side turning points never grows (ratio <= 1 + 1e-3; the open outlet makes body + spring + fluid energy rise during inflow by -1/2 rho A v^3, which cancels over a full period, so energy is not compared mid-cycle). Out of scope: strong (implicit) coupling and added-mass stabilisation (mass ratio > 0.2), comparison with published falling-sphere or falling-cylinder experiments or wall-correction tables (no source read), cross-flow vortex-induced vibration, free 3-D rotation with Newmark, contact and multi-body, turbulence or energy on moving meshes.
note: Split from F-229 on 2026-10-21 (partials audit; ADR 0033 reads these two clauses as flow-coupled and not delivered). Uses the moving-mesh path (F-063, partial). Size M. REFINED 2026-10-21 (not yet user-approved): the lead's text had no named case and no closed form for 'terminal velocity with drag from the flow' or 'added mass included'. (a) now names a falling block whose drag comes from fluid displaced past it (not the tangential Couette shear of C1) with a lubrication closed form derived in the ADR. (b) now names a spring-mounted piston-column (C1/C2 are the existing flow-coupled checks; the new cases must differ and must fail without the fluid, hence the 4x frequency-shift requirement). Added a dt-halving check (moving meshes run implicit Euler only). Added asserted continuity and GCL (the F-063 audit found continuity printed but not asserted). Added an amplitude non-growth check at same-side turning points (energy injection is how explicit coupling fails; a mid-cycle energy bound would be wrong because the C2 outlet is open). The 0.2 bound is on added mass, which for a block pushing fluid through narrow gaps far exceeds its displaced mass. The lead's 'needs strong coupling or added-mass stabilisation' holds only above mass ratio 0.2 (ADR 0033 D7). PROPOSED SPLIT: strong (implicit) fluid-structure coupling with added-mass stabilisation as its own item (a feature, not a validation), with a mass-ratio >= 1 version of (b) as its acceptance. OPEN QUESTION: the title's 'spring-mounted body in a flow' is read as free decay in still fluid; a cross-flow (vortex-induced vibration) case would need a published data set chosen by the user. USER DECISION 2026-10-22: split as proposed; "in a flow" is read as free decay in still fluid (no VIV case). Strong coupling is F-251. DONE (ADR 0211, the registration of F-244, 2026-11-07, branch f244-six-dof-validation, not merged): every registered check is met by library tests (crates/rcfd-fv/tests/sixdof_flow_f244.rs, test code only, no library or schema change); the acceptance is still the maintainer's. (a) A block 4 h wide and 500 h tall falling in a closed 2-D channel (gaps h) reaches 1.00545 of the lubrication terminal velocity (M - rho V_b) g / C, C = 2 mu H_b dz (3 B^2 + 1)/h, after 10 time constants (limit 2 %; added-mass ratio 0.178 from the closed form, Re_U 0.1, travel 0.42 h, smallest cell volume 0.916 of its start against the F-063 limit 0.5). The neglected terms were bounded to 0.46 % before the run: the end effect to [0, 0.363 %] by the minimum-dissipation theorem (lubrication is a lower bound of the Stokes drag; an explicit trial field gives the upper bound), inertia and finite time to 0.10 %. Halving dt changes it by 3.4e-6; the drag of a block whose sides did not move is 21 % off (negative control). (b) The C2 piston on a spring (mass ratio 0.2, amplitude 0.01 L0) oscillates at 1.0013 of sqrt(k/(M + rho A L0)) (limit 2 %), dt halving 2e-4; with the fluid force off it is 9.5 % off; successive same-side turning points decay by 4.7 % per period at T/100 (the lag of the explicit coupling), never grow. Both: continuity at most 3.9e-11 per step (limit 1e-10), discrete GCL 6.5e-16 mean(V), a uniform flow on both moving meshes stays uniform to 4.2e-15; four library mutations each made their checks fail. Found, not fixed (ADR 0211 amendment 1): the baseline PISO step is unstable on the block-in-channel mesh above a time step between tau/40 and tau/20 (cell diffusion number 3 to 6 across the gap), on a fixed mesh as well; the registered tau/10 run is kept as an ignored known miss and (a) runs at tau/40 and tau/80. Open: ADR 0211 Q1 (approval of the refined acceptance text), Q2 (a case-tree version), Q3 (status), Q4 (a new item for the PISO time-step limit).

title: Particle models: droplet evaporation (d-squared law) and breakup
acceptance: Two parts, each gated on its own. (A1) a single droplet evaporating in quiescent hot gas follows the quasi-steady d^2 law with the evaporation constant derived in the ADR from the registered model, measured d^2 slope within 2 percent, and the droplet mass lost equals the vapour mass source delivered to the carrier to 1e-10 relative; (A2) the breakup model reproduces its own analytic breakup time and child-size relation for a drop given a step relative velocity within 2 percent, with liquid mass conserved through breakup to round-off (critical Weber number and model constants read from the source); Out of scope: spray penetration against data (F-252), wall film (F-253), wall interaction (F-254), dispersion and reactions (F-255), group and file injections (F-056 scope).
note: Split from F-128 on 2026-10-21 (partials audit). Depends on F-128 and F-056 (partial: no cyclone case). Size L. REFINED 2026-10-21 (not yet user-approved): The lead's text gated only spray and film against data while the title also lists breakup, erosion and rough-wall interaction. Each sub-model now has a closed-form or self-consistency check (d^2 law, model breakup time, impact-flux identity, rebound-distribution KS) plus a mass-conservation check, so the code can be verified before any data set is chosen. The Nusselt thickness is derived from the steady incline film profile (u = g sin(theta)/nu (delta y - y^2/2)), not cited. 'Track files' dropped: particles.tracks / particle_tracks.csv was delivered in wave 21C. PROPOSED SPLIT (this is three items, not one): spray = A (breakup, evaporation, heat/mass transfer; A3 needs a variable-density carrier with energy, a vapour species and two-way mass/energy exchange, which should be confirmed before scheduling and may itself be a fourth item since it alone is data-dependent); wall film = B; wall interaction = C (erosion, rough-wall rebound). OPEN QUESTIONS: which public vaporising-spray data set (not yet identified or read); dispersion from turbulence-model fields and particle reactions were in F-128's not-delivered list and are now tracked nowhere; should 'track files' mean something beyond particle_tracks.csv. USER DECISION 2026-10-22: split into four items plus dispersion and reactions: F-252 (A3), F-253 (B), F-254 (C), F-255. This item keeps A1 and A2, verifiable without a data set. DONE (ADR 0224, the registration of F-245, 2026-11-08, branch f245-droplet, not merged): every registered check is met in the library (rcfd-particles, no case key); the acceptance is still the maintainer's (ADR 0224 Q1). (A1) Evaporation (rcfd_particles::evaporation, Tracker::set_evaporation): the quasi-steady film model with Bird's correction (model B of Both, Mira and Lehmkuhl, arXiv:2201.02818, read), Ranz-Marshall Nu and Sh, Clausius-Clapeyron through the boiling point; d^2 linear and one exponential Euler step of the temperature per sub-step (its fixed point is the wet bulb); the vapour booked per cell. The evaporation constant K = 8 rho D ln(1 + B_M(T_wb))/rho_l was derived in the ADR (3.4196739796e-7 m^2/s for the test inputs): the d^2 slope of a droplet at its wet bulb in still 800 K gas is within 1.1e-15 of K, of one injected at 300 K within 7.1e-12 after the heat-up (limit 2 percent); the vapour equals the liquid lost to 2.9e-16 for the droplet and 3.0e-12 in a spray of 160 parcels with breakup (limit 1e-10). (A2) TAB breakup (rcfd_particles::breakup, Tracker::set_breakup) with the constants and the numerical method read in O'Rourke and Amsden, LA-UR-87-2105 (1987) (C_F = 1/3, C_k = 8, C_d = 5, C_b = 1/2, K = 10/3, We_crit = 6): the breakup time arccos(1 - 12/We)/omega and the product radius r/(4/3 + We/6) of a drop at rest in a step relative velocity are reproduced to 1.5e-14 at We 6.1 to 1000 (limit 2 percent), a viscous drop to equal bits, the source's limits (eqs. 12a, 13, 16, 23) within 0.82 percent; n d^3 through breakup to 3.9e-16 and liquid plus vapour against the injected mass to 8.8e-16 in the spray. Five negative controls held, eleven mutations made their checks fail, no amendment; defaults unchanged (the particle suites of rcfd-particles and rcfd-api, H1, baseline hashes). New State::Evaporated. Open: ADR 0224 Q1 (acceptance), Q2 (case-tree wiring, recommended with F-252), Q3 (two-way exchange of mass, heat and momentum), Q4 (chi-squared product sizes), Q5 (boiling), Q6 (Abramzon-Sirignano), Q7 to Q9.

title: Pressure-interpolation variants for poor meshes
acceptance: Pressure-interpolation variants: the set of variants is named in the ADR before the work; on an incompressible manufactured solution (per-cell momentum source) on the F-208 skewed, warped and stretched meshes at n = 16, 32, 64, each variant's finest-pair L2 order is >= 1.7 for velocity and >= a pressure limit registered in the ADR, and on the near-orthogonal meshes no variant raises the error over the default by more than 1.10x (the F-208 M3 limit); a body-force-weighted variant, if named, cuts the spurious velocity of a quiescent stably stratified Boussinesq box on the skewed mesh by at least 10x against the default, below an absolute bound registered in the ADR. Out of scope: new gradient schemes, limiter changes, a separate warped-face correction (dropped, see the note), compressible-solver interpolation, automatic option selection by mesh quality, case-tree wiring (F-256).
note: Split from F-208 on 2026-10-21 (partials audit). F-208 is done (ADR 0098 M5: stretched-mesh 32 -> 64 order 1.908 for C0/C1/C2), so the earlier remark that F-208 stays partial is obsolete and removed. Size M. REFINED 2026-10-21 (not yet user-approved): The phrase 'each implemented variant' was unbounded, so the ADR must name the set first. F-208's MMS exercises the scalar diffusion gradient, not pressure interpolation, so (A) needs the incompressible MMS harness ADR 0016 D2 said was missing, plus a stratified-box test where body-force weighting matters. (B) must show an error reduction, because ADR 0016 states the existing face correction already is the warped-face treatment and found it raised the error constant 2.1x on the skewed mesh, so 'does not degrade the order' alone is vacuous. (C) uses the usual wiring checks. PROPOSED SPLIT: A (M, SIMPLE kernel work) stays as F-246; C as its own S item covering the existing GradientOptions (it can ship before A); B decided by the user. OPEN QUESTION: is a separate warped-face correction wanted at all, given ADR 0016 D2 treats the corrected face gradient as the warped-face treatment? USER DECISION 2026-10-22: split: case-tree wiring is F-256; the separate warped-face correction (B) is dropped because ADR 0016 D2 already treats the corrected face gradient as the warped-face treatment and found the correction raised the error constant 2.1x on the skewed mesh; reopen only if A shows a warped-mesh residual. PARTIAL (ADR 0193, the registration of F-246, 2026-11-06, branch f246-pressure-interp, not merged): The set named before the work, on the steady simple/simplec kernel: linear (the default), skew_corrected (the Green-Gauss face pressure moved to the face centre with the interpolated cell gradient) and body_force_weighted (the same discretisation applied to the pressure minus a local potential of the body force: in the Green-Gauss face pressures, the wall pressures, the least-squares gradients of the non-orthogonal correction and the body-force part of the face flux). Case key solver.pressure_interpolation, left out of the settings hash at its default, wired under F-256's checks: located errors, tree equals library exactly (0, limit 1e-12), the default unchanged bit for bit. Met: the stably stratified Boussinesq box on the skewed mesh K at n = 16: body_force_weighted cuts the largest spurious cell speed from 1.6e-2 to 3.7e-12 (SIMPLEC with face_flux) and from 4.6e-3 to 1.0e-11 (SIMPLE with one corrector); limits 10x and 1e-6 (1e-8 of the buoyancy velocity 100). skew_corrected keeps the velocity error on the near-orthogonal meshes at 1.000 (G) and 1.0015 (G3) times the default's (limit 1.10). Met on the manufactured flow (orders of the pair (32, 64), limits 1.7 velocity and 1.2 pressure): skewed mesh K, skew_corrected 2.176 / 1.491 and body_force_weighted 2.235 / 1.444; stretched mesh S, body_force_weighted 1.966 / 1.318, skew_corrected 1.735 / 1.756. The n = 64 sequences take about two hours each and are ignored heavy tests run by name. Missed (ignored *_known_miss tests, limits unchanged): the default kernel diverges on F-208's warped mesh W from n = 32 under every set-up tried (relaxation, viscosity, convection scheme, correctors, pseudo-time, face_flux, SIMPLEC); skew_corrected and body_force_weighted diverge there too, so M1 on W is not met; amendment 1 added a milder warp W2 (amplitude 0.07, 45 degrees) as supplementary evidence, on which both variants meet the limits (skew_corrected 1.999 / 1.745, body_force_weighted 1.999 / 1.648); body_force_weighted raises the velocity error on the near-orthogonal meshes 1.342 (G) and 1.150 (G3) times (limit 1.10): it assumes the pressure balances the body force, and the manufactured source does not. Amendment 1 also corrected the stratified-box set-up B-a (SIMPLEC at alpha_p = 1 without correctors diverged for both variants) by adding face_flux. Open (ADR 0193 Q1 to Q9): the key's name, the transient kernel, the rotating-frame sources, the readings of the acceptance, the default, the wiring, further variants, W2 as the warped mesh, and whether the divergence on W reopens the dropped warped-face item. USER DECISION 2026-11-06 (ADR 0193 decision record): stays PARTIAL; W stays the binding warped mesh and W2 is supplementary evidence only (Q8 (a)); amendment 1 and the heavy tests run by hand are accepted as evidence; the divergence on W is the new item F-285 (Q9 (b)), after which M1 on W is run again unchanged; the R2 cases of T1 are redone by the house rule, separately. Q1 to Q7 were not asked and stay open.

title: Dynamic mesh: local remeshing on unstructured tetrahedral meshes
acceptance: Every limit not stated here is registered in the ADR before the run. Local remeshing: the ADR 0090 piston in a closed cylinder on an unstructured tetrahedral mesh, with remeshing instead of layering, keeps p_bar V^gamma within 2e-2 at full compression and after re-expansion, conserves volume, mass, momentum and energy through every remeshing event to 1e-13 relative (conservative remap), triggers at least 5 events, and keeps the minimum cell quality above the ADR threshold. Out of scope: sliding interfaces / AMI (F-250), elastic-analogy smoothing (F-063), six-DOF coupling (F-244), more than one moving layered boundary, non-planar layer surfaces, turbulence or energy in the incompressible moving-mesh path.
note: Split from F-230 on 2026-10-21 (partials audit). Depends on F-063 (partial). Size L. REFINED 2026-10-21 (not yet user-approved): The lead's text bundled six sub-scopes under one unnamed 'closed-form or benchmark result' and asked for incompressible case-tree selectability, which already exists for prescribed and six-DOF motion (ADR 0033 D8, T1-T4); what is missing is wiring of layering and compressible ALE. Each part now has a named case reusing a registered closed form (ADR 0090 piston p V^gamma, ADR 0033 G5 piston flux) plus conservation checks. ADR 0098's Mach 0.2 piston passed with the |u| + c time step but did not deliver the mesh-speed time step; it stays in (C). PROPOSED SPLIT: remeshing = A (L); layering extensions = B (M); compressible ALE boundaries and time step = C (S to M); wiring = D (S, can ship first). OPEN QUESTION: should more than one moving layered boundary (in ADR 0090's not-delivered list) be tracked here or dropped. USER DECISION 2026-10-22: split four ways: B is F-257, C is F-258, D is F-259; more than one moving layered boundary is dropped as out of scope (no use case). This item keeps A (remeshing), size L. DONE (ADR 0215, the registration of F-247, 2026-11-07, branch f247-local-remeshing, not merged): every registered check is met; the acceptance is still the maintainer's (ADR 0215 Q6). Library only. rcfd_mesh::remesh::TetRemesher holds a tetrahedral mesh bounded by axis-aligned planes; move_plane_with_band moves a piston plane and drags the points within 2 h0 behind it in proportion; a cell below mean ratio 0.3 or an edge outside [0.5 h0, 2 h0] triggers an event of local operators (edge split, collapse, edge removal including the 2-2 flip of a wall edge, 2-3 flip, point relocation), each checked to tile the same region; every operator gives the cell totals to the new cells by exact tetrahedron intersection volumes, and remesh::remap carries them through CompressibleSolver::replace_mesh. ADR 0090's piston on the Delaunay tetrahedral mesh M0 (1711 cells): p V^gamma 3.7e-6 at full compression and 9.4e-6 after re-expansion (limit 2e-2); 1806 events (limit 5); volume, mass, momentum and energy through every event within 1.6e-15 (1e-13); smallest mean ratio 0.241 (ADR threshold 0.2); per-step mass 7.6e-15 and volume 5.0e-15; no point below x = 0.35 touched (limit 0.2); raw intersection mismatch 5.1e-14 (1e-11); 55497 steps in 193 s. Negative controls: a largest-source remap changes the mass by 7.9e-7; without remeshing the mean ratio falls below 0.2 at t = 5.2 (T = 16). Unit checks met; four mutations failed their checks, the fifth did not and was replaced by amendment 3 (MU3': Q 0.097). Amendments before the registered runs: 1 (U2 gradual), 2 (band motion, collapse rules, boundary edge removal, from development runs on scratch set-ups). Defaults: new files and one pub mod line; baseline hashes and H1 unedited; no case-schema key. Gate of 6e7ee92: fmt 0, clippy 0, 3150 passed, 0 failed, 889 ignored. Open (ADR 0215 Q1 to Q7): case-tree wiring, the quality measure and threshold, remeshing in the incompressible path, non-planar walls, a higher-order remap, the status, a panic of the existing mesher seen while choosing M0.

title: SIMPLEC robustness: velocity inlet with a forward vent (K > 0) diverges from the first iteration
acceptance: The registered vent test x7_vent_at_fixed_pseudo_dt (pseudo-dt 0.02, u = +-0.5, +-1, +-2; outlet pressure 0.5 K u|u| within 1e-6) passes as a non-ignored test with plain SIMPLEC, without changing the default settings of existing cases (baseline hashes unchanged)
note: Size M. Done with an opt-in key (solver.simplec_boundary_compensation), accepted by the user on 2026-10-22; making the key the default is NOT approved. The default-code X7 test still gives NaN at u = 2, and with the key plain SIMPLEC with a strong vent (K = 10) still fails. Found by wave 39D (ADR 0095): plain SIMPLEC diverges from the first iteration with a velocity inlet and a forward vent when K > 0; X7 gave NaN at u = 2 and is an ignored known miss. User decision 2026-10-21: fix in the next foundations wave with the SIMPLEC seam-compensation defect. WAVE 41B (ADR 0102): DONE with an opt-in key. Root cause (diagnosed by registered switch runs): SIMPLEC added the flux compensation (rAtU - rAU) snGrad(p_old) on internal faces only, so a change of the vent pressure kicked the vent-cell velocity by (rAtU - rAU) times the pressure jump (5.06 m/s in the first plain iteration at u = 1, 1.125 at u = 2 with pseudo-time 0.02). The vent law, which reads that velocity, fed it back with the gain G = 0.5 (rAtU - rAU) (A/V) K |u|. The run diverges when G > 1 (10.1 plain, 1.125 at u = 2, pseudo 0.02), not by Courant number (K = 1 at Courant 2 settles, K = 10 at Courant 1 diverges). Inlet treatment and seams play no role in X7; a face-velocity vent law is not a cure (it diverges through a transverse mode). Fix: solver.simplec_boundary_compensation (default false, bit-identical; steady simplec only, located error otherwise; docs/case-schema.md) adds the compensation on fixed-pressure and periodic boundary faces, so the fixed point equals SIMPLE's (B1 pressure outlet 3.5e-12, B2 periodic seams 4.7e-13 against default differences 4.8e-3 and 2.6e-3; the same key addresses ADR 0084 finding S (seams), opt-in). Acceptance: x7_vent_at_fixed_pseudo_dt (crates/rcfd-api/tests/heat_exchanger.rs, non-ignored) is the registered X7 sweep with the one added line simplec_boundary_compensation = true: worst error 2.93e-12 (limit 1e-6) at all six flows; the default-code x7_vent_at_fixed_pseudo_dt_known_miss stays ignored and still gives NaN at u = 2; baseline hashes unchanged. Reading of the acceptance: 'plain SIMPLEC' = the simplec algorithm with this one opt-in key; the default settings of existing cases are unchanged. Also: X7 without pseudo-time settles with the key (errors <= 6.4e-13). Remains: with the key, plain SIMPLEC with a strong vent (K = 10) still fails through a transverse vent-face mode (F-200 C3 channel non-finite at iteration 2767), pseudo-time needed there; the key is not the default because it changes every converged SIMPLEC result with a pressure boundary or periodic seam; the FAN-01 residual stall is not caused by the missing compensation (ADR 0102 R3, falsified). USER DECISION 2026-10-22: accepted done with the opt-in key solver.simplec_boundary_compensation. Making the key the default is NOT approved (it changes every converged SIMPLEC result with a pressure boundary or seam). Queued: a located diagnostic that suggests the key when a steady SIMPLEC run diverges. WAVE 42A (ADR 0105): the queued diagnostic is delivered. When the steady divergence guard (ADR 0077, unchanged: non-finite values, continuity growth 1e6 over the 50-iteration minimum, speed / pressure runaway) stops a steady SIMPLEC run whose case has a fixed-pressure or periodic boundary face and solver.simplec_boundary_compensation is false, the run-control reason and service error append a hint naming solver.simplec_boundary_compensation = true (only Simulation::steady_divergence_message, read-only; other algorithms and texts unchanged; defaults unchanged). Tests in rcfd-api tests/heat_exchanger.rs: d1 (X7 vent u = 2, pseudo 0.02, no key: diverged at iteration 9, reason names the key; limit 15); d1n (diverging SIMPLE cavity: no hint); d2 (X7 vent u = 0.5 converging, 600 iterations bit-identical with and without querying the message every iteration).

title: Sliding interface (AMI): arbitrary mesh interface between non-conforming moving or rotating zones
acceptance: A rotor-stator case with a sliding interface, the mesh sliding by at least one full cell pitch, conserves mass across the interface to 1e-10 relative per step summed over all interface faces; rigid rotation of a fluid across the interface differs from the same case on a conforming mesh by no more than 1.5 times the conforming-mesh velocity error; a Taylor-Couette torque across the interface is within 2 percent of the closed form; a case without the interface is bit-identical (baseline hashes unchanged)
note: Split from F-063 on 2026-10-21 (user decision after the F-063 audit). Acceptance text proposed by the lead; refine when scheduled. F-114 handles planar interfaces only; F-126 covers frozen-rotor and mixing-plane. Size L. USER DECISION 2026-10-22: acceptance tightened with numeric limits (the 1.5x ratio and 2 percent are fixed here; refine only with the user). ADR 0216 (registration of F-250, 2026-11-07, branch f250-sliding-interface, not merged): PARTIAL, library only. Met: rigid rotation (A2) 5.94e-4 against 1.5 x the static conforming controls (8.90e-4), and the equal-count cell difference 2.36e-4 against 8.63e-4; Taylor-Couette torque (A3) on the rotor wall +1.41 %, on the stator wall -1.34 %, through the interface -0.10 % (limit 2 %); uniform flow held to 9e-15 (2-D) and 4e-15 (3-D); the decaying azimuthal mode at -0.41 % of nu k^2 (closed form); a case without the interface unchanged (no tree change). A1 missed as registered (two non-orthogonal correctors): interface mass 1.51e-10 against 1e-10, the lagged non-orthogonal flux; met with six correctors (amendment 2): 3.0e-15. Other known misses: continuity 1.8e-9 to 1.7e-8 with two correctors (limit 1e-9), and R1b against rotating conforming controls (the static stator wall's pressure condition). title: Strong (implicit) fluid-structure coupling with added-mass stabilisation
acceptance: A spring-mounted piston driving a fluid column at an added-mass to body-mass ratio of at least 1 oscillates at omega = sqrt(k/(M + rho A L0)) within 2 percent, the amplitude at successive same-side turning points never grows (ratio <= 1 + 1e-3) over at least 10 periods, and the explicit coupling of ADR 0033 D7 grows or diverges on the same case (registered before the run); halving dt changes the frequency by <= 0.5 percent
note: Split from F-244 on 2026-10-22 (user decision). Size L. Needed for light structures; not on the first fan path. DONE pending acceptance (ADR 0250, registered 2026-11-12 before the code, merged 2026-11-12): opt-in library function rcfd_fv::fsi::strong_step (new module, nothing calls it; pimple.rs, pimple/moving.rs, sixdof.rs, ale.rs, rcfd-api and the case schema untouched; the loose coupling of ADR 0033 D7 is unchanged and with max_iterations = 1 the strong step equals it bit for bit). Within a time step it iterates on the fluid force and moment held over the body step, each iterate restarting body and flow from t_n, with a fixed or an Aitken relaxation; the Aitken start and the best fixed factor come from an added-mass estimate, 2M/(2M + m_a) (the added-mass term of the body equation written as a relaxation; the half belongs to RK4 with a constant force and a wall velocity taken from the displacement). Derived and measured: the loose loop as built is unstable above a mass ratio of 2, not 1, with a growth of sqrt(ratio/2) per step whatever the time step (flow: stable at 1.5, diverges at 3 and 4; growth 1.39 per step at ratio 4 for T/100 and T/200); the gain of the sub-iteration is 1 + ratio/2 (measured 2.952 at ratio 4), so a fixed factor converges below 4/(2 + ratio). Acceptance case, the spring-mounted piston of ADR 0211 at ratio 4 (M = 0.01, 11.5 periods): omega_m/omega 1.005081 at T/100 (limit 2 %), dt halving 1.7e-5 (limit 0.5 %), successive same-side turning points fall by 7.5 % a period at T/100 and 3.9 % at T/200 and never grow (lag of dt/2 of the end-of-step force), the loose coupling passes 10 X at step 28 (T/100) and 31 (T/200) and ends with the piston through the outlet; 3.0 flow solves per step at a tolerance of 1e-8, never more than 4 (cap 20). Also met: ratio 20 (1.005968, 3.25 solves per step), agreement with the loose coupling at ratio 0.2 (frequency within 2.0e-4, the trajectory difference halves with dt), the restart of an iterate bit-exact, refusals leave flow and body untouched, the existing sixdof, sixdof_coupled, sixdof_flow_f244, ale_flows and ale_gcl suites pass unedited; eight library mutations each failed their tests. Amendment 1 (before any run): the unrelaxed-iteration control was registered with a cap it cannot reach and was replaced by one with cap 10. Not delivered: selecting the coupling from a case file (no key; follow-up item), Newmark with the sub-iteration, a rotating body in a flow. Found, not fixed: the discrete added mass of the column is 1.25 % below rho A L0 at every ratio (the +0.1 % of ADR 0211, +0.5 % here); follow-up item. Open: ADR 0250 Q1 (reword "ratio of at least 1" to 4), Q2 (case key), Q3 (stop or warn at the cap), Q4 (added-mass deficit), Q5, Q6. Follow-ups (recommendation taken on the maintainer's standing instruction of 2026-11-11): F-350 (case key; Q2, Q3), F-351 (the added-mass deficit; Q4).

title: Particle wall film (Nusselt thickness, mass conservation)
acceptance: Wall film: a laminar film fed by impinging parcels on an inclined wall reaches the Nusselt thickness derived in the ADR, delta = (3 mu Gamma / (rho^2 g sin(theta)))^(1/3) with Gamma the mass flow per unit width, within 5 percent at a station away from the feed, at a film Reynolds number inside the laminar range registered in the ADR; film + airborne + escaped parcel mass conserved to 1e-10 relative. Out of scope: comparison with measured data beyond the stated data set, particle reactions, discrete-element coupling.
note: Split from F-245 on 2026-10-22 (user decision). Size M. PARTIAL (ADR 0192, the registration of F-253, 2026-11-05, branch f253-wall-film, not merged): every registered check is met; marking the item done is the maintainer's (ADR 0192 Q1). A thin laminar film lives on the faces of wall patches (rcfd_particles::film; the optional table particles.film with enabled, patches and viscosity, absent from every existing case). A parcel that reaches it is absorbed (state film). The film moves down the wall with the lubrication velocity rho h^2 g_t/(3 mu) by donor-cell fluxes under a Courant limit on the kinematic wave, and drains at open edges. On a 30-degree incline fed by four parcel streams at Re_f = 4 Gamma/mu = 2 (laminar range 0 to 30, long-wave threshold 5.77 at 30 degrees), the station six rows below the feed is within 2.6e-15 of the Nusselt thickness as a window average and 1.7e-11 at 20 s (limit 5 percent); injected = airborne + deposited + escaped + stuck + film + drained to 6.1e-13 (limit 1e-10). The case tree, with gravity tilted instead of the mesh, gives 1.7e-11 and equals the library bit for bit. Runs without the film are unchanged bit for bit (records R1 and R2, made on main before the code). The first run of the tree checks stopped at a set-up defect of case K (frozen flow needs energy.enabled), corrected by amendment 1 before the corrected run; the tests on the registered K stay ignored. Open: gas buoyancy is left out of the film so that its steady state is the roadmap formula (ADR 0192 Q2); gas shear (Q3) and splash or rebound at impact (Q4) are not delivered. USER DECISION 2026-11-06 (ADR 0192 decision record): stays PARTIAL (Q1, not closed yet); gas buoyancy and gas shear are the new item F-292 (Q2, Q3); splash and rebound at the film are the new item F-284, not part of F-254 (Q4).

title: Particle wall interaction: erosion and rough-wall rebound
acceptance: Wall interaction: for a uniform parcel stream hitting a plate at three angles, the reported erosion rate equals the closed-form impact-flux expression of the chosen correlation (constants read from the source) to 1e-10 relative; the rough-wall rebound model's sampled rebound angles match its prescribed distribution (Kolmogorov distance below the 1 percent critical value for the sample size). Out of scope: comparison with measured data beyond the stated data set, particle reactions, discrete-element coupling.
note: Split from F-245 on 2026-10-22 (user decision). Size M. PARTIAL (ADR 0194, the registration of F-254, 2026-11-06, branch f254-wall-interaction, not merged): every registered check is met; marking the item done is the maintainer's (ADR 0194 Q1). Erosion (rcfd_particles::erosion; the optional table particles.erosion with enabled, patches, k, n and density, absent from every existing case) books m K U^n F(alpha) of DNV RP O501 (Revision 4.2-2007, eq. 7.1 to 7.3, constants of Table 7-1 read from the source; K and n are inputs) on each face at every parcel hit, as an observation that never changes a parcel, and reports the rate per face over the tracked time. For three uniform streams on a plate at 15, 35 and 90 degrees the reported rate equals G K U^n F(alpha) to 5.4e-13 (limit 1e-10), in the library and in the case tree. Rough walls (rcfd_particles::rough; the optional table particles.rough_wall with enabled, patches, angle_std and seed) reflect about a virtual wall tilted in the plane of incidence by a Gaussian roughness angle (Sommerfeld 1992 as restated by Tian et al. 2007), with a registered realizability rule (redraw until the parcel meets the virtual wall from the fluid side and rebounds away from the wall). The rebound angles of 20 000 parcels at 10, 40 and 75 degrees match the prescribed distribution with Kolmogorov distances 0.0047, 0.0059 and 0.0058 against the 1 percent critical value 0.0115; the untruncated Gaussian is rejected (0.27). The case tree equals the library bit for bit. Runs without the models are unchanged bit for bit (records R3 and R4, made on main before the code, and R1, R2 of ADR 0192). Open: the shadow-effect distribution of Sommerfeld and Huber (1999) was not read, so the realizability rule stands in for it (ADR 0194 Q2); K and n have no default (Q3); the DNV edition read is a third-party copy of Revision 4.2-2007 (Q4); splash and rebound at the wall film (ADR 0192 Q4) are not delivered (Q5); wall friction and particle rotation are not modelled (Q6). USER DECISION 2026-11-06 (ADR 0194 decision record): stays PARTIAL (Q1, not closed yet); named steel presets for K, n and the target density (Q3, against the recommendation), made separately, which must say that the Table 7-2 values come from a third-party copy of DNV RP O501 Revision 4.2-2007 not checked against the maintainer's edition; Q2 (the Sommerfeld and Huber 1999 paper) and Q4 (the DNV edition) wait for the maintainer; splash and rebound at the film are the new item F-284 (Q5); Q6 was not asked.

title: Particle dispersion from turbulence-model fields and particle reactions
acceptance: Particle dispersion driven by turbulence-model fields reproduces the analytic dispersion growth of a passive cloud in homogeneous turbulence (Taylor result, closed form derived in the ADR) within 5 percent, and a particle surface reaction conserves the mass of each species to 1e-10 relative
note: Split from F-245 on 2026-10-22 (user decision): these were in F-128's not-delivered list and tracked nowhere. Acceptance text proposed by the lead; refine when scheduled. Size L. PARTIAL (ADR 0208, the registration of F-255, 2026-11-07, branch f255-particle-dispersion, not merged): every registered check is met, the surface reaction in the library only; marking the item done is the maintainer's (ADR 0208 Q1). Dispersion: the opt-in table `particles.dispersion_from_model` (`enabled`; hash_omit_default, absent from every existing case; amendment 2 moved it out of `particles` because H1 of `case_hashes_w48u` compares the written text) makes the random walk of ADR 0057 take k and epsilon per cell from `k_epsilon` (its epsilon) or `k_omega_sst` (epsilon = 0.09 k omega), once for steady and frozen tracking and before every tracking step of a transient run (the old time level with two-way coupling); library `Tracker::set_dispersion_fields`. The closed form for a Stokes parcel released at rest (`rcfd_particles::drw_msd`, Taylor's `taylor_msd` for tau -> 0) is derived in the ADR and matches the moment equations of the walk to 7.6e-12. A cloud of 20 000 tracer parcels (tau = 1e-3 T_L) on the k-epsilon and SST models' homogeneous fields is within 0.04 to 0.79 percent of both forms at 0.25, 1, 4 and 10 T_L (limit 5 percent), an inertial cloud (tau = T_L) within 1.1 percent; the tree equals the library bit for bit on non-uniform fields, and the transient and two-way refreshes give the fields of the right time level bit for bit. Reaction (`rcfd_particles::reaction`, `Tracker::set_reaction`): a first-order kinetic surface reaction with an inert residue (a choice of the ADR, Q7), linear shrinkage to 1.7e-14, the mass of the solid and of each gas species measured on the parcel side and on the carrier side within 2.0e-14 at every step of a run with wall hits (limit 1e-10). Runs without the new keys and calls are unchanged bit for bit (records R8, R9, R1 to R7, H1, baseline hashes). Ten mutations made their checks fail; two set-up defects of checks and the place of the key were corrected by amendments 1 to 3 before the corrected runs. Open (ADR 0208 Q1 to Q10): the key; the models (RSM, SA, LES refused); C_mu of the eddy length; the homogeneous check on the model's initial state; the zero eddy held forever; the reaction law, its case keys, parcels that burn out completely and the molar masses.

title: Dynamic mesh: prism layering and incompressible layering
