title: Consistent correctors: fold the flags into one key and extend the refused combinations
acceptance: The optional table carries all consistent-corrector flags in one place with a located refusal for each unsupported combination; defaults bit-identical.
note: PARTIAL (ADR 0258, 2026-11-12), the library half. Delivered: one settings value `ConsistentCorrectors` (enabled, periodic, body_force, non_orthogonal, component_diagonal, face_jump) as `PimpleSettings::consistent`, read together with the three older fields, which are kept (`consistent_flags`, `set_consistent`); one validation `ConsistentCorrectors::conflicts` / `validate` returning a located `ConsistentRefusal` (flag, other setting, reason) for each of 13 unsupported combinations, used by the solver before any work and per outer iteration, every earlier refusal kept with its stage and its sentence and the located part appended (R1 of ADR 0214 and R2 of ADR 0223 pass unedited); three combinations extended on fixed meshes without periodic faces, each with a steady identity and a transient check: non-orthogonal correctors (the non-orthogonal part of the compensation as ADR 0050, with the fixed-pressure boundary part in the pressure equation only; S1N 3.7e-12 U0 and 5.1e-11 of the pressure range against 1e-10), the component diagonal (no new term; S1D 3.8e-12, 3.2e-11) and face jumps (S1J and from the hook 2.5e-12, 2.5e-11), all together with a body force (S1X 3.0e-12, 4.2e-11); the option differs from the default in a start-up transient by 2.4e-5, 7.9e-5 and 5.6e-6 U0 at dt 0.001, falling by 3.3 to 5.9 per halving; eight mutations each fail a test. Defaults bit-identical (the rcfd-fv transient files, baseline_hashes, case_hashes_w48u, the F-301 case tests). Missing (why partial): the case table still has only `enabled` (schema golden and docs/case-schema.md: the maintainer's), sim.rs still writes its own located errors instead of calling `conflicts`, overset.rs reads the older field. Still refused: the new flags with periodic faces or on a moving mesh (F-321), non-orthogonal correctors with pressure gradient options, the fractional step. Follow-ups: F-366 (the case table; needs the maintainer for the schema golden), F-367 (periodic faces).

title: Droplet models: feedback to the carrier and use with the exchange record
acceptance: Vapour mass, heat and momentum from evaporating and breaking-up parcels are returned to the gas, conserved to 1e-10 relative; the evaporation and breakup models may be used with the particle exchange record.
note: From ADR 0224 question 3, recommendation taken: a separate item before F-252. DONE (ADR 0230, the registration of F-323, 2026-11-12, merged 2026-11-12): every registered check is met in the library (rcfd-particles, no case key); the acceptance is still the maintainer's. `Tracker::enable_droplet_exchange()` starts the exchange record of ADR 0057 with the droplet terms, and `advance` then accepts evaporation and breakup (`enable_coupling()` is unchanged and still refuses them). Per sub-step the carrier receives in the start cell the drag with the mass of the start, the heat `m0 c_l (T1 - T0) + dm L_v`, and the vapour `dm` with its momentum `dm v1`, kinetic energy and enthalpy `dm (c_l T1 + L_v)`; gravity, wall and breakup terms are booked so that the balances close; `Coupling::droplet_sources` gives the per-cell mass, momentum and energy sources. Mass, momentum and energy balances at every step: single droplets to 6.9e-16, the spray of ADR 0224 (160 parcels, evaporation and TAB breakup, 300 steps) to 8.8e-16, 2.7e-15 and 1.5e-15 (limit 1e-10); a droplet at its wet bulb draws `L_v` times its mass from the gas to 5.3e-16; the heat of a sub-step is first-order consistent with the model's `Q` (ratio 1.9996); a closed box whose carrier receives the vapour and the heat stops evaporating within 3e-12 K of the adiabatic saturation temperature (limit 1e-6 K). Three negative controls held, seven mutations made their checks fail, no amendment; the record is an observation (fingerprints equal) and the record of ADR 0057 is unchanged bit for bit (the particle suites of rcfd-particles and rcfd-api, H1, baseline hashes). Not in it: no flow solver of rcfd consumes the record; the normal momentum of a TAB breakup is booked as a residual without a carrier counterpart (the source conserves it on the average; 1.45e-3 of the drag impulse in the spray). Open: ADR 0230 Q1 (one method or two), Q2 (breakup momentum), Q3 (enthalpy datum, constant latent heat), Q5 (where the solver wiring goes). Case-tree wiring of the transient two-way path (optional particles.evaporation and particles.breakup tables) done by F-326 (ADR 0348, 2026-11-12); the comparison with data stays with F-252. Q5: the recommendation (a separate item) taken on the maintainer's standing instruction of 2026-11-11: F-326.

title: Tet mesher: output validity check inside tetrahedralize
acceptance: tetrahedralize checks its output (every cell positive, volume equal to the enclosed volume) and returns a located error instead of an overlapping Ok; the F-306 sweep inputs still give identical meshes.
note: From ADR 0228 question 3, recommendation taken: a small follow-up item. DONE (ADR 0231, the registration of F-324, 2026-11-12, merged 2026-11-12): every registered check is met after amendment 2 (a set-up defect of two control tests, corrected before the corrected run); the acceptance is still the maintainer's (ADR 0231 Q1). tetrahedralize ends with TetMesh::check_output: every cell positive by the exact orient3d, and the cell volumes equal to the volume enclosed by the output surface within a rigorous rounding bound (Shewchuk's orient3d error bound per simplex, Neumaier summation; about 1e-14 of the volume), else a located Error::Mesh naming the cell, or the first face shared by more than two cells, with two cells on one side, or free but not on the surface. It reads the mesh only: the 111 + 7 fold-free F-306 fingerprints, the R outputs and the existing suites are unchanged; with the F-306 fold put back (MU1) the five overlapping Ok outputs of main become located errors and no overlapping Ok remains. Cost: below 0.1 percent of the mesher's time (F12, F14). Four registered mutations failed their checks. Open: ADR 0231 Q2 (face pairing on every run; the F-247 remesher's outputs), Q3 (the neighbour-link panics). Q2: the recommendation (the remesher follow-up) taken on the maintainer's standing instruction of 2026-11-11: F-327.

title: Tet mesher: Linux fingerprint records for the F-306 checks
acceptance: Fingerprints for the 118 fold-free inputs of the F-306 sweep are recorded on Linux by the ADR 0137 procedure at the next Linux gate, and the F-306 N1 checks compare them.
note: From ADR 0228 question 6, recommendation taken. Needs a Linux gate run.

title: Droplet feedback in the transient two-way path
acceptance: With the droplet exchange on, the transient two-way particle path gives the carrier the vapour mass (a species source), the momentum and the energy sources of Coupling::droplet_sources, and the tracker reads the carrier temperature and vapour fraction of the step; gas plus liquid mass, momentum and energy of a closed case are conserved to 1e-10 relative per step; optional particles.evaporation and particles.breakup tables (hash-omitted when absent); a case without them is bit-identical.
note: From ADR 0230 question 5, recommendation taken on the maintainer's standing instruction of 2026-11-11 (a separate item, checked by conservation without a data set). DONE (ADR 0348, 2026-11-12; registered before the code, three amendments, two of them after runs that stopped at step 1 on the relative measures before the first injection, no limit changed): optional tables [particles.evaporation] (the film-model data of ADR 0224 and the transported species that receives the vapour) and [particles.breakup] (TAB constants), absent from every case that does not write them; transient two-way only (piso, pimple; evaporation also needs heat_transfer). The tracker records with enable_droplet_exchange and reads T and the vapour fraction of the old time level (bit for bit); over each flow step the carrier receives the mass of Coupling::droplet_sources as the species source, its momentum as the body acceleration, and of its energy the sensible part energy_heat + vapour_enthalpy - vapour_mass (c_l T + L_v) in the temperature equation, the mechanical part and the enthalpy of the arrived vapour kept in a ledger. A closed adiabatic box (16 cells, 10 parcels breaking up and evaporating 98.6 percent of their mass) conserves gas plus liquid mass, momentum and energy at every step to 1.8e-15, 5.8e-16 and 6.7e-13 of the largest term (limit 1e-10), with pimple too (5.8e-13); three negative controls held, six mutations caught. A case without the tables or with them disabled is bit-identical (baseline hashes, case_hashes_w48u, the particle suites). Not in it: the steady path, a variable-density carrier (the vapour is not a continuity source), the breakup's normal momentum (a residual, ADR 0230 D5). Open: ADR 0348 Q1 to Q4. STATUS recorded PARTIAL by the lead: two registered measures (the per-step identities before the first parcel) stopped at step 1 on set-up defects and passed only after amendments 2 and 3, written after those runs (no limit changed; the stopped tests kept as *_setup_defect records); done is the maintainer's call.

title: F-247 remesher: run the tet output check on its outputs
acceptance: TetRemesher's output meshes pass TetMesh::check_output after every remeshing step, or the step returns its located error; the remesh_f247 hashes stay unchanged.
note: From ADR 0231 question 2, recommendation taken on the maintainer's standing instruction of 2026-11-11. DONE (ADR 0236, the registration of F-327, 2026-11-12, merged 2026-11-12): every registered check is met at the first run; the acceptance is still the maintainer's (ADR 0236 Q1). TetRemesher::event (and remesh) ends every event that applied an operator with a step check before committing: TetMesh::check_output on the output with the surface of its free faces (the remesher has no stored surface; its boundary is re-triangulated), every free face exactly on its plane, and the cell volume equal to that of the step's input within a rigorous bound (an event does not change the region); a failure returns a located Error::Mesh ("remesh output check: ...", naming the cell, the face or the volumes, and the event's operators and box) and leaves the mesh as it was. The check only reads: M0's hash aaf8f4c36f6446e4 and every P-T number of ADR 0215 are unchanged, and all 1806 P-T events and the 572 events of a geometric piston pass. A duplicated cell, a negative cell, a missing cell and a valid tiling of a changed region are each rejected and located. Cost: 10.3 percent of an event. Four registered mutations failed their checks. Library only; RemeshChange gains the field check. Open: ADR 0236 Q2 (checking new() and motions), Q6 (V2 and V3 not decisive in the piston).

title: Compressible impedance boundary, sponge layer and mass-spring-damper wall: case-schema wiring
acceptance: `compressible_bc = "impedance"` with `impedance_value` runs the ADR 0233 tube from a case file with R within 1e-2 of the closed form for z/(rho c) = 1/3, 1, 3; located validate errors for a negative impedance and a non-positive pressure; every existing case file's settings hash and written text unchanged after the registered normalisation of the new key at its default. Sponge layer (ADR 0237): A case file selects a sponge layer in front of a boundary patch (thickness, form, target reflection); the ADR 0237 tube check runs from a case file with a reflection below 1 percent; located validate errors for a non-positive thickness, a reflection outside (0, 1) and the matched form with a moving reference; every existing case file's settings hash and written text unchanged after the registered normalisation of the new keys at their defaults. max_dt takes the sponge rate into account. Mass-spring-damper wall (ADR 0243): a case file selects the wall on a patch (mass, stiffness, damping); the M2 check of ADR 0243 runs from a case file within 2 percent in magnitude and phase; one oblique angle is checked against its closed form; a wall together with a sponge layer runs (the two step paths merged).
note: From ADR 0233 question 1, recommendation taken on the maintainer's standing instruction of 2026-11-11. NEEDS THE USER before merge: the new key needs an edit of the registered hash test case_hashes_w48u.rs.

title: Sponge layer for the compressible solver
acceptance: A plane pulse leaving through a sponge layer at 0, 30, 45 and 60 degrees reflects less than 1 percent; a case without a sponge is bit-identical.
note: From ADR 0233 question 4. The job of 2026-11-12 (ADR 0237). The acceptance text is MET IN THE LIBRARY, not from a case file. Built: an opt-in sponge layer of the compressible solver (rcfd-fv sponge.rs, `CompressibleSolver::set_sponge`), in two forms: `Plain` (every conserved variable relaxes to a reference state) and `Matched` (a perfectly matched layer of linear acoustics about a state at rest: mass, energy and normal momentum relax, the tangential momentum is forced through one scalar of memory per cell); polynomial profile, peak rate from the wanted two-way attenuation (`rate_max_for_reflection`). The registration showed beforehand that the plain form cannot reach 1 percent at 45 and 60 degrees in a practical thickness (175 pulse widths at 60 degrees), so the acceptance is met by the matched form. Measured (limit 1 percent, layer of 40 cells, largest difference to a run on an extended grid against the incident peak): normal incidence 9.2e-7 in front of the Thompson boundary and 1.1e-6 in front of a rigid wall; one isolated plane pulse 2.4e-5 at 30 degrees and 1.4e-4 at 45 degrees; pulse trains in a rigid duct 1.2e-4, 2.8e-4, 1.2e-3 at 30, 45, 60 degrees (the Thompson boundary alone 0.081, 0.196, 0.372; the plain form at 45 degrees 0.150). Without a sponge the solver is bit-identical (the F-258 bit records and the ADR 0233 tests pass unedited; a set-and-cleared sponge and a zero-rate sponge give the same bits). Six mutations caught. One amendment: the first oblique set-up (a wave train started inside the layer with zero memory) measured 3.8e-2, 6.2e-2, 8.7e-2 and was diagnosed as a defective set-up before the corrected runs; its tests are kept as ignored records. Not done: case-schema wiring (a new key needs an approved edit of a registered hash test; this is why the status is partial). Limits: the matched form is one planar layer with a reference at rest, does not damp waves along the layer (a transient inside the layer leaves transverse standing waves in a rigid duct, the 4 to 9 percent of the first set-up) and has a memory without decay; the plain form is quiet only near normal incidence; 60 degrees is checked with pulse trains, not with an isolated pulse; explicit source (`rate dt` well below 2.5, `max_dt` does not know it); not on moving meshes; Cartesian grids, gas at rest. Open questions in ADR 0237 addendum 1 (wiring, an isolated pulse at 60 degrees, memory decay and damping along the layer, `max_dt`, moving meshes). Follow-ups (recommendation taken on the maintainer's standing instruction of 2026-11-11): the wiring goes with F-330; F-340 (memory decay, damping along the layer, corners); F-341 (moving meshes).

title: Frequency-dependent wall impedance (time-domain model)
acceptance: The reflection coefficient of a mass-spring-damper wall matches the closed form in magnitude and phase within 2 percent at three frequencies around the resonance.
note: From ADR 0233, proposed follow-up, taken on the maintainer's standing instruction of 2026-11-11. The job of 2026-11-12 (ADR 0243): the acceptance text is MET IN THE LIBRARY, not from a case file. Built: `MsdWall { p, r, m, k }` (rcfd-fv compressible_bc.rs; `CompressibleSolver::set_msd_wall`, `msd_wall_state`, `set_msd_wall_state`, `msd_dt_limit`), a locally reacting mass-spring-damper wall with the impedance Z(omega) = r + i(omega m - k/omega): displacement and velocity per face, advanced with the solver's Runge-Kutta stages; the face keeps the outgoing Riemann invariant of ADR 0233 and takes the wall velocity; m = 0 is the algebraic form and m = k = 0 is `CompBc::Impedance` bit for bit; the wall's step limit 0.8 min(2m/(r + rho c), (r + rho c)/k) is part of `max_dt` and a larger step is refused. Registered checks, all met at the first run, no amendment: a tone at 0.8, 1 and 1.25 times the resonance frequency, complex reflection coefficient by a least-squares split into incident and reflected wave at 400 probes: magnitude within 2.9e-4 (limit 2e-2), phase within 2.4e-4 rad (limit 1.93e-2 rad, the strictest reading of 2 percent) of (Z - rho c)/(Z + rho c) = 0.797 at -55.3 degrees, 1/3 at 180 degrees, 0.797 at +55.3 degrees; the same measurement on walls with a known real reflection (impedance rho c/2 and rigid) within 1.3e-4 and 5e-5 rad; a wall without damper reflects with magnitude 1 within 2.8e-3; free decay of the wall with the radiation damping rho c within 1.2e-6; a light mass and a stiff spring at a third and a sixth of the CFL step stable and within 4.3e-5 of their limits; 1400 steps bit-identical with the impedance wall at m = k = 0; a cleared wall and the existing compressible tests (F-258 bit records, ADR 0233, ADR 0237) bit-identical and unedited. Eight mutations caught. Not done: case-schema wiring (a new key needs an approved edit of case_hashes_w48u.rs; this is why the status is partial). Limits: one degree of freedom per face, no coupling between faces, no multi-pole fit of a measured impedance; the mesh face does not move (transpiration velocity; mass crosses the face and returns); normal incidence only checked; not together with a sponge, not on moving meshes; gas at rest, Cartesian grids, verification against closed forms only. The wiring (with one oblique angle and the wall together with a sponge, ADR 0243 questions 1 to 3, recommendations taken on the maintainer's standing instruction of 2026-11-11) goes with F-330.

title: Acoustic wave-equation solver and modal export
acceptance: A duct mode propagates with the closed-form axial wavenumber within 1 percent; a sponge layer ends the duct with less than 1 percent reflection; the modal amplitudes of a synthetic field are exported and recovered within 1 percent.
note: DONE pending acceptance, merged 2026-11-12. ADR 0351, 2026-11-12. The acceptance text is MET IN THE LIBRARY, not from a case file. Built: rcfd-fv `acoustic_wave.rs` (`AcousticWaveSolver`), the linear acoustic equations about a medium at rest on any FV mesh: exact linear Riemann flux, unlimited least-squares reconstruction, SSP-RK3; boundaries `Wall`, `Open` (characteristic), `Driven` (a ghost state for an entering wave); sponge `WaveSponge` plain or matched (the ADR 0237 layer in the linear unknowns) on `SpongeLayer`. rcfd-post `duct_modes.rs`: hard-walled rectangular and circular duct modes (Bessel functions and zeros of J' computed), `axial_wavenumber`, `HarmonicDft`, weighted least-squares section fit, axial split into the two directions (closed-form or fitted kz), modal power, the `rcfd-duct-modes` v1 JSON export with located read errors. Registered checks, all met at the first run, no amendment: a 0.12 m channel, 32 cells across, mode 1 at cos theta = 0.8 (2361 Hz): axial wavenumber 1.86e-3 below the closed form sqrt(k^2 - k_mn^2) (limit 1e-2; a Fourier analysis of the scheme predicted -1.854e-3), loss 2.3e-3 per wavelength (limit 1e-2); a 40-cell matched layer before a rigid end reflects 9.0e-5 (limit 1e-2; 7.9e-5 on a sheared mesh); a plain layer 9.8e-7 of the plane wave; the open end 0.109 against 1/9; the rigid end without a layer 1.003; a cut-off mode decays 1.7e-3 off the closed form; a synthetic rectangular field (five modes both ways and a cut-off one) through DFT, fit, split and JSON recovered within 4e-15 and a circular section with two truncated modes within 1.3e-4 (limit 1e-2). Eight mutations caught. Limits: medium at rest, linear, no impedance wall, not run inside a CFD run (the source is a driven boundary, which can be built from a sampled rcfd-surface-series section under F-452, ADR 0372, 2026-11-12); the solver was checked in two-dimensional channels here; circular ducts on an O-grid under F-453 (ADR 0366, 2026-11-12); one planar layer; no case key or CLI (ADR 0351 question 1).

title: SV202's fuller text: what the solvers do with a case without boundary conditions

title: Overset: the first-order error term of the calculated component cells
acceptance: Set-up RL of ADR 0232 (component at rest, fringe phase locked) on levels 1 to 4: the root mean square of the error of the calculated component cells converges at order 1.7 or more between successive levels, or the ADR names the source of the first-order term (coefficient 1.0e-4) with a number.
note: From ADR 0232 question 3, recommendation taken on the maintainer's standing instruction of 2026-11-11. ADR 0246 (registration of F-334, 2026-11-12, merged 2026-11-12): PARTIAL, a diagnosis, tests only, no library change. The order check is missed: RL on levels 1 to 4 gives 1.549e-4, 6.39e-5, 3.98e-5, 2.49e-5 in the root mean square of the calculated component cells, orders 1.277, 1.166, 1.626 (limit 1.7); the fit of ADR 0232 predicted 2.86e-5 at level 4. The source is named: the truncation of the linear donor interpolation. With stencils exact for biquadratic fields on both fringes (nine cells, test code) the error is 3.24e-4, 8.55e-5, 3.90e-5, 2.23e-5, orders 1.922, 1.935, 1.950, and equals the error of the background alone. The error with the library stencils is the sum of that part and of the response to the truncation, which is 1.35 to 1.90 times larger, opposed to it (cosine -0.96 to -0.88) and converges at 1.693, 1.588, 1.800; they cancel to 88 to 96 percent, so the library stencils give the smaller error at levels 1 and 2 and the lower order. The coefficient 1.0e-4 is the increment per level of that response times L^2 (1.04e-4, 0.98e-4, then 0.38e-4). Its part from the background fringe is of first order on levels 1 to 3 (4.9e-5, 2.2e-5, 1.41e-5: 1.153, 1.093) and still growing at t = 0.5; the part from the component fringe converges at 1.782, 1.698. Ruled out with numbers: a time error, the single-mesh solution, the outer boundary of the component, the reference cell, the interpolated pressure and the convection (the error is linear in the amplitude to 0.07 percent), a mass defect, the flux at the fringe faces, the transient Rhie-Chow term; with coincident meshes the coupling gives the background alone to 7e-9. Traced by ADR 0340 (F-349): the normal velocity of a fringe cell is imposed on the calculated cells through a resistance proportional to nu / h (a flux defect held by a pressure jump dJ = -(16 nu / 3 h) D), so the response per unit of truncation grows with the refinement; the truncation of the background fringe of RL also alternates between odd and even levels. Controls held, four mutations caught. Follow-ups (ADR 0246 questions 2 and 4, recommendations taken on the maintainer's standing instruction of 2026-11-11): F-336 with RL added to its acceptance, and F-349 on the response to the background fringe.

title: Overset: outer iterations on the overset path
acceptance: OversetSolver accepts n_outer above 1 as an opt-in (defaults bit-identical, Q0 of ADR 0219 still bit for bit); with three outer iterations the time error of TG_2 at dt 0.0025 (max abs(d_200) of ADR 0232, 4.49e-4) falls below 1.2e-4 and T2 at level 2 of ADR 0219 holds at the registered step, or the ADR names why not with a number.
note: From ADR 0232 question 4, recommendation taken on the maintainer's standing instruction of 2026-11-11. ADR 0238 (registration of F-335, 2026-11-12, merged 2026-11-12): PARTIAL as recorded by the lead: the registered rule reads done through the acceptance's "or names why not" clause (one acceptance number missed, its cause named); done is left to the maintainer (ADR 0238 Q1). Built: OversetSolver::set_outer_iterations(n_outer, alpha_u, alpha_p), an opt-in of the solver (OversetSolver::new still refuses n_outer above 1, so no existing test is edited); every outer iteration repeats the PISO pass on the kinds, donors and weights of the new pose with the convecting flux and pressure of the pass before it, the pressure system of both meshes rebuilt per pass, under-relaxation as the library. Defaults bit for bit: Q0 of ADR 0219 (hash af2c9e6bd3e5596d), three records of overset runs taken before the change (U, TG_1, TR), the existing overset suites unedited; with every cell calculated three outer iterations equal the library's ALE step bit for bit, with and without relaxation; a uniform flow stays uniform to 1.0e-14. Met (acceptance): T2 at level 2 of ADR 0219 holds at the registered step with three outer iterations, 1.862 against 2 (3.31 with one). Missed (acceptance): the time error of TG_2 at dt 0.0025, max abs(d_200), falls from 4.49e-4 to 1.69e-4, not below 1.2e-4. Named with numbers: the rest is converged in the outer iterations (1.69e-4 with five), first order in the step (ratio 3.00) and grows with the speed as the second derivative along the cell paths (3.97 for a factor two): the truncation of the implicit Euler scheme on the moving cells, which outer iterations do not remove; the lagged flux was 0.62 of the time error on the coupled meshes, not the 0.85 of the single mesh of ADR 0232. Four mutations caught. Cost: 2.6 times the wall time on TG_2. Not delivered: the case-tree wiring; a second-order time scheme on the overset path (follow-up). Follow-up (ADR 0238 questions 3 and 4, recommendation taken on the maintainer's standing instruction of 2026-11-11): F-338.

title: Overset: donor interpolation of higher order
acceptance: An opt-in donor interpolation that reproduces quadratic fields; with it the largest error over the calculated and fringe cells of TG_L converges at order 1.7 or more on levels 1 to 3 with dt proportional to h^2, the root mean square of the error of the calculated component cells of RL of ADR 0232 converges at order 1.7 or more on levels 1 to 4 (ADR 0246 TQ: 1.922, 1.935, 1.950 with test-supplied stencils), the uniform-flow check U1 of ADR 0219 holds, and the default stencils and results are bit-identical.
note: From ADR 0232 question 5, recommendation taken on the maintainer's standing instruction of 2026-11-11. ADR 0251 (registration of F-336, 2026-11-12, merged 2026-11-12): DONE pending acceptance. Built: an opt-in of rcfd_mesh::overset, Overset::set_donor_interpolation(DonorInterpolation::Quadratic): the stencil of a fringe cell is the donor and the calculated cells that share a point with it (9 on quadrilaterals, 27 on hexahedra; a fringe or hole cell is never a donor), with the weights of the weighted least-squares quadratic (the minimum of sum w^2/omega under the reproduction of the 6 monomials in 2-D, 10 in 3-D, by a pivoted Householder QR). The weights sum to one, can be negative (smallest -0.067, sum of absolute values 1.40 on a whole block) and are not clipped; a stencil with fewer cells than monomials, of deficient rank or with a sum of absolute values above 4 keeps the linear stencil and is listed (Connectivity::fallbacks, OversetInfo::n_fallback), and a step whose interpolated rAU is not positive is refused. Met: quadratics are reproduced to 1e-15 on Cartesian, distorted, O-grid and sheared 3-D donor meshes; the truncation converges at 3.00; TG_L with dt proportional to h^2 converges at 1.993 and 2.000 on levels 1 to 3 (largest error 7.68e-4, 1.93e-4, 8.58e-5, now in a background cell at the domain boundary; 1.0785e-3, 3.514e-4, 1.712e-4 with the linear stencils); the calculated component cells of RL converge at 1.916, 1.924, 1.952 on levels 1 to 4 (3.20e-4, 8.48e-5, 3.89e-5, 2.22e-5); the uniform flow holds to 1.1e-14; coincident meshes give the background alone to 6e-12; no fallback and no unconverged solve on the registered set-ups; without the opt-in the stencils are those of ADR 0219 bit for bit, Q0 and the records R2 hold. Said plainly: on the two coarsest levels of RL the calculated component cells have 2.07 and 1.33 times the error of the linear stencils (the cancellation of ADR 0246), 0.98 and 0.89 at levels 3 and 4. Limits: a donor next to a wall or to its own fringe ring falls back to the linear stencil; no flow run of the cylinder case or in 3-D with the opt-in. Six mutations caught. Found on the way: the donor search of F-134 finds no donor in cells with non-planar faces. Open for the maintainer: whether the opt-in should become the default (ADR 0251 Q1). Follow-ups (ADR 0251 questions 2 and 5, recommendation taken on the maintainer's standing instruction of 2026-11-11): F-352, F-353. Open: question 1 (the quadratic interpolation as the default changes a default). no flow run in 3-D with the opt-in; the cylinder case TR with it is F-353 (ADR 0259: acceptance met, no fallback, mean drag error 3.42e-3 against 3.21e-3 of the linear stencils, recommendation against the default)

title: Immersed solid: second-order force and moment
acceptance: The torque on the immersed rotating cylinder of circular Couette flow (the CC set-up of ADR 0218, second-order forcing) reaches an observed order of 1.5 between N 48 and 96, and the DFG 2D-1 drag and lift on M2 are within 1 percent and 3 percent of the FeatFlow values.
note: DONE in the library (ADR 0239, 2026-11-12), pending acceptance. From ADR 0234 question 5. Diagnosis by measurement (five hypotheses registered before any code): the force of the forcing was never first order (it is the momentum balance of the forced cells, its error that of the velocity field); the moment was, because `force_moment` applies the modification term of a first fluid cell at the surface crossing and not at the centre of its cell (1.49 and 0.72 percent of the torque at N 48 and 96); the one-sided wall difference, the staircase face pressure, the quadrature at the crossings (order 1.50) and the momentum of the mass-source cells were measured and ruled out. Delivered: rcfd-fv immersed.rs, `ImmersedForcing::force_moment_second_order` (opt-in; `force_moment` unchanged and bit-identical, hashes checked): the same force, and the moment with every term at the centre of its cell, which is the angular-momentum balance of the forced cells, that is the moment of the full traction and momentum flux on the regular fluid faces around them (derived in the ADR; checked against that sum to 1.5e-6 of the torque). Measured (limits registered before the code): circular Couette torque error 0.396, 0.107, 0.027, 0.0069 percent at N 24, 48, 96, 192, observed order 1.98 between 48 and 96 (limit 1.5; 1.96 from 96 to 192) against 1.11 of `force_moment`; DFG 2D-1 on M2 C_D -0.306 %, C_L +2.534 % (limits 1 % and 3 %; the force is that of `force_moment`, unchanged); six mutations caught. Not included: the new evaluation as the default of `force_moment` (open, a change of a default); unsteady flow (the momentum of the forced cells); any caller outside the tests, a case key; non-orthogonal meshes; the limits of F-219 and F-309. Follow-up (ADR 0239 Q3, recommendation taken on the maintainer's standing instruction of 2026-11-11): F-346. Open: Q1 (the cell arms as the moment of force_moment changes a default).

title: Overset: a second-order time scheme on the overset path (BDF2, opt-in)
acceptance: OversetSolver accepts BDF2 as an opt-in (defaults bit-identical, Q0 of ADR 0219 and the records R2 of ADR 0238 still bit for bit); with it and three outer iterations max abs(d_200) of TG_2 at dt 0.0025 (1.69e-4 in ADR 0238) falls below 1.2e-4 and its ratio to max abs(d_400) is at least 4 (second order gives 5), and T1c of ADR 0219 is run with it as a new check against its limit 1.7, or the ADR names why not with a number.
note: From ADR 0238 questions 3 and 4, recommendation taken on the maintainer's standing instruction of 2026-11-11. ADR 0241 (registration of F-338, 2026-11-12, merged 2026-11-12): PARTIAL, one of three acceptance numbers met. Built: OversetSolver::set_time_scheme(Bdf2), an opt-in of the solver (OversetSolver::new still refuses BDF2, so no existing test is edited): the three-level backward difference of V u on the moving cells, the mesh flux (c0 W - c2 W_old) / dt of the swept volumes of the last two steps (the geometric conservation law of the three-level scheme), the first step an implicit Euler step, one implicit Euler row for a cell that was a hole two steps back, the first outer iteration extrapolated as the library does; only crates/rcfd-fv/src/overset.rs changed. Defaults bit for bit: Q0 of ADR 0219 (hash af2c9e6bd3e5596d), the records R2 of ADR 0238, the existing overset suites unedited. With every cell calculated on a mesh at rest the step equals the library's BDF2 step bit for bit; the library has no BDF2 on a moving mesh, so the moving terms are checked by a uniform flow on a deforming mesh (3e-15) and through a moving, turning component (1.4e-14). Met (acceptance): max abs(d_200) of TG_2 at dt 0.0025 with three outer iterations falls from 1.69e-4 to 2.1e-5 (limit 1.2e-4). Missed (acceptance): its ratio to max abs(d_400) is 2.46 (limit 4): located, not explained: the library's own BDF2 step on a single mesh at rest leaves 5.1e-6 with the ratio 2.30, independent of the start, the correctors and the outer iterations; the five times larger remainder on the coupled meshes is not that term (ADR 0245: with the at-rest term removed by an opt-in it is 2.06e-5 at a ratio of 2.45; it is made by the motion of the component through the coupling). Missed (acceptance): T1c of ADR 0219 with BDF2 is 1.664 (limit 1.7): with BDF2 the error of both levels is free of time error (0.2 and 0.3 percent between 200 and 800 steps), so this is the spatial order of the pointwise maximum diagnosed by ADR 0232; the 1.80 observed in ADR 0238 was time error at level 1. Two set-up checks were defective and corrected by amendments; six mutations caught. Not delivered: the case-tree wiring. BDF2 for the library's moving-mesh step and the three-level follow conditions of a moving wall came with F-345 (ADR 0379; prepare takes them when BDF2 is on, and the BDF2 overset step with every cell calculated equals the library's bit for bit). Follow-ups (ADR 0241 questions 1, 4 and 5, recommendation taken on the maintainer's standing instruction of 2026-11-11): F-344, F-345. ADR 0359 names the coupled remainder: donor switches of the fringe stencils (2.06e-5 -> 1.2e-6 with a pose-continuous stencil) and kind changes next to the hole (9.9e-6, ratio 1.85).

title: Matched sponge layer: memory decay, damping along the layer, corners
acceptance: The set-up D record of ADR 0237 (a wave train started inside the layer with zero memory in a rigid duct) falls below 1 percent within its registered window; a constant pressure offset with a gradient along the layer gives a bounded tangential momentum over 100 transit times of the layer; a pulse leaving through the corner of two layers reflects less than 1 percent; an isolated plane pulse at 60 degrees reflects less than 1 percent; the checks A0, A30b, A45b, A60b, X1 and X45 of ADR 0237 still meet 1 percent.
note: From ADR 0237 questions 2 and 3, recommendation taken on the maintainer's standing instruction of 2026-11-11. The job of 2026-11-12 (ADR 0248): four of the five clauses are MET IN THE LIBRARY, clause 1 is MISSED with a diagnosis that the registration gave before the runs. Built (rcfd-fv sponge.rs, opt-in, `Plain` and `Matched` untouched): `SpongeForm::MatchedShifted(MatchedOptions { normal, shift, along, second })`, the matched layer as a complex coordinate stretching with (i) a complex frequency shift `shift` (the memories decay: under a held pressure the memory and the force along the layer saturate at p'/a instead of growing; below omega ~ a the layer does not absorb and it leaves a static offset alone), (ii) a second planar layer with an orthogonal normal for a corner (`Sponge::corner`: the same memory, one product term, the force of each layer on the momentum along the other's normal; a second memory for an edge in three dimensions), (iii) a damping of the momentum along the layer `along` (a mismatch with a measured price); `Sponge::planar_shifted`, `CompressibleSolver::sponge_memories` and `set_sponge_memories`. Measured with shift 0.25/s (0.05 c/L) and along 0 on the 40-cell layer of ADR 0237 (limit 1 percent, largest difference to a run on an extended grid against the incident peak): an isolated plane pulse at 60 degrees 8.1e-4 (the form of ADR 0237 in the same run 8.0e-4; 705 000 and 770 000 cells, the set-up of X45 with tails of 3.5 pulse widths and a reference grid shortened by a causality argument that a model confirmed to 12 digits); a quarter of a cylindrical pulse through two layers and their corner 5.3e-5 (no sponge 0.058, one layer 0.029); the checks of ADR 0237 repeated with the shift: A0 9.4e-7 (1.2e-6 in front of a rigid wall), A30b, A45b, A60b 3.1e-4, 3.6e-4, 1.3e-3, X1 2.3e-5, X45 1.4e-4; a closed box with a pressure offset varying along the layer over 100 transit times: momentum along the layer at most 3.0 delta/c and not growing (the form of ADR 0237 in the same run 3.2 and not growing either: in a run neither form grows, the difference is under a held pressure, checked by algebra to 4e-6). Without the options the new form produces the bits of `Matched`; the existing compressible, F-258, ADR 0233, ADR 0237 and ADR 0243 tests pass unedited. Eight mutations caught. MISSED, clause 1: the set-up D record (a wave train started inside the layer with zero memory in a rigid duct) stays at 3.7e-2, 6.1e-2, 8.6e-2 at 30, 45, 60 degrees with the shift (3.8e-2, 6.2e-2, 8.7e-2 without) and at 2.2e-2, 3.6e-2, 4.2e-2 with along = 0.05, against 1e-2; kept as three ignored known_miss records. Diagnosis (ADR 0248 DR12, a scratch model predicted the five numbers within 20 percent before the runs): the ringing sits at the cut-off frequencies of the duct; a field that does not vary across the layer solves the equations of every matched layer, so no matched layer damps it; a damping along the layer is a mismatch that reflects about 1.3 along of a pulse at 60 degrees whatever its frequency (along = 0.05 measured 4.4e-2 of the steady train at 60 degrees), and the strength needed to remove the ringing within the registered window costs far more than 1 percent. Not a parameter that could be tuned at this thickness. Limits: linear acoustics about a state at rest; one layer or two orthogonal ones (no corner of three layers; the three-dimensional edge is checked by algebra only); explicit source; not on moving meshes; not with a mass-spring-damper wall; library only (the wiring goes with F-330); Cartesian grids. Open questions in ADR 0248 addendum 1 (what to do with clause 1; a default for the shift in the wiring; whether to keep `along`; a corner run in three dimensions). Open: the default shift in the F-330 wiring (a default; ADR 0248 question 2). The clause-1 follow-up (a plain damping zone behind a thicker layer) is proposed in ADR 0248 only for when a ducted case shows the ringing; no item added.

title: Sponge layer on moving meshes
acceptance: With a sponge, a uniform reference state stays to round-off under `step_ale` on a deforming mesh; the ADR 0237 tube check on a uniformly translating mesh reflects less than 1 percent; without a sponge `step_ale` is bit-identical.
note: From ADR 0237 question 5, recommendation taken on the maintainer's standing instruction of 2026-11-11. ADR 0265, 2026-11-12: the acceptance text is MET IN THE LIBRARY. Built (rcfd-fv, opt-in): `sponge::SpongeFrame { StaticMesh (default: step_ale refuses a sponge, as before), AttachedToMesh }` and `CompressibleSolver::set_sponge_frame`. When attached, the rates (of both layers of a corner) and the memories belong to the cells and move with them; the reference stays a lab-frame state; the memory of a cell is the time integral of p - p_ref along its path; and `step_ale` adds the source at the volume of each Runge-Kutta stage, which keeps the damping consistent with the geometric conservation law (a uniform offset decays as exp(-rate t) for any deformation). `replace_mesh` still refuses a sponge, because the solver has no map from old to new cells and a matched layer reset under a wave rings: clear it, replace the mesh, then set a new sponge and the caller's mapped memories. Measured: a uniform reference state on the deforming set-up U of ADR 0207 stays within 3.3e-15 over 121 to 136 steps in the plain, matched and shifted-corner forms (limit 1e-12); the ADR 0237 tube with both grids translating at Mach 0.2 reflects 9.6e-7 (plain and matched, Thompson end and pressure-release end) and 9.8e-7 (shifted) against 1e-2; on a mesh whose cells change volume by 16 percent a uniform offset decays within 3.1e-7 of exp(-2 t), the memory is within 8.3e-6 of its integral, and the shifted form is within 1.2e-7 of the static step. `step_ale` is bit-identical without a sponge, with a sponge set and cleared, with the frame setting alone and with zero-rate sponges; the F-258 bit records, the ADR 0233, 0237, 0243 and 0248 tests and baseline_hashes pass unedited. Seven mutations caught. One amendment: the control without sponge (pressure release, peak measure) gave 0.864 against 0.9. It was diagnosed as the peak loss of a pulse that the reflection on the moving mesh narrows to 2/3, and replaced by the time-integral ratio, 0.9995 (that value was seen in the diagnostic before the amendment; disclosed). Limits: attached frame only (no layer fixed in space); on a moving mesh the matched forms are matched at normal incidence only, because the medium moves relative to the layer (oblique incidence, motion along the layer and rotation not checked); library only, like the sponge itself; two-dimensional checks. STATUS recorded PARTIAL by the lead: the no-sponge control NCr missed its registered limit (0.864 against 0.9) and its replacement NCr2 was registered after a diagnostic had shown its value, so it is not blind; done is the maintainer's call (ADR 0265 Q1). ACCEPTED AS DONE by the maintainer in person on 2026-11-12 (the amended check).

title: Case-file key for the adaptive steady loop
acceptance: An optional adapt block on a steady incompressible box-mesh case runs rcfd_fv::adaptive and reproduces the ADR 0242 cavity numbers; cases without the block give identical hashes.
note: From ADR 0242 R1, recommendation taken on the maintainer's standing instruction of 2026-11-11. DONE pending acceptance (ADR 0262, 2026-11-12): the optional table [mesh.adapt] (absent from every case that does not write it; an empty table is ADR 0242's loop) runs rcfd_fv::adaptive on a steady laminar simple / simplec case of mesh.generator cavity_2d, box_2d or box_3d (uniform): the lattice takes the generator's coordinates and patches, the first step runs the whole loop and leaves the final mesh and solver; keys cycles, max_level, marking (fixed_fraction / target_count with target_cells), refine_fraction, indicator (velocity_gradient, velocity_gradient_unscaled, edge_length with edge_length_exponent), register and register_use (confine / refine; ADR 0247 R3), balance, transfer, max_iterations, tolerance. Tree runs equal library runs bit for bit on the 8 x 8 cavity (316 cells), with each criterion, on a box_2d channel and on a box_3d cube; the case file cases/cavity/adapt_re100.toml equals the library on its lattice bit for bit and gives ADR 0242's numbers (cells 576, 1269, 2799 with ADR 0242's iteration counts, centreline difference to the 96 x 96 solution 0.002311, Ghia 0.009159; within 9.9e-11 of ADR 0242's run, whose slab is 0.1 thick against the generator's 1/24); models and solver options the loop would drop, non-uniform or file meshes and other algorithms are located errors (also through rcfd validate); rcfd run gives the in-process run's monitors; baseline hashes, case_hashes_w48u and ADR 0257's K0 tests pass unedited; six mutations each failed their tests. Open: graded and inflated lattices (ADR 0262 Q4), per-solve monitors (Q5). Gate 4 (2026-11-13): the shipped case cases/cavity/adapt_re100.toml was registered in the every-shipped-case tests of rcfd-studio and rcfd-cli (maintainer-approved test edits, ADR 0262 addendum); the Studio preview and the field store do not yet follow the adapted mesh (F-475, F-476).

title: Further adaptation criteria (target cell count, edge-length weighting, anisotropic, register-based) and a case where adaptation pays
acceptance: Each criterion has a closed-form marking check, and a target-count run lands within 10 percent of its target on the ADR 0242 cavity; on a case with a localised feature the adapted mesh reaches the fine solution's error with at most half the cells of the uniform mesh that reaches it.
note: PARTIAL (ADR 0247): opt-in criteria in rcfd_fv::adaptive with closed-form marking checks: target cell count (target_count_marks, geometric target_schedule, run_adaptive_simple_target), edge-length weighting (cell_extents, edge_length_weighted_indicator, velocity_edge_length_indicator with exponent r), registers (Register from mask, region indicator, field range or levels, with and, or, complement and face-neighbour growth; register_marks, restrict_marks) and the loop with any marks (run_adaptive_simple_marked; run_adaptive_simple and _with unchanged bit for bit). Target-count runs on the ADR 0242 cavity land at 2307 for 2304 and 4611 for 4608 (limit 10 percent). Suction-layer case (Couette flow with transpiration, R = 80, closed form): the adapted mesh (16 x 16 base, five target-count cycles, 3841 cells) has error 0.0116 against 0.0439 for the uniform 128 x 128 (16384 cells); the uniform 90 x 90 (8100 cells) misses it (0.0846); the inverted indicator gives 1.20. ADR 0242's surviving MU6 is now caught. Not delivered: anisotropic (directional) refinement, which needs per-axis levels in the lattice (follow-up); merge-based polyhedral conversion, multigrid precoarsening and parallel adaptation stay listed here until split. Follow-up (ADR 0247 R1, recommendation taken on the maintainer's standing instruction of 2026-11-11): F-348; the new options join F-342's case key (R3). Follow-up (ADR 0247 R1, recommendation taken on the maintainer's standing instruction of 2026-11-11): F-348; the new options are case keys since ADR 0262 (2026-11-12, F-342): [mesh.adapt] marking = "target_count", indicator = "edge_length", register and register_use. The anisotropic criterion is delivered by F-348 (ADR 0267, 2026-11-12): a second lattice with per-axis levels and a directional criterion; on this suction layer 1547 cells give error 0.00298.

title: BDF2 PISO: the step-size-dependent remainder of the library's BDF2 step
acceptance: The remainder of PimpleSolver::step with BDF2 and three outer iterations on a mesh at rest (max abs(d_200) 5.13e-6 with the ratio 2.30 to max abs(d_400) on the mesh of SMc, ADR 0241 H16) is traced to a named term of the step with a number, and either removed as an opt-in (defaults bit-identical; the ratio at least 4 at rest and D2 of ADR 0241 at least 4 on TG_2) or shown to be a spatial term with its order in h, or the ADR names why not with a number.
note: Merged as an opt-in on the maintainer's decision in person of 2026-11-12. From ADR 0241 question 1, recommendation taken on the maintainer's standing instruction of 2026-11-11. ADR 0245, 2026-11-12: PARTIAL. Named: the remainder of the BDF2 step at rest is the step-size dependence of the converged face flux where the momentum diagonal differs across a face (the commutator C(G p) of ADR 0073 and the step dependence of interp(rAU)), largest next to fixed-velocity boundaries. Built, opt-in, internal faces only, merged as an opt-in by the maintainer's decision in person of 2026-11-12 (not the default): PimpleSettings::rhie_chow_step_consistent (the harmonic face value of rAU and the commutator of the lagged pressure gradient, in PimpleSolver::step at rest and in the overset step); defaults bit for bit on the tree merged with main (F-322 included). Met: at rest the ratio 2.30 -> 5.02 (limit 4), the steady cavity the same to 2.4e-13 for two steps (3.7e-4 by default). Missed: D2 on TG_2, 2.454 (limit 4): the remainder of the moving coupled meshes is another term (named in ADR 0359: the donor switches of the component's outer fringe and the background cells changing kind next to the hole) (with the component at rest 1.3e-7, ratio 4.98). ADR 0076's seam rows with the opt-in: bit-inert on periodic and rotational faces (operator level), no-harm met (TG-S N1 at most 1.0018, R4 at most 1.0026, PIMPLE-4 rows at most 0.999); R2b on SECT-M missed as predicted, 0.578 (default 0.538): the seam floor of ADR 0076, which the opt-in does not touch. Eight mutations caught (the fringe branch of the overset change by a direct check of its formula). Its body-force path is exercised by the SECT-M runs. Follow-ups proposed (ADR 0245 questions 1 and 3). Since ADR 0352 (F-443) the opt-in also acts with the consistent correctors and on step_ale / step_ale_with_walls and has the case key [solver.rhie_chow] step_consistent; step_sliding, the fractional step and coupled faces keep the default.

title: BDF2 for the library's moving-mesh step and the follow conditions of a moving wall
acceptance: PimpleSolver::step_ale_with_walls accepts BDF2 as an opt-in (defaults bit-identical); a uniform flow stays uniform to 1e-10 on the deforming meshes of ADR 0033 G2; with every cell calculated OversetSolver with BDF2 equals it to 1e-12 on BF of ADR 0219; the wall velocity and acceleration of set_follow_conditions are three-level with BDF2 and the time error of the cylinder case TR falls at a ratio of at least 4 between two step sizes, or the ADR names why not with a number.
note: From ADR 0241 questions 4 and 5, recommendation taken on the maintainer's standing instruction of 2026-11-11. After the rework of the corrector flags in pimple.rs (F-322). ADR 0379, 2026-11-12: PARTIAL, every clause met but the measured TR ratio, whose cause is named with a number. Built: PimpleSolver::set_moving_mesh_time_scheme(Bdf2), an opt-in of the library's moving-mesh step (without it step_ale_with_walls refuses BDF2 as before): the mesh flux (c0 W - c2 W_old) / dt of the swept volumes of the last two steps (the discrete geometric conservation law of BDF2), the old and old-old volumes in the transient term, the three-level Rhie-Chow defect, an implicit Euler step when the step before was not a moving step with the opt-in; ale::set_follow_conditions_bdf2 with a FollowHistory: the wall velocity the mid-step velocities of the last two steps extrapolated to the end of the step with the normal part carrying the three-level mesh flux, dp/dn from the BDF2 derivative of the wall velocity; OversetSolver::prepare takes it when BDF2 is on. Defaults bit for bit (Q0 of ADR 0219 hash af2c9e6bd3e5596d, baseline_hashes, the existing moving-mesh and overset suites unedited). Met: a uniform flow stays uniform to 7e-15 on the four motions of ADR 0033 G2 with uniform and alternating steps; with every cell calculated OversetSolver with BDF2 equals the library's BDF2 moving step bit for bit on BF (one and three outer iterations, with and without rhie_chow_step_consistent); the wall velocity and acceleration are exact for a constant acceleration and of second order (ratio 4.000) for a cubic motion; the body-fitted cylinder BF to t = 1 falls by 5.04 when the step is halved (3.04 with BDF2 and the two-level walls, 2.97 with implicit Euler). Missed: the time error of TR falls by 1.09 (limit 4): it sits in the background cells one ring outside the hole, which change kind as the cylinder passes (ADR 0359 event 2); the component cells fall by 4.22. Nine mutations caught. Not delivered: the case-tree wiring, BDF2 for step_sliding, replace_mesh and set_rest_conditions.

title: Immersed solid: force and moment in unsteady flow
acceptance: The force and moment of an immersed solid subtract the rate of change of the momentum and angular momentum of its forced cells; DFG 2D-2 maximum drag and lift on M2 are within 1.5 percent of the FeatFlow level-6 values, and a steady case returns the values of F-337 to round-off.
note: PARTIAL (ADR 0249, 2026-11-12), in the library. From ADR 0239 question 3. The premise did not survive the derivation, written before any code: the reaction of the forcing is the discrete force on the staircase surface of the solid cells minus the storage of those cells, so for a body at rest it already is the force in unsteady flow, and the storage of the first fluid cells is fluid momentum that must not be removed; the storage that is not fluid momentum is that of the solid cells of a body whose rigid velocity changes in time. Delivered: rcfd-fv immersed.rs, `ImmersedForcing::force_moment_unsteady` (opt-in: the pair of `force_moment_second_order` plus the rate of change of the momentum and angular momentum held by the solid cells; `force_moment` and `force_moment_second_order` unchanged, hashes checked) and `immersed::velocity_rate` (the solvers' Euler and variable-step BDF2 difference; the caller keeps the older fields, no hunk in pimple.rs). Measured (limits registered before the code; three defective set-ups of the registration corrected by amendment 1 before their runs): the moment on a cylinder accelerated in a fixed outer one within 0.167 and 0.078 percent of the closed form at N 48 and 96 (limit 0.5; the reaction alone 4.3 percent, the literal reading with the first fluid cells 1.8 and 0.9 percent); the force on an accelerated plate within 0.056 and 0.014 percent (limit 1; the reaction alone 42.8 percent, the literal reading 5.1 and 2.6 percent); a steady case returns F-337 exactly (2D-1 on M2 5.56246454, 0.0108880492; Couette by PISO); DFG 2D-2 against the recorded FeatFlow level-6 values, on M2 max C_D +0.261 %, max C_L -0.161 % (limit 1.5 %: met, but the old evaluation gives the same numbers, the two differ by 1.9e-6), on T (the mesh of ADR 0218) max C_D +0.815 %, max C_L +2.580 % (KNOWN MISS, predicted in the registration: not a storage term; the mean drag is +0.79 % and the steady 2D-1 lift on M2 +2.7 %; the two D/40 meshes differ by 2.7 points in the lift, so the M2 agreement is not shown to be convergence); nine mutations caught. Missing (why partial): the lift of 2D-2 on T; the unsteady evaluation as a default or behind a case key (open); the slivers between the staircase and the surface for an accelerating body; Crank-Nicolson and bounded BDF2 rates; moving shapes. Found on the way: 2D-2 on M2 with the second-order forcing of F-309 stops in PISO at step 6 (Courant 1.1e7), not diagnosed. Open: ADR 0249 Q1 (reword the first clause to the solid cells), Q2 (the 2D-2 clause: M2 as written, or replaced by the closed forms), Q3 (default). Follow-ups: F-354, F-355. ADR 0268 (2026-11-12, F-354) located the +2.58 percent lift of T: refining only the mesh around the cylinder to D/80 takes it to +0.02 percent; the -0.16 percent of M2 was a cancellation of that D/40 error by the coarse outer mesh; on the D/80 meshes both forcings are within 0.43 percent.

title: Vendor heat-flux card for the structural load deck from a cited open specification
acceptance: A specification of the card (fields, sign, required surface elements) from an open source is placed in the repository; the deck writes it beside RCFDQ; the tube heat rate after a round trip through the repository reader matches the fluid heat rate to 0.1 percent
note: Priority P3. Size S. Area: io. Opened by ADR 0244: RCFDQ is the repository's own card; no vendor heat-flux card layout is specified in the repository, so none was written. NEEDS THE USER: an open specification of the card has to be placed in the repository first (clean-room rule).

title: Anisotropic (directional) refinement: a lattice with per-axis levels
acceptance: A lattice with per-axis refinement levels gives valid closed meshes for random directional marks (validate, closure, volume) and transfers linear fields exactly; on the ADR 0247 suction layer a directional run reaches the isotropic adapted error E(A) with at most half of its 3841 cells; the isotropic AmrMesh paths stay bit for bit.
note: PARTIAL (ADR 0267, 2026-11-12): rcfd_mesh::adapt::aniso::AnisoMesh, a second lattice with one refinement level per axis (AxisLeaf, AxisMark; AmrMesh untouched): faces are the intersections of the sides of two leaves, with the corners of all face rectangles in the vertex set, so cells are closed for any tiling by dyadic boxes; optional balance of one level per refined axis across every face (at most 2 faces per side in a slab, 4 in 3-D); the existing Transfer and transfer_field. Random directional marks on a graded 3-D box, a slab and a box refined along two of three axes give valid closed meshes (validate, closure and volume to 1e-13) and linear fields transfer to 4.4e-16; on isotropic marks the mesh, the transfer and the adaptive loop equal AmrMesh's bit for bit. Directional criterion in rcfd_fv::adaptive (axis_variations, directional_axes with theta = 1/2, directional_target_marks, run_adaptive_simple_directional and _target). On the ADR 0247 suction layer the directional run has error 0.00298 with 1547 cells against the isotropic 0.01159 with 3841 (limit: at most 1920 cells); held at the isotropic finest size it reaches 0.01158 with 960 cells; with the axis choice inverted 1.18. ADR 0054, 0242 and 0247 tests pass unedited (the heavy ones included); ten mutations each failed their tests. Partial by the rule because two registered supporting checks missed and were corrected under amendments: pair coarsening in 3-D can leave a five-box tiling of a cell that it cannot merge further (valid mesh; slabs return to the base), and the fast layer test on an 8 x 8 base (cell Peclet 10) had no converged solution on its first directional mesh (replaced by a 16 x 16 base). Open: a box merge for 3-D coarsening (R2), the case key (R5), cells spent along x in early cycles (R4). Follow-ups: F-438 (case key), F-439 (three-dimensional box merge). The box merge is delivered by F-439 (ADR 0341, 2026-11-12): repeated all-axes box coarsening returns any state, the five-box tiling included, to the base.

title: Overset: the response to the truncation of the background-fringe interpolation
acceptance: The response R_b of ADR 0246 (the difference of the RL runs with the library stencils and with a third-order interpolation on the background fringe: 4.87e-5, 2.19e-5, 1.41e-5 at levels 1 to 3, orders 1.153 and 1.093) is traced to a named term of the coupled step by a switch that brings its order to 1.7 or more on levels 1 to 4, or is shown to reach order 1.7 on finer levels or at a later time, or the ADR names why not with a number.
note: From ADR 0246 question 4, recommendation taken on the maintainer's standing instruction of 2026-11-11. ADR 0340, 2026-11-12: PARTIAL, a diagnosis, tests only, no library change. No clause of the order check is met. R_b (the library's quadratic donor interpolation of F-336 on the background fringe against the default stencils; within 2.5 percent of ADR 0246) is 4.996e-5, 2.177e-5, 1.412e-5, 8.917e-6, 6.425e-6 at t = 0.5 on levels 1 to 5, orders 1.198, 1.068, 1.598, 1.469; run on to t = 3 on levels 1 to 3 it is 1.403e-4, 5.250e-5, 3.376e-5, orders 1.418, 1.089, and still growing; half the time step changes it by under 1 percent. Found on the way: the truncation of the background fringe of RL alternates between odd and even levels (coefficient 0.0685, 0.0781, 0.0621, 0.0693, 0.0638; the reflection of the fringe phase is not a symmetry), so orders between successive levels of RL carry a factor 1.26; within the parity families R_b has 1.150, 1.288, 1.542. On a set-up locked exactly, with equal spacings and no modulation along the ring (RE), the truncation converges at 1.995, 1.956 and R_b at 0.983, 1.015: the response per unit of truncation is proportional to the level (0.168, 0.339, 0.497) with no levelling off. Ruled out with numbers: a time-step or splitting term, a late settling at second order, the unequal spacings and the modulation. Named and confirmed: the normal velocity of a fringe cell is imposed softly. The flux of a face between a calculated and a fringe cell is that of the pressure equation with the interpolated fringe pressure and differs from the face-interpolated velocity by a defect D held by a pressure jump dJ = -(16 nu / 3 h) D (measured face by face on RE: 0.9986, 1.0162 of that, correlation 0.995, 0.999), a resistance proportional to nu / h. The calculated cell across a fringe face follows a change of the normal fringe velocity by 0.51, 0.66, 0.76, 0.79, 0.83 at the background fringe (levels 1 to 5, t = 0.5; 0.10 to 0.51 at t = 0.025) and by 0.34 to 0.83 at the component fringe; each fringe costs about half an order on these levels. Refining the background alone raises R_b. Not shown: the level or time at which R_b reaches 1.7, and a formula for R_b from the resistance. One registered kinematic check missed (the truncation order between levels 3 and 4, 1.621 against 1.8, the alternation) and is kept as a known miss. Controls held, five mutations caught. Follow-up (ADR 0340 question 2, recommendation taken on the maintainer's standing instruction of 2026-11-11): an opt-in that prescribes the flux of the calculated-fringe faces from the interpolated velocity. ADR 0347 (F-445), 2026-11-12: with the flux of the fringe faces prescribed and the pressure gradient of the neighbouring calculated cells taken from their own part, the order of R_b is 1.962, 1.789 on RE and 2.704, 2.124 within the parity families of RL: removing the soft imposition named here restores the order. The response is then larger on the levels run (R_b 9.0 to 3.3 times), because the interpolation error is handed on in full.

title: Strong body-flow coupling selectable from the case tree
acceptance: A case with dynamic_mesh.six_dof.coupling = "strong" (default "loose") and its relaxation, added-mass estimate, tolerance, force scale and iteration cap as keys runs the spring-mounted piston at a mass ratio of 4 through the case driver and reproduces ADR 0250 S1 to S3 (omega within 2 percent, no growth of same-side turning points over 10 periods, dt halving within 0.5 percent), the same case with coupling = "loose" stops with a located error or grows; a step that reaches the cap stops the run with a located message unless a key says to continue; every static check of the new keys is located; with the default every existing case hash is bit-identical.
note: From ADR 0250 questions 2 and 3, recommendation taken on the maintainer's standing instruction of 2026-11-11. PARTIAL (ADR 0266, 2026-11-12; registered before the code, one amendment): the optional table [dynamic_mesh.six_dof.coupling] (absent from every case that does not write it; a key inside the existing table six_dof would need an entry in the H1 hash table, so the acceptance's coupling = "strong" is written scheme = "strong" in that table) selects the strong coupling of rcfd_fv::fsi::strong_step in the case driver; keys scheme (loose default, strong), relaxation (aitken default, fixed), added_mass (the factor 2M/(2M + m')), tolerance, force_scale, moment_scale, max_iterations, at_cap (stop default, continue). Tree runs equal strong_step called directly bit for bit (60 steps with ADR 0250's settings, 40 with a fixed factor and every key away from its default). The spring-mounted piston of ADR 0250 at mass ratio 4 through the case driver gives ADR 0250's numbers to their printed digits: omega_m/omega 1.005081 at T/100 (limit 2 %), dt halving 1.7e-5 (limit 0.5 %), largest ratio of same-side turning points 0.92452 and 0.96141 over 11 crossings (never grows), 3.0 flow solves a step; with scheme = "loose" (or no table) it passes 10 X at step 28 (T/100) and 31 (T/200) and stops at steps 34 and 40 with a located mesh error. A step at the cap stops the run with "dynamic_mesh: step N, t = ...: dynamic_mesh.six_dof.coupling.max_iterations: ..."; with at_cap = "continue" the run goes on with one warning event, and the cap 1 equals the loose run bit for bit. Every static check of the new keys is located at its key (strong with a prescribed motion, rest patches or Newmark; tolerance, scales, added mass, cap; unknown values and keys). Without the table nothing changes: baseline hashes, case_hashes_w48u, the K0 tests of ADR 0257 and 0262 and the dynamic_mesh tree tests pass unedited; a table with scheme = "loose" equals no table bit for bit. The one mutation of ADR 0266 that passed its named test (force_scale not read; the floor k X was inert in E1 because moment_scale = 0 makes the moment term the unfloored force ratio) is caught by the binding-floor test of ADR 0349 (F-437, 2026-11-12); proposed done by ADR 0349 Q1. Done is the maintainer's call (ADR 0349 Q1 recommends done). Open: ADR 0266 Q1 (status), Q2 (the key name), Q3 (Newmark), Q4 (rest patches). The wall pressure of the body force stays the default extrapolation (F-358). Follow-up: F-437. The key naming (Q2: scheme = "strong" in the table [dynamic_mesh.six_dof.coupling]) accepted by the maintainer in person on 2026-11-12.

title: Wall pressure of the body force on a fixed-flux moving wall (the 1.25 percent added-mass deficit)
acceptance: The cause of the discrete added mass of the piston column lying 1.25 percent below rho A L0 (ADR 0250 C1 and S1, ADR 0211 B1) is identified by a test that separates the wall-pressure extrapolation of patch_force_moment from the pressure of the flow step; if it is the extrapolation, an opt-in evaluation that uses the prescribed pressure gradient of the wall brings the sub-iteration gain at ratio 4 within 0.2 percent of the 2.977 of the model and omega_m/omega within 0.1 percent of 1 on the 20-cell column, and the convergence of the deficit with the cell size is shown on 20, 40 and 80 cells; the default force evaluation is unchanged unless the maintainer approves the change with its effect on the existing hashes listed.
note: DONE pending acceptance, merged 2026-11-12. From ADR 0250 question 4, recommendation taken on the maintainer's standing instruction of 2026-11-11. DONE (ADR 0252, 2026-11-12; registered before the code, four amendments). Cause, measured: the wall-pressure extrapolation of patch_force_moment. Its least-squares gradient (weights 1/d^2) takes the stored zero-gradient wall value of the pressure field as a data point with the weight of the neighbour cell, while the pressure equation of the moving-mesh step used the prescribed gradient -n . a_wall; the gradient of the wall cell is therefore exactly half (0.5 to 1e-16) and the wall pressure a quarter cell short: the force is low by 1/(4N), first order in the cell size (prescribed piston, flow step converged: 1.2510e-2, 6.258e-3, 3.129e-3 on 20, 40, 80 cells, orders 0.9993 and 0.9998), 1.25 percent on the 20-cell column at every mass ratio. The pressure of the flow step carries none of it (2e-6 with the step converged, 7e-6 with the registered two correctors). Delivered, opt-in, nothing calls it: sixdof::patch_force_moment_wall_gradient (the normal part of the cell-gradient extrapolation replaced by the gradient of ale::set_follow_conditions, p_c + dn g on an orthogonal wall cell, second order) and fsi::strong_step_with with fsi::WallPressure, which carries that gradient from step to step. With it: gain of the sub-iteration at ratio 4 2.97693 (model 2.977, limit 0.2 percent); omega_m/omega 1.000042 at ratio 4 on 20, 40 and 80 cells (limit 0.1 percent; 1.005081, 1.002552, 1.001294 with the default), 0.999963 at ratio 20, 1.000068 at 0.2, 1.000264 for the loose loop at 0.2 (1.001307 before: the unexplained +1.0e-3 of ADR 0211 was this deficit); deficit of the force 3e-6 on 20, 40, 80 cells. Every number equals the piston model with the exact added mass to six digits. Unchanged: patch_force_moment and strong_step (bit-identical over 40 steps; the sixdof, sixdof_coupled, sixdof_flow_f244 and strong_fsi_f251 suites pass unedited; baseline_hashes 3 passed, 0 failed, 1 ignored (the file unedited)); pimple.rs, pimple/moving.rs, rcfd-api and the case schema untouched. Seven library mutations: six failed their checks; one added variant passed every test and a check (the gain at the third step of a run) was added by amendment and catches it. Disclosed: the first registered diagnosis missed its limits because its reference was the column of the new mesh; the pressure of the implicit Euler moving-mesh step is the acceleration times the column of the old mesh (first order in dt, not a mean deficit), and the reference was corrected by amendment after an exploration; the missed tests are kept as ignored records. Also found: the non-iterated step leaves a viscous splitting error that grows with the cell count and does not move the frequency. Not delivered: the case driver (rcfd-api dynmesh) still uses the default evaluation; a skewed wall cell and a moment in a flow are not tested. Open, the maintainer's: whether the prescribed gradient becomes the default (ADR 0252 Q1; not taken, it moves existing results), the case key (Q2), the audit of other walls with a prescribed gradient (Q3). Note of the lead: the acceptance limits were never changed, but the limits of the diagnosis were corrected by amendment 2 after a run and a prints-only exploration, so they were set with numbers seen. Follow-up (ADR 0252 questions 1 to 3, recommendation taken on the maintainer's standing instruction of 2026-11-11): F-358. Open: question 1 (the prescribed gradient as the default changes existing hashes).

title: Overset: donor search on cells with non-planar faces
acceptance: On the set-up B3d of ADR 0251 (two hexahedral parts whose interior points are displaced by up to 0.15 of the cell size in all three directions) every fringe centre gets a donor that agrees with a full search, the linear and the quadratic stencils reproduce linear and quadratic fields to 1e-11, and on meshes with planar faces the donors and stencils are bit-identical to those of today (the unit tests K2 and K4 of ADR 0219 and D1 of ADR 0251).
note: DONE pending acceptance, merged 2026-11-12. From ADR 0251 question 2, recommendation taken on the maintainer's standing instruction of 2026-11-11. ADR 0253, 2026-11-12: DONE. Derived: one plane for each face leaves no gap across a face but a sliver along every edge at which the planes of the four faces do not meet in one line, a gap or an overlap with equal chance, of cross-section at most (w_F + w_F')(w_G + w_G') for the warps w of the faces, second order in the warp; on B3d (warp up to 0.142 of the cell size) the estimate was 6e-4 of the volume each and 116 and 114 of 200000 random points were measured in no cell and in two. Built in rcfd_mesh::overset: a cell with a face warped beyond the locator's tolerance (1e-10 of its box diagonal) is tested as the polyhedron of the triangles about its face centres, the same triangles from both sides of a face (triangulated_margin: the distance from the triangles, signed by the winding number, behind a bounding-box shortcut); a cell with planar faces keeps the plane test of ADR 0219 M3 unchanged; a point on a shared triangle goes to the lowest-numbered cell. Met: on B3d all 1069 fringe centres get a donor equal to the full search and confirmed by an independent tetrahedral test, the linear stencils reproduce a linear field to 3e-16 and the quadratic stencils q3 to 9e-16 with no fallback; 250000 random points in the two warped parts each lie in exactly one cell; 39744 face centres and 12167 mesh points go to the lowest-numbered cell; on the planar set-ups (RL, TG_L, U, TR, DC, FB, B3, B3s) no cell is warped and the donors and default stencils equal those built from the rule of M3 bit for bit; K2, K4, D1, Q0 and the records R2 pass unedited. Cost: a search takes 4.5 microseconds on B3d, the connectivity 1.8 times that of B3. The present rule finds no cell for the fringe cells 16035 (as recorded) and 16245. Six mutations caught. Limits: kinematic only, one family of warped meshes; non-convex cells with planar faces keep the plane test. Open for the maintainer: whether every cell should use the triangulated test (it changes one donor of TR at a tie, ADR 0253 Q1). Follow-ups (ADR 0253 questions 2 and 3, recommendation taken on the maintainer's standing instruction of 2026-11-11): F-356, F-357. Open: question 1 (the triangulated test for every cell changes one donor at a tie).

title: Overset: the moving cylinder with the quadratic donor interpolation
acceptance: The set-up TR of ADR 0219 run with DonorInterpolation::Quadratic: mass of the domain and continuity within 1e-9, no fallback or the count reported, drag within 5 percent of the body-fitted run at every step from t = 2 to t = 8 and the difference to the linear-stencil run reported; the ADR recommends for or against making the quadratic interpolation the default.
note: DONE pending acceptance, merged 2026-11-12. From ADR 0251 question 5, recommendation taken on the maintainer's standing instruction of 2026-11-11. ADR 0259, 2026-11-12: DONE (tests and ADR only, no library change). The set-up TR of ADR 0219 with DonorInterpolation::Quadratic over 400 steps: continuity 5.6e-17, net outflow 9.4e-15 of U D L, no fallback (156 stencils of nine cells at every step), no unconverged solve, drag within 5.86e-3 of the body-fitted run at every step from t = 2 to t = 8 (linear stencils 6.25e-3; the linear run and the body-fitted run reproduce ADR 0219 to every printed digit). Against the linear run: C_D lower by 2.1e-4 on average (largest 1.6e-3), mean drag error 3.42e-3 against 3.21e-3, worse by more than 1e-4 at 164 of 301 steps; the step-to-step drag oscillation as the body crosses background cells halves (rms 0.98e-3 against 1.80e-3 of C_D); time 1.03 times. By the rule fixed before the run the ADR recommends against making the quadratic interpolation the default; the default stays the maintainer's decision (ADR 0259 Q1). Three mutations caught by the fast test.

title: Immersed solid: DFG 2D-2 force extrema, mesh and time-step convergence
acceptance: DFG 2D-2 with the immersed cylinder is run on the T mesh and on T refined once (D/80, half the time step) and on M2 and M3; the maximum drag and lift on the finest mesh are within 1.5 percent of the FeatFlow level-6 values and the error decreases from D/40 to D/80 on both families, or the part that does not converge (mesh of the wake, forcing order, outlet condition, time step) is identified by a registered measurement.
note: PARTIAL (ADR 0268, 2026-11-12), measurement only, no library code. From ADR 0249 question 5. DFG 2D-2 with the immersed cylinder was run to t = 8 on T and on T refined once (T2, D/80, dt 5e-4) and on M2 and M3 (M3 also at dt 5e-4), with `build` and with `build_second_order_bounded`, against the FeatFlow level-6 values. On the D/80 meshes max C_D and max C_L are within 0.43 percent with either forcing (T2 build +0.272/+0.325, T2 bounded +0.136/+0.175, M3 build +0.143/-0.283, M3 bounded +0.007/-0.429; St within 0.13 percent). The error decreases from D/40 to D/80 on the T family with build (lift 2.580 to 0.325), on the M family with the bounded form (1.011 to 0.429), and on the M family with build in the drag (0.261 to 0.143) but not in the lift (0.161 to 0.283, a known miss accounted for by the part measurements). Part measurements, each registered with its decision numbers: refining only the core around the cylinder on T takes the lift error from +2.69 to +0.02 percent, so the mesh at the cylinder carries the T anomaly; the rest of the mesh then moves it 0.31 point, halving the time step 0.11 (T) and 0.04 (M2) point, and moving the outlet from x = 2.2 to 4.4 changes nothing to six digits; the T and M families differ by 2.74 points of lift at D/40 and by 0.61 at D/80, so the M2 agreement of ADR 0249 was a cancellation between the D/40 core and the coarse outer mesh; the forcing order moves the extrema by up to 1.17 points at D/40 (M2) and at most 0.15 at D/80. Missing (why partial): T with the bounded forcing (D/40) stopped at step 2951 by the divergence guard, with pressure NaN in the pressure solve at the inlet corner cell, so the decrease on the T family with the bounded form is not formed; not diagnosed (library work). Open: ADR 0268 Q5 (the stop), Q6 (quote the D/80 values as the validation), Q7 (status). ADR 0363 (2026-11-12, F-466): the stop of T with the bounded form was a breakdown of the AMG-preconditioned pressure CG at step 2951 (r^T z < 0, finite inputs); with the opt-in pressure_ic_fallback T runs to t = 8, max C_D +0.216 and max C_L +1.687 percent, so A2-T-2 is met (0.216 to 0.136, 1.687 to 0.175) and the forcing order on T moves the extrema by -0.60 and -0.89 point.

title: Second-order immersed forcing: transient PISO at Re 100
acceptance: DFG 2D-2 on M2 with `build_second_order` runs to t = 8 in PISO with BDF2 and gives a Strouhal number within 1 percent of the first-order forcing on the same mesh, or the cause of the stop at step 6 is diagnosed by a registered measurement and the configuration is refused with a located message.
note: PARTIAL (ADR 0254, 2026-11-12), in the library. From ADR 0249 question 6. The stop was reproduced (step 6, Courant 1.1094e7) and diagnosed by registered variant runs, each with its first-order control: it needs a fluid-solid face whose surface crossing lies close to the fluid cell centre, so that the linear extension of ADR 0234 D1 has a weight above 5 (it multiplies the velocity of the first fluid cell relative to the wall by up to 38 on M2), together with the impulsive start; runs with weights of at most 5 (theta_min 0.1, 0.25, 0.5; mesh M1) and a run started from a developed field do not stop, and at each of the five steps the largest flux velocity sits on the face of weight 38.99 (2.49, 23, 1426, 9.2e4, 6.9e5). Ruled out, each by its number: the ddt flux correction, the corrector count, BDF2, the convection scheme, the time step (5e-4 to 8e-3 all stop) and the continuity of the fluid cells (7e-7). A hand estimate of a linear growth criterion (weight times the share of the time term in the diagonal) was refuted by its registered rule. Delivered: rcfd-fv immersed.rs, `ImmersedForcing::build_second_order_bounded` (opt-in): on the faces with a weight above 2 the flux is that of the wall value reflected through the image point of the face in the fluid, interpolated between the first fluid cell and the cell behind it, weights of magnitude at most 1, second order; `build` and `build_second_order` are bit-identical (three hashes, the existing immersed tests, baseline_hashes). With it DFG 2D-2 on M2 runs to t = 8 in PISO with BDF2: Strouhal number 0.30112 against 0.30041 of the first-order forcing (+0.24 percent, limit 1), C_D max -0.33 percent and C_L max -1.01 percent of FeatFlow; circular Couette error 5.91e-3, 1.63e-3, 4.23e-4, order 1.947 (limit 1.5), PISO equal to SIMPLEC to 0.1 percent. `build_second_order` itself is refused by PimpleSolver with a located message where a flux face has a weight above 5 and can return more than the time term carries (`flux_growth`; 2D-2 on M2 at step 1, value 2.2; the runs of ADR 0234 and 0249 are not refused); the refusal is a sufficient condition, not a stability criterion (time steps of 4e-3 and 8e-3 still stop by the Courant guard). Seven mutations caught. Partial by the registered rule because of two known misses: the flux velocity after the first step was registered as at least 4.5 and is 2.49 (the growth builds over steps 2 to 5), and the bounded form with a single PISO corrector stops at step 34 (any flux face that returns the wall-normal velocity at full size does, with one corrector; with two or more it runs).
