Acceptance: the second branch (diagnosis and located refusal) is met; the first is met with the bounded opt-in, not with `build_second_order` as named. Open (ADR 0254 questions 1 to 3): whether `build_second_order` should build the bounded form (changes recorded numbers of ADR 0234 and 0239), the form of the refusal, the single corrector. Not run: M3, T, three dimensions, PIMPLE outer iterations, SIMPLE with under-relaxation. Follow-ups: F-363 (the single corrector), F-364 (the bounded form as build_second_order; needs the maintainer). ADR 0268 (2026-11-12, F-354): `build_second_order_bounded` ran 2D-2 to t = 8 on T2 and M3 (D/80, within 0.43 percent of FeatFlow) but stopped on T (D/40, dt 1e-3) at step 2951, with pressure NaN in the pressure solve at the inlet corner cell; not diagnosed. ADR 0363 (2026-11-12, F-466): the stop of build_second_order_bounded on T (ADR 0268) is not a stop of the forcing but of the AMG-preconditioned pressure CG (r^T z < 0 at step 2951); with the opt-in PimpleSettings::pressure_ic_fallback the run reaches t = 8. ADR 0374 (2026-11-12, F-363): with one PISO corrector a flux face with an image or a weight above 1 is refused at step 1 with a located message; the stop of the bounded form with one corrector (step 34) depends on the time step (it runs at dt 5e-4 and 2.5e-4) and is not explained by the pressure-lag map.

title: Overset: donor search on non-convex cells with planar faces
acceptance: On a mesh of non-convex polyhedral cells with planar faces every one of 100000 random points inside the mesh lies in exactly one cell of the locator and the located cell agrees with a full search and with an independent containment test; on meshes of convex cells with planar faces the donors and stencils are bit-identical to those of today (the checks A4 of ADR 0253).
note: DONE pending acceptance, merged 2026-11-12. From ADR 0253 question 2, recommendation taken on the maintainer's standing instruction of 2026-11-11. ADR 0260, 2026-11-12: DONE. Derived: the planes of M3 enclose only the kernel of a cell, exact for a convex cell with planar faces and refusing points of its own cell for a non-convex one (smallest example a dart prism); a cell is non-convex exactly when one of its points lies outside one of its face planes. Built in rcfd_mesh::overset: a flat cell with a point outside one of its face planes by more than the locator's tolerance (1e-10 of its box diagonal) is tested by the triangles of its faces as a warped cell of ADR 0253; the fan about the face centre keeps the winding number exact but, where it folds out of a non-convex face, its distance is wrong, so such a face is ear-clipped, the same from both sides (face_fan_folds, face_ear_triangles, CellLocator::n_nonconvex, n_ear_clipped, n_unsupported). Met: on a mesh of dart prisms (1125 of 1280 cells non-convex) and one of L-shaped prisms with triangle prisms in their notches (288 non-convex, 324 ear-clipped faces) every one of 100000 random points lies in exactly one cell, agrees with the full search and with an independent containment test in lattice space; face centres, mesh points and 20000 points on layer planes in the notches are located consistently; an overset on the L-mesh gets all 296 donors, linear and quadratic fields reproduced to 1.3e-15 and 8.9e-16. The present rule leaves 26305 and 44680 of the points in no cell. On the convex set-ups of ADR 0253 no cell is reclassified (largest outward vertex distance 1.5e-4 of the tolerance) and every overset test of rcfd-mesh and rcfd-fv passes unedited; B3d keeps the donors of ADR 0253. Five mutations caught; one ill-posed check corrected by amendment 1. Limits: kinematic only, prism meshes only; a face that cannot be ear-clipped is only counted. Open for the maintainer: whether such faces should be refused (ADR 0260 Q1). Open for the maintainer: ADR 0260 Q1 (refuse a face that cannot be ear-clipped or a folded warped face; today they are only counted, and refusing could turn an existing result into an error).

title: Overset: uniform flow on a warped three-dimensional overset mesh
acceptance: The uniform-flow check U1 of ADR 0219 on the set-up B3d of ADR 0251 with the component moving: velocity and pressure within 1e-10, continuity of the calculated cells within 1e-9 at every step, with the default and with the quadratic donor interpolation.
note: DONE pending acceptance, merged 2026-11-12. From ADR 0253 question 3, recommendation taken on the maintainer's standing instruction of 2026-11-11. ADR 0255, 2026-11-12: DONE. The uniform flow U = (1, 0.5, 0.25) through B3d (two hexahedral parts with interior points displaced by up to 0.15 h, face warp up to 0.142 h) with the component turning by 0.1 rad and translating by 0.087 over 40 steps of 0.005, the hole and fringe rebuilt every step (92 kind changes): velocity 7.7e-15 and 7.3e-15, pressure 1.0e-13 and 1.1e-13, continuity of the calculated cells 6.4e-15 and 5.0e-15 at every step with the default and the quadratic donor interpolation (no fallback), GCL 6.1e-16, outflow 9e-15. Separating checks met: the warped component alone at rest and moving and the warped background alone keep the uniform state to 7e-15, the planar B3 with the same motion to 5e-15 and 7.9e-14. Controls held (weights times 1.001: 1.3e-3; a GCL residual of 3.1e-7 in the mesh flux: 1.0e-6). Mutations caught: a quadratic weight off by 1e-6 (1.3e-6), the M9 flux refresh skipped (3.1e-2); a non-closing face area vector is refused by the mesh validation before the flow. No library change. Limits: a uniform flow only; it shows the identities (closed area vectors, GCL, weights summing to one) on a warped moving overset mesh, not the accuracy of a non-uniform flow there. Follow-up (recommendation taken on the maintainer's standing instruction of 2026-11-11): F-359.

title: Wall pressure of the body force from the prescribed gradient, selectable in the case driver, and the default decided
acceptance: A case key of dynamic_mesh.six_dof selects the wall pressure of the body force ("extrapolated", the default, or "prescribed_gradient"), the case driver keeps the vector of ale::set_follow_conditions and hands it to sixdof::patch_force_moment_wall_gradient, and the spring-mounted piston of ADR 0211 run through the case driver at a mass ratio of 0.2 gives omega_m/omega within 0.05 percent of 1 with the key against 1.0013 without; the existing cases whose hashes would move if the prescribed gradient became the default are listed with the size of the change, for the maintainer's decision on the default; the callers that evaluate a wall force after a step with a prescribed wall gradient (ale::set_rest_conditions, the sliding step) are listed with the measured error on one case each, and the corrected evaluation is checked on a wall cell whose centre does not lie on the face normal; with the default every existing case hash is bit-identical.
note: From ADR 0252 questions 1 to 3, recommendation taken on the maintainer's standing instruction of 2026-11-11. DONE (ADR 0269, 2026-11-12; registered before the code, two amendments). The key wall_pressure ("extrapolated" default, "prescribed_gradient") in the optional table [dynamic_mesh.six_dof.coupling] (a plain key of six_dof would need an H1 hash-table entry, ADR 0266; the coupling table holds it because the strong step takes it beside the coupling settings) selects the wall pressure of the body force in both schemes: the case driver keeps the fixed-flux gradient vector of ale::set_follow_conditions (merged with set_rest_conditions) from step to step (Simulation::dynamic_wall_gradients) and hands it to sixdof::patch_force_moment_wall_gradient (loose) or fsi::strong_step_with (strong). Tree runs equal strong_step_with called directly bit for bit (loose 100 steps as one iteration, strong 60 steps); the kept vector equals (w_n - w_(n-1))/dt to 1e-15. The spring-mounted piston of ADR 0211 at mass ratio 0.2 through the driver: omega_m/omega 1.000264 with the key (limit 0.05 percent), 1.001307 without; at ratio 4 strong 1.000042 (1.005081 without). Corrected evaluation off the face normal: exact for linear fields and second order on a uniformly sheared wall cell; on a cell whose neighbour does not lie along the wall face first order with 1/19 of the error (default 9/19), as derived. Callers listed with one measurement each: rest walls of a rigid column low by 1.2505e-2 (4e-6 corrected); the tree's force reports low by 1/(2N) = 2.5e-2 on a moving wall; the rotor wall of the sliding step misses 0.41 g dn (0.06 corrected); cosim already defaults to the prescribed gradient. Listing for the default: no registered hash moves (baseline_hashes and case_hashes_w48u hold no six-DOF case); with the default flipped the six-DOF results move (T4 -5e-4, ADR 0266's piston -5.0e-3 in frequency, SP -1.0e-3) and ADR 0266's R1, R2, E1, E2 fail. Without the table nothing changes (K0 unedited; a table with "extrapolated" equals no table bit for bit). Six mutations, all caught. Disclosed: the rest-wall check missed as registered because its case text jumped by X in the first step; corrected by amendment before the corrected run, the miss kept as a record. Open, the maintainer's: the default (ADR 0269 Q1), the table (Q2), the force reports on moving walls (Q3), the sliding step (Q4), skewed walls (Q5). STATUS recorded PARTIAL by the lead: the registered check AU1 missed (a defect of the case text) and passed only as AU1b after amendment; done is the maintainer's call. The default flip (Q1) waits for the maintainer's approval of the listed changes. ACCEPTED AS DONE by the maintainer in person on 2026-11-12 (the amended check). Default flip (Q1) approved by the maintainer in person on 2026-11-12, together with ADR 0342 Q1 (F-440). Default flip applied (ADR 0346, 2026-11-12): without the key the body force takes prescribed_gradient in both schemes; wall_pressure = "extrapolated" gives the old bits (digests equal to the old tree's); no registered hash moved; the predicted moves measured: SP 1.001307 -> 1.000264, ADR 0266's strong piston 1.005081 -> 1.000042 (turning 0.92469), T4 x 0.506503 at 92 steps, ADR 0266 L stop 34 -> 35; ADR 0266 E1, E2 now compare with strong_step_with(PrescribedGradient), its R1, R2 and ADR 0269 A2 write the old value; a coupling table that leaves the key out now writes wall_pressure = "prescribed_gradient".

title: Overset: a non-uniform closed-form flow on a warped three-dimensional overset mesh
acceptance: A three-dimensional closed-form flow (a divergence-free linear field u = A x with its pressure, or a decaying three-dimensional vortex with a known solution) on the set-ups B3 and B3d of ADR 0251 with the component moving as in ADR 0255: the error of the calculated and fringe cells on B3d at most twice that on B3, with the default and with the quadratic donor interpolation, and continuity of the calculated cells within 1e-9 at every step.
note: From ADR 0255, recommendation taken on the maintainer's standing instruction of 2026-11-11. ADR 0264, 2026-11-12: PARTIAL. The linear shear u = U0 + 0.5 a (b . (x - x0)) with a = (1, 2, 1)/sqrt(6), b = (0, 1, -2)/sqrt(5), U0 = (1, 0.5, 0.25) (an exact steady Navier-Stokes solution with zero pressure for every viscosity, all six background patches Dirichlet) on B3 and B3d with the component moving as in ADR 0255, 40 steps: continuity of the calculated cells 1.9e-14 or less at every step with the default and the quadratic donor interpolation (met), the stencils reproduce the field to 3e-15, the planar operators keep it to 2e-14 (K2, K3); the error of the calculated and fringe cells 1.36e-2 on B3d against 8.7e-4 on B3, ratio 15.6 with either interpolation, against the limit 2 (missed, kept as ignored known-miss records). Diagnosed by measurement: the single warped mesh, not the coupling. The warped parts alone have 9.6e-3 (background at rest) and 1.21e-2 (component moving), 0.89 of the overset error, and the worst cell of the overset run is the worst cell of the warped component alone; the discrete operators leave a residual of the exact field of 0.14 (convection, skewness of the central face value), 0.025 (diffusion without the non-orthogonal correction) and 0.075 per second (continuity) on the warped cells, zero on the planar ones. Control (weights times 1.001: 1.85e-3) held; three mutations caught. No library change. Limits: one flow, one warp, one motion, 40 steps; B3's own error is 4 times that of the planar component alone (not diagnosed). Follow-ups: F-368, F-369.

title: Co-simulation protocol over the solver service
acceptance: The calls of docs/cosimulation-protocol.md (describe, time, checkpoint, restore, forces, advance) are served by the JSON-RPC service under a new protocol version; an out-of-process mock structural participant driven over TCP reproduces ADR 0256 A1 and A2 (every step converged, omega_m/omega within 0.5 percent and 3 percent) and the same displacements as the in-process run to 1e-12; a dropped connection or a participant error stops the step with a located error and both sides restored; the protocol document is versioned; existing service tests and case hashes are unchanged.
note: Merged 2026-11-12. DONE pending acceptance (ADR 0345, 2026-11-12; registered before the code, two amendments). The calls of docs/cosimulation-protocol.md are served by the JSON-RPC service for participants that the embedding program hosts (rcfd_api::cosim_service: Service::host_fluid, host_structure, each participant on its own thread so it need not be Send; rcfd serve hosts none; no case key, CLI or MCP change): methods cosim.list, cosim.open, cosim.describe, cosim.time, cosim.checkpoint, cosim.restore, cosim.forces, cosim.advance, plain JSON numbers that cross bit for bit (serde_json float_roundtrip), error codes 1005 (the participant error, its own message) and 1006 (no such participant). Service protocol 1.1: the identifier rcfd-service/1 is kept (the pinned tests are unedited), service.info gains protocol_version 1.1 and cosim rcfd-cosim/1; both protocol pages are versioned. The coupler is the unchanged cosim::coupled_step driven with the proxies RemoteStructure and RemoteFluid (TCP). A lease per participant (cosim.open) refuses requests left over from an old connection; a proxy whose connection is lost fails at once except restore, which reconnects once and restores the participant, so a dropped connection ends the step with the located error and both sides at the start of the step. Measured on the model problem of ADR 0256 with the mock structure in a second process: every one of 650 steps converged, 7 to 10 iterations (mean 8.766), omega_m/omega 0.998618 and 1.011453, and the displacements of every node at every step equal to the in-process run bit for bit (limit 1e-12 X), also with both participants remote (100 steps); a participant error (structure in the other process, fluid hosted) and a dropped connection (cut before the request, after the reply, between steps, fluid or structure) each give an error naming participant, time and iteration with 0 bits of either state changed and the next step equal to the reference; a killed participant process gives the located error in 2.1 s with the fluid restored and the failed reconnection reported; refusals with their codes; a control with springs stiffer by 1e-9 is seen (4e-9 X). Amendment 1: the first transport cost 2 ms per call (lines written in pieces), now 0.05 ms (one write per line, TCP_NODELAY on accepted connections; no byte changes). Amendment 2: the 650-step out-of-process tests are ignored heavy records (minutes on the loaded machine; run twice, identical), the gate runs the 100-step both-remote comparison and the failure tests. Existing service, CLI and MCP suites and the case hashes pass unedited; seven mutations each failed their tests. Not delivered: participants built from a case or hosted by rcfd serve, structural elements in describe, authentication, a test of a call outlasting the time-out. Open: ADR 0345 Q1 to Q5. Follow-up F-444 (ADR 0380, 2026-11-12): participants from the case hosted by rcfd serve --cosim, elements in describe, one write per service::Client request (ADR 0345 Q3, Q4, Q5).

title: Quasi-Newton acceleration of the coupled iteration
acceptance: A least-squares (quasi-Newton) update of the nodal force from the residual history of the step, opt-in beside the fixed and Aitken factors, converges the model problem of ADR 0256 to 1e-8 in at most 7 iterations per step and 6 or fewer on average (Aitken: 8.8), gives the same frequencies within 1e-6, and with one rigid node needs no more iterations than Aitken; registered before the run with the plain fixed point as the diverging control.
note: DONE pending acceptance (ADR 0261, 2026-11-12; registered before the code, no amendment). Opt-in fsi::Relaxation::LeastSquares { initial, filter } (CouplingSettings::least_squares) in cosim::coupled_step: after a first update relaxed with initial, the next nodal force is the flow's force plus the combination of the step's output differences whose residual differences best cancel the current residual (interface quasi-Newton with a least-squares inverse Jacobian), solved by Householder QR newest column first with a filter that drops a column whose part outside the newer ones is below 1e-2 of its norm (no vanishing pivot); no reuse across steps; fsi::strong_step refuses it. Derived: on a linear map it is GMRES plus one pass, exact at iteration d + 2. Measured on the model problem of ADR 0256 (6 nodes, 16 faces, tolerance 1e-8): every one of 650 steps converged, at most 7 iterations (one step), mean 5.980 (Aitken 8.766, histogram identical to ADR 0256), frequencies equal to Aitken's within 3.1e-10; one rigid node (SPm1): the same 301 iterations as Aitken, the same count in every step, positions bit-identical; the plain fixed point diverges (510.85 in 10). Mock affine and cubic fluids check the termination count and the equality with Aitken's secant. Existing suites cosim_f139, strong_fsi_f251, added_mass_f351 and the baseline hashes pass unedited; four mutations caught. Open: ADR 0261 Q1 to Q3.

title: Interface mapping by geometric search and radial-basis functions, with an unmapped-value policy
acceptance: InterfaceMap weights are built from the two interface meshes alone (nearest-element projection and a radial-basis interpolation) for a planar and a cylindrical wall with non-matching meshes; rigid translation and rotation are reproduced to 1e-12, resultant force, moment and work are conserved to 1e-12 by the transposed map, a wall point outside the structure is refused or mapped by a stated policy, and the model problem of ADR 0256 gives the same frequencies within 1e-3 with the built weights.
note: PARTIAL (ADR 0263, 2026-11-12; registered before the code, one amendment after the registered run). Opt-in cosim::interface_rows and InterfaceMap::build build the weights from the structure's nodes and elements (points, segments, triangles, quadrilaterals) and the fluid's wall points alone; nothing calls them. Derived: scalar weights reproduce every rigid motion iff each row sums to 1 and reproduces the point's coordinates; the transpose then conserves resultant and moment, and conserves work for any weights. Nearest-element projection with an offset correction on the ring of elements (exact on a curved wall; plain barycentric selectable); radial basis with Wendland's C2 function of support 3 h and a degree-1 polynomial in the nodes' own directions, dense Cholesky with a Schur complement, condition estimate (8 to 85 here). Policy: a wall point farther than max_distance is refused (the default; the message names point and distance) or moves with its nearest structural point (Unmapped::Nearest). Measured on a planar and a cylindrical wall with non-matching meshes: rigid translation and rotation to 1.3e-15, resultant, moment and work to 1.4e-16 (both methods); without the correction the cylinder loses 5e-3 of the rotation and 1e-4 of the moment; outside points follow their nearest points to 9e-16 and the moment changes exactly as predicted. Model problem of ADR 0256: the projection gives the piecewise-linear rows to 1e-16 and the same frequencies (1.4e-15); the radial basis shifts them by -5.2e-4 and +1.9e-4 (limit 1e-3). cosim_f139, cosim_f361 and the baseline hashes pass unedited; eight mutations caught. Partial because the registered check E1 accepted two coincident nodes with the radial basis (an absolute pivot test); amendment 1 refuses pivots below 2 n eps a_jj, and E1b passes with it. Protocol option in docs/cosimulation-protocol.md. Open: ADR 0263 Q1 to Q3. ACCEPTED AS DONE by the maintainer in person on 2026-11-12 (the amended check).

title: Second-order immersed forcing: the single PISO corrector
acceptance: The stop of DFG 2D-2 on M2 with one PISO corrector and a second-order immersed flux face of weight above 1 (ADR 0254 D11: step 34 with the bounded form, step 126 with weights up to 2) is explained by a registered measurement, and the setting either runs 200 steps or is refused with a located message; two correctors are unaffected.
note: PARTIAL (ADR 0374, 2026-11-12), in the library. From ADR 0254 question 3. The stop of DFG 2D-2 on M2 with one PISO corrector was reproduced to the step (weights up to 2: step 126; bounded form with theta_min 0.1: 46; bounded: 34; the first-order forcing and weights of at most 1 run) and narrowed by registered measurements: it depends on the time step (the bounded form with one corrector runs 200 steps at dt 5e-4 and 2.5e-4, unlike the large-weight stop of F-355), it grows at the first fluid cells of the body, alternating from step to step, and two correctors damp it (largest flux-face velocity 0.87 to 0.21 over 34 steps). The hypothesis that it is the pressure-lag instability of the single corrector (the reversed flux face returning the lagged pressure gradient reversed) was tested with an opt-in pressure-lag map that includes the face-flux reconstruction (PimpleSolver::immersed_lag) and is not supported: with one corrector the map gives 1.13 to 1.20 at step 2 for all five forcings, the two that run included, with or without the reconstruction (a mode at the body, for the first-order forcing in a solid cell), and below 0.1 with two correctors. Delivered: the setting is refused at step 1 with a located message (ImmersedForcing::single_corrector_face; quantity immersed flux corrector; the fluid cell and the weight of the reversed face; names ADR 0374 and n_correctors >= 2) wherever a flux face has an image or a weight above 1, with one corrector and one outer iteration, unless flux_weight_check is off; two correctors, the first-order forcing, weights of at most 1 and PIMPLE are not refused, and the defaults are bit-identical (fingerprints of three runs and two estimates, the immersed tests, baseline_hashes). Six mutations caught. Partial by the registered rule: four known misses (the lag map of the settings that run below one; the map without the reconstruction below one; the raise of the map by the reconstruction; the faces leading the growth). Open (ADR 0374 Q1 to Q4): the form of the refusal (a smaller step also runs), PIMPLE with one corrector, the mechanism (a linearisation of the whole step), the lag estimate at an immersed body (above one for a setting that runs).

title: Second-order immersed forcing: one constructor with bounded weights
acceptance: `build_second_order` builds the bounded form of ADR 0254, the refusal of the unbounded form is removed, and the checks of ADR 0234 (A1, V1 to V4) and ADR 0239 are measured again and reported next to the old numbers.
note: NEEDS THE USER. From ADR 0254 questions 1 and 2. Needs the maintainer's decision: it changes the recorded numbers of a merged opt-in (circular Couette e(96) 4.243e-4 to 4.232e-4, face-flux error 1.612e-4 to 3.078e-4; the DFG 2D-1 values asserted to nine digits in immersed_unsteady_force_f346.rs).

title: Mesh-speed time step as the default of moving compressible tree runs
acceptance: Every limit not stated here is registered in the ADR before the run. Needs the maintainer's lift of the bit-identical default for moving compressible tree runs (ADR 0207 Q2 (b)). The moving compressible step of the case tree takes max_dt_ale() by default, with [dynamic_mesh.compressible] time_step = "absolute" restoring the step of ADR 0191; the library loops of ADR 0191's equality tests are restated by a registered edit (the old tests kept as ignored records); a tree run equals the library run to 1e-12 for both values; fixed-mesh compressible runs and incompressible runs are bit-identical (baseline hashes and ADR 0191's D0 unchanged); the CFL number of the piston cell of the Mach 0.2 piston stays within the registered bound of the set value over the stroke.
note: From ADR 0257 question 1 (ADR 0207 Q2 (b)). NEEDS THE USER: it changes the bits of existing moving compressible runs.

title: Consistent correctors: the case table carries every flag
acceptance: `[solver.consistent_correctors]` has the keys enabled, periodic, body_force, non_orthogonal, component_diagonal and face_jump with defaults that leave every existing case's hash and result unchanged; sim.rs sets `PimpleSettings::set_consistent` from it and reports each `ConsistentRefusal` of `ConsistentCorrectors::conflicts` at `solver.consistent_correctors.<flag>`; overset.rs reads `consistent_flags().enabled`; the three older PimpleSettings fields are removed with amendments to ADR 0214 and ADR 0223; the schema golden edit is made only with the maintainer's approval; defaults bit-identical.
note: The remaining half of F-322 (ADR 0258). NEEDS THE USER before merge: the schema golden edit.

title: Consistent correctors: the new combinations with periodic faces
acceptance: Non-orthogonal correctors, the component diagonal and face jumps are each accepted with periodic pressure faces under the consistent correctors once a registered periodic steady identity (velocity, and pressure with the mean removed against the default's own drift) is met for it; a combination that misses stays refused with its located message; defaults bit-identical.
note: PARTIAL (ADR 0360, 2026-11-12). From ADR 0258 question 3, recommendation taken on the maintainer's standing instruction of 2026-11-11. The consistent correctors accept non-orthogonal correctors, the component diagonal and face jumps with periodic pressure faces under the opt-in PimpleSettings::consistent_periodic_extensions (default false; ConsistentRefusal::PERIODIC_EXTENSIONS, ConsistentCorrectors::conflicts_extended / validate_extended; conflicts and validate unchanged, so ADR 0258's V2 and R3 pass unedited). No numerical term is added: the default has no non-orthogonal part on a coupled face and face jumps act on internal faces only, so the compensations of X1, X2, X3 and E2 together already cover every face. Periodic steady identity on ADR 0223's periodic channel (velocity 1e-10 U0; mean-removed pressure against max(1e-10, 2x the default's own drift) of the range): non-orthogonal correctors on a 26.6-degree shear 1.5e-12 U0 and 7.1e-11; face jumps 2.1e-12 and 4.2e-11 (also from the hook); the component diagonal 3.9e-12 and 5.2e-10 (drift 5.6e-10); all three together 1.4e-12 and 1.2e-11; ADR 0223's E2 alone passes the same limit (2.5e-10 against 6.6e-10). Transients differ from the default by 2e-6 to 2e-5 U0 at dt 0.001. The other rows stay refused with their located messages (moving mesh, gradient options, periodic faces without the periodic flag). Nine mutations caught. Defaults bit-identical (seven fingerprints recorded on 2ad9dcb9, the rcfd-fv transient suites, baseline_hashes, case_hashes_w48u). Why partial: the registered set-up checks of the component-diagonal and all-together channels missed (3000 steps do not reach a steady state with a symmetry plane, whose start-up decays at nu (pi/2H)^2); their identities were met only after amendment 1 (8000 steps). The opt-in is not yet folded into ConsistentCorrectors (ADR 0360 Q1) and there is no case key.

title: Overset: opt-in skewness and non-orthogonal corrections in the overset step
acceptance: An opt-in of the overset step that adds the explicit non-orthogonal correction to the momentum diffusion and the pressure Laplacian and a skewness correction to the central face value and the Rhie-Chow face flux; with it the linear shear of ADR 0264 on B3d with the component moving has an error of the calculated and fringe cells at most twice that on B3 with the default and with the quadratic donor interpolation, continuity of the calculated cells within 1e-9 at every step, the uniform flow of ADR 0255 within 1e-10, and the defaults bit-identical.
note: From ADR 0264 Q1, recommendation taken on the maintainer's standing instruction of 2026-11-11. ADR 0367, 2026-11-12: DONE (pending acceptance). Opt-in OversetSolver::set_geometry_corrections(true): the face flux of a cell field (the Rhie-Chow flux of HbyA, the refreshed and the initial flux, the ddt_correction interpolation) is the exact flux of a linear field through the mesh's triangulated faces (skewness term plus a warp tensor for non-planar faces, least-squares gradients donor-interpolated in fringe cells), the convected face value carries the same correction, the momentum diffusion the explicit non-orthogonal correction, and phiHbyA the explicit non-orthogonal flux of the pressure (shared by the pressure equation and the flux). With it the linear shear of ADR 0264 on B3d with the component moving has E 9.97e-4 (default stencils) and 1.005e-3 (quadratic) against 8.72e-4 on B3: ratios 1.14 and 1.15 (limit 2; 15.6 without), whether B3 runs with the opt-in or the default; continuity 1.9e-14 or less every step; the uniform flow of ADR 0255 within 7.5e-15 (velocity) and 1.3e-13 (pressure). The corrected operators keep the exact field to round-off in continuity, diffusion and the pressure flux (from 0.075, 0.025, 0.27) and to 1.8e-3 in convection (second order, from 0.14). Defaults bit-identical: eight fingerprints equal before and after, baseline_hashes and the 14 overset test files and the rcfd-fv lib tests pass unedited. Control held; seven mutations caught by their registered checks. Refused with BDF2, a prescribed fringe flux and rhie_chow_step_consistent. Limits: one linear flow (constant pressure), one warp, one resolution; planar boundary faces; the rest of the error on B3d is the coupling's (warped meshes alone 3.1e-4), the open excess of ADR 0264 Q2.

title: Overset: the coupling's share of the error of a linear field on the planar B3
acceptance: On the planar B3 with the linear shear of ADR 0264 (error 8.7e-4 against 2.1e-4 for the planar component alone moving), the share of the fringe pressure, of the mass offset and of the flux of the faces that change kind measured separately, each by a run that removes it, with the cause of the excess named or the excess shown to be the time error of the turning mesh.
note: From ADR 0264 question 2, recommendation taken on the maintainer's standing instruction of 2026-11-11. Low priority. ADR 0340 (F-349) found that the fringe velocity is imposed softly on the calculated cells (the following coefficient a_c of 0.5 to 0.83 and the kink relation dJ = -(16 nu / 3 h) D at the fringe faces); both are candidates for the measurements of this item. ADR 0347 (F-445), 2026-11-12: the following coefficient a_c carries the decay of the response over one cell (0.60 at once on a coarse mesh even when the flux is imposed exactly); where the hardness of the imposition is meant, measure the flux defect or abs(a_m - (1 + a_c) / 2). The opt-in OversetSolver::set_fringe_flux(PrescribedOwnGradient) removes the defect and is available as a switch for this item's measurements; it has no accuracy check with a moving component yet.

title: Crate rcfd-fem: the data model of a solid model and the structured builders
acceptance: Every limit not stated here is registered in the ADR before the run. A new crate rcfd-fem (dependencies rcfd-core, rcfd-mesh, rcfd-linalg only) holds the solid data model; the workspace graph test passes with the one registered line for the new crate, the architecture page lists it, and nothing existing changes (baseline hashes unchanged). On a box of n^3 hexahedra and on its six-tetrahedra split, for n = 1, 2, 5 with unequal edge lengths: every element has a positive Jacobian at every node, the element volumes sum to the box volume within 1e-12 relative, the area of each of the six face sets equals the box face within 1e-12, and every interior face is shared by exactly two elements; the quadratic upgrade has (nodes + edges) nodes and each mid-edge node is the mean of its two ends within 1e-15; an inverted element, a node repeated in an element, an empty set, E <= 0 and a Poisson ratio outside (-1, 0.5) are each refused with an error naming the element or the key.
note: DONE pending acceptance, merged 2026-11-12. Structural solver, basic tier (plan ADR 0270). ADR 0271, 2026-11-12: the crate rcfd-fem in layer 2 (rcfd-core, rcfd-mesh, rcfd-linalg only; the one approved line of workspace_graph.rs, the architecture page) with the solid data model as validated data through constructors (private fields, non-exhaustive enums and variants): SolidMesh with Tet4, Hex8, Tet10 blocks in the VTK node order (to be confirmed by ADR 0278), outward local faces, node, element and surface sets, and refusals naming the element, node, block, set or key (node out of range, node repeated, det J <= 0 at any node, empty or duplicate sets); DofMap (the only place that knows the unknowns per node), Material (isotropic elastic: e > 0, nu in (-1, 0.5), density >= 0), Constraint, Load (plain data on named sets: nodal force, traction, pressure, gravity, centrifugal, nodal body force, temperature), SolidModel, SolidResult; the builders hex_box, tet_box (Kuhn six-tetrahedra split) and upgrade_to_tet10; the module stubs of the tier. On boxes of 1, 8 and 125 hexahedra and their 6, 48 and 750 tetrahedra (edges 1.3, 0.7, 2.1): det J > 0 at every node, volume within 1.9e-15 relative (limit 1e-12), each face set's area within 7.6e-16 (limit 1e-12), outward normals, boundary faces exactly the six sets and interior faces shared by two oppositely oriented elements; the quadratic upgrade has 27, 125, 1331 nodes (nodes plus edges, counted and closed form) with every mid-edge node at the mean of its ends exactly (limit 1e-15) and passes the same geometry checks; inverted elements, a repeated node, empty sets, E <= 0 and nu outside (-1, 0.5) are refused naming the element or the key. Baseline hashes unchanged; ten mutations caught.

title: Solid mesh from the existing meshes: polyhedral mesh, tetrahedral mesher output, patches as surface sets, curved edges
acceptance: Every limit not stated here is registered in the ADR before the run. A SolidMesh built from box_mesh (hexahedra), from the annulus generator (hexahedra with curved faces) and from the tetrahedral mesher's output of a box surface has the node and element counts of its source, element volumes summing to the source volume within 1e-12 relative (tetrahedra, planar hexahedra) or 1e-3 (annulus, registered from the chord error), one surface set per patch whose area equals the patch area within 1e-12 and whose face normals point along the source's outward area vectors; a prism, pyramid or general polyhedral cell is refused naming the cell. With mid-edge nodes projected onto the cylinder walls of a quarter annulus the projected nodes lie on their radius within 1e-14 and the volume error of the quadratic tetrahedra falls at an observed order of at least 3 under refinement.
note: Structural solver, basic tier (plan ADR 0270, 2026-11-12). Size M. Stub ADR 0272; the registration is written by the implementation agent before any code. ADR 0271 (2026-11-12): upgrade_to_tet10 returns the list of mid-edge nodes with their ends (for the projection); a moved mesh is rebuilt through SolidMesh::new and add_block, which re-validate det J at every node; box surface and node sets are named xmin to zmax as the rcfd_mesh::gen patches.

title: Element library: linear tetrahedron, trilinear hexahedron, quadratic tetrahedron; isotropic elasticity matrix
acceptance: Every limit not stated here is registered in the ADR before the run. For Tet4, Hex8 (2 x 2 x 2 Gauss) and Tet10, on the reference element and on randomly distorted ones (registered seed): the shape functions sum to 1 and their derivatives to 0 within 1e-14 at 100 random points; the analytic derivatives agree with central differences within 1e-7; each quadrature rule integrates every monomial up to its stated degree within 1e-13; the element stiffness is symmetric within 1e-13 of its norm, gives no force for the six rigid-body motions within 1e-11 relative and has rank n - 6; each of the six unit strain states gives the strain energy V/2 eps:D:eps within 1e-12 relative; D gives stress E eps in uniaxial stress and G gamma in shear within 1e-14.
note: DONE pending acceptance, merged 2026-11-12. Structural solver, basic tier (plan ADR 0270). ADR 0273, 2026-11-12: rcfd_fem::element with the Element trait (shape functions, derivatives from ElementKind::shape_gradients of ADR 0271, the isoparametric point with J, det J and physical gradients, integration points with w det J, stiffness with its own or a given rule computed in both triangles, strain at a point; refusals by key: coordinates, displacement, jacobian) for Tet4 (1 point), Hex8 (2 x 2 x 2 Gauss) and Tet10 (4 points), element_for(kind); rcfd_fem::quadrature with tet_1, tet_4, tet_14 (degree 5, positive weights, constants by Newton on the invariant moment equations) and Gauss 1 to 3 on the cube; rcfd_fem::material with the isotropic D and the constitutive call stress(strain, point context, state) returning stress and tangent. On the reference elements and 10 randomly distorted ones of each kind (Tet10: 10 curved and 5 straight-sided; seed 0xF372_0273): partition of unity within 2.2e-16 and derivative sums within 7.0e-16 (limit 1e-14), central differences within 7.1e-11 (limit 1e-7), every monomial up to each rule's degree within 1.8e-15 (limit 1e-13, and each rule misses degree d + 1), stiffness symmetric within 1.9e-16 (limit 1e-13), rigid-body force within 6.2e-17 relative (limit 1e-11), rank n - 6 by rcfd_linalg::eigen with the threshold 1e-9 lambda_max (rigid modes at 1.5e-16, the seventh at 1.4e-3 or more), strain energy of the six unit strains within 7.4e-16 (limit 1e-12); D gives E eps in uniaxial stress within 6.0e-16 and G gamma in shear exactly (nu = 0, 0.3, 0.45, -0.5; limit 1e-14). Twelve mutations caught.

title: Sparse direct solver for symmetric positive definite matrices (envelope L D L^T after reverse Cuthill-McKee)
acceptance: Every limit not stated here is registered in the ADR before the run. rcfd-linalg gains a direct factorisation of a symmetric positive definite CsrMatrix, reusable for many right-hand sides: on the 7-point Laplacian of 12^3 unknowns, on a randomly permuted copy (registered seed) and on a matrix with three unknowns per node built from it (Kronecker product with a 3 x 3 SPD block) the relative residual is <= 1e-12 and the solution agrees with cg (tolerance 1e-13) within 1e-9; the permuted matrix factorises with an envelope no larger than 1.2 times that of the unpermuted one; a zero or negative pivot, an unsymmetric matrix and a non-finite entry are refused with the row; the result is bit-identical for 1 and 8 threads; a heavy record factorises 30^3 unknowns and reports time and memory. No existing function of the crate changes.
note: DONE pending acceptance, merged 2026-11-12. Structural solver, basic tier (plan ADR 0270). ADR 0274, 2026-11-12: rcfd_linalg::skyline, envelope L D L^T after reverse Cuthill-McKee (the existing rcm_order unchanged), factor once and solve many, located refusals (non-square, non-finite entry, unsymmetric pair, zero or negative or numerically zero pivot with row and position), the NonZero rule and inertia() for ADR 0283, orderings Rcm (default), Natural, Given and SmallerEnvelope. 7-point Laplacian 12^3, a permuted copy and its Kronecker product with a 3 x 3 SPD block: relative residual 7.4e-16 to 1.3e-15 (limit 1e-12), agreement with cg 8.3e-14 to 1.1e-13 (limit 1e-9); the permuted matrix's envelope 141 867 = 0.618 of the natural order's 229 691 (limit 1.2), within the derived level-structure bound 271 986; bit-identical for 1 and 8 threads; inertia of shifted Laplacians as the closed form. Heavy records: 30^3 Laplacian factor 0.79 s, 109 MB; the Hex8 20^3 box sparsity (27 783 unknowns) 5.6 s and 295 MB in natural order, 34.9 s and 452 MB in RCM order. Measured rate 4.6e9 multiply-adds per second: reach about 1e5 unknowns in minutes, memory not the limit. Nine mutations caught (two after amendment 1). Existing rcfd-linalg tests unedited and passing.

title: Assembly, displacement constraints, nodal forces and the linear static solve; patch test
acceptance: Every limit not stated here is registered in the ADR before the run. The stiffness of a SolidModel is assembled into a CsrMatrix deterministically (bit-identical for 1 and 8 threads) and is symmetric within 1e-13 of its norm; displacement constraints per node and component, zero or not, are imposed by symmetric elimination and the reactions recovered. Patch test (Tet4, Hex8, Tet10; a box whose interior nodes are displaced by a registered seed; boundary displacements of a linear field with all six strains non-zero): interior displacements within 1e-10 of the field, relative to its maximum. Uniaxial tension by nodal forces with statically determinate constraints: elongation F L/(E A) and lateral contraction nu times the axial strain within 1e-10. The reactions balance the applied forces and their moment within 1e-10; a model that leaves a rigid-body motion free is refused with a message saying so, a constraint on a missing node with its id.
note: Structural solver, basic tier (plan ADR 0270). ADR 0275, 2026-11-12: rcfd_fem::assemble (pattern from node adjacency, element matrices by std threads in batches and a sequential scatter in element order, so bit-identical for any thread count; stiffness, stiffness_with(threads) and the generic hook assemble_with, which locates element errors as FemError::Element); rcfd_fem::constraint (Prescribed per node and component from Constraint::Displacement and per-node lists, missing node or component refused with its id, conflicting values refused; free rigid-body motions refused per connected part from the 6 x 6 Gram matrix of the rigid modes at the prescribed components, threshold 1e-10 lambda_max; symmetric elimination by removal, reduce and ReducedSystem::expand; reactions K u - f); rcfd_fem::loads::nodal_load_vector (nodal forces from the model and per node, every other load refused by name); rcfd_fem::solve (solve_static and solve_static_with, SkylineLdlt by default with a pivot test d <= 1e-10 a_ii for mechanisms, CG with Jacobi as the alternative). Stiffness symmetric within 2.1e-16 (limit 1e-13), bit-identical for 1 and 8 threads; patch test on boxes with interior nodes displaced (seed 0xF374_0275) and a linear field with six non-zero strains: interior error 4.4e-16, 6.1e-16, 1.2e-15 for Tet4, Hex8, Tet10 (limit 1e-10); uniaxial tension by nodal forces on a 3-2-1 support: elongation within 1.1e-13 and lateral contraction within 6.4e-12 (limit 1e-10); reactions balance forces and moments within 2.4e-15 (limit 1e-10); free rigid-body motions (a roller plane, a 3-2-1 set less one, collinear supports, a disjoint part) refused with the count and an example motion, a constraint on a missing node with its id, a hinge mechanism refused by the pivot test. Twelve mutations, eleven caught (M10 after amendment 1), M6 survives as the rule allows. STATUS recorded PARTIAL by the lead: mutation M10 (nodal force keeps only x) survived the registered run (R1 balanced against the library's own load vector) and is caught only by R3, added by amendment 1 after that run; done is the maintainer's call.

title: Surface and body loads: traction, pressure, gravity, centrifugal load of a rotating part, body force field
acceptance: Every limit not stated here is registered in the ADR before the run. Consistent nodal loads for surface traction, pressure (positive pressing on the solid), gravity, the centrifugal load rho omega^2 r_perp about a given axis, and a body force field, for Tet4, Hex8 and Tet10. Resultants on a box: a uniform pressure on the closed surface gives zero force and moment within 1e-12 p A L; the traction resultant is t A, gravity rho V g and the centrifugal resultant rho omega^2 V r_c (r_c the centroid's distance from the axis), each within 1e-12. Closed forms with nu = 0, displacements only: hanging bar, u(x) = rho g (L x - x^2/2)/E: Tet10 nodal error <= 1e-9 relative, Hex8 and Tet4 tip displacement within 1 percent at 8 elements along; rotating radial bar clamped on the axis: tip displacement rho omega^2 L^3/(3 E) within 1 percent (Tet10 at 8, Hex8 at 16 elements along); thin rotating ring (thickness/radius 0.02): radial displacement rho omega^2 r^3/E within 2 percent.
note: DONE pending acceptance, merged 2026-11-12. Structural solver, basic tier (plan ADR 0270). Resultants on a box with moved interior nodes, Tet4, Hex8, Tet10: closed-surface pressure force and moment within 4.4e-17 and 1.3e-17 (limit 1e-12 p A, p A L), traction t A, gravity rho V g, centrifugal rho omega^2 V r_c about an oblique axis and a linear body force field within 9.8e-16 (limit 1e-12); per-node loads against the closed forms within 9.1e-16.
