title: Stress and strain recovery: integration-point, element and nodal values; von Mises and principal stresses
acceptance: Every limit not stated here is registered in the ADR before the run. Strain and stress at integration points, element means and nodal averages; von Mises stress, principal stresses with directions, strain energy. For 1000 random symmetric tensors (registered seed) the principal values from the routine agree with an independent method (Jacobi rotations against the closed trigonometric form) within 1e-12 of the tensor norm, are ordered, have orthonormal directions within 1e-12 and are unchanged by a random rotation of the tensor within 1e-12; von Mises equals |s| in uniaxial stress, sqrt(3) tau in pure shear and 0 for a hydrostatic state within 1e-14 of the norm; a tensor with repeated roots gives finite values. On the patch test of the static solve every recovered stress equals D eps within 1e-10; the strain energy equals half the work of the loads within 1e-10 for a uniaxial and a bending load.
note: Structural solver, basic tier (plan ADR 0270). ADR 0277, 2026-11-12: rcfd_fem::recover. IntegrationPointField (compute(model, displacement), from_result) with the position, weight w det J, strain B u and stress D eps at every point of each element's stiffness rule; element_means, element_strain_energy and strain_energy (sum w det J eps . sigma / 2); attach puts strain and stress into SolidResult; extrapolation_matrix (a polynomial space fitted to the rule's points: constant for Tet4, linear for Tet10, trilinear for Hex8), element_nodal_values and nodal_average (volume-weighted over an element set or all elements; a node joining two different materials is refused naming the node and both sets); tensor_norm, von_mises, principal (values descending with orthonormal directions: the closed trigonometric form for the separated root, its direction by the largest cross product of rows of C - b I, the other two by one exact 2 x 2 Jacobi rotation in the orthogonal plane) and principal_values_trigonometric (the bare closed form). 1000 random tensors (seed 0xF376_0277): routine against rcfd_linalg's Jacobi 7.1e-16 of the norm and the bare closed form 1.2e-15 (limit 1e-12), all ordered, directions orthonormal within 8.9e-16, a random rotation changes the values by 1.3e-15 (limit 1e-12); von Mises uniaxial 0, pure shear 2.7e-16, hydrostatic 0 (limit 1e-14); 57 repeated-root tensors (zero, hydrostatic, uniaxial, double roots, rotated hydrostatic, near-repeated rotated) finite, ordered, orthonormal within 6.7e-16 and within 1.1e-15 of the exact roots (the bare closed form 6.8e-9). Patch test of ADR 0275: stress and strain at the points, element means and nodal averages equal D eps and eps within 3.2e-14 (limit 1e-10). Strain energy equals half the work of the loads within 2.6e-12 (Hex8) and 1.5e-11 (Tet10, the residual of the direct solve on a slender model) for a uniaxial and a bending load (limit 1e-10); uniaxial energy equals sigma^2 V/(2E) within 2.1e-14. Eleven mutations caught. STATUS recorded PARTIAL by the lead: the registered R1 test stopped at its count assertion (the registration listed 54 repeated-root tensors for a list of 57) and passed only as the corrected test of amendment 1, written after that run; no limit changed; done is the maintainer's call.

title: VTK output of a solid result: finite-element cells with point and cell data
acceptance: Every limit not stated here is registered in the ADR before the run. rcfd-io gains a writer of an unstructured grid of finite elements from plain arrays (VTK cell types 10, 12 and 24, point data and cell data); the existing writers are unchanged and their tests pass unedited. rcfd-post writes a SolidResult through it: displacement at the nodes, nodal von Mises and principal stresses, the six stress components per element, reactions. A test parses the file back: counts, offsets and cell types are consistent, every value has the bits that were written, and a box under uniform strain read back has displacement eps x at every node within 1e-15; a field of the wrong length is refused by name.
note: DONE pending acceptance, merged 2026-11-12. Structural solver, basic tier (plan ADR 0270). ADR 0278, 2026-11-12: rcfd_io::vtk gains fe_vtu_string and write_fe_vtu, an XML .vtu (ASCII, shortest round-trip floats, the existing writer's layout) of finite-element cells from plain arrays (FeCellBlock with VTK_TETRA 10, VTK_HEXAHEDRON 12, VTK_QUADRATIC_TETRA 24; FeArray point and cell data of any component count), refusing an unknown type, a broken connectivity and an array of the wrong length, without components or with a bad name, each naming the array or key; the existing writers are unchanged (211 lines inserted before the test module, none changed) and their tests pass. rcfd_post::solid_output (rcfd-post now depends on rcfd-fem) writes a SolidResult: point arrays displacement, nodal-averaged stress, von_mises, principal_stress and principal_direction_1..3 of that tensor, reaction; cell array stress (element means); solid_fields exposes the arrays. Node orders of Tet4, Hex8 and Tet10 confirmed identical to VTK's from the vtkTetra, vtkHexahedron, vtkQuadraticHexahedron and vtkQuadraticTetra class documentation (no mapping needed; vtk_from_fem keeps the identity table); the type numbers are recalled. Tests parse the files back: counts, offsets and types consistent; every value bit-equal; a 2 x 2 x 2 box under uniform strain has displacement eps x at every node within 8.7e-19 (limit 1e-15) for Hex8, Tet4 and Tet10; documented node orders hold on the files (Tet10 midpoints exact, Hex8 edges within 9.3e-17 L); stresses equal D eps within 1.5e-15; wrong-length arrays refused by name (and a result of another mesh as displacement). Eleven mutations caught. Not checked in a viewer (the maintainer's visual check). ADR 0281 (2026-11-12): with a temperature load, IntegrationPointField::from_result already gives the thermal stress D (eps - eps_th) and field.strain() stays the total strain B u; the thermal strain per point is field.thermal_strain() (None without temperature).

title: Verification by a manufactured solution: observed order of displacement and stress for the three elements
acceptance: Every limit not stated here is registered in the ADR before the run. Manufactured solution: a smooth trigonometric displacement field on the unit cube with nu = 0.3, the body force from the analytic divergence of the stress (checked against finite differences within 1e-6), displacements prescribed on all faces, and a second case with tractions on three faces. On at least three meshes, each halving h, the observed order of the L2 displacement error over the finest pair is >= 1.8 for Tet4 and Hex8 and >= 2.7 for Tet10, the observed order of the energy-norm error is >= 0.9 and >= 1.8, and both errors fall monotonically. Negative control: a body force with the sign of the lambda term reversed gives an order below 0.5.
note: Structural solver, basic tier (plan ADR 0270). ADR 0279, 2026-11-12: manufactured solution on the unit cube (u_i = prod_j sin(k_ij x_j + phi_ij), k up to pi, nu = 0.3), body force from the analytic second derivatives, checked against central differences of the stress within 1.5e-8 (limit 1e-6); case D all faces prescribed, case T tractions sigma n on xmax, ymax, zmax by a test-side face integral (equal to Load::traction to the bit for a uniform traction); errors with 125-point rules of degree 7 (tet) and 9 per variable (hex); tests crates/rcfd-fem/tests/sb_mms.rs only. Tet4 and Hex8 on 4, 8, 16, Tet10 on 2, 4, 8 cells per edge: L2 orders over the finest pair, case D 1.979, 1.999, 2.982, case T 1.7925 (Tet4, MISSED, limit 1.8), 1.997, 2.972; energy orders D 0.994, 0.999, 1.956, T 0.975, 0.997, 1.919; all errors fall monotonically; negative control (lambda term reversed) orders -0.005 to 0.015 (limit < 0.5). Heavy record on 6, 12, 24 / 3, 6, 12 (case D, 36 501 unknowns, 108 s): 1.990, 2.000, 2.989 and 0.997, 1.000, 1.978. The Tet4 case T miss is pre-asymptotic by diagnosis (orders 1.67, 1.79, 1.92 on successive pairs, 16 -> 32 run as a diagnostic), kept as a known-miss record with the limit. Mutations: four of six caught; the body load on the stiffness rule (registered as may survive) and the one-point Hex8 stiffness survive (regular meshes hold the hourglass modes; the element tests catch it). Partial by the registered rule; done is the maintainer's call. The one-point Hex8 stiffness that survived here is caught on moved meshes by ADR 0355 (F-459). The Tet4 case T L2 clause that missed on the pair 8 -> 16 (1.7925) is met one level finer, 1.9176 on 16 -> 32, by F-458 (ADR 0365, 2026-11-12); the limit of F-378 is unchanged and its status stays partial.

title: Closed-form benchmarks: cantilever bending and the thick-walled cylinder under pressure
acceptance: Every limit not stated here is registered in the ADR before the run. Cantilever of slenderness L/h = 20 (square section, nu = 0.3, clamped root, tip shear force): the tip deflection is within 1 percent of P L^3/(3 E I) (1 + 3 E I/(kappa G A L^2)), kappa = 5/6, with Tet10 on a registered mesh, and within 5 percent with Hex8 at four elements through the thickness; the bending stress at the surface one section height from the clamp is within 3 percent of M c/I (Tet10); Tet4 on the same nodes is the registered locking control (deflection below 90 percent of the closed form). Thick-walled cylinder, b/a = 2, plane strain, internal pressure, quarter model: the radial displacement at the bore and at the outer wall is within 0.5 percent and the hoop stress at the bore within 2 percent of Lame's solution (Hex8 and Tet10 with curved edges on registered meshes), and the observed order of the radial displacement error with Hex8 is >= 1.8.
note: Structural solver, basic tier (plan ADR 0270, 2026-11-12). Size M. Stub ADR 0280; the registration is written by the implementation agent before any code.

title: Thermal strain: nodal temperature field, expansion coefficient, thermal load and stress
acceptance: Every limit not stated here is registered in the ADR before the run. With a nodal temperature field, an expansion coefficient and a reference temperature: a uniformly heated, statically determinately held box expands by alpha dT x at every node within 1e-10 with stresses below 1e-10 E alpha dT; a box held on all faces has the hydrostatic stress -E alpha dT/(1 - 2 nu) within 1e-10; a bar held at both ends with free sides has the axial stress -E alpha dT within 1e-10 (nu = 0.3); a linear temperature through the thickness of a free beam gives the curvature alpha dT/h within 1 percent and stresses below 1 percent of E alpha dT (Tet10); a model without temperature is bit-identical to the same model before this change.
note: DONE pending acceptance, merged 2026-11-12. Structural solver, basic tier (plan ADR 0270). ADR 0281, 2026-11-12: rcfd_fem::thermal: the one temperature field of a model (Load::Temperature { nodal, reference }; a second one refused naming the key 'temperature'), the isotropic thermal strain alpha (T - T_ref) (1, 1, 1, 0, 0, 0) from the nodal differences T_b - T_ref interpolated with the element's own functions, and the element load sum w B^T D eps_th on the stiffness rule (element_thermal_load); loads::nodal_load_vector adds it (the last UnsupportedLoad arm removed); recover::IntegrationPointField gives sigma = D (eps - eps_th) at the same points, keeps the thermal strain per point (thermal_strain()) and its strain energy is the elastic energy 1/2 sum w (eps - eps_th) . sigma. nu = 0.3, alpha dT = 6e-4, boxes with moved interior nodes, Tet4, Hex8, Tet10: free expansion under a 3-2-1 support u = alpha dT x within 1.1e-13 and stresses within 1.1e-13 E alpha dT (limits 1e-10); box with rollers on all faces -E alpha dT/(1 - 2 nu) within 1.4e-15; bar held at both ends with free sides sigma_xx = -E alpha dT within 5.6e-14, its lateral field and reactions within 2.0e-12; free Tet10 beam with a linear temperature through the thickness: curvature alpha dT/h within 2.8e-12 (limit 1e-2) and stresses 1.6e-12 E alpha dT (limit 1e-2); recovered stress in discrete equilibrium with the reactions for random nodal temperatures within 4.0e-15; elastic energies within 4.9e-15 of the closed forms. A model without temperature is bit-identical to d4bde1e0: FNV digests of load vector, displacement, reactions, residual and the recovered field of nine models (nodal force, all mechanical loads, a bar; three kinds) equal (test sb_thermal_bits). Nine mutations caught. ADR 0275's E3 (sb_static) and ADR 0276's X1 (sb_loads) assert the thermal refusal and fail by construction: the lead deletes both blocks (ADR 0281 remaining question 1, checked on a scratch copy as X3, X4). On merging, the lead removed the two now-obsolete refusal checks (ADR 0275 E3 in sb_static, ADR 0276 X1 in sb_loads), as ADR 0281 recommended.

title: Iterative route for larger models: CG with block Jacobi and incomplete Cholesky on the stiffness matrix
acceptance: Every limit not stated here is registered in the ADR before the run. CG on the stiffness matrix with (a) 3 x 3 block Jacobi and (b) incomplete Cholesky with zero fill on CSR and a diagonal shift on breakdown, selectable beside the direct solver: on a cantilever of about 5e3 unknowns (fast) and of at least 1e5 unknowns (heavy record) the relative residual reaches 1e-10; on the fast case the displacement agrees with the direct solution within 1e-7 relative, incomplete Cholesky needs at most half the iterations of block Jacobi, and the iteration count and the solution are bit-identical for 1 and 8 threads; a breakdown is reported with the shift used, never as a non-finite result. The default solver and its results are unchanged bit for bit.
note: Structural solver, basic tier (plan ADR 0270). ADR 0282, 2026-11-12: rcfd_linalg::precond (appended, no re-export) BlockJacobi (Cholesky of each diagonal block of a given partition) and IncompleteCholesky (L D L^T with zero fill on the lower CSR triangle; on a pivot not above 1e-10 of its diagonal the factorisation restarts with A + alpha diag(A), alpha <- max(2 alpha, 1e-3), which terminates by diagonal dominance; every breakdown recorded with shift, row and pivot; IcOptions, PrecondError). rcfd_fem::solve: StaticSolver::PreconditionedCg { preconditioner: CgPreconditioner::{BlockJacobi, IncompleteCholesky(IcOptions)}, tolerance, max_iterations } on the true relative residual with up to three iterative-refinement steps, node_blocks, solve_static_report with SolveReport (iterations, restarts, shift, breakdowns by node and component), a shifted factor named in SolverStats ("cg-ic0, shift ... after k breakdown(s)"), non-finite iterates refused. Hex8 cantilever 32 x 6 x 6 (4704 unknowns): relative residual 9.6e-11 (block Jacobi, 156 iterations) and 9.5e-11 (IC, 85), within 3.3e-13 of the direct solution (limit 1e-7), iterations and solutions bit-identical for 1 and 8 threads; IC needs 0.545 of block Jacobi's iterations against the limit 0.5: missed (0.535 on the heavy case, 0.705 at L/h = 10.7; the low bending modes set the count). Heavy 96 x 18 x 18 (103 968 unknowns): 7.6e-11 and 7.2e-11 (limit 1e-10), 477 and 255 iterations (amendment 4; two earlier heavy runs were on a 24 m beam by a test-helper defect). A Kershaw-type matrix breaks down at row 3 with pivot -5 and is factored with shift 0.256 after 9 breakdowns, pivots within 5.9e-17 of the closed form; forced breakdowns on the cantilever are reported with shift 2.048 and solved to 7.9e-11. Default and CG-Jacobi results bit-identical to main, baseline hashes pass; ten mutations caught (M6 after amendment 3). Partial by the registered rule; done is the maintainer's call. ADR 0357 (2026-11-12, F-460): with one level of fill, incomplete Cholesky needs 0.372 of block Jacobi's iterations on the fast cantilever (58 against 156), so IC(1) meets the half-iterations target of this item; IC(0) itself is unchanged.

title: Eigensolver for K x = lambda M x: dense Jacobi and subspace iteration on the direct factorisation
acceptance: Every limit not stated here is registered in the ADR before the run. rcfd-linalg gains a dense symmetric eigensolver and the lowest m eigenpairs of K x = lambda M x (K symmetric, M symmetric positive definite) by subspace iteration on the factorisation of K + sigma M, with a count of the eigenvalues below a value from the signs of D. Checks: the tridiagonal matrix (2, -1) of n = 200 with M = I: the lowest 10 eigenvalues equal 4 sin^2(j pi/(2 (n + 1))) within 1e-10 relative; the 5-point Laplacian on 30 x 30: repeated eigenvalues come with their multiplicity and the vectors are M-orthonormal within 1e-10; the same with a non-uniform diagonal M against the dense solver within 1e-9; residual |K x - lambda M x| <= 1e-8 |K x| for every returned pair; a singular K (free chain) with sigma > 0 returns its zero eigenvalue below 1e-9 of the first non-zero one; the count below the m-th eigenvalue equals m - 1; no convergence within the cap is an error stating the residuals.
note: DONE pending acceptance, merged 2026-11-12. Structural solver, basic tier (plan ADR 0270). ADR 0283, 2026-11-12: rcfd_linalg::eigen: dense symmetric eigensolver by cyclic Jacobi with the relative rotation test (symmetric_eigen; generalized_eigen_dense by Cholesky reduction), and lowest_eigenpairs of K x = lambda M x by subspace iteration on the envelope factor of K + sigma M (ADR 0274) with a Rayleigh-Ritz step, q = max(2m, m+8) start vectors, a residual test per pair (1e-10 on the shifted operator), clusters crossing m completed, an automatic or given shift, and a Sturm count from the signs of D of K - s M (count_below, Sylvester's law of inertia) that verifies no eigenvalue was missed. Tridiagonal (2, -1) n = 200: lowest 10 within 4.0e-15 relative (limit 1e-10); 5-point 30 x 30: four doubled eigenvalues with their multiplicity, within 8.1e-16, M-orthonormal within 1.8e-15 (limit 1e-10); with a non-uniform diagonal M against the dense solver within 1.5e-12 (limit 1e-9); residuals at most 8.3e-11 (limit 1e-8); free chain with sigma > 0: zero eigenvalue 2.1e-13 of the first non-zero one (limit 1e-9); counts below the m-th eigenvalue m - 1; the cap is an error stating the residuals; a deliberately deficient start is caught by the count (9 eigenvalues below the shift, 5 found). Consistent-mass bar within 5.0e-14 of the closed form; bit-identical for 1 and 8 threads; dense reference of 900 unknowns in 22.6 s. Nine mutations caught. Existing rcfd-linalg tests unedited and passing. ADR 0274 (2026-11-12) provides PivotRule::NonZero and SkylineLdlt::inertia() (counts of negative and positive pivots) for the eigenvalue count, checked on shifted 12^3 Laplacians (1 and 32 eigenvalues below the shift); rcfd-linalg/src/lib.rs already has the skyline line, and ADR 0283 adds its own.

title: Mass matrix and linear modal analysis of a solid model
acceptance: Every limit not stated here is registered in the ADR before the run. Consistent mass matrix for Tet4, Hex8 and Tet10: for a box, the total mass, the centre of mass and the inertia tensor obtained from rigid motions r^T M r equal the closed forms within 1e-12. Modal analysis: a free box has six frequencies below 1e-6 of the seventh; a fixed-free bar with nu = 0 has f_n = (2n - 1) sqrt(E/rho)/(4 L), n = 1, 2, 3, within 0.5 percent on a registered mesh, and the error of f_1 falls at an observed order >= 1.8 with Hex8; a cantilever of slenderness 20 and square section has its first bending frequency within 1 percent of (1.8751)^2 sqrt(E I/(rho A L^4))/(2 pi) and its second (4.6941) within 2.5 percent with Tet10, the Euler-Bernoulli value less the shear and rotary-inertia correction estimated in the registration (0.15 and 0.9 percent); on a symmetric Hex8 mesh the two bending planes give the same frequency within 1e-6 relative; mode shapes are M-orthonormal within 1e-9.
note: Structural solver, basic tier (plan ADR 0270). ADR 0284, 2026-11-12: rcfd_fem::mass::consistent (consistent mass by the mass rules of ADR 0273, tet_4, gauss_3, tet_14, through assemble_with; exactly symmetric, bit-identical for 1 and 8 threads), element_mass, rigid_motions and mass_properties from r^T M r; rcfd_fem::modal::modal_analysis (zero constraints by symmetric elimination, lowest_eigenpairs of ADR 0283 with sigma = 0 when the constraints hold every rigid motion and Shift::Auto for a free body; massless unknowns and non-zero constraints refused; modes M-orthonormal over the full DofMap). Box with moved interior nodes: mass, centre and inertia from rigid motions within 7.3e-16 (Tet4, Hex8, Tet10; limit 1e-12), about the centre within 3.9e-15. Free box: six rigid frequencies at most 6.5e-8 of the seventh (limit 1e-6). Fixed-free bar, nu = 0, Hex8 32 x 1 x 1: f_1..3 within 1.0e-4, 9.0e-4, 2.5e-3 (limit 5e-3), equal to the discrete 1-D chain within 2.2e-14, observed order of f_1 2.0001; Tet4 and Tet10 below their 1-D chain bounds. Cantilever L/b = 20, Tet10 80 x 4 x 4: first and second bending within 2.7e-3 and 2.9e-3 of Euler-Bernoulli less the exact Timoshenko correction (0.199 and 1.361 percent, kappa 5/6; the draft's 0.15 and 0.9 used beta_n^2 for the cantilever's J_n), within 7.2e-4 and 1.08e-2 of pure Euler-Bernoulli (limits 1 and 2.5 percent); symmetric Hex8 mesh: bending planes equal within 4.0e-11 (limit 1e-6); mode shapes M-orthonormal within 6.0e-15 (limit 1e-9). Amendment 1: slender models need ModalOptions::tolerance(1e-7) (residual floor of the eigensolver, c eps lambda_max/lambda_1); amendment 2: check C5 of the element mass matrices against closed forms added after mutation M8 (Tet10 mass with a degree-2 rule) survived the registered checks; eight of nine mutations caught by the registered tests, M8 by C5. Partial by the rule until the maintainer accepts amendment 2. ADR 0354 (2026-11-12): the slender-model tolerance of amendment 1 is answered by ModalOptions::new(m).tolerance(1e-12).residual_test(ResidualTest::Backward), which converges for the 40 x 2 x 2 Tet10 cantilever in 7 iterations with the same frequencies.

title: One-way coupling 1: loads of the F-237 deck applied to the solid surface
acceptance: Every limit not stated here is registered in the ADR before the run. A surface set of a solid mesh is turned into the shell surface that the F-237 export writes onto, and a deck read back (PLOAD4, TEMP) is applied to the solid: the resultant force and moment of the nodal loads equal deck_force_moment within 1e-12 relative; a deck element or node that matches no solid face or node within a stated tolerance is refused with its id. Tube: the wall pressure of the fluid mesh of the F-237 tube check, uniform, exported, written, parsed and applied to a thick solid tube (b/a = 2, plane strain) gives the radial displacement at the bore within 1 percent and the hoop stress within 2 percent of Lame's solution; with a pressure varying along the axis and around the circumference the solid's reactions equal the fluid's integrated force within 0.1 percent (the F-237 limit); TEMP of a uniform temperature gives the free expansion alpha dT r within 1e-6.
note: Structural solver, basic tier (plan ADR 0270, 2026-11-12). Size M. Stub ADR 0285; the registration is written by the implementation agent before any code. ADR 0278 (2026-11-12) added the rcfd-fem dependency of rcfd-post and the stub module rcfd_post::solid_loads; the solid result's VTK output is rcfd_post::solid_output::write_solid_vtu. ADR 0281 (2026-11-12): the TEMP values of the deck map to Load::temperature(nodal, reference) with one value per solid node (a model takes one temperature field; a second is refused); the expansion coefficient comes from Material::isotropic_elastic.

title: One-way coupling 2: fluid face forces in process, and a static solid as a co-simulation participant
acceptance: Every limit not stated here is registered in the ADR before the run. Fluid face forces on a wall are mapped to the nodes of a solid surface set by a given InterfaceMap and solved statically: resultant force, moment and work equal the fluid side's within 1e-12; for a matching planar interface under uniform pressure the solid's displacement equals the uniaxial closed form within 1e-10, and for a 3:2 non-matching one within a limit registered from the estimate of the mapping error. A StaticSolid implements cosim::Structure (advance is a static solve; restore returns the checkpoint bit for bit) and, with a test-only mock fluid whose force falls linearly with the wall displacement (stiffness k_f), coupled_step converges to u = F0/(k_s + k_f) within 1e-8 with the Aitken and with the least-squares update; a failing solve stops the step with the participant's name and both sides restored. No flow solver is coupled.
note: Structural solver, basic tier (plan ADR 0270). ADR 0286, 2026-11-12: rcfd_post::solid_coupling. SolidInterface takes the nodes of a surface set of a rcfd_fem model (ascending) and the corners of its faces as interface elements (build_map is InterfaceMap::build on them); face_forces_to_nodes and solve_face_forces map the fluid's face forces with a given InterfaceMap (forces_to_nodes, the transpose) and solve statically with the model's own constraints; StaticSolid implements cosim::Structure (advance a static solve, the state time, displacement and forces of the last advance; checkpoint and restore bit for bit; a failed solve leaves the state unchanged). No mass: for mock fluids and quasi-static use only (the added-mass ratio against an incompressible flow is unbounded); no flow solver is coupled. Checks on a Hex8 bar 4 x 1 x 1 m (8 x 2 x 2, E 2e11, nu 0.3, rollers): resultant, moment and work equal the fluid side's to 1.1e-16 (limit 1e-12) for a matching and a 3:2 wall, uniform and random face forces, Hex8 and Tet4; matching wall under uniform pressure: uniaxial closed form to 4.4e-15 (limit 1e-10), mapped loads equal to Load::pressure's to 1.2e-16; 3:2 wall: consistent-weighted mean face displacement to 4.2e-15 (exact by Betti, limit 1e-10), largest error on the loaded face 0.131 p L/E (limit 0.25 from a half-space estimate 0.05 to 0.11; control >= 0.005), at x <= L/2 2.3e-4 (limit 0.01, Saint-Venant). With a test-only mock fluid of stiffness 1.5 k_s, coupled_step converges in 3 iterations to u = F0/(k_s + k_f) within 1.9e-15 (limit 1e-8) with Aitken and with the least-squares update; the plain fixed point fails at the cap. A failing solve (CG capped at one iteration) stops the step naming the participant 'solid' in iteration 1 and, after a load step (amendment 1), in iteration 2, both sides restored bit for bit. Partial: the registered failing-solve check in iteration 2 was not reached on its registered run (the step after a converged one starts at the fixed point); the corrected test, registered by amendment 1 before its run, met it. Nine of nine mutations caught. Tet10 interfaces get no force on mid-edge nodes (open ADR 0286 Q2). Partial by the registered rule; done is the maintainer's call. The follow-up F-463 (ADR 0361, 2026-11-12) registers the failing solve in iterations 2 and 3 and meets it.

title: A solid case file of its own and the library entry that runs it
acceptance: Every limit not stated here is registered in the ADR before the run. A solid case file (TOML of its own: mesh from a generator or a Gmsh file, material, constraints and loads on named sets, static or modal analysis, solver choice, output) is read and run by a library function of rcfd-api that writes the .vtu and a JSON report (displacement and stress extremes, reactions, frequencies, solver statistics): an unknown key, a missing set, a wrong unit or type each give an error with the key and the line; a file run gives the bits of the same model built by library calls (limit 1e-12, expected identical); the cantilever and the bar-frequency checks pass when run from files, and a Gmsh tetrahedral mesh of a box read through rcfd-io gives the uniaxial closed form within 1e-10; no flow case key, CLI help text, MCP tool list, hash table or golden changes (the existing schema, CLI and tool-list tests pass unedited).
note: Structural solver, basic tier (plan ADR 0270, 2026-11-12). Size M. Stub ADR 0287; the registration is written by the implementation agent before any code. ADR 0278 (2026-11-12): a solid run writes its result with rcfd_post::solid_output::write_solid_vtu(path, model, result); a multi-material model is refused by the nodal average (per-set output is an open question of ADR 0278). ADR 0282 (2026-11-12): the static solve's iterative route is StaticSolver::PreconditionedCg with CgPreconditioner::BlockJacobi or CgPreconditioner::IncompleteCholesky(IcOptions::default()); a case-file key for it maps onto these. ADR 0357 (2026-11-12): the recommended iterative choice is CgPreconditioner::IncompleteCholeskyFill { options: IcOptions::default(), level: 1, ordering: IcOrdering::Natural } (two thirds of IC(0)'s iterations at twice its memory); a case-file key for the iterative route should map onto it and onto the ordering. ADR 0305 (2026-11-12): for large solid models the iterative choice with the fewest iterations is CgPreconditioner::SmoothedAggregation(ElasticAmgSettings::default()) (15 to 22 iterations on the ADR 0282 cantilevers against 58 to 132 for IC(1)); a case-file key for the iterative route should be able to select it. ADR 0370 (2026-11-13): for meshes of quadratic elements an iterative key should be able to select CgPreconditioner::SmoothedAggregation(ElasticAmgSettings::quadratic()) (Tet10 slenderness 20: 31 iterations against 79 with the default settings). ADR 0375 (2026-11-13): a quadratic-mesh key could also offer CgPreconditioner::SmoothedAggregation(ElasticAmgSettings::quadratic_smoothed()) (Tet10 slenderness 20: 23 iterations, 3.56 s, against 31 iterations, 2.84 s with quadratic()).

title: Demonstration on a fan blade: static response to centrifugal and pressure load, and the modes at rest; user page
acceptance: Every limit not stated here is registered in the ADR before the run. One blade of the parametric fan geometry, meshed in quadratic tetrahedra and clamped at the hub: under the centrifugal load at a registered speed the reactions equal rho omega^2 V r_c within 1e-8 and under a uniform pressure the integrated pressure force within 1e-8; the strain energy equals half the work of the loads within 1e-8; between two meshes (the second with at least twice the elements) the tip displacement and the first natural frequency change by less than 5 percent, both numbers recorded; as the flat-plate limit, an untwisted rectangular cantilever plate of the blade's span, mean chord and thickness has its first bending frequency between the Euler-Bernoulli beam value and that value divided by sqrt(1 - nu^2), with a 1 percent margin on each side. The page docs/structural-solver.md states the scope, the limits and that nothing is validated against a measured blade.
note: Structural solver, basic tier (plan ADR 0270, 2026-11-12). Size M. Stub ADR 0288; the registration is written by the implementation agent before any code. ADR 0284 (2026-11-12): rcfd_fem::modal::modal_analysis gives the modes at rest; a slender blade needs ModalOptions::new(m).tolerance(1e-7) or so (the residual floor of lowest_eigenpairs is about c eps lambda_max/lambda_1, 2.7e-9 for a 40 x 2 x 2 Tet10 cantilever of L/b = 20), and modes are best identified by effective mass fractions from mass::rigid_motions, as sb_modal does. ADR 0354 (2026-11-12): for a slender blade use ModalOptions::new(m).tolerance(1e-12).residual_test(rcfd_linalg::eigen::ResidualTest::Backward) instead of a hand-set relative tolerance; the default stays the relative test of ADR 0283.

title: Scaffold of the intermediate tier: module layout, model extension data, element-trait extension points
acceptance: Every limit not stated here is registered in the ADR before the run. The modules, element kinds, property data, constraint and support data and the three defaulted element entry points of ADR 0290 section 2 exist in rcfd-fem and rcfd-post; every test of the basic tier (the sb_ files of rcfd-fem, rcfd-linalg, rcfd-io, rcfd-post and rcfd-api) compiles and passes unedited, and a registered set of basic models (patch test, cantilever, bar modes) gives displacements, stresses and frequencies with the same bits as before the change; the generic assembly hook called with the element stiffness reproduces assemble::stiffness bit for bit for 1 and 8 threads; each new element kind, formulation, constraint and support variant is refused by the static solve with an error naming the variant and the set, never ignored; the baseline hashes are unchanged.
note: Structural solver, intermediate tier (plan ADR 0290, 2026-11-12). Size S. Stub ADR 0291; the registration is written by the implementation agent before any code. ADR 0275 (2026-11-12): a generic assembly hook exists as assemble::assemble_with; per-node prescribed values and forces are arguments of solve::solve_static_with, not model fields. ADR 0291, 2026-11-13: the intermediate tier's scaffold. rcfd-fem declares hex20, hex8x, beam, shell, mpc, cyclic, geometric, buckling, rotating, nonlinear, transient, harmonic and rcfd-post solid_dynamic, solid_fsi; ElementKind gains Hex20, Beam2, Shell4 (is_solid, pending; their data and element delegated to their module, a placeholder element whose every fallible entry refuses); BlockProperty (Solid with SolidFormulation Full, BBar, Incompatible; Beam with BeamSection and orientation; Shell with thickness) set by SolidMesh::set_block_property; Constraint::Linear, RigidSet, Cyclic and ElasticSupport (NodalSpring, Foundation) with SolidModel::add_support, all validated when added; Element::geometric_stiffness, internal_force, tangent refusing by default; the generic hook is ADR 0275's assemble_with. Each new kind, formulation, constraint and support is refused by the static solve (also by the modal analysis and assemble::stiffness) with FemError::NotYetSupported naming the variant, its block or set and the package, every string exact (10 cases, 30 more paths); VTK cell types 3, 9, 25 admitted and mapped. Patch test, cantilever (direct and PCG) and bar modes give displacements, reactions, stresses, nodal stresses, eigenvalues, frequencies, modes and stiffness with the bits of main ee449e26 (26 digests equal); assemble_with with the element stiffness equals assemble::stiffness bit for bit for 1 and 8 threads on four models; every sb_ test of rcfd-fem, rcfd-linalg, rcfd-io, rcfd-post passes unedited (rcfd-api has none); baseline hashes unchanged. Eleven mutations, all caught. 2026-11-13: with Hex20 (ADR 0292) and the mpc package (ADR 0296) landed, si_scaffold's X1, X3, R1 to R11 are ignored records of ADR 0291 and _after_landed copies without the retired rows (R1, R5, R6, R8, R9; R8 modal refused by the ADR 0296 follow-up) pass; maintainer decision: every later package of the tier does the same for its own rows.

title: Quadratic hexahedron (Hex20) with its face loads, mass and the quadratic upgrade of a hexahedron box
acceptance: Every limit not stated here is registered in the ADR before the run. Hex20 on the reference element and on randomly distorted ones (registered seed): shape functions sum to 1 and derivatives to 0 within 1e-14, analytic derivatives agree with central differences within 1e-7, the 3 x 3 x 3 rule integrates every monomial of degree <= 5 per direction within 1e-13, the stiffness is symmetric within 1e-13, has rank 54 and gives no force for the six rigid motions within 1e-11. Patch test with all six strains on a box with displaced interior nodes: 1e-10. A uniform pressure on an 8-node face gives the nodal loads -1/12 (corners) and 1/3 (mid-edge) of p A within 1e-13, and uniaxial tension the closed form within 1e-10. Cantilever L/h = 20, nu = 0.3, ONE element through the thickness and 10 along: tip deflection within 1 percent of P L^3/(3 E I) (1 + 3 E I/(kappa G A L^2)). Thick cylinder b/a = 2 in plane strain on a curved mesh: bore displacement within 0.2 percent and bore hoop stress within 1 percent of Lame. Manufactured solution of F-378: observed L2 order >= 2.7. Mass: total mass and inertia tensor of a box within 1e-12; first axial frequency of a fixed-free bar (nu = 0) within 0.1 percent at 8 elements. The upgrade has (nodes + edges) nodes.
note: ADR 0292, 2026-11-12: Hex20 serendipity element in rcfd-fem (hex20.rs; node order confirmed as VTK type 25 from the published vtkQuadraticHexahedron definition; 3 x 3 x 3 rule for stiffness and mass; triquadratic recovery; 8-node face loads as per-node forces; upgrade_to_hex20 and upgrade_to_hex20_mapped). Met: partition 4.4e-16, derivatives against central differences 2.6e-11, monomials 1.8e-15, symmetry, rank 54 and rigid motions on 21 elements, patch 4.4e-15, face loads -1/12 and 1/3 of p A to 1.6e-16, uniaxial 1.6e-12, bore displacement 7.3e-5, manufactured solution L2 orders 3.05 (cases D and T), box mass and inertia 3e-15, bar frequency 1.03e-6 at 8 elements, 111 = 36 + 75 nodes; nine mutations caught. Missed (known misses, diagnosed): cantilever 1.8 percent (ratio 0.981949; the full clamp with nu = 0.3, 0.999 with nu = 0) and bore hoop stress 1.17 percent on 4 x 8 elements (radial resolution). Model-path pressure and traction on Hex20 faces stay refused by loads.rs, and SolidMesh::face_area panics on an 8-node face (follow-up). si_scaffold X1, X3, R1, R10 of ADR 0291 fail because Hex20 is no longer refused: needs the maintainer. Resolved 2026-11-13 by the maintainer's decision (records and copies): the retired si_scaffold rows stay as ignored records of ADR 0291 and the _after_landed copies without them pass. ADR 0383, 2026-11-13: the model-path refusal of Hex20 face loads and the panic of SolidMesh::face_area on an 8-node face are retired (F-484).

title: Hex8 without locking: mean-dilatation (B-bar) and incompatible-mode formulations, opt-in per element block
acceptance: Every limit not stated here is registered in the ADR before the run. Two opt-in formulations of Hex8, default unchanged bit for bit. Both pass the patch test of F-374 on distorted meshes within 1e-10 and a single element of either has exactly six zero eigenvalues (the seventh above 1e-6 of the largest) for aspect ratios 1, 10 and 100. Cantilever of F-379 (L/h = 20, tip shear force) with ONE element through the thickness and 20 along: incompatible modes within 1 percent of the closed form at nu = 0 and within 3 percent at nu = 0.3, while full integration on the same mesh is the registered locking control (below 80 percent); at L/h = 100 with elements of aspect ratio 5 incompatible modes stay within 2 percent. Thick cylinder b/a = 2 in plane strain with nu = 0.4999: B-bar gives the bore displacement within 1 percent of Lame on the mesh on which full integration is below 90 percent (control). Recovered stress on the patch test equals D eps within 1e-10; the condensed internal modes are recovered for the stress.
note: Structural solver, intermediate tier (plan ADR 0290, 2026-11-12). Size M. Stub ADR 0293; the registration is written by the implementation agent before any code. ADR 0291 (2026-11-13): the formulation is ElementBlock::formulation() (set by SolidMesh::set_block_property with BlockProperty::solid); hex8x::PENDING gates it. The stiffness and the recovery do not delegate to hex8x: the package needs assemble.rs (stiffness_with) and recover.rs in its file list.

title: Six unknowns per node: rotations in the DofMap, nodal moments, and a two-node shear-flexible beam element
acceptance: Every limit not stated here is registered in the ADR before the run. Nodes carry three or six unknowns; a model without structural elements gives the bits it gave before. Beam, ONE element, any orientation in space (registered seed): tip deflection P L^3/(3 E I) + P L/(kappa G A), tip rotation P L^2/(2 E I), twist T L/(G J) and elongation F L/(E A) within 1e-10, section forces at the root equal to the applied loads within 1e-10, reactions (forces and moments) balancing the loads within 1e-10; a rotation of the whole model leaves the results unchanged within 1e-10. Quarter-circle arch of radius R clamped at one end, 32 elements, slender: deflection under the tip load pi P R^3/(4 E I) within 0.5 percent. Free beam: six zero frequencies below 1e-6 of the seventh. Pinned-pinned beam, 20 elements, slenderness 50: f_n = (n pi/L)^2 sqrt(E I/(rho A))/(2 pi), n = 1, 2, 3, within 0.5, 1 and 2 percent after the registered shear and rotary-inertia correction. A beam node shared with a solid element is refused (no rotational stiffness from the solid) with the node id.
note: Structural solver, intermediate tier (plan ADR 0290, 2026-11-12). Size M. Stub ADR 0294; the registration is written by the implementation agent before any code.

title: Four-node shell element (flat facet, assumed shear strain): plates, housings and thin blades as surfaces
acceptance: Every limit not stated here is registered in the ADR before the run. Membrane patch test and constant-curvature bending patch test on a distorted flat mesh within 1e-8. Simply supported square plate under uniform load, 16 x 16 elements, nu = 0.3: centre deflection within 1 percent of the Navier series (0.004062 q a^4/D, recomputed in the registration) at thickness/side 0.01 and within 1.5 percent at 0.001 (no shear locking), the fully integrated shear control being below 20 percent at 0.001. Cantilever strip, nu = 0: tip deflection P L^3/(3 E I) within 0.5 percent and surface stress 6 M/t^2 at mid-span within 2 percent. Curved: a ring strip of radius R pinched by two opposite forces, nu = 0, 32 elements per quarter: change of the loaded diameter (pi/4 - 2/pi) P R^3/(E I) within 2 percent; a cylinder under internal pressure with free ends: radial displacement p R^2/(E t) within 0.5 percent. Frequencies of the simply supported plate: omega_mn = pi^2 (m^2 + n^2)/a^2 sqrt(D/(rho t)) within 1 percent for (1,1) and 3 percent for (1,2) and (2,2). A free plate has six zero frequencies; a facet warped beyond the registered limit is refused with the element.
note: Structural solver, intermediate tier (plan ADR 0290, 2026-11-12). Size M. Stub ADR 0295; the registration is written by the implementation agent before any code.

title: Linear multi-point constraints by a transformation, rigid sets with a reference point, elastic supports
acceptance: Every limit not stated here is registered in the ADR before the run. A model with prescribed displacements only gives the bits of the basic tier; the same constraints written as linear constraints give the same displacements within 1e-12. The reduced matrix is symmetric within 1e-13 and the constraint forces do no work on any admissible motion within 1e-12. Skew roller: a block in uniaxial stress along a direction 30 degrees off the axes, held by the constraint u.n = 0 on its inclined faces, has the rotated uniaxial solution within 1e-10. Periodic pair u(high) - u(low) = eps L on a box with displaced interior nodes: uniform strain within 1e-10. Rigid set on the end face of a bar: an axial force at the reference point gives F L/(E A) within 1e-10 (nu = 0), a moment the tip rotation M L/(E I) within 1 percent (Tet10, slenderness 20), and the constraint forces have the resultant and moment applied within 1e-10. Supports: a bar on an end spring k has the tip displacement F (1/k + L/(E A)) within 1e-10; a block on a foundation k_f under pressure p settles by p/k_f within 1e-10. A redundant constraint is dropped with a report, a contradictory one and a chain that closes on itself are refused naming the constraints.
note: ADR 0296, 2026-11-13: linear multi-point constraints, rigid sets and elastic supports by the transformation u = T q + g in rcfd-fem::mpc (mpc::PENDING = None). Rows are eliminated in a fixed order (prescribed, then the model's Linear and RigidSet constraints) with designated dependents (the first term of a Linear constraint) by Gauss-Jordan substitution; a row implied by earlier ones is dropped and reported (threshold 1e-10), a contradictory row and a row that closes a chain on itself are refused naming the constraints. A rigid set has six auxiliary reference unknowns (translation and small rotation; no six-unknown node needed) and takes a force and a moment through solve_static_mpc; nodal springs and a consistent foundation are added to K. solve_static_report dispatches to it for any model with a Linear or RigidSet constraint or a support; every other model runs the old code (A1 bit-equal, si_scaffold_bits and baseline hashes unchanged). Results: Linear-written prescribed values 3e-16 (limit 1e-12); K_r symmetric to 1e-16; constraint work 3e-13; skew roller 7e-16; periodic box with displaced nodes: strain 4e-15, 33 redundant rows dropped as computed beforehand; rigid end of a Tet10 bar: F L/(E A) 3e-14, M L/(E I) 9e-11 (limit 1 percent), resultant and moment 5e-13; end spring 1.5e-14; foundation p/k_f 3e-14 (Hex8, Tet10); threads 1 and 8 bit-equal. Ten mutations caught. Modal analysis and the preconditioned CG refuse these constraints; Cyclic stays refused. Four tests of ADR 0291's si_scaffold.rs (the mpc::PENDING assertion, cases R5, R6, R8, R9 and R8 modal) now fail as registered and need the maintainer's edit. Resolved 2026-11-13 by the maintainer's decision (records and copies): the retired si_scaffold rows stay as ignored records of ADR 0291 and the _after_landed copies without them pass.

title: Cyclic symmetry: one sector of a rotor for statics and for modal analysis by harmonic index
acceptance: Every limit not stated here is registered in the ADR before the run. Equivalence: for a ring and for a disc with N = 12 sectors, the frequencies of the sector for every harmonic index 0 to 6 equal the frequencies of the full 360 degree model built from the same sector mesh within 1e-8 relative, with the same count below a registered cut-off (single for k = 0 and 6, double otherwise); the expanded mode shapes satisfy the full model's eigen-equation within 1e-7. Closed forms: in-plane bending of a thin ring (thickness/radius 0.05, nu = 0), omega_n^2 = E I n^2 (n^2 - 1)^2/(rho A R^4 (n^2 + 1)) for n = 2 and 3 found at harmonic index 2 and 3 within 2 percent; a thin annular disc b/a = 4 spinning about its axis (statics, k = 0): rim displacement rho omega^2 b ((3 + nu) a^2 + (1 - nu) b^2)/(4 E) within 1 percent. Boundaries that do not match under the rotation within the registered tolerance are refused with the first unmatched node; N < 2 and a harmonic index above N/2 are refused.
note: Structural solver, intermediate tier (plan ADR 0290, 2026-11-12). Size M. Stub ADR 0297; the registration is written by the implementation agent before any code. ADR 0291 (2026-11-13): Constraint::Linear { terms: Vec<LinearTerm>, value }, Constraint::RigidSet { set, reference }, Constraint::Cyclic { low, high, axis, origin, sectors } and ElasticSupport::{NodalSpring, Foundation} exist and are validated when added; constraints are refused in constraint::prescribed_equations (gated by mpc::PENDING and cyclic::PENDING), supports in SolidModel::check_supported. ADR 0296 (2026-11-13): mpc::transformation builds T and g from rows c . x = b (Gauss-Jordan with designated dependents, mpc::DEPENDENCE_TOLERANCE 1e-10); Transformation::reduce gives T^T K T and T^T (f - K g), Transformation::expand gives x. The cyclic rows can be added as rows of the same elimination; prescribed_equations still refuses Cyclic (gated by cyclic::PENDING). Modal analysis on the transformation is refused by mpc::refuse_in_modal and is needed by the cyclic modes. ADR 0384 (2026-11-13): the modal analysis runs on the transformation (mpc::modal_analysis_mpc: T^T K T, T^T M T, modes x = T q, Auto shift); the cyclic modes can add their rows to the same elimination and reuse it (complex rows for a non-zero harmonic are not covered).

title: Geometric (initial-stress) stiffness of solid elements: pre-stressed modal analysis and linear buckling
acceptance: Every limit not stated here is registered in the ADR before the run. K_sigma is symmetric within 1e-13 of its norm, gives no force for a rigid translation within 1e-12, and for a uniform uniaxial stress s and a linear displacement field w gives x^T K_sigma x = s V |grad w . e|^2 within 1e-12. rcfd-linalg: for K = tridiagonal (2, -1), n = 200, and K_sigma = -I the ten lowest buckling factors equal 4 sin^2(j pi/(2 (n + 1))) within 1e-10; a K_sigma with no negative direction returns no factor and says so. Pre-stressed modes: a beam on knife-edge supports at its neutral axis (slenderness 20, nu = 0) under an axial tension stress s has (omega_n^2 - omega_n,0^2) = (n pi/L)^2 s/rho within 1 percent for n = 1 and 2, and under compression the frequency falls by the same amount. Buckling: the same beam in compression has the critical load pi^2 E I/L^2 reduced by the shear term (0.6 percent at this slenderness, registered) within 1 percent, the second factor four times the first within 2 percent; a clamped-free column pi^2 E I/(4 L^2) within 1 percent (Tet10 or Hex20).
note: Structural solver, intermediate tier (plan ADR 0290, 2026-11-12). Size M. Stub ADR 0298; the registration is written by the implementation agent before any code.

title: Modes of a rotating part: stress stiffening by the centrifugal pre-stress, spin softening, Campbell diagram
acceptance: Every limit not stated here is registered in the ADR before the run. At zero speed the result has the bits of the modal analysis of F-383. Radial bar clamped on the axis, nu = 0, axial modes: (omega_n,0^2 - omega_n^2)/Omega^2 = 1 within 1e-3 for n = 1, 2 at a speed with centrifugal stress below 1e-4 E. Radial beam of square section clamped on the axis (slenderness 20): the first out-of-plane (flap) and in-plane (lag) frequencies satisfy omega_flap^2 - omega_lag^2 = Omega^2 within 1e-4 Omega^2 on a symmetric mesh; the stiffening (omega_flap^2 - omega_0^2)/Omega^2 equals at Omega = 0.2 omega_0 the Rayleigh quotient of the centrifugal tension with the mode at rest (1.19, recomputed in the registration) within 2 percent and stays between 1 and that value up to Omega = 5 omega_0. Campbell table: on a synthetic family omega^2 = omega_0^2 + S Omega^2 the crossings with orders 1 to 4 equal omega_0/sqrt(k^2 - S) within 1e-8, and on the beam within 1 percent; a flap and a lag mode of a rectangular section that cross are tracked without exchange (modal assurance above 0.9). A speed at which K_eff is not positive definite is reported as a loss of stiffness with the speed, never as a non-finite frequency.
note: Structural solver, intermediate tier (plan ADR 0290, 2026-11-12). Size M. Stub ADR 0299; the registration is written by the implementation agent before any code.

title: Geometric nonlinearity: total Lagrangian solid elements, Newton iteration with load steps
acceptance: Every limit not stated here is registered in the ADR before the run. The tangent agrees with central differences of the internal force within 1e-6 relative on distorted elements at displacements of 20 percent of the element size (registered seed). A rigid rotation by 90 degrees with a translation gives an internal force below 1e-10 E L^2. Uniform stretch lambda = 1.2 of a bar with nu = 0: nominal stress E lambda (lambda^2 - 1)/2 within 1e-9; under load control the last three residuals of each step show an order >= 1.8. A load factor of 1e-6 reproduces the linear solution within 1e-5 relative. Elastica: a cantilever of slenderness 50, nu = 0, with tip force P L^2/(E I) = 1 and 2 has the tip deflection and shortening within 2 percent of the elliptic-integral solution (recomputed in the registration by integrating the elastica equation; recalled 0.302 L, 0.056 L and 0.494 L, 0.161 L). An element inverted during the iteration and a step that does not converge after the registered halvings are errors with the element or the step.
note: Structural solver, intermediate tier (plan ADR 0290, 2026-11-12). Size M. Stub ADR 0300; the registration is written by the implementation agent before any code.

title: Linear transient dynamics: Newmark and generalised-alpha integration, Rayleigh damping, load histories
acceptance: Every limit not stated here is registered in the ADR before the run. Free vibration started in the first axial mode of a bar (the discrete eigenvector): with Newmark the amplitude after 100 periods is within 1e-9 and the total energy constant within 1e-10; the measured period is long by (omega dt)^2/12 within 5 percent of that amount at omega dt = 0.2 and 0.1, observed order >= 1.9. A step load proportional to M phi_1 gives the peak displacement twice the static one within 0.5 percent at 40 steps per period. Rayleigh damping with a registered ratio 0.02 on that mode: logarithmic decrement 2 pi zeta/sqrt(1 - zeta^2) within 1 percent. Generalised-alpha: with spectral radius 1 the result equals Newmark within 1e-12; with 0.5 and 0.8 a mode at omega dt = 1e3 decays per step by that factor within 1e-3 while the period error of the first mode keeps order >= 1.9. A run split in two by save and restore has the bits of the unsplit run; results are bit-identical for 1 and 8 threads; a non-positive step, a table that does not cover the run and a singular effective matrix are refused.
note: Structural solver, intermediate tier (plan ADR 0290, 2026-11-12). Size M. Stub ADR 0301; the registration is written by the implementation agent before any code.

title: Harmonic response by mode superposition: modal damping, static correction, effective mass, force harmonics
acceptance: Every limit not stated here is registered in the ADR before the run. A load proportional to M phi_1 at omega_1 gives the amplitude of the static response divided by 2 zeta within 1e-8 and a phase lag of 90 degrees within 1e-6 rad; the half-power width of that peak is 2 zeta omega_1 within 1 percent (zeta = 0.01). Fixed-free bar with nu = 0 under a harmonic tip force, undamped, at 0.5 and 1.5 times the first frequency: tip amplitude F tan(k L)/(E A k), k = omega/c, within 0.5 percent with 10 modes and the static correction, the same without the correction being the registered control (error above 1 percent at 0.5). Effective mass: the first axial mode of the bar carries 8/pi^2 of the mass within 0.5 percent, the first bending mode of a cantilever 0.613 (recomputed in the registration) within 1 percent, and the sum over all modes of a small model equals the unconstrained mass within 1e-10. Force harmonics of a sampled signal with three harmonics: amplitudes and phases within 1e-12; a record that is not a whole number of periods is refused.
note: Structural solver, intermediate tier (plan ADR 0290, 2026-11-12). Size M. Stub ADR 0302; the registration is written by the implementation agent before any code.

title: Dynamic solid as a co-simulation participant, on interface weights built from the two surfaces
acceptance: Every limit not stated here is registered in the ADR before the run. A bar (nu = 0) whose end face is the interface, coupled by coupled_step to a mock fluid that returns the force -m_a times the wall acceleration: the first coupled frequency equals the root of k L tan(k L) = rho A L/m_a within 1 percent at 100 steps per period, for mass ratios m_a/(rho A L) of 0.5 and 4; at ratio 4 the plain iteration (factor 1) diverges as the protocol predicts (registered control) while Aitken's factor and the least-squares update converge to 1e-8 within registered iteration caps. With a mock spring k_f and a slow load the response tends to F_0/(k_s + k_f) of F-385 within 1e-6. Mapping built by F-362 for a matching and for a 3:2 non-matching interface: resultant force, moment and work conserved within 1e-12, and the coupled frequency changes by less than 1e-3 between the two. Restore returns the checkpoint bit for bit; a failing structural step stops the coupled step with the participant's name and both sides restored. No flow solver is coupled.
note: Structural solver, intermediate tier (plan ADR 0290, 2026-11-12). Size M. Stub ADR 0303; the registration is written by the implementation agent before any code.

title: Two-way coupling of an elastic solid with the incompressible flow solver: the piston on an elastic bar
acceptance: Every limit not stated here is registered in the ADR before the run. Elastic bar (nu = 0) closing a channel of incompressible fluid of length L_f, started from a displaced state, mass ratios rho_f L_f/(rho_s L_s) of 0.5 and 4: the coupled iteration converges in every step to 1e-6 with Aitken's factor and with the least-squares update, iteration counts recorded; the frequency of the first coupled mode equals the root of k L tan(k L) = rho_s L_s/(rho_f L_f) within 2 percent after the registered estimate of the time-step and viscous effects; over ten periods the work of the fluid on the interface equals the change of the solid's energy within 1e-4 of its amplitude; the loose coupling (one pass) at ratio 4 grows (registered control). With a 3:2 non-matching interface mapped by F-362 the frequency changes by less than 2e-3. A failure of either participant leaves both at the start of the step. The existing co-simulation tests (cosim_f139, cosim_f361, cosim_f362) pass unedited.
note: Structural solver, intermediate tier (plan ADR 0290, 2026-11-12). Size M. Stub ADR 0304; the registration is written by the implementation agent before any code.

title: Aggregation multigrid for elasticity: rigid-body modes as near-null space, as a preconditioner of CG
acceptance: Every limit not stated here is registered in the ADR before the run. On every level the rigid-body modes are in the range of the prolongator: |B - P B_c| <= 1e-12 |B|. CG preconditioned by one V-cycle reaches a relative residual of 1e-10 on a clamped cube of Hex8 with about 5e3, 4e4 and (heavy record) 3e5 unknowns in a number of iterations that grows by at most 1.5 times from the smallest to the largest and stays below 40; on a cantilever of slenderness 20 with about 1e5 unknowns it needs at most one fifth of the iterations of the incomplete Cholesky of F-381; the same on a Tet10 mesh within twice the Hex8 count. The solution agrees with the direct solver within 1e-7 on the smallest case; operator complexity <= 1.5; iteration counts and solution are bit-identical for 1 and 8 threads. The scalar AMG and its tests are unchanged; the default solver's results are unchanged bit for bit.
note: Structural solver, intermediate tier (plan ADR 0290, 2026-11-12). ADR 0305, 2026-11-12: rcfd_linalg::amg_elastic (new, beside the untouched scalar AMG): smoothed aggregation on the node-block graph (theta 0), tentative prolongator by a local QR of the six rigid-body modes per aggregate with a registered drop rule (1e-10), prolongator smoothed by damped block Jacobi (4/3 over the spectral radius), Galerkin coarse operators, V(1,1) cycle with forward / backward block Gauss-Seidel and a dense LU on the coarsest level; rcfd_fem::solve::CgPreconditioner::SmoothedAggregation and solve::smoothed_aggregation (the modes from the node coordinates). Rigid-body modes in the range of the tentative prolongator on every level to 1.1e-15; operator complexity 1.03 to 1.18. Clamped Hex8 cube: 16, 17 and 20 iterations to 1e-10 at 4752, 39 744 and 304 842 unknowns (growth 1.25), 4.1e-12 from the direct solve, bit-identical for 1 and 8 threads. ADR 0282 cantilevers: 15 (BJ 156, IC0 85, IC1 58), 22 (292, 206, 132) and 17 (477, 255, 171) iterations. Partial by Rule I: the dense coarsest solve applied row interchanges in the wrong order (found by the symmetry check, fixed by amendment 1); on the slenderness-20 cantilever (121 680 unknowns) 1e-10 is below the rounding floor of the residual (both solvers stop at 1.4e-9; amendment 2 compares at 1e-8): Hex8 AMG 15 against IC(0) 887 (met), Tet10 AMG 79 against the limit 2 x 15 = 30 (missed; the first coarse level is 5 times coarser than on Hex8; Tet10 IC(0) 1971). Defaults and the scalar AMG hash-identical; baseline hashes pass; eight mutations caught. Follow-ups: Tet10 aggregation, the scalar AMG's coarse LU. Partial by the registered rule; done is the maintainer's call.

title: Solid case file: the analyses and model data of the intermediate tier
acceptance: Every limit not stated here is registered in the ADR before the run. Each new analysis run from a file gives the bits of the same model run by library calls (limit 1e-12, expected identical), and the closed-form checks of the library pass from files: the Euler column (ADR 0298), the rotating radial bar and a Campbell table with its crossings (ADR 0299), the ring at harmonic index 2 (ADR 0297), the resonance peak (ADR 0302), the free vibration of the bar (ADR 0301), the skew roller (ADR 0296). An unknown key, an analysis that lacks a required table, a harmonic index above N/2, a speed list that is not increasing and a property that names a missing set are each refused with the key and the line. Every solid case file of the basic tier's tests gives the same report and the same .vtu bytes as before. No flow case key, CLI help text, MCP tool list, hash table or golden changes (the existing schema, CLI and tool-list tests pass unedited).
note: Structural solver, intermediate tier (plan ADR 0290, 2026-11-12). Size M. Stub ADR 0306; the registration is written by the implementation agent before any code.

title: A [solid] table in the flow case and the library entry that runs the coupled case
acceptance: Every limit not stated here is registered in the ADR before the run. Gate (as check K0 of ADR 0257): with the optional table in the schema the tests case_hashes_w48u, baseline_hashes, w48v_adaptive_correctors, rules_w19c, mesh_transform_w48u and physics_schema of rcfd-api, cli of rcfd-cli, and default_f1, project_list_f270 and tool_list_f275 of rcfd-mcp pass with no file edited. The piston of ADR 0304 written as a flow case with a [solid] table and a solid case file and run by the library entry gives the interface displacement history of the library set-up within 1e-12 (expected identical) and so its frequency; the report carries the iterations and residuals of every step. A case with the table run through the ordinary path is refused with the key; a missing patch, a missing surface set, a solid file without a transient analysis and a time step that differs between the two files are each refused with the key and the line. A flow case without the table gives the bytes it gave before.

The optional table follows the route of ADR 0257 (no golden edit); the one refusal in the ordinary run path is decision N3 of ADR 0290.

title: Demonstration on the fan rotor: Campbell diagram of the blade, the bladed disc by cyclic symmetry, response to blade-passing forcing
acceptance: Every limit not stated here is registered in the ADR before the run. Blade of the parametric fan geometry in quadratic tetrahedra, clamped at the hub, at registered speeds from rest to the registered maximum: the Campbell table of the four lowest modes is written from a solid case file, with every crossing of the engine orders 1 to the blade count listed; at rest the frequencies have the bits of F-387; for each mode the slope of omega^2 against Omega^2 at the lowest speed equals the Rayleigh quotient phi^T (K_sigma,1 - M_perp) phi of the mode at rest within 1 percent and lies between -1 and the registered flap bound; between two meshes (the second with at least twice the elements) the first frequency at the maximum speed changes by less than 5 percent, both recorded. Bladed hub with Z blades: the sector frequencies for harmonic indices 0 to Z/2 equal those of the full rotor on the coarse mesh within 1e-6 (heavy record). Blade-passing response: at a registered Campbell crossing the tip amplitude under a unit pressure harmonic equals the modal estimate (participation over 2 zeta omega^2) within 1 percent and falls to the static value within 1 percent at one tenth of the frequency. The page docs/structural-solver.md states the scope, that the Coriolis term is neglected, that the damping is assumed and that nothing is validated against a measured blade.
note: Structural solver, intermediate tier (plan ADR 0290, 2026-11-12). Size M. Stub ADR 0309; the registration is written by the implementation agent before any code.

title: Matched sponge on a mesh moving along the layer or rotating
acceptance: An isolated plane pulse at 30 and 45 degrees through a matched layer attached to a mesh translating along the layer at Mach 0.2 reflects less than 1 percent and stays bounded over 20 transit times of the layer, or the reflection and any instability are measured and documented; a plain layer on a rotating mesh reflects a normal pulse less than 1 percent.
note: From ADR 0265 question 3, recommendation taken on the maintainer's standing instruction of 2026-11-11. ADR 0344, 2026-11-12: the acceptance text is MET IN THE LIBRARY with a new opt-in frame. Derived: the F-341 attached memory, the integral of p - p_ref along each cell's path, makes a matched layer unstable for grazing waves when the mesh moves along the layer, with growth rate M/(2(1-M)) times the layer rate. A column along a uniform layer at Mach 0.2 grew 6 times by t = 1.5, where at rest it stays at 0.30. Built (rcfd-fv): `sponge::SpongeFrame::AttachedWithLabMemory`, with the rates attached to the cells and the memories of the matched forms taken in the lab frame (each cell's memory gains w_c.grad Q), which on a mesh translating along a planar layer is the matched layer at rest. Measured: a plane pulse with a smooth envelope along its front (the solver has no periodic condition, and the moving boundaries exclude a mirror wall), through the layer of ADR 0237 on grids translating along it at Mach 0.2, reflects 1.6e-4 at 30 degrees and 3.5e-4 at 45 degrees (2.7e-4 and 3.6e-4 at rest; limit 1e-2) and stays bounded over 20 transit times of the layer (largest amplitude the incident peak). The F-341 frame reflects 7.2e-3 and 3.2e-2 in the same runs. It did not blow up within 20 transit times there, although the one-dimensional check shows the instability. A plain radial layer on a rotating O-grid, Mach 0.2 at the layer, reflects 2.8e-3 of an outgoing cylindrical pulse, as at rest; the plain form reflects about w/(8r) of a cylindrical pulse, which comes from the geometry. The transport matches a closed form to 1.9e-13. The frame gives the bits of the F-341 frame for the plain form and without motion. The F-341, F-331 and F-340 tests, the F-258 bit records and baseline_hashes pass unedited, and five mutations were caught. One amendment: the first closed-form check excluded too few boundary cells (8.9e-3); it was diagnosed and replaced on a longer grid. Limits: the lab memory is derived for translation along a planar layer; matched forms on rotating meshes are not built; library only; two-dimensional checks. STATUS recorded PARTIAL by the lead: the registered check G3 missed (a defect of its set-up, 8.92e-3 against 1e-12) and passed only as G3b after amendment 1, which is not blind to the scratch model that explained the miss; done is the maintainer's call.

title: Scaffold of the advanced tier: module layout, material variants with a point context and a state layout, extension points of the Newton driver
acceptance: Every limit not stated here is registered in the ADR before the run. The modules, material variants, point context, state layout, element kind, layup property, section-stiffness hook and the two driver extension points of ADR 0310 section 2 exist; every test of the basic and intermediate tiers (the sb_ and si_ files) compiles and passes unedited, and a registered set of models (patch test, cantilever, bar modes, the elastica of F-397, the free vibration of F-398, a Shell4 plate) gives displacements, stresses, frequencies and histories with the same bits as before the change; with an empty contribution list and no step hook the Newton driver takes the same iterations with the same residuals bit for bit; the default point context (no temperature, no time increment, global axes) reproduces the isotropic stress and tangent bit for bit; each new material variant, the element kind Shell3 and the layup property are refused by every solve with an error naming the variant and the set, never ignored; the complex type satisfies (a b) conj(b) = a |b|^2 and a/a = 1 within 1e-15 on a registered sample and prints and parses losslessly; the baseline hashes are unchanged.
note: Structural solver, advanced tier (plan ADR 0310, 2026-11-12). Size M. Stub ADR 0311; the registration is written by the implementation agent before any code.

title: Orthotropic elasticity with material axes, orthotropic expansion, and temperature-dependent properties from tables
acceptance: Every limit not stated here is registered in the ADR before the run. Orthotropy: with isotropic constants the elasticity matrix equals the isotropic one within 1e-13 relative; constants that are not positive definite are refused naming the constant. Off-axis tension of a block with the material axes turned by 15, 30, 45 and 60 degrees about z: axial strain sigma/E_x with 1/E_x = c^4/E1 + s^4/E2 + (1/G12 - 2 nu12/E1) s^2 c^2 and the shear-extension ratio from the rotated compliance within 1e-10; rotating the model and the axes together leaves the strain energy unchanged within 1e-12. Cantilever of slenderness 20 with E1 along the span and E2 = E1/10: tip deflection P L^3/(3 E1 I) + P L/(kappa G13 A) within 1 percent. Free heating gives the strains alpha_i dT in material axes with zero stress, full restraint the stress -D alpha dT, both within 1e-10. Cylindrical axes: a tube b/a = 2 with E_theta/E_r = 4 under internal pressure in plane stress has the bore hoop stress of the polar-orthotropic closed form (powers r^(k-1) and r^(-k-1), k = sqrt(E_theta/E_r), derived in the registration) within 1 percent. Tables: a bar whose temperature and so its modulus vary linearly from E0 to E1 along it stretches under an end force by F L ln(E1/E0)/(A (E1 - E0)) within 0.1 percent with 20 elements; with alpha = a0 + a1 T the free expansion is a0 (T - Tref) + a1 (T^2 - Tref^2)/2 within 1e-10; a constant table gives the bits of the constant material; a temperature outside a table is refused with the element and the temperature.
note: Structural solver, advanced tier (plan ADR 0310, 2026-11-12). Size M. Stub ADR 0312; the registration is written by the implementation agent before any code.

title: Linear viscoelasticity: Prony series in time, complex modulus in frequency, time-temperature shift
acceptance: Every limit not stated here is registered in the ADR before the run. Relaxation of one element after a strain step: sigma(t) = eps0 (E_inf + sum E_i exp(-t/tau_i)) within 1e-10 at every step end for three branches. Creep of the standard solid under constant stress: eps(t) = sigma0 (1/E_inf - (1/E_inf - 1/E_0) exp(-t/tau_c)), tau_c = tau E_0/E_inf, within 0.1 percent at 20 steps per tau with observed order >= 1.9. The complex modulus function returns E' = E_inf + sum E_i w^2 tau_i^2/(1 + w^2 tau_i^2) and E'' = sum E_i w tau_i/(1 + w^2 tau_i^2) within 1e-13, and a strain cycled in time dissipates pi eps0^2 E'' per cycle and volume within 1 percent at 200 steps per cycle. Shift: the relaxation curve at a temperature with shift factor a_T equals the reference curve at t/a_T within 1e-10. Free vibration of a bar of the standard solid with a loss factor near 0.05 at its first frequency: logarithmic decrement pi E''/E' within 3 percent. A material without branches gives the bits of the elastic one; the internal stresses are saved and restored bit for bit with the integrator state; a non-positive relaxation time or modulus is refused with the key.
note: Structural solver, advanced tier (plan ADR 0310, 2026-11-12). Size M. Stub ADR 0313; the registration is written by the implementation agent before any code.

title: Creep: power law with time hardening, implicit integration with a consistent tangent
acceptance: Every limit not stated here is registered in the ADR before the run. The tangent agrees with central differences within 1e-6. Uniaxial constant stress: creep strain A sigma^n t within 1e-8 for m = 0 and A sigma^n t^(m+1)/(m+1) within 0.1 percent for m = -0.5. Relaxation at fixed strain, n = 3 and 5: sigma(t) = (sigma0^(1-n) + (n - 1) E A t)^(1/(1-n)) within 0.5 percent at the registered step count, observed order >= 0.9. Thick cylinder b/a = 2 in plane strain under internal pressure, n = 4: the stress starts at Lame within 1 percent and tends to the stationary field sigma_r = -p ((b/r)^(2/n) - 1)/((b/a)^(2/n) - 1), sigma_theta = p ((2 - n)/n (b/r)^(2/n) + 1)/((b/a)^(2/n) - 1) within 2 percent after the registered redistribution time. Radial bar clamped on the axis of rotation, n = 3: the tip creeps at the rate A times the integral of (rho Omega^2 (L^2 - r^2)/2)^n over the length within 0.5 percent (the stress is statically determinate). A step whose creep-strain increment exceeds the registered limit is halved; a non-converged local iteration is an error with the element.
note: Structural solver, advanced tier (plan ADR 0310, 2026-11-12). Size S. Stub ADR 0314; the registration is written by the implementation agent before any code.

title: Direct harmonic solve: complex symmetric factorisation, structural (hysteretic) damping, discrete dampers, base excitation
acceptance: Every limit not stated here is registered in the ADR before the run. rcfd-linalg: a random complex symmetric diagonally dominant matrix of order 200 is solved to a residual of 1e-12 relative; a real matrix gives the real factorisation's solution within 1e-13; a pivot below the registered threshold is refused with the equation. Fixed-free bar, nu = 0, loss factor 0.02, tip force: tip response F tan(k L)/(E* A k) with E* = E (1 + i eta) and k = w sqrt(rho/E*), amplitude and phase within 0.5 percent at 0.5, 1.0 and 1.5 times the first frequency. With Rayleigh damping the direct solve equals the mode superposition of F-399 with all modes within 1e-8 on a small model. Tip dashpot c on the same bar: response F/(E A k cot(k L) + i w c) within 0.5 percent, and with c = A sqrt(E rho) the amplitude is F |sin(k L)|/(E A k) (no resonance) within 0.5 percent at five frequencies. Base motion of the clamped end, undamped: tip amplitude 1/cos(k L) of the base within 0.5 percent at half the first frequency. A table of modulus against frequency reproduces the constant-modulus result when constant (1e-12). An undamped solve at a resonance is refused with the frequency; results are bit-identical for 1 and 8 threads.
note: Structural solver, advanced tier (plan ADR 0310, 2026-11-12). Size M. Stub ADR 0315; the registration is written by the implementation agent before any code.

title: High-cycle fatigue: stress-life curves, mean-stress corrections, harmonic and counted histories, linear damage
acceptance: Every limit not stated here is registered in the ADR before the run. Curves and corrections reproduce N = (sigma_a/sigma_f)^(1/b)/2, sigma_a/(1 - sigma_m/sigma_u) (Goodman), sigma_a/(1 - (sigma_m/sigma_u)^2) (Gerber) and Soderberg within 1e-12; a mean stress at or above the strength is refused. Harmonic amplitude: for a normal and a shear component 90 degrees out of phase the von Mises amplitude equals the closed-form maximum over the phase within 1e-10. Cantilever with a static and a harmonic tip force: the largest damage lies on the root surface and the life there equals the hand value from 6 P L/(b h^2) within the registered factor that a 2 percent stress error allows. Plate with a small circular hole (radius/width 0.05) under remote harmonic tension: stress amplitude at the hole edge within 3 percent of 3 sigma (Kirsch) and the life the Basquin life of that stress. Counting: n cycles of constant amplitude give n cycles of that range; a large cycle carrying m small ripples gives 1 and m; a periodic history started at its maximum closes with no residual; a history and its mirror image give the same counts; two load blocks give n1/N1 + n2/N2 within 1e-12. Narrow band: the damage rate nu0 (sqrt(2) s)^m Gamma(1 + m/2)/C within 1e-12 as a function, and the counted damage of a synthesised narrow-band history (registered seed, 1e5 cycles) within 5 percent of it.
note: Structural solver, advanced tier (plan ADR 0310, 2026-11-12). Size M. Stub ADR 0316; the registration is written by the implementation agent before any code.

title: Damped and complex modes: a dense eigensolver for general real matrices and the quadratic eigenproblem on a modal subspace
acceptance: Every limit not stated here is registered in the ADR before the run. rcfd-linalg: the companion matrix of a polynomial with registered real and complex roots returns them within 1e-10; a random matrix of order 50 has residuals |A v - lambda v| <= 1e-10 |A|; a symmetric matrix reproduces the Jacobi values of F-382 within 1e-10; a Jordan block is returned with its eigenvalue within 1e-6 and a report, not a failure; no convergence within the registered sweeps is an error. One oscillator: lambda = -zeta w +/- i w sqrt(1 - zeta^2) within 1e-12. Rayleigh damping a M + b K on a solid model: every mode has the ratio (a/w_j + b w_j)/2 within 1e-8. Skew coupling: a two-unknown system with G = g [[0, 1], [-1, 0]] has the closed-form split frequencies within 1e-12. Fixed-free bar with a tip dashpot c below A sqrt(E rho): lambda_j = (c0/L) (-atanh(c/(A sqrt(E rho))) + i (2 j - 1) pi/2), the first three within 2 percent on 40 modes; at c above that value no oscillating root is returned and the result says so. Damping ratios are -Re(lambda)/|lambda|; conjugate pairs are reported once.
note: Structural solver, advanced tier (plan ADR 0310, 2026-11-12). Size M. Stub ADR 0317; the registration is written by the implementation agent before any code.

title: Coriolis term of a rotating part: gyroscopic matrix in the rotating frame and the Campbell table with split modes
acceptance: Every limit not stated here is registered in the ADR before the run. G is skew within 1e-13 of its norm and x^T G x = 0 within 1e-12. Without the option the table has the bits of F-396; with it at zero speed the frequencies equal those of F-396 within 1e-10. A mass on isotropic springs in the plane of rotation (two unknowns): frequencies |w0 - Omega| and w0 + Omega within 1e-10; the same as a stiff block on elastic supports within 1e-3. Thin ring spinning about its axis (thickness/radius 0.05, nu = 0, full model): the two travelling waves of in-plane mode n differ in frequency by 4 n Omega/(n^2 + 1) within 2 percent for n = 2 and 3 at Omega = 0.1 w_2. Radial beam of square section: the flap frequency equals that of F-396 within 1e-6 relative and the lag frequency moves by the registered second-order estimate within 20 percent of that estimate. Crossings of split modes are tracked without exchange (modal assurance on the complex shapes above 0.9). A speed at which an eigenvalue has a positive real part is reported as unstable with the speed.
note: Structural solver, advanced tier (plan ADR 0310, 2026-11-12). Size M. Stub ADR 0318; the registration is written by the implementation agent before any code.

title: Flexible rotor on bearings in the stationary frame: whirl, critical speeds, unbalance response, joined to the rigid-rotor model
acceptance: Every limit not stated here is registered in the ADR before the run. At zero speed the frequencies equal those of the beam model of F-391 within 1e-10. Disc on a light shaft between two bearings: critical speed sqrt(k/m) and unbalance amplitude e r^2/sqrt((1 - r^2)^2 + (2 zeta r)^2) within 1e-3 at r = 0.5, 1 and 2. In the stiff-shaft limit the critical speeds and the response equal rotordyn::critical_speeds and rotordyn::response for the same rotor within 1e-6.
