Uniform shaft on pins with rotary inertia, 20 elements: forward and backward whirl of modes 1 and 2 equal the roots of E I k^4 - rho A w^2 - rho I k^2 w^2 +/- 2 rho I k^2 Omega w = 0, k = n pi/L, within 0.5 percent at three speeds. Overhung disc on a massless cantilever shaft: the four whirl speeds equal the roots of the two-unknown closed form (derived in the registration) within 0.5 percent. Anisotropic bearings split the critical speed into sqrt(kx/m) and sqrt(ky/m) within 1e-3. A cross-coupled stiffness k_c on a damped disc is stable below c w_n and unstable above, the threshold within 1 percent. Forward and backward are labelled by the sense of the orbit; an unstable speed is reported, never dropped.
note: Structural solver, advanced tier (plan ADR 0310, 2026-11-12). Size M. Stub ADR 0319; the registration is written by the implementation agent before any code.

title: Random vibration: response to force and base-acceleration spectra by modal superposition, root-mean-square stress
acceptance: Every limit not stated here is registered in the ADR before the run. One mode under a flat one-sided force spectrum G: mean-square displacement (pi/2) f_n Q G/k^2 with Q = 1/(2 zeta), and under a flat base acceleration spectrum the mean-square absolute acceleration (pi/2) f_n Q G (for Q well above 1; the exact integral is computed in the registration), both within 0.5 percent at zeta = 0.02 on the registered grid, observed convergence under grid refinement; zero-crossing rate f_n within 1 percent. Two well separated modes: the mean square is the sum within 1 percent. A band-limited spectrum equals the numerical integral registered beforehand within 1e-6. For a uniaxial stress state the root-mean-square von Mises stress equals the root-mean-square stress within 1e-10. Two fully correlated patterns equal one summed pattern within 1e-12; uncorrelated ones add in mean square. A spectrum with a negative value or a non-increasing frequency list is refused with the entry.
note: Structural solver, advanced tier (plan ADR 0310, 2026-11-12). Size S. Stub ADR 0320; the registration is written by the implementation agent before any code.

title: Radiated sound of a vibrating surface: equivalent radiated power and the Rayleigh integral of a baffled plane
acceptance: Every limit not stated here is registered in the ADR before the run. Equivalent radiated power: a rigid piston gives rho c S v^2/2 within 1e-12 and a plate mode sin sin gives rho c A v0^2/8 within 0.5 percent. Rayleigh integral of a circular piston of radius a: on-axis pressure 2 rho c v |sin(k (sqrt(z^2 + a^2) - z)/2)| within 1 percent for z from a to 20 a at k a = 2 and 10 with faces of a tenth of a wavelength; far-field directivity |2 J1(k a sin theta)/(k a sin theta)| within 1 percent; radiated power over the equivalent radiated power equal to 1 - J1(2 k a)/(k a) within 1 percent at k a = 0.5, 2 and 10, and at k a = 0.1 the power rho c k^2 (S v)^2/(4 pi) within 2 percent. Levels: 1e-12 W gives 0 dB and the third-octave sums equal the narrow-band total within 1e-10. A surface that is not plane within the registered tolerance is refused by the Rayleigh integral with its deviation; the equivalent radiated power accepts any surface and its report says that it assumes a radiation efficiency of one.
note: Structural solver, advanced tier (plan ADR 0310, 2026-11-12). Size S. Stub ADR 0321; the registration is written by the implementation agent before any code.

title: Three-node shell element (flat facet, assumed shear strain) for triangulated surfaces
acceptance: Every limit not stated here is registered in the ADR before the run. Membrane patch test and constant-curvature bending patch test on an irregular flat mesh, and on a mesh mixing Shell3 and Shell4, within 1e-8. Simply supported square plate under uniform load, 32 x 32 squares each cut in two, nu = 0.3: centre deflection within 2 percent of the Navier series at thickness/side 0.01 and within 3 percent at 0.001, and within 1 percent of each other for the two diagonal directions. Cantilever strip, nu = 0: tip deflection within 1 percent. Pinched ring strip, 32 elements per quarter: loaded diameter within 3 percent of (pi/4 - 2/pi) P R^3/(E I). Cylinder under internal pressure: radial displacement p R^2/(E t) within 1 percent. First frequency of the simply supported plate within 2 percent. A free plate has six zero frequencies below 1e-6 of the seventh; a single element has exactly six zero eigenvalues; a triangle with an angle below the registered limit is refused with the element.
note: Structural solver, advanced tier (plan ADR 0310, 2026-11-12). Size M. Stub ADR 0322; the registration is written by the implementation agent before any code.

title: Stress stiffening of beams and shells: buckling, pre-stressed modes and the Campbell table of a shell blade
acceptance: Every limit not stated here is registered in the ADR before the run. Beam: Euler loads pi^2 E I/L^2 (pinned) and pi^2 E I/(4 L^2) (clamped-free) with the registered shear correction within 0.1 percent at 8 elements; under tension w_n^2 = (n pi/L)^4 E I/(rho A) + (n pi/L)^2 T/(rho A) within 0.5 percent for n = 1, 2. Rotating radial beam of square section: w_flap^2 - w_lag^2 = Omega^2 within 1e-6 Omega^2 and the stiffening slope equal to the Rayleigh quotient of F-396 within 1 percent. Shell: a simply supported square plate buckles at 4 pi^2 D/a^2 per width in one direction and at 2 pi^2 D/a^2 under equal compression in both, within 2 percent at 16 x 16 Shell4 and 4 percent at 32 x 32 x 2 Shell3; a stretched strip has the tension frequencies above within 1 percent. Equivalence: a flat plate strip twisted by 30 degrees, thickness/chord 0.02, clamped at the root and rotating: the Campbell table of the first four modes as a shell equals that of the solid model of F-396 (Hex20) within 2 percent at the registered speeds. Models of solid elements only keep their bits.
note: Structural solver, advanced tier (plan ADR 0310, 2026-11-12). Size M. Stub ADR 0323; the registration is written by the implementation agent before any code.

title: Aerodynamic damping and added mass of a mode by prescribed motion of the wall (energy method)
acceptance: Every limit not stated here is registered in the ADR before the run. Force harmonics: for a synthetic force history with known in-phase and quadrature parts the extraction returns them within 1e-10, and the work per cycle equals pi q0 times the quadrature part within 1e-10. Piston on a column of incompressible fluid with an open end (the case of F-401): added mass rho_f A L_f within 2 percent and a damping ratio below the registered viscous and time-step estimate. Piston driving a plane channel of gap h and length L_f: force per piston velocity equal to A times the oscillating-channel impedance i w rho L_f/(1 - tanh(kappa)/kappa), kappa = (h/2) sqrt(i w/nu), real and imaginary parts within 3 percent at Womersley numbers 1 and 5 after the registered extrapolation in the time step, and the low-frequency limit 12 mu L_f/h^2 within 3 percent. The damping ratio of the bar on the open column from this method and from the decay of the coupled run of F-401 are both recorded. A history that has not become periodic within the registered tolerance is refused with the cycle-to-cycle change.
note: Structural solver, advanced tier (plan ADR 0310, 2026-11-12). Size M. Stub ADR 0324; the registration is written by the implementation agent before any code.

title: J2 plasticity with isotropic and kinematic hardening: radial return and consistent tangent
acceptance: Every limit not stated here is registered in the ADR before the run. The tangent agrees with central differences within 1e-6 in the elastic and in the plastic branch. Uniaxial bar, bilinear: the stress follows sigma_y + (E H/(E + H)) (eps - sigma_y/E) within 1e-10 in one step and in 100; on reversal the bar yields again at -sigma_max with isotropic and at sigma_max - 2 sigma_y with kinematic hardening within 1e-10. Thick sphere b/a = 2, perfectly plastic, internal pressure: the pressure at plastic radius c equals 2 sigma_y ln(c/a) + (2 sigma_y/3)(1 - c^3/b^3) within 1 percent at c = 1.25 a and 1.5 a, the solve converges at 0.98 of the limit pressure 2 sigma_y ln(b/a), and the residual hoop stress at the bore after unloading equals the closed form within 2 percent. Beam of rectangular section in pure bending: M/M_y = 1.5 - 0.5 (kappa_y/kappa)^2 within 1 percent up to kappa = 5 kappa_y. The last three residuals of each step show an order >= 1.8; a halved step restores the state bit for bit; a non-positive yield stress and a softening curve are refused with the key.
note: Structural solver, advanced tier (plan ADR 0310, 2026-11-12). Size M. Stub ADR 0325; the registration is written by the implementation agent before any code.

title: Nonlinear transient dynamics: Newton iteration inside the Newmark and generalised-alpha step
acceptance: Every limit not stated here is registered in the ADR before the run. At a load factor of 1e-6 the history equals the linear one of F-398 within 1e-9 relative. A stiff slender bar pinned at one end and released from the horizontal under gravity swings with the period 2 pi sqrt(2 L/(3 g)) (2/pi) K(sin 45 degrees) (factor 1.1803, recomputed in the registration) within 1 percent, the total energy constant within 1e-3 of its swing over five periods at the registered step. A free spinning elastic bar keeps its linear momentum within 1e-10 and its angular momentum within 1e-6 relative over ten turns. Large axial oscillation of a bar element with nu = 0 from the stretch 1.2: period equal to the quadrature of the energy integral (computed in the registration) within 0.5 percent. With the spectral radius 1 the generalised-alpha result equals Newmark within 1e-10. A run split by save and restore has the bits of the unsplit run, with a material state included. A step that does not converge after the registered halvings is an error with the time.
note: Structural solver, advanced tier (plan ADR 0310, 2026-11-12). Size M. Stub ADR 0326; the registration is written by the implementation agent before any code.

title: Follower pressure, arc-length continuation, and modes about a nonlinear equilibrium
acceptance: Every limit not stated here is registered in the ADR before the run. Follower pressure: the load stiffness agrees with central differences of the load within 1e-6. Thin ring (thickness/radius 0.02, nu = 0) under internal pressure up to the stretch 1.5: p = E t (lambda^2 - 1)/(2 R) within 1 percent, the dead pressure on the same mesh being the registered control (off by the factor lambda). Linear buckling of the ring under external pressure with the load stiffness: 3 E I/R^3 within 2 percent; without it the registered control 4 E I/R^3 within 3 percent. Arc-length: a two-bar truss of solid bars (nu = 0, height h, bar length L0) is followed to the apex displacement 2.2 h with P = E A (h - w)(2 h w - w^2)/L0^3 within 1e-6 at the registered points and the limit load 2 E A h^3/(3 sqrt(3) L0^3) within 0.5 percent, load control failing at the first limit point (control). Modes about a state: a clamped-clamped beam stretched by an end displacement has the tension frequencies of F-395 within 1 percent, and at a small stretch the tangent modes equal the linear pre-stressed modes within 1e-4; for the rotating radial beam at 0.2 w_0 they equal F-396 within 1e-4, and the difference at higher speed is recorded.
note: Structural solver, advanced tier (plan ADR 0310, 2026-11-12). Size M. Stub ADR 0327; the registration is written by the implementation agent before any code.

title: Hyperelastic materials (neo-Hookean, Mooney-Rivlin) with a mean-dilatation element for near incompressibility
acceptance: Every limit not stated here is registered in the ADR before the run. The tangent agrees with central differences within 1e-6; a rotation of the deformed state leaves the energy unchanged within 1e-10; at a strain of 1e-6 the stress equals linear elasticity with the same shear and bulk modulus within 1e-6 relative. With bulk/shear = 1e4: uniaxial nominal stress mu (lambda - lambda^-2) (neo-Hookean) and 2 (C1 + C2/lambda)(lambda - lambda^-2) (Mooney-Rivlin) for stretches 0.7 to 3, equibiaxial mu (lambda - lambda^-5), simple shear tau = mu gamma with the normal stress difference mu gamma^2, each within 0.1 percent after the registered compressibility correction. Thick spherical shell B/A = 2, neo-Hookean, inflated to the inner stretch 1.5: pressure (mu/2) ((1/l_b^4 + 4/l_b) - (1/l_a^4 + 4/l_a)) with l_b^3 = 1 + (A/B)^3 (l_a^3 - 1) (recomputed by quadrature in the registration) within 1 percent with the mean-dilatation element, the standard Hex8 on the same mesh being the registered locking control. A non-positive modulus is refused; an inverted element is an error with the element.
note: Structural solver, advanced tier (plan ADR 0310, 2026-11-12). Size M. Stub ADR 0328; the registration is written by the implementation agent before any code.

title: Tied non-matching meshes, shell and beam joints to solids, non-matching cyclic boundaries and nodes on the axis
acceptance: Every limit not stated here is registered in the ADR before the run. With matching meshes the tied model equals the merged one within 1e-10. Flat non-matching interfaces 2:3 and 3:5 under uniaxial stress: far-end displacement within 0.1 percent and interface stress within the registered 3 percent (a one-sided node-to-surface tie does not pass the patch test exactly), the error falling with an observed order >= 1 under refinement. A cantilever cut in two and tied 2:3 (Tet10 to Hex20): tip deflection within 1 percent of the closed form. The constraint forces of a tie have zero resultant and moment within 1e-10. A node farther from every face than the registered tolerance is refused with its id. Joints: a beam continuing a solid bar and a shell continuing a solid plate give the tip deflection of the one-piece cantilever within 1 and 2 percent. Cyclic: the ring sector of F-394 with a 2:3 boundary has its frequencies within 0.5 percent of the matching sector; a solid disc with nodes on the axis, spinning (index 0): centre stress (3 + nu) rho Omega^2 b^2/8 within 1 percent; a rod on the axis at index 1 has the bending frequency of the beam within 1 percent, and at index 2 its axis nodes are held.
note: Structural solver, advanced tier (plan ADR 0310, 2026-11-12). Size M. Stub ADR 0329; the registration is written by the implementation agent before any code.

title: Frictionless contact: node-to-surface with an augmented Lagrangian, rigid and deformable targets, interference fits
acceptance: Every limit not stated here is registered in the ADR before the run. A bar pushed against a rigid stop across a gap g: the piecewise-linear force-displacement closed form within 1e-8, the penetration after augmentation below 1e-8 L. Two stacked blocks with matching meshes under pressure p: uniform stress and contact pressure p within 1e-8; pulled apart they separate with no tensile contact force (every multiplier >= 0). Elastic sphere on a rigid plane: contact radius (3 F R/(4 E*))^(1/3), peak pressure 3 F/(2 pi a^2) and approach a^2/R within 5, 5 and 3 percent at a/R = 0.1 with at least ten nodes across the contact radius. Interference fit of a ring (outer radius b) on a solid shaft (radius a) of the same material with radial interference d, plane stress: contact pressure E d (b^2 - a^2)/(2 a b^2) within 2 percent, and the hoop stress of the ring that of Lame under that pressure within 2 percent. The contact tangent agrees with central differences within 1e-6 in a fixed active set; the last residuals of a step with a settled active set show an order >= 1.8; an active set that cycles beyond the registered count is an error with the nodes.
note: Structural solver, advanced tier (plan ADR 0310, 2026-11-12). Size M. Stub ADR 0330; the registration is written by the implementation agent before any code.

title: Laminated shell: layup stiffness, ply stresses and failure indices
acceptance: Every limit not stated here is registered in the ADR before the run. One isotropic ply gives the bits of the Shell4 of F-392. Layup stiffness: a symmetric layup has no coupling (|B| <= 1e-12 |A| t); [0/90]s has A11 = A22 = t (Q11 + Q22)/2; [0/+60/-60]s and [0/45/-45/90]s have A11 = A22, A66 = (A11 - A12)/2 and A16 = A26 = 0, all within 1e-12 relative. Simply supported square plate of a cross-ply symmetric layup under a sinusoidal load: centre deflection q0 a^4/(pi^4 (D11 + 2 (D12 + 2 D66) + D22)) within 1 percent at thickness/side 0.01 with 16 x 16 elements. Unsymmetric [0/90] strip heated uniformly: curvature equal to the closed form of the two-ply laminate (solved by hand in the registration) within 0.5 percent with zero resultants. Off-axis coupon at 15, 30, 45 and 60 degrees: ply stresses sigma c^2, sigma s^2 and -sigma s c within 1e-10, Tsai-Hill failure stress (c^4/X^2 + (1/S^2 - 1/X^2) s^2 c^2 + s^4/Y^2)^(-1/2) within 1e-10, and Tsai-Wu equal to the tensile and compressive strengths on the axes within 1e-12. A layup with a non-positive thickness or an unknown material is refused with the ply.
note: Structural solver, advanced tier (plan ADR 0310, 2026-11-12). Size M. Stub ADR 0331; the registration is written by the implementation agent before any code.

title: Fracture parameters: J-integral by the domain form, stress intensity factor, crack-growth life
acceptance: Every limit not stated here is registered in the ADR before the run. Centre crack of half-length a in a plate of half-width W = 10 a under tension, plane strain (one layer, held in z), Hex20: K_I from J within 2 percent of sigma sqrt(pi a) sqrt(sec(pi a/(2 W))), the values of rings 2 to 4 within 1 percent of each other, and J equal to the change of potential energy between two models with half-lengths a +/- 0.02 a within 2 percent. K_I from the opening displacement within 5 percent. Penny-shaped crack of radius a in a cylinder of radius 10 a under tension (heavy record): K_I = 2 sigma sqrt(a/pi) within 3 percent, uniform along the front within 2 percent. Under pure shear loading of the centre crack the mode-I factor from the opening is zero within 1e-8 of the tension value. Growth: the cycles from a0 to a1 by the Paris law with K = d sigma sqrt(pi a) equal the closed-form integral for m = 3 and the logarithm for m = 2 within 1e-6. A front that is not straight within the registered tolerance and a ring that reaches the boundary are refused.
note: Structural solver, advanced tier (plan ADR 0310, 2026-11-12). Size M. Stub ADR 0332; the registration is written by the implementation agent before any code.

title: Substructuring: static condensation and fixed-interface component mode synthesis (Craig-Bampton)
acceptance: Every limit not stated here is registered in the ADR before the run. Statics: the condensed model gives the retained displacements and, after recovery, the interior ones and the stresses of the full model within 1e-10. Keeping every fixed-interface mode reproduces all frequencies of the full model within 1e-8 (small model). A bar of two substructures with five modes each: the first three frequencies of the assembly within 0.1 percent of the full model and not below it (1e-10), the error falling monotonically with the number of modes. The reduced matrices are symmetric within 1e-13 and the reduced mass is positive definite; a free substructure keeps six zero frequencies below 1e-6 of the seventh. Harmonic response of the assembly equals the full model within 1 percent up to half the lowest omitted fixed-interface frequency. A reduced part written to its file and read back gives the same bits. An interface set with no nodes and a mode count above the interior size are refused.
note: Structural solver, advanced tier (plan ADR 0310, 2026-11-12). Size M. Stub ADR 0333; the registration is written by the implementation agent before any code.

title: Sparse L D L^T with a fill-reducing ordering, and its use by the static, buckling and modal solves
acceptance: Every limit not stated here is registered in the ADR before the run. Five-point grid 100 x 100 and seven-point grid 30^3: residual below 1e-12 relative, and on the 30^3 grid at most half the factor entries of the envelope after reverse Cuthill-McKee (both counts recorded). On a solid model the solution equals the envelope solver's within 1e-10 and the modal frequencies through either factorisation agree within 1e-9. Inertia: for the tridiagonal (2, -1) of order 200 and three shifts the number of negative pivots of K - s I equals the number of eigenvalues 4 sin^2(j pi/(2 (n + 1))) below s. A matrix that is not positive definite is reported with the equation when positive definiteness was requested. Factor and solution are bit-identical for 1 and 8 threads. Heavy record: a clamped cube of about 3e5 unknowns is solved, time and memory recorded beside the envelope's estimate. The default solver's results keep their bits.
note: Structural solver, advanced tier (plan ADR 0310, 2026-11-12). Size M. Stub ADR 0334; the registration is written by the implementation agent before any code.

title: Stress recovery by element patches and an energy-norm error estimate
acceptance: Every limit not stated here is registered in the ADR before the run. A linear displacement field gives the exact stress and a zero estimate within 1e-10. On the manufactured solution of F-378 for Hex8, Tet10 and Hex20: the effectivity index (estimate over true error in the energy norm) lies in [0.8, 1.2] on the three finest meshes and its distance from 1 does not grow under refinement; the recovered stress of Hex8 converges in L2 at an observed order >= 1.7 where the raw stress shows >= 0.9. Plate with a small circular hole under tension: the recovered peak stress is within 2 percent of 3 sigma on the mesh on which the averaged nodal stress of F-376 is recorded, and the tenth of the elements with the largest indicator contains the elements at the hole edge. Boundary and corner nodes take the patch of the nearest interior node by the registered rule; the result is bit-identical for 1 and 8 threads; a patch with too few points is reported, not solved.
note: Structural solver, advanced tier (plan ADR 0310, 2026-11-12). Size S. Stub ADR 0335; the registration is written by the implementation agent before any code. ADR 0277 (2026-11-12): recover::IntegrationPointField carries per element the positions, weights w det J, strain and stress of the stiffness rule's points (offsets, points_of(e)); recover::nodal_average is the averaged nodal stress to compare against.

title: Elasticity solves on the ranks of rcfd-dist and on the CUDA device
acceptance: Every limit not stated here is registered in the ADR before the run. Ranks: with one rank the iteration counts and the solution have the bits of the serial CG of F-381 with the same preconditioner; with 2, 4 and 8 ranks the solution of a clamped cube (about 4e4 unknowns) and of a cantilever of Tet10 equals the serial one within 1e-8 relative at a residual of 1e-10, in at most twice the iterations of one rank (counts recorded); repeated runs with the same rank count give the same bits; the three unknowns of a node are never split; a rank that fails or times out ends the solve with a located error. Scaling is recorded, not asserted. Device: with a usable device the device CG equals the CPU CG with the same preconditioner within 1e-9 on a cube of at least 3e5 unknowns, times recorded; `auto` below the threshold runs on the CPU; without a device `cuda` is a located error and `auto` falls back with the reason recorded, and the device clauses are reported as not run. The default solver's results and the baseline hashes are unchanged.
note: Structural solver, advanced tier (plan ADR 0310, 2026-11-12). Size M. Stub ADR 0336; the registration is written by the implementation agent before any code. rcfd-api gains a dependency on rcfd-dist (decision A5 of ADR 0310).

title: Public coupled benchmark (the elastic flag behind a cylinder): structural tests CSM1 to CSM3 and the steady coupled case FSI1 (needs the maintainer: reference values)
acceptance: Every limit not stated here is registered in the ADR before the run. NEEDS THE MAINTAINER'S APPROVAL to record the published values in docs/reference-data.md before it starts; no limit below uses a value recalled from memory. Structure alone (plane strain, one element thick): the tip displacement of CSM1 and CSM2 within 1 percent of the published values, both components; CSM3 (released under gravity, undamped): mean, amplitude and frequency of both tip components within 2 percent, on two meshes with the change recorded. Flow alone with a rigid flag (CFD1): drag within 2 percent and lift within 10 percent of the published values (gate; if it misses, the coupled case is not run and the item is partial). Coupled steady case FSI1: drag within 2 percent, tip displacement in x within 5 percent and in y within 10 percent, lift within 10 percent, with the coupling converged to 1e-6 in the final state and the iteration counts recorded. The unsteady cases FSI2 and FSI3 are not run.
note: Structural solver, advanced tier (plan ADR 0310, 2026-11-12). Size M. Stub ADR 0337; the registration is written by the implementation agent before any code. Blocked until the maintainer approves recording the published values of the benchmark in docs/reference-data.md (decision A2 of ADR 0310); nothing depends on it.

title: Solid case file: the materials, analyses and results of the advanced tier
acceptance: Every limit not stated here is registered in the ADR before the run. Each new analysis run from a file gives the bits of the same model run by library calls (limit 1e-12, expected identical), and one closed-form check of each library package passes from files: the off-axis block (ADR 0312), the relaxation curve (ADR 0313), the rotating creeping bar (ADR 0314), the bar with a loss factor (ADR 0315), the cantilever life (ADR 0316), the plane oscillator's split (ADR 0318), the single-mode mean square (ADR 0320), the piston's equivalent radiated power (ADR 0321). An unknown key, a material that lacks a required constant, a fatigue request without a mean or an alternating case, a table that is not increasing and an analysis that names a missing set are each refused with the key and the line. Every solid case file of the tests of the earlier tiers gives the same report and the same .vtu bytes as before. No flow case key, CLI help text, MCP tool list, hash table or golden changes (the existing schema, CLI and tool-list tests pass unedited).
note: Structural solver, advanced tier (plan ADR 0310, 2026-11-12). Size M. Stub ADR 0338; the registration is written by the implementation agent before any code.

title: Demonstration on the 120 mm fan: a polymer blade (orthotropy, temperature, creep, fatigue at a Campbell crossing) and the radiated power of the frame
acceptance: Every limit not stated here is registered in the ADR before the run. Blade from solid case files. With isotropic constants and no temperature the Campbell table has the bits of F-406. A uniform temperature at which the table gives 0.8 E scales every frequency at rest by sqrt(0.8) within 1e-8. For the orthotropic blade the change of each squared frequency at rest for a 1 percent change of E1 equals the Rayleigh-quotient sensitivity within 1 percent. With the Coriolis term the first four frequencies at the maximum speed differ from those without by less than the registered bound, both recorded. Creep at the maximum speed over the registered time: tip growth monotone, its initial rate within the registered factor of the one-dimensional estimate, change between two meshes below 5 percent. Fatigue at a registered crossing: the safety-factor field is written, the largest alternating stress changes by less than 10 percent between two meshes and lies in the same region, and doubling the pressure harmonic changes the Goodman factor as the formula says within 1e-8. Frame: the equivalent radiated power spectrum at the rotation and blade-passing frequencies is written and equals (rho c/2) sum A |v_n|^2 recomputed from the output within 1e-10. The page docs/structural-solver.md lists every assumed input and states that no material datum, life, creep growth or sound level is validated against a measurement.
note: Structural solver, advanced tier (plan ADR 0310, 2026-11-12). Size M. Stub ADR 0339; the registration is written by the implementation agent before any code.

title: Strong coupling in the case tree: a case whose force floor decides the convergence test
acceptance: A tree-against-library equality test of the strong coupling whose force_scale decides the convergence test of every step (for instance force_scale = 100 k X on the piston of ADR 0266) is bit-identical, and fails when the driver does not read force_scale; registered before the run.
note: DONE pending acceptance, merged 2026-11-12. From ADR 0266 question 1, recommendation taken on the maintainer's standing instruction of 2026-11-11. DONE (ADR 0349, 2026-11-12; registered before the code, test-only, no library or driver line changed): crates/rcfd-api/tests/strong_coupling_force_floor_f437.rs runs the spring-mounted piston of ADR 0266 at mass ratio 4 through the case driver with force_scale = moment_scale = 100 k X and the default wall pressure (prescribed_gradient), against strong_step_with(PrescribedGradient) with a carried vector: 60 steps bit-identical in the flow, the body, the iteration counts and, new against ADR 0266 E1, the test quantity of every step; at all 180 iterations the test quantity is |r_F|/force_scale bit for bit (the largest force is 0.0088 of the floor). The driver mutated to ignore force_scale fails it at step 1 (bits, 4 iterations against 3, test quantity); the same case with force_scale = 1e-9 k X (the floor never binds; the smallest force is 1.6e7 times it) is equal with and without that mutation. Why ADR 0266 E1 could not catch it: with moment_scale = 0 the moment term of the test is the unfloored force ratio (the piston's moment is a fixed arm times its force), so a force floor alone is inert on that case; the moment floor is written with it here. Open: ADR 0349 Q1 (F-350's status), Q2 (a force floor without a moment floor).

title: Directional lattice in the case key [mesh.adapt]
acceptance: With lattice = "directional" in [mesh.adapt] a steady box-mesh case runs the directional loop and equals the library run bit for bit on the ADR 0267 suction layer (1547 cells, error 0.00298); options the directional lattice does not take are located errors; cases without the key give identical hashes.
note: TODO (from ADR 0267 R5): keys lattice, axis_ratio (theta) and per-axis finest levels; fixed_fraction and register on the directional lattice need small additions to rcfd_fv::adaptive; a cycle whose solve does not converge should be named in the stop reason (ADR 0267 amendment 2). Changes the schema golden. From ADR 0267 R5, recommendation taken on the maintainer's standing instruction of 2026-11-11. The agent reports that the keys change the schema golden; check the optional-table route of ADR 0257 and 0266 first, else it needs the maintainer. The coarsening of F-441 (ADR 0343, 2026-11-12) would add a key coarsen_ratio (phi, default 0 = off, at most axis_ratio / 4).

title: Directional lattice: coarsening in three dimensions by a box merge
acceptance: On a lattice with three refined axes, repeated all-axes coarsening returns every state made by splits and merges, including the five-box tiling of ADR 0267 amendment 1, to the base with sum V q conserved; slab results and the isotropic AmrMesh paths stay bit for bit.
note: DONE pending acceptance, merged 2026-11-12. DONE (ADR 0341, 2026-11-12): rcfd_mesh::adapt::aniso::AnisoMesh::adapt_with(marks, balance, Coarsening::Box), opt-in: for each cell marked coarsen along axes C, the smallest dyadic ancestor box (levels lowered only along C) that is exactly tiled by leaves of the mesh, each marked along every axis on which it is coarsened, is merged into one leaf with the levels of the box; with balance the merge is accepted only if the new leaf stays within one level of its face neighbours along every refined axis; the transfer is the existing Merged source (volume-weighted mean, so sum V q is conserved and linear fields stay exact). Under all-axes marks the base cell is always an admissible ancestor, so every call merges at least once and repeated all-axes coarsening without balance returns any tiling to the base. The five-box tiling of ADR 0267 amendment 1 goes to one cell in one call; 26 states on two 3-D lattices (G6's 146 cells, the pair-stuck state, 24 random sequences of splits, pair merges and box merges, 6 of them pair-stuck) return to the base in at most 6 calls with sum V q to 1e-13 and linear fields to 1e-12; single-axis marks give the pair merges; consent and balance refuse the registered cases. adapt (Coarsening::Pair) is unchanged: equal to adapt_with(.., Pair) bit for bit, the ADR 0267 tests (G6b in the slab among them, the G6 known miss unchanged) and the AmrMesh tests pass unedited. Six mutations caught. With balance the return to the base is not derived (one recorded run reached it). Follow-up: F-441.

title: Corrected wall-force reports on moving walls in the case tree (opt-in)
acceptance: An opt-in key makes the force, moment and force-coefficient reports of a moving-mesh case take the wall pressure of the kept fixed-flux gradient (the face pressure of sixdof::patch_force_moment_wall_gradient) on the following and resting walls; on the rigid column of ADR 0269 AU1b the report's force deficit falls from 2.5e-2 to at most 1e-4; without the key every report value is bit-identical; registered before the run.
note: DONE pending acceptance, merged 2026-11-12. From ADR 0269 question 3, recommendation taken on the maintainer's standing instruction of 2026-11-11. DONE (ADR 0342, 2026-11-12; registered before the code, one amendment before any run). The optional table [dynamic_mesh.force_reports] with wall_pressure = "prescribed_gradient" (default "boundary_value"; a key per report or in dynamic_mesh would be filled into every case by coerce and need an H1 hash-table entry, ADR 0266; the six_dof.coupling table is refused for prescribed motion) makes the force, moment and force-coefficient reports of a moving-mesh case take, on the following and resting walls, the face pressure of sixdof::patch_force_moment_wall_gradient with the kept fixed-flux gradient (Simulation::report_pressure_face_values), bit for bit per face. On the rigid column of ADR 0269 AU1b the report's force deficit falls from 2.5004597e-2 to 4.6e-6 (limit 1e-4); total force, moment and coefficient likewise (4.4e-6, 4.4e-6, 4.6e-6), the same with the wall following the mesh. Without the table every report value and the run are bit-identical, and the key does not change the flow. No existing input combines a moving mesh and a force report; with the default flipped no test moves. K0 unedited; five mutations caught, one equivalent. Open, the maintainer's: the default (ADR 0342 Q1, with ADR 0269 Q1). Default flip approved by the maintainer in person on 2026-11-12, together with F-358's. Default flip applied (ADR 0346, 2026-11-12): without the table the force, moment and force-coefficient reports on moving walls take prescribed_gradient (the column's fp deficit 2.5004597e-2 -> 4.597e-6), except with layering or the compressible solver, which keep the stored values silently (only a written table is refused there); wall_pressure = "boundary_value" gives the old bits; no registered hash moved; ADR 0342's T0, Z0 to Z2, E3, A1c and F1 controls now write boundary_value.

title: Directional lattice: coarsening inside the directional adaptive loop
acceptance: On the ADR 0267 suction layer, a directional loop that also box-coarsens cells whose per-axis variation is below a registered fraction of the largest reaches the error E(D) = 0.00298 of ADR 0267's run D with fewer than its 1547 cells and fewer leaves split along x than its 704; runs that do not ask for coarsening are bit for bit unchanged.
note: DONE pending acceptance, merged 2026-11-12. DONE (ADR 0343, 2026-11-12): rcfd_fv::adaptive, opt-in: directional_coarsen_axes and directional_coarsen_marks mark a cell to coarsen along axis a when its per-axis variation E_a is below phi times the cell's largest and its level along a is above 0; phi <= theta / 4 (1/8 with theta = 1/2) is required, derived so that a just-split axis is not coarsened back and an axis merged by one or two levels is not split again (checked exactly on a 129 x 129 grid of variations). Each cycle of run_adaptive_simple_directional_coarsen_target (and of run_adaptive_simple_directional_coarsening with any coarsening marks) first box-merges with Coarsening::Box and then refines on the coarsened lattice towards the scheduled count (directional_coarsen_refine_step; merged cells ranked by the volume-weighted mean of their children's gradients, merged_gradients); a merged cell takes the volume-weighted mean of the values it replaces, then the refinement transfer of the settings applies. On the ADR 0267 suction layer (16 x 16 base, levels 5, 6 cycles, target 1280) the coarsening run has error 0.0029776 (limit 0.00298) with 1292 cells and 413 leaves split along x, against ADR 0267's run D (1547 cells, 704) and the same target without coarsening (1283 cells, 0.0029752, 494 leaves); 62 merges, no alternation; marking every cell to coarsen along every axis gives 0.48. With phi = 0 the loop equals run_adaptive_simple_directional_target bit for bit; no existing line changed; the ADR 0267, 0341, 0247 and 0242 tests pass unedited (the F-348 heavy layer runs included). Six mutations caught. Not removed: x splits outside the layer, where the variations are at the solver tolerance and the ratio carries no information (251 of the 413).

title: Overset BDF2: the step-size-dependent remainder made by the motion through the coupling
acceptance: The remainder of TG_2 with BDF2, three outer iterations and rhie_chow_step_consistent (max abs(d_200) 2.057e-5 with the ratio 2.454 to max abs(d_400), ADR 0245 A2; 1.3e-7 with the ratio 4.98 on the coupled meshes of level 1 at rest against 5.2e-5 moving, ADR 0245 H10) is traced to a named event or term of the moving coupling with a number, and either removed as an opt-in (defaults bit-identical; D2 of ADR 0241 at least 4 on TG_2) or the ADR names why not with a number.
note: From ADR 0245 question 1, recommendation (a), taken on the maintainer's standing instruction of 2026-11-11. ADR 0359, 2026-11-12: PARTIAL. Named, with numbers: the remainder of TG_2 with BDF2, three outer iterations and rhie_chow_step_consistent (2.057e-5, ratio 2.454, reproduced to five digits) is made by two events of the moving coupling, both at moments fixed by the motion and not by the step (first-order events). (1) The donor switch of the component's outer fringe: the library's stencil is chosen by the cell of the other part that contains the fringe centre, so the interpolant jumps when the centre crosses a face of that part (about 2600 switches per run); with a pose-continuous bilinear stencil on the component's fringe (test side) the component cells fall from 2.06e-5 to 1.16e-6, ratio 2.45 -> 4.15. (2) The background cells changing kind next to the hole (275 cells, 503 changes per run): with every stencil continuous 9.92e-6 remains at a ratio of 1.845, 8.8 times larger within two cells of a kind change than elsewhere. Ruled out: the outer loop under motion (6.6e-8). Why no opt-in: a stencil removes event 1 but not event 2, so the most continuous stencil gives D2 1.845 on TG_2 (limit 4); no library code was built, the defaults are untouched (fingerprints of the default and the BDF2 overset runs and of the linear and quadratic connectivities equal to the base tree; baseline_hashes passes). Partial by the registered rule: the events were confirmed by hypotheses of an amendment after the first runs (the registered H1 and H2 fell between their limits). Both parts are below the spatial error of TG_2 (3.2e-4) by a factor 15. Follow-ups proposed (ADR 0359 questions 1 and 2), not taken.

title: Transient step: the step-consistent face coefficient on the remaining paths
acceptance: rhie_chow_step_consistent acts with the consistent correctors and on PimpleSolver::step_ale_with_walls (defaults bit-identical); with a body force a hydrostatic column stays at rest to 1e-10 and the steady solution of a buoyant cavity is the same to 1e-9 for two step sizes; the case tree has a key for it; the check C3 of ADR 0245 holds on each path, or the ADR names why not with a number.
note: DONE pending acceptance, merged 2026-11-12. From ADR 0245 question 3, recommendation (a), taken on the maintainer's standing instruction of 2026-11-11. ADR 0352, 2026-11-12: DONE. PimpleSettings::rhie_chow_step_consistent (ADR 0245's harmonic face coefficient and lagged-gradient commutator) now acts with the consistent correctors (their compensation takes interp(rAtU) - Gamma face by face, so a converged step is C's) and on step_ale / step_ale_with_walls (the gate's moving-mesh and consistent exclusions dropped); step_sliding keeps the default step (bit for bit) and the fractional step is unchanged (its face coefficient is uniform, so C would change nothing; bit for bit). Defaults bit for bit (the rcfd-fv suites touching the changed lines and baseline_hashes, case_hashes_w48u unedited). C3 of ADR 0245 on each path: consistent correctors 4.7e-13 between dt 0.04 and 0.01 (3.75e-4 without C), translating cavity through step_ale_with_walls 2.2e-13 (3.06e-4 without), buoyant cavity at Ra 1e3 2.1e-14 relative between dt 0.004 and 0.001 (6.0e-5 without), 4.0e-14 with the consistent correctors too; a hydrostatic column stays at rest to 2.1e-14 and reaches rest from zero pressure to 1.6e-12 (limit 1e-10). Why not on the other paths: the fractional step's own steady cavity differs by 8.7e-2 between the two steps (a first-order defect dt R(p) without a carry-over, not C's term); coupled faces bit-inert (P1), seam floor of ADR 0076 unchanged. Case key: the optional table [solver.rhie_chow] step_consistent (default false; absent from every case's text and hash), located errors with steady, compressible, variable-density and VOF runs, the fractional step and lumped components; acts on the tree's dynamic mesh. Eight mutations caught. Follow-up proposed for the fractional step (ADR 0352 Q2).

title: Co-simulation participants from the case, hosted by rcfd serve
acceptance: A case key names a moving wall patch as a co-simulation fluid participant and rcfd serve hosts it under protocol rcfd-cosim/1; a structural participant in its own process (the mock of ADR 0345) and the coupler of rcfd_fv::cosim drive it over TCP and reproduce ADR 0256 A1 and A2 with the displacements of the in-process run to 1e-12; describe of a structure may carry its elements so that the map builders of ADR 0263 run on the side of the coupler; service::Client writes a request with one call; without the key every case hash is unchanged and the schema, CLI help and MCP goldens change only by the approved additions.
note: PARTIAL (ADR 0380, 2026-11-12; registered before the code, one amendment before any run). An optional case table [cosim] (patch, participant, fixed_patches, smoothing_method, smoothing_exponent, smoothing_tolerance, initial_displacement) names a moving wall patch of an incompressible piso/pimple case as the co-simulation fluid participant (rcfd_api::cosim_case::fluid_from_case: the case's mesh is the reference, the flow starts at rest on it moved by initial_displacement, every advance smooths the interior and makes one flow step; any other model the simulation would advance is refused by name; rcfd run refuses the case), and rcfd serve --cosim <case> hosts it under rcfd-cosim/1 (cosim_case::host). On the model problem of ADR 0256 written as a case, with the mock structure of ADR 0345 in a third process and the unchanged coupled_step driving both over TCP: all 650 steps converged (7 to 10 iterations, mean 8.766, last test 9.995e-9), omega_m/omega 0.998618 and 1.011453, and the displacements of every node at every step equal to the in-process run of the same case bit for bit (limit 1e-12 X; the case also equals the hand-built CWs bit for bit over 100 steps); a structure stiffer by 1e-9 is seen (4.15e-9 X). Structure::elements (a provided method, empty by default) is carried by cosim.describe only when not empty and returned by RemoteStructure::elements, so InterfaceMap::build runs on the coupler's side with the bits of the in-process build. service::Client writes each request with one call (unit-tested; 0.047 ms per call). Without the table every case hash, written case text and baseline hash is unchanged and the MCP goldens pass unedited; the schema gains the optional property cosim and the help of serve gains [--cosim <case>], both awaiting the maintainer's approval (ADR 0380 Q1). Seven of eight mutations caught; treating fixed_patches as sliding is not seen by this model problem (its wall moves along x only, so a sliding and a fixed xmax give the same mesh; Q3). Not delivered: a structure from a case, the participant's own name (always fluid, Q2), more than one participant per rcfd serve, models other than the incompressible flow. Open: ADR 0380 Q1 to Q4. ADR 0381 (2026-11-13, F-481): MU5 is now caught by a tangential wall displacement; F-444 stays partial for the schema and serve help approval (ADR 0380 Q1).

title: Overset: prescribed flux on the faces between calculated and fringe cells
acceptance: An opt-in of the overset step under which the flux of a face between a calculated and a fringe cell is the face interpolation of the interpolated fringe velocity plus one correction per closed fringe ring that makes the net flux of each enclosed part zero (ADR 0340, the switch described there): on RE of ADR 0340 at levels 1 to 3 the following coefficient a_c at both fringes is at least 0.9 at t = 0.025 and the order of R_b at t = 0.5 is at least 1.7 on both pairs, on RL the order of R_b is at least 1.7 within the parity families (levels 1 to 3 and 2 to 4), continuity of the calculated cells and the mass of the domain hold to 1e-9, the uniform-flow check U1 of ADR 0219 holds, and without the opt-in every overset result is bit-identical; or the ADR shows with a number why the prescribed flux is not admissible.
note: From ADR 0340 question 2, recommendation taken on the maintainer's standing instruction of 2026-11-11. ADR 0347, 2026-11-12: PARTIAL. Built as an opt-in of the overset solver, OversetSolver::set_fringe_flux, default off, every result without it bit-identical (state hashes of two runs equal to those of the library before, baseline_hashes and the twelve existing overset test files pass unedited). The flux of a face between a calculated and a fringe cell is the face interpolation of the velocity each pressure corrector starts from plus one correction per region of calculated cells that makes its net flux zero (it replaces the offset of the background fringe pressures). The switch as ADR 0340 words it (variant P, the interpolated fringe pressure left in the Green-Gauss gradient of the calculated cells next to the fringe) is not admissible: the Taylor-Green run on RE blows up at step 5 (level 1) and step 3 (level 2), the error growing 11-fold and 60-fold per step, as predicted before the run from the pressure mismatch of the two parts (growth with the refinement). With that gradient taken from the own part (variant G, FringeFlux::PrescribedOwnGradient) it is stable: continuity 4.5e-13, flux through the hole ring 1.9e-14, U1 3.6e-15, a uniformly accelerating flow exact to 2e-15, the flux of a ring face equal to the mean of the two cell velocities to 4e-4. Order of R_b at t = 0.5 on RE 1.962, 1.789 (default coupling 0.983, 1.015); on RL within the parity families 2.704 (levels 1 to 3) and 2.124 (2 to 4); the response per unit of truncation is 1.51, 1.54, 1.65 at levels 1 to 3 (default 0.168, 0.339, 0.497). Missed: a_c at t = 0.025 is 0.598, 0.856, 0.931 at the background fringe and 0.867, 1.037, 1.053 at the component fringe against 0.9 (levels 1 and 2 miss); diagnosed as the decay of the answer of the calculated cells over one cell (the dipole estimate made before the run gave 0.65 at level 1), not a softness of the imposition; it rises to 0.906, 0.968, 0.989 by t = 0.5. Found on the way, registered checks missed and kept as known misses: under G the interpolation error reaches the calculated cells in full, so the velocity error against the exact solution on RE is 1.77, 1.64, 1.62 times that of the default coupling (limit 1.5) and R_b itself is 9.0, 4.6, 3.3 times the default's; with the quadratic donor interpolation of F-336 on both fringes the error of G falls to 0.63, 0.60, 0.56 of that and is 1.145, 1.056, 1.035 times the default's (hypothesis confirmed by its registered numbers). Not a candidate for a default. One unit check missed by round-off of its own test values (2.0e-12 against 1e-12) and was corrected by an amendment before the corrected run. Seven mutations caught. Not covered: accuracy with a moving component, RL at level 5, the combination with the other overset opt-ins beyond a smoke check. ADR 0376 (F-450), 2026-11-12: G runs with the moving, turning component of ADR 0219 without a fault (TG_1 and TG_2, quadratic stencils, continuity 6e-13, no refusal); the motion does not add to its excess over the default coupling, which sits in the calculated background cells next to the background fringe (the one-sided gradient of D5).

title: Lab-frame memory as the behaviour of the attached matched sponge
acceptance: With the maintainer's approval, the matched forms in SpongeFrame::AttachedToMesh use the memory of the lab frame (ADR 0344); the F-341 matched records are re-recorded once with that approval, the plain form and every run without motion stay bit-identical, and the ADR 0344 checks pass unchanged.
note: NEEDS THE USER: it changes the results of the F-341 matched forms (re-recording their records).

title: Electron over the rcfd APIs: performance spike (control, live events, field transfer, scrubbing, WebGPU draw)
acceptance: The checks P1 to P12 of ADR 0350 are run once as registered on the maintainer's machine, with the rcfd-studio control column measured first; each bulk route (R0 JSON baseline, R1 binary side channel under an opt-in data.* method family of protocol 1.2, R2 a TypeScript reader of store.rts, R3 a WebAssembly reader if it needs no new crate) is recorded; the negative controls NC1 and NC2 hold; the decision of ADR 0350 section 4 (viable, viable with conditions, not viable) is stated with the numbers; no existing service method, golden or hash changes.
note: ADR 0350 (2026-11-12), asked for by the maintainer. Q1 (run the spike) answered by the maintainer in person on 2026-11-12; Q2 to Q5 taken with the recommendations (ADR 0350 decision record). ADR 0350, 2026-11-12. The Electron spike ran once on the maintainer's machine (Electron 45.1.0, RTX 5080, 60 Hz display, load 0.3 to 0.6). Bulk data is fast enough and exact by both routes: R1 (the opt-in `data.*` methods, `rcfd-data/1`, service protocol 1.2, raw `f32` on a second TCP connection) loads a 1e6-cell scalar to a GPU buffer in p50 25.9 ms, p99 57.7 ms; R2 (a reader of `store.rts` in Node) in p50 14.2 ms, p99 22.4 ms; JSON (R0) takes 552 ms. Scrubbing 30.8 and 60.1 snapshots per s at 1e6 cells, 10.5 and 17.8 at 4e6; first picture of the 1e6 surface 1.15 s (R1, first opening 1.58 s) and 0.06 s (R2); 1e6 triangles at 332 frames per s without a rate limit and p99 16.9 ms per frame with vertical sync; cold start median 0.38 s (one start of ten took 6.7 s); renderer memory 112 MB with 20 snapshots; 0 differing bits in 672e6 values; service round trip p50 0.06 ms; event latency p99 under 2.1 ms. Missed: P3, `monitors.get` of 4 series of 1e5 samples takes 127 ms against 100 ms (a 12 MB reply, most of the time on the service's side). R3 (WebAssembly) not run: it needs `unsafe` exports or `wasm-bindgen`. The rcfd-studio control, offscreen: 12.7 ms per snapshot, 73 per s, first picture 1.25 s. The registered rule has no outcome for a miss of P3 alone, so viability is the maintainer's decision; questions QA1 to QA5 of addendum 1. P3 is met after F-456 (ADR 0353, 2026-11-12): median 82.6 ms against 100; viability remains the maintainer's decision.

title: Electron Studio to parity with rcfd-studio
acceptance: An Electron shell in TypeScript over the service and the bulk route chosen by F-447 passes every parity check of ADR 0350 section 5 (the docs/ui-restart-plan.md section 6 list and the Studio checks added since), automated with Playwright where a check can be automated and by the maintainer's view-and-report where it cannot; its field values equal the Rust reader's bit for bit; rcfd-studio is frozen while it is built.
note: ADR 0350 section 5. NEEDS THE USER: starts only on the maintainer's go-ahead after a viable F-447. ADR 0350 addendum 1 (2026-11-12) measured both bulk routes as fast enough; recommended: the Node reader of `store.rts` (R2) for local projects, `data.*` (R1) for a remote service, monitors fetched once and then by increments. Open before the start: the maintainer's go-ahead, QA1 (the cost of `monitors.get`) and QA2 (the route). F-456 (ADR 0353): the history is fetched once, then `since` increments at 0.3 ms; QA1 is answered.

title: Retire rcfd-studio and rcfd-gui
acceptance: After F-448 passes and the maintainer has used the new shell and approved, rcfd-studio and the frozen rcfd-gui are removed with their tests, docs that name them are updated, and the two layer lines of crates/rcfd-cli/tests/workspace_graph.rs are removed with the maintainer's approval; every other crate and test is unchanged and the gate passes.
note: ADR 0350 section 5. NEEDS THE USER: removal of crates and an edit of an existing test.

title: Overset: the prescribed fringe flux with a moving component
acceptance: With OversetSolver::set_fringe_flux(PrescribedOwnGradient) and the quadratic donor interpolation of F-336, the Taylor-Green set-up of ADR 0219 with the moving, turning component (levels 1 and 2, the corrected time step of its amendment 2) is run against the default coupling with the same stencils: the largest velocity error over the calculated and fringe cells is at most 1.2 times that of the default coupling at both levels, continuity and the outflow balance hold to 1e-9 in every step, and no step is refused for a calculated cell between fringe cells on opposite sides; or the ADR names with a number what the moving fringe adds (the lag of the prescribed flux on the faces that change kind is the first candidate).
note: From ADR 0347 question 4, recommendation taken on the maintainer's standing instruction of 2026-11-11. ADR 0376, 2026-11-12: PARTIAL. No library change: OversetSolver::set_fringe_flux(PrescribedOwnGradient) runs with the moving, turning component as it stands. On TG_L of ADR 0219 with the quadratic donor interpolation on both runs and dt proportional to h^2 (200 and 800 steps), every step is taken (no refusal of a cell between fringe cells, no unconverged solve, no fallback), continuity 1.6e-13 and 6.2e-13, the flux into the hole region 3.8e-15 and 8.9e-15 and through the domain boundary 0, 142 and 503 kind changes. The largest error over the calculated and fringe cells is 1.2636 times that of the default coupling at level 1 (9.7081e-4 against 7.6831e-4; limit 1.2, missed, kept as a known miss) and 1.0001 at level 2 (both in the domain-boundary cell); the order of the error of G is 2.33. What the moving fringe adds, measured against the same runs with the component at rest: nothing; the excess of G over the default on the overlap is 1.21 and 1.06 moving against 1.43 and 1.10 at rest (m_G / m_default 0.844, 0.965), so the lag on the faces that change kind does not show. The excess is local to the calculated background cells within two cells of the background fringe (1.93 and 1.52 times the default there; elsewhere equal within 4 percent; the hypothesis as registered after the first run is ruled out by its deciding numbers, its maximum leaving the band at level 2), the one-sided pressure gradient of the ring cells of ADR 0347 D5. The root mean square error of each class is that of the default within 1.1 percent or smaller. Defaults untouched (two hashes equal to the library before, baseline_hashes and the existing overset tests pass). Four mutations: three caught by their checks, the fourth (the flux taken relative to the moving faces) seen only by the number of the check that already misses (1.59e4). Open: whether the alternative clause of the acceptance makes it done (ADR 0376 Q1).

title: rcfd duct-modes command
acceptance: rcfd duct-modes reads a saved pressure time series on a duct section and writes the rcfd-duct-modes export; on the ADR 0351 X1 field it reproduces the library's export bit for bit; located errors for a section outside the duct and a non-integer number of periods; the CLI help golden updated with the maintainer's approval.
note: From ADR 0351 question 1. NEEDS THE USER: the command's help text changes the CLI golden.

title: Wave solver driven by a sampled CFD surface
acceptance: A driven boundary built from an rcfd-surface-series file reproduces, in a duct, the modal amplitudes of a closed-form duct field sampled into that file within 1 percent; a series that does not cover a whole number of periods is refused.
note: From ADR 0351 question 2, recommendation taken on the maintainer's standing instruction of 2026-11-11. DONE pending acceptance, ADR 0372, 2026-11-12. Library only. Built: rcfd-post `wave_drive.rs` (`SurfaceDrive`, `DuctFrame`, `DriveOptions`): an rcfd-surface-series section is read as a whole number of periods of a given fundamental, each harmonic of every face taken by a DFT on the file's clock (the mean dropped and reported), fitted on a hard-walled duct-mode basis, and played back periodically as the `WaveBc::Driven` ghost state of the wave entering the duct, each mode with its own axial wavenumber and impedance kz p/(rho0 omega), carried from the sampling plane to the driven faces. Registered checks, all met at the first run, no amendment: a 0.12 m channel, a closed-form field of the plane wave at 1181 Hz and the plane wave and mode 1 at 2361 Hz plus a 3 Pa mean, sampled on a wall-clustered 24-face section 0.02 m upstream of the wave mesh into the file through JSON text; on 64 cells across the amplitudes measured at the inlet agree with the closed form within 8.8e-4, 3.5e-3 and 2.3e-3 (limit 1e-2; 1.4e-2 at worst on 32 across, second order: the error is the scheme's driven face, the file chain adds 1.1e-14 against a run driven by the closed form); the drive's state equals the closed form within 1.7e-13; a 128-sample two-period file is accepted and 127 and 96 samples are refused as not a whole number of periods; eleven other refusals located. Six mutations caught (plane-wave impedance, lost file clock, period test removed, wrong axial carry, harmonics played at the fundamental, Nyquist test removed). Limits: the sampled pressure must be the entering wave only; periodic signals; static section, medium at rest; only the two-dimensional channel was run; no case key or CLI (F-451). The returning-wave limit is lifted for two or more sampled sections by F-478 (ADR 0378, 2026-11-12); since then the off-plane refusal names the farthest face.

title: Circular and three-dimensional ducts through the wave solver
acceptance: A spinning mode (1, 0) and a radial mode (0, 1) of a hard-walled circular duct on an O-grid propagate with the closed-form axial wavenumber within 1 percent after the polygonal cut-off error of the grid, estimated in the registration, is accounted for; a matched layer ends the duct with less than 1 percent reflection.
note: PARTIAL, ADR 0366, 2026-11-12. Library only. The acceptance clauses are met; two registered checks missed and one registered mutation escaped its registered check, so the item is partial by Rule I. Built: rcfd-mesh `circular_duct_ogrid` (an O-grid of a circular duct: an n x n core and four n x n/2 ring blocks, extruded along z; patches wall, inlet, outlet), and tests that drive the duct through the F-333 `AcousticWaveSolver` and measure it with `duct_modes`. Radius 0.06 m, each mode at cos theta = 0.8, matched layer one axial wavelength thick before a rigid end. The spinning mode (1, 0) at 2768 Hz on n = 16 (110 k cells) has an axial wavenumber 2.58e-3 below the closed form corrected for the 64-sided polygon (the correction is the equal-area radius, first-order Hadamard, -4.5e-4; 3.03e-3 below the circle's form); the layer reflects 3.6e-5. The radial mode (0, 1) at 5760 Hz on n = 32 (424 k cells) is 2.56e-3 below (correction -1.1e-4); reflection 6.5e-5. Both match a Fourier analysis of the scheme within about 5 percent. The Bessel zeros are computed in the test from the power series and agree with the library within 1.1e-14. Coarse covering runs met their limits, and the rigid end without a layer reflects 0.9995. Missed: the counter-rotating (-1, 0) content of the spinning runs is 1.2e-5 against a registered 1e-6 (estimate "round-off"). Diagnosed (amendment 1): the solver commutes with the grid's rotation to 1e-15, and the content falls in a longer run, so it is left over from the start-up ramp of the drive. Mutation MU3 (wall given the open flux) escaped the registered conservation check U8, whose initial field has a zero boundary mean; four duct checks caught it. Limits: two modes at one frequency each, one O-grid topology, no rectangular 3-D duct, one planar layer, medium at rest; no case key or CLI (ADR 0351 question 1, F-451). The blind spot of U8 (mutation MU3 escaping with a zero-boundary-mean field) is closed by F-473 (ADR 0371, 2026-11-12), whose closed-duct check with a non-zero boundary mean catches it.

title: Fractional step: a step-consistent face flux for the projection
acceptance: The steady lid-driven cavity of ADR 0245 C3 with solver.time_advance = "fractional_step" (8.7e-2 between dt = 0.04 and 0.01, ADR 0352 F0) is traced to its face term with a number, and either made the same to 1e-9 for the two step sizes by an opt-in (defaults bit-identical) or the ADR names why not with a number.
note: From ADR 0352 question 2, recommendation (a). ADR 0356, 2026-11-12: PARTIAL by the rule (every acceptance clause met; mutation MF5 equivalent by construction, not caught). The fractional step's 8.69e-2 between dt 0.04 and 0.01 is its face term: in a steady state the increment vanishes, the cell equations carry no step, and the face defect is dte R(p) (measured to 6.5e-16 relative), a first-order pressure smoothing. The opt-in PimpleSettings::fractional_step_consistent (incremental form; default false) takes on internal faces Gamma R(p^n) + (Gamma/dt)(c1 d^n - c2 d^{n-1}) with Gamma the harmonic face value of V/a_P of the predictor, so the steady defect is R(p)/interp(a): the steady cavity is then the same to 1.5e-13 for the two steps (1.2e-13 with the plain boundary, 1.1e-13 with BDF2, printed) and equal to the PISO step's with ADR 0245's C to 1.6e-13 (4.4e-2 without). Defaults bit for bit (fingerprints before and after equal; the rcfd-fv suites touching the changed lines and baseline_hashes unedited). The Chorin form is not changed (its cell equations carry dt; 3.7e-2 printed). No case key; outlets and periodic faces keep dte R. Four of five mutations caught. Partial by the registered rule; done is the maintainer's call; making the opt-in the default (Q3) is the maintainer's.

title: Residual of the direct static solve on slender models, and iterative refinement
acceptance: Every limit not stated here is registered in the ADR before the run. The relative residual of the default direct static solve is recorded for Tet4, Hex8 and Tet10 cantilevers of slenderness 5, 10, 20 and 40 at registered meshes; with one step of iterative refinement (opt-in, the default bit-identical) the relative residual is at most 1e-14 on every one of them and the strain energy equals half the work of the loads within 1e-12; the cost of the refinement step is recorded.
note: From ADR 0277 remaining question 1, recommendation taken on the maintainer's standing instruction of 2026-11-11 (the Tet10 cantilever of L/h 10 had a direct-solve relative residual of 6.7e-11). ADR 0282 (2026-11-12): on Hex8 cantilevers the direct solve's relative residual sits at the evaluation floor eps |||A| |x||| / ||b|| (6.5e-12 against a floor of 1.3e-11 at L/h = 5.3, 7.1e-11 against 1.4e-10 at L/h = 10.7), so iterative refinement cannot lower the computed residual there; a backward-error statistic relative to |||A| |x||| + ||b|| would separate the two.

title: monitors.get at 1e5 samples: build only what is asked for
acceptance: `monitors.get {names, since}` applies `names` and `since` before the document is built, with replies equal to today's byte for byte for every existing test; P3 of ADR 0350 measured again as registered (4 series of 1e5 samples, request to parsed object in the renderer) with the 100 ms limit unchanged, and an increment of 100 samples at 1e5 stored in at most 2 ms; a miss is recorded, not tuned.

title: Scale-aware convergence test of the subspace eigensolver
acceptance: Every limit not stated here is registered in the ADR before the run. rcfd_linalg::eigen::lowest_eigenpairs gains a residual test relative to an estimate of ||A|| ||x|| (for example from the factorisation or a few power steps), selectable without changing the existing default; the 40 x 2 x 2 Tet10 cantilever of ADR 0284 then converges with the scale-aware tolerance 1e-12 in at most 20 iterations, its first two bending frequencies agree with the runs of ADR 0284 amendment 1 within 1e-10 relative, and every check of ADR 0283 still passes with the default unchanged.
note: Scale-aware convergence test of the subspace eigensolver (follow-up of F-383). ADR 0354, 2026-11-12: rcfd_linalg::eigen::ResidualTest { Relative (default, the test of ADR 0283 D6, the same operations and bits), Backward } selected by SubspaceOptions::residual_test and ModalOptions::residual_test; Backward measures each pair by its normwise backward error ||A x - mu M x|| / ((||A||_inf + |mu| ||M||_inf) ||x||) (the pair is exact for a pencil within that relative distance; rounding floor about c eps whatever lambda_max/lambda_1). Tet10 40 x 2 x 2 cantilever of ADR 0284 at the scale-aware tolerance 1e-12: converged in 7 iterations (limit 20), Sturm 6 = 6, M-orthonormality 4.2e-15; its first two bending pairs equal the amendment-1 run bit for bit (limit 1e-10; both runs stop at iteration 7, and runs stopping at iterations 4 to 8 deviate by at most 1.8e-15); the default test on this tree reproduces the amendment-1 frequencies bit for bit; every ADR 0283 check (sb_eigen), every rcfd-fem test and baseline_hashes pass unedited. Extensions: Hex8 40 x 2 x 2 converges in 7 iterations, equal to amendment 1; T^2 (kappa 2.7e8) converges in 7 iterations within 1.1e-9 of the closed form where the default test stops at its floor 2.8e-8 after 200. Seven mutations, all caught by registered tests. Done pending the maintainer's acceptance.

title: Manufactured solution: the Tet4 traction-case L2 order on the pair 16 -> 32 as a registered check
acceptance: Every limit not stated here is registered in the ADR before the run, which discloses that ADR 0279 ran this pair once as a diagnostic (L2 order 1.9176). The manufactured solution and case T of ADR 0279 with Tet4 on 8, 16, 32 cells per edge (98 304 unknowns, direct solver, an ignored heavy record): the L2 order over the pair 16 -> 32 is >= 1.8 and the energy order >= 0.9, both errors fall monotonically.
note: From ADR 0279 addendum 1 (2026-11-12), Q1 recommendation. F-458 (ADR 0365, 2026-11-12): done pending acceptance. title: Manufactured solution on distorted meshes: orders of Tet4, Hex8, Tet10 with moved interior nodes, and the Hex8 stiffness rule
acceptance: Every limit not stated here is registered in the ADR before the run. The manufactured solution of ADR 0279, case D, on boxes whose interior nodes are moved by a registered seed and amplitude (elements valid at every node): on at least three meshes, each halving h, the observed L2 order over the finest pair is >= 1.8 for Tet4 and Hex8 and >= 2.7 for Tet10, the energy-norm order >= 0.9 and >= 1.8, both errors fall monotonically; a mutation of the Hex8 stiffness rule to one point is caught by these checks.
note: From ADR 0279 addendum 1 (2026-11-12), Q2 recommendation. Structural solver, basic tier. ADR 0355, 2026-11-12: the manufactured solution of ADR 0279 (case D) on boxes with interior nodes moved by seed 0xF459_0355, uniform offsets of at most 0.15 h per component for Hex8 and 0.075 h for Tet4 and Tet10 (Tet10 from the moved Tet4, straight edges), validity guaranteed by diagonal dominance (det J >= 1e-3 of the regular value) and measured: minimum det J at the nodes 0.37 (Hex8) to 0.65 (tetrahedra) of the regular value; tests crates/rcfd-fem/tests/sb_mms_distorted.rs only. title: Incomplete Cholesky at half the block-Jacobi iterations on the elastic cantilever: ordering and one level of fill
acceptance: Every limit not stated here is registered in the ADR before the run. Beside IC(0) in the natural order, an incomplete Cholesky with one level of fill and IC(0) after a node-wise reverse Cuthill-McKee ordering, both with the shift strategy of ADR 0282, selectable in StaticSolver::PreconditionedCg: on the fast Hex8 cantilever of ADR 0282 (32 x 6 x 6, 4704 unknowns) at least one of them reaches the relative residual 1e-10 in at most half the iterations of block Jacobi (156), agrees with the direct solution within 1e-7 and is bit-identical for 1 and 8 threads; the iteration counts at L/h = 5.3 and 10.7 and on the 103 968-unknown case are recorded; IC(0) in the natural order and every default are unchanged bit for bit.
note: From ADR 0282 addendum 1 (2026-11-12), Q1 recommendation. ADR 0357, 2026-11-12: rcfd_linalg::precond (appended) ic_fill_pattern (level-of-fill pattern of IC(p) on the lower CSR triangle), IncompleteCholesky::with_fill (the factor on that pattern with ADR 0282's shift A + alpha diag(A); level 0 equals IncompleteCholesky::new bit for bit) and Permuted (the preconditioner of P A P^T applied to A); rcfd_linalg::reorder::block_rcm_order (reverse Cuthill-McKee of the block graph, the rows of a block kept together); rcfd_fem::solve::CgPreconditioner::IncompleteCholeskyFill { options, level, ordering: IcOrdering::{Natural, NodeReverseCuthillMcKee} }, breakdowns mapped through the ordering to node and component. Fast Hex8 cantilever 32 x 6 x 6 (4704 unknowns): IC(1) needs 58 iterations against block Jacobi's 156 (ratio 0.372, limit 0.5), relative residual 5.4e-11, 2.4e-13 from the direct solution, bit-identical for 1 and 8 threads; IC(0) after node RCM 82 (0.526, recorded), IC(1) after RCM 57. Ratios to block Jacobi at L/h = 10.7: IC(0) 0.705, IC(1) 0.452, RCM IC(0) 0.671, RCM IC(1) 0.455; heavy case, 103 968 unknowns: 477 (block Jacobi), 255, 171, 250, 160 iterations. Forced breakdowns are reported with shift 2.048 (IC(1)) and 1.024 (RCM) and solved to 7.7e-11 and 6.1e-11. IC(0) in the natural order, block Jacobi, CG-Jacobi and the direct default are hash-identical to main; baseline hashes pass; nine mutations caught. Done pending the maintainer's acceptance. Done pending the maintainer's acceptance.

title: Element tests: the constant-strain patch test of Hex8 on a moved mesh
acceptance: Every limit not stated here is registered in the ADR before the run. A linear displacement field on a box of Hex8 whose interior nodes are moved by a registered seed and an amplitude below the validity bound of ADR 0355, all boundary nodes prescribed, no body force: the relative L2 and energy errors are <= 1e-9, and the same test with the stiffness rule mutated to one point gives a relative energy error >= 1e-5.
note: Structural solver, basic tier. ADR 0358, 2026-11-12: the constant-strain patch test of Hex8 on a unit box with interior nodes moved by seed 0xF461_0358, uniform offsets of at most 0.15 h and 0.05 h per component (validity bound 1/6 of ADR 0355; minimum det J at the nodes 0.389 to 0.95 of the regular value), n = 3, 4, 6 cells per edge, three draws, two linear fields, all boundary nodes prescribed, no body force; tests crates/rcfd-fem/tests/sb_patch_moved.rs only. Over the 36 solves the relative L2 error is at most 3.0e-16 and the relative energy error at most 2.4e-15 (limit 1e-9); the quadratic field is not reproduced (L2 2.3e-3 to 9.1e-3, energy 3.3e-2 to 6.7e-2, so the test can see an error). With the Hex8 stiffness rule mutated to one point (scratch copy) the relative energy error is 6.1e-5 to 6.7e-3 in every solve (limit 1e-5) and the relative L2 error 1.1e-5 to 4.2e-4; the same one-point rule on an unmoved mesh passes at 2e-16, so the error comes from the moves. The 3-point over-integration survives as expected; a 1e-6 offset of one prescribed value and an amplitude above the bound are caught. One check is weak: the check that the mesh is moved has a limit relative to the amplitude and cannot see an unmoved mesh (that mutation was caught only by a rounding artifact of the validity check); the move itself is evidenced by the contrast between the one-point rule on the moved and on the regular mesh. Follow-up proposed below. Partial by the lead's reading of the registered rule: the registered mutation M3 (unmoved mesh) was not caught by its registered check V2 (caught only by a rounding artifact of V1); the agent proposed done; done is the maintainer's call. F-461 note addition: the remaining question 1 of ADR 0358 (V2 cannot see an unmoved mesh) is closed by F-464 (ADR 0362, 2026-11-12).

title: Scale-aware default of the modal analysis
