title: Static solid participant: the failing solve in a later iteration as a registered check
acceptance: Every limit not stated here is registered in the ADR before the run, which discloses that ADR 0286 ran the test once after its amendment 1. With the StaticSolid and the mock fluid of ADR 0286, a coupled step that starts away from its fixed point (the mock's F0 doubled after a converged step) and whose static solve fails in iteration 2 stops with the participant's name and iteration 2, the solver's message, and both participants bit-equal to the start of the step; a step whose solve fails in iteration 3 does the same.
note: From ADR 0286 addendum (2026-11-12), Q1 recommendation. Structural solver, basic tier. ADR 0361, 2026-11-12: tests only, crates/rcfd-post/tests/sb_solid_coupling_fail.rs (ADR 0286's test file is not edited; the single run of ADR 0286's corrected F2b after its amendment 1 is disclosed). With the StaticSolid and the mock fluid of ADR 0286 (k_f 1.5 k_s, Aitken and least squares, tolerance 1e-10), a converged step then the mock's F0 doubled: worked out by hand before the run that the healthy step takes exactly 3 iterations (test quantities 15, 0.366, then rounding) from the start f = 1.4 F0, so iteration 3 exists; measured 15 to 7e-14, 0.36585 to 1.5e-14, 5.8e-16, three solid advances, u = 2 u* to 1.9e-15. A wrapper switches the solid to a failing CG (one iteration) at its n-th advance: for n = 2 and n = 3 the step stops with participant 'solid', iteration n, the solver's text (solver cg-jacobi: not converged in 1 iterations), the error's time the start time, n advances, and fluid and solid state (time, displacement, forces) bit-equal to the start of the step; the same step run again with the healthy solver reproduces the control bit for bit. A failure switched at the 4th advance is never reached. Twelve of twelve mutations registered as caught were caught (restore without displacement, forces, time on the solid and on the mock fluid, participant name dropped, solver text dropped, iteration reported k+1 and k-1, coupler restore removed, wrapper off by one); the two registered equivalent mutants (the coupler's restore at the error, redundant for a structure failure) survived. Not covered: a failing fluid or time check in a later iteration, iterations beyond 3, a flow solver (open ADR 0361 Q1). Done pending the maintainer's acceptance.

title: Element tests: the moved-mesh check of the Hex8 patch test measures the stored mesh
acceptance: Every limit not stated here is registered in the ADR before the run. In a new test file, for the moved boxes of ADR 0358 (n = 3, 4, 6; alpha 0.15 and 0.05; three draws), the rms of the offsets read from the stored node coordinates of the moved mesh against the regular builder mesh (interior nodes only, relative to h) is >= 0.3 alpha and the boundary nodes are unchanged bit for bit; the same test on an unmoved mesh (alpha = 0 passed through the same code) fails these checks; the existing tests are not edited.
note: From ADR 0358 addendum 1 (2026-11-12), Q1 recommendation. F-464 (ADR 0362, 2026-11-12): done pending acceptance. New test file sb_patch_moved_stored.rs reads the node coordinates stored in the 18 moved Hex8 boxes of ADR 0358 against the regular builder mesh: interior rms offset 0.534 to 0.634 alpha (limit 0.3 alpha, and an absolute 1e-3), every interior node moved (min node maximum 3.9e-3 h against 1e-5), largest offset at most alpha, boundary nodes unchanged bit for bit (0 differing), connectivity unchanged. The same code on an unmoved mesh (alpha = 0) fails the rms and node-moved checks on all 18 meshes, also with the expected amplitude set to 0 (absolute floors). Nine mutations (unmoved mesh through the real test, stored nodes unmoved, boundary moved, one boundary node moved by 1e-12, offsets scaled 1e-4 and 1.1, every second node unmoved, connectivity rotated, control built moved) each caught by the check registered for it. Tests only, ADR 0358 tests unedited. Done pending the maintainer's acceptance.

title: Coupled step: a failing fluid in a later iteration as a registered check
acceptance: Every limit not stated here is registered in the ADR before the run. With the StaticSolid and the mock fluid of ADR 0286 and the start of ADR 0361 (a converged step, then F0 doubled), a mock fluid whose advance returns an error in iteration 2, and in iteration 3, stops the step with the fluid's name, that iteration number and its message, and both participants bit-equal to the start of the step; mutations that skip the coupler's restore of the fluid or of the structure at the error, or at the start of an iteration, are each caught by at least one check (the pair of restores that ADR 0361 M9 and M11 could not observe).
note: From ADR 0361 addendum 1 (2026-11-12), Q1 recommendation. Structural solver, basic tier. ADR 0364, 2026-11-12: tests only, crates/rcfd-post/tests/sb_solid_coupling_fail_fluid.rs. With the StaticSolid and the mock fluid of ADR 0286 and the start of ADR 0361 (a converged step, then F0 doubled), a mock fluid whose advance takes its new state and then returns an error in its 2nd and its 3rd call (Aitken and least squares) stops the step with participant 'fluid', that iteration number, the mock's message (entered at the start time) and the start time, after n advances of the structure and of the fluid; fluid and solid state (time, displacement, forces) bit-equal to the start of the step, with a check that both were off the start at the failure; the retry with a healthy fluid reproduces the healthy step bit for bit; the control reaches iteration 3 as derived (15 to 7e-14, 0.36585 to 1.5e-14, 5.8e-16) and a failure at the 4th call is never reached. The coupler's restores at the error, the equivalent mutants M9 and M11 of ADR 0361, are caught: skipping the structure's, the fluid's or both fails the bit-equality checks; a wrong iteration, participant or message and a wrong mock restore are caught by the registered checks. Partial: the mutations that skip the restores at the start of an iteration (fluid or structure, from iteration 2 or from iteration 3) and a mock restore without the time were caught only by a panic in the set-up, which is itself a converged 3-iteration step that uses those restores, not by the registered failing-step checks. Not covered: a fluid failing before it takes its state, the fluid's time check, bad force arrays, a failing restore, iterations beyond 3, a flow solver.

title: Bounded second-order immersed forcing: the stop of DFG 2D-2 on T.
acceptance: The stop of DFG 2D-2 on the T mesh with `build_second_order_bounded` (ADR 0268 R1: step 2951, pressure NaN in the pressure solve, inlet corner cell) is located by a registered measurement (the step reproduced from a restart, the linear solve and the source of the solid cells examined), and either the run reaches t = 8 and its max C_D and max C_L decide the decrease from T to T2 of ADR 0268 (A2-T-2), or the configuration is refused with a located message.
note: DONE pending acceptance (ADR 0363, 2026-11-12). From ADR 0268 question 5. The stop of DFG 2D-2 on T with build_second_order_bounded (dt 1e-3) was reproduced from t = 0 (the printed coefficients and the message of ADR 0268 R1 exactly) and from a state written to disk at step 2900 (the same stop, every Courant number bit-equal); the flow is healthy one step before (Courant 1.136, max |u| 0.995 of step 2000). Located by an opt-in capture of the pressure systems (PimpleSolver::pressure_capture, replayed bit for bit with pressure::pressure_system_src) and a read-only AMG trace: in corrector 1 of step 2951 the inputs are finite, the matrix is a symmetric M-matrix and the volume source of the solid cells is finite and balanced (sum 1e-15 of its maximum, the same size as at steps 2949 and 2950), but the AMG-preconditioned CG has r^T z < 0 from its first iteration, stagnates and overflows (beta not finite at iteration 801), so the whole pressure is NaN; cell 0 at the inlet corner is only the first index of an all-NaN vector. Incomplete-Cholesky CG solves the same system in 448 iterations. The stop is a breakdown of the linear solver, not of the forcing. Delivered (opt-in, defaults bit-identical, baseline_hashes pass): PimpleSettings::pressure_ic_fallback repeats a non-finite pressure solve with IC-CG from the same start and records it in PimpleSolver::pressure_fallbacks. With it T runs to t = 8 with one repeat in 5050 steps (S2 held, 7 crossings): max C_D 3.22695 (+0.216 percent), max C_L 1.00253 (+1.687 percent), St 0.30144 (-0.146 percent), so A2-T-2 of ADR 0268 is met (0.216 to 0.136, 1.687 to 0.175). Nine mutations caught. Open (ADR 0363 Q4 to Q6): why the AMG hierarchy loses definiteness on this system, making the repeat the default, a guard on rz <= 0 inside cg. ADR 0369 (2026-11-12, F-474): the AMG breakdown at step 2951 is the coarsest dense LU order defect (F-471); with AmgSettings::coarse_lu_interchanges_first the stopping system converges in 10 iterations and T does not stop.

title: Coupled step: failing-participant checks with a start state that does not use the restores at the start of an iteration
acceptance: Every limit not stated here is registered in the ADR before the run. With the StaticSolid and the mock fluid of ADR 0286, a start state reached without any coupler iteration beyond the first (a loose-coupling first step, then F0 doubled), registered with its arithmetic, a mock fluid failing in iteration 2 and in iteration 3 stops the step with the fluid's name, the iteration number and its message and both participants bit-equal to the start; mutations that skip the coupler's restore of the fluid or of the structure at the start of iteration 2 or of iteration 3 (ADR 0364 M16 to M19) and the mock's restore of the time (M25) are each caught by a failing-step or control check, not by a panic in the set-up.

title: Elasticity multigrid on quadratic tetrahedra: aggregation that coarsens Tet10 like Hex8
acceptance: Every limit not stated here is registered in the ADR before the run. In rcfd_linalg::amg_elastic, an opt-in aggregation rule for meshes of quadratic elements (a registered strength threshold or an aggregate size bound, derived before the run) such that on the Tet10 cantilever of slenderness 20 of ADR 0305 (tet_box 120 x 6 x 6 upgraded, 121 680 unknowns) the first coarse level has between 1/15 and 1/6 of the fine unknowns, CG with one V-cycle reaches 1e-8 in at most twice the Hex8 count of ADR 0305 H2b (15), operator complexity <= 1.5, the rigid-body modes in the range of the tentative prolongator to 1e-12 on every level; every count and bit of ADR 0305 with the default settings unchanged.
note: From ADR 0305 question 2, recommendation taken on the maintainer's standing instruction of 2026-11-11. From ADR 0305 question 2, recommendation taken on the maintainer's standing instruction of 2026-11-11. ADR 0370, 2026-11-13: rcfd_linalg::amg_elastic::Aggregation::Geometric (opt-in through ElasticAmgSettings::quadratic() and ElasticAmg::with_points; rcfd_fem::solve::smoothed_aggregation passes the node points): a coupled block is a candidate when it lies within (sqrt 3 + 2)/2 of the distance to the nearest coupled block (the gap between the Chebyshev-1 and Chebyshev-2 lattice neighbours), seeds visited in coordinate order, coarse points the aggregate centroids. On the Tet10 cantilever of slenderness 20 (121 680 unknowns) the first coarse level is 12 000 (1/10.14, the Hex8 number; default 2220), operator complexity 1.476, rigid-body modes in the range of the tentative prolongator to 2.8e-16; CG with one V-cycle reaches 1e-8 in 31 iterations (default 79) against the limit 30, steady at about 3 iterations per decade, so the remaining gap is the smoother, not the floor or the coarsening. On Hex8 the rule reproduces the default aggregates bit for bit. Defaults unchanged bit for bit (hashes against main, ADR 0305 counts 15 and 2220 measured again, baseline hashes pass). Partial by Rule I: the iteration limit missed by one, and one of seven mutations (pass 2 over all neighbours) equivalent on these meshes and not caught. Follow-up: the smoother on quadratic elements. Partial by the registered rule; done is the maintainer's call. ADR 0375 (2026-11-13, F-477): with ElasticAmgSettings::quadratic_smoothed() (two block Gauss-Seidel sweeps per side) the slenderness-20 Tet10 cantilever reaches 1e-8 in 23 iterations, and the mutation M5 left uncaught here is caught on graded Tet10 boxes.

title: Scalar AMG coarsest dense LU: row interchanges applied before the forward substitution
acceptance: Every limit not stated here is registered in the ADR before the run. A test shows whether the coarsest dense LU of rcfd_linalg::amg (DenseLu) interchanges rows on each fluid case of the baseline set and records where; DenseLu::solve applies every interchange before the forward substitution (as rcfd_linalg::amg_elastic after ADR 0305 amendment 1) so that a coarsest matrix that needs interchanges is solved to a relative residual of 1e-12; the rcfd-linalg, rcfd-fv and rcfd-api tests and the baseline hashes are run, and any changed hash is reported to the maintainer, not re-recorded.
note: PARTIAL (ADR 0369, 2026-11-12, with F-474). The defect is shown in rcfd_linalg::amg DenseLu: whole-row swaps in the factorisation with interleaved interchanges in the solve give (-13, 15, -5) for (1, 1, 1) on a 3 x 3 SPD matrix, a relative residual of 4e-3 on a 20 x 20 SPD tridiagonal, and 0.21 on the coarsest operator of the T pressure system of ADR 0363, where it is the cause of the AMG-CG breakdown (F-474). Interchanges at step 0 alone are harmless. On the baseline set only kepsilon_channel (coarsest 56) and cavity-coupled (Schur, coarsest 71) reach an AMG, and neither interchanges (scratch instrumentation). The corrected order is built as the opt-in AmgSettings::coarse_lu_interchanges_first (5e-15 and 9e-19 relative residual). With it as the default on a scratch copy, baseline_hashes, case_hashes_w48u, rcfd-linalg (except ADR 0369 L1, which pins the old default), rcfd-fv lib and the defaults tests f301/f367 pass, so no registered hash moves; the T bounded run of ADR 0268/0363 changes (no stop, different from step 2917). Remaining (NEEDS THE USER): switch the default and run the AMG-using rcfd-fv/rcfd-api test files in the gate; ADR 0363's records H1, H2 and H3a and ADR 0369 L1 assert the old behaviour. NEEDS THE USER: switching the default (no registered hash moves; ADR 0363's stop records and ADR 0369 L1 would need new records).

title: Overset: the geometry corrections with a varying pressure on B3d
acceptance: With OversetSolver::set_geometry_corrections on, a three-dimensional flow with a known varying pressure (a decaying vortex or a manufactured solution) on B3 and B3d with the component moving as in ADR 0255: the error of the calculated and fringe cells on B3d at most twice that on B3 with the default and the quadratic donor interpolation, continuity within 1e-9 at every step, with a run that names the share of the uncorrected Green-Gauss pressure gradient.
note: From ADR 0367 Q2, recommendation taken on the maintainer's standing instruction of 2026-11-11. ADR 0382, 2026-11-12: PARTIAL. A Taylor-Green vortex with an axial velocity (exact, zero normal pressure gradient on the box, pressure range V^2) on B3 and B3d with the component moving as in ADR 0255, OversetSolver::set_geometry_corrections on: E on B3d 1.588e-2 (default stencils and quadratic) against 4.80e-3 and 2.34e-3 on B3, ratios 3.31 and 6.80 (limit 2; missed, kept as known misses), the same against B3 with the default solver; continuity 2e-14 or less every step. The share of the uncorrected Green-Gauss pressure gradient is named by the new diagnostic opt-in OversetSolver::set_least_squares_pressure_gradient (only with the corrections): it carries 63 % and 66 % of the error on B3d (91 % and 77 % of the excess over B3); with it the ratios are 1.22 (met) and 2.33 (missed: the warped background's own error stays while the quadratic stencils halve B3's). At operator level the Green-Gauss gradient of a linear pressure is off by 0.195 |grad p| on B3d, the least-squares one exact. Defaults and the opt-in without the new flag bit-identical (ADR 0367's eight fingerprints and two new ones equal; baseline_hashes and the overset tests pass). Control held after an amendment (N1b 1.0e-3); three mutations caught by their registered checks. Limits: one flow, one warp, one resolution; a pressure error of 4.3e-2 V^2 common to all runs is not diagnosed.

title: Conservation check of the wave solver with a non-zero boundary mean
acceptance: On the closed circular O-grid duct, an initial pressure with a non-zero mean on every patch keeps sum p V to 1e-12 over 100 steps with every patch a wall, and changes it by more than 1e-3 when one patch is open.
note: From ADR 0366 question 2, recommendation taken on the maintainer's standing instruction of 2026-11-11. Size S. DONE, ADR 0371, 2026-11-12. Tests only: crates/rcfd-post/tests/wave_conservation_f473.rs; no library change. On the closed circular O-grid duct (circular_duct_ogrid(6, 3, 6), 648 cells) the initial pressure p = 1 + 0.4 x/R + 0.3 y/R + 0.5 z/L has a mean of 1.25 on the wall, 1.04 on the inlet and 1.46 on the outlet. With every patch a wall, 100 steps of cfl 0.48 change sum p V by 3.7e-15 relative (limit 1e-12). With one patch open the integral decreases by 0.76 (inlet), 0.72 (outlet), 0.98 (wall) of sum |p0| V (limit 1e-3; the registered estimate of 0.05 to 0.3 was too low). Mutations: the wall given the open flux (MU3 of ADR 0366, which U8 missed with its zero-mean field) changes the integral by 0.955 and is caught by the closed check; a wall leak of 1e-9 is caught (7.8e-9 against 1e-12); an open face that lets no mass out is caught by all three open checks; the old U8 field is rejected by the boundary-mean check, and with it the MU3 mutation is again invisible to the conservation check. Limits: one mesh, one field, 100 steps, one patch open at a time; no driven patch. Done pending the maintainer's acceptance.

title: AMG pressure preconditioner: loss of definiteness on the immersed T system
acceptance: On the pressure system of ADR 0363 (T, bounded immersed forcing, step 2951 corrector 1, rebuilt from the state of step 2950 and the opt-in capture) the cause of r^T M^-1 r < 0 of the smoothed-aggregation AMG is located by a registered measurement (per level, the Rayleigh quotient of the cycle, the smoothed prolongator and the coarse operators against a higher-precision product), and either the AMG is repaired so that AMG-CG converges on that system with every registered hash unchanged, or the breakdown is detected inside cg (rz <= 0) and reported with a located message.
note: PARTIAL (ADR 0369, 2026-11-12). From ADR 0363 Q4/Q6. Cause located on the stopping system of ADR 0363 (T, bounded forcing, step 2951 corrector 1, rebuilt from the state of step 2940): it is the coarsest dense LU order defect of F-471. The coarsest operator (24 unknowns) interchanges rows at steps 13, 16 and 17; the default interleaved DenseLu::solve misses by a relative residual of 0.21; the cycle becomes non-symmetric (0.13 at the coarsest level, 4.2e-3 at the finest) and indefinite (negative Rayleigh quotients at levels 4 and 0), hence r^T M^-1 r < 0. Everything else is sound against double-double: Galerkin products to 6e-16, every operator symmetric to 5e-16 and positive definite, no zero prolongator column. Delivered (opt-in, defaults bit-identical, baseline_hashes pass): AmgSettings::coarse_lu_interchanges_first applies every interchange before the forward substitution; with it the coarse solve is exact to 5e-15, the cycle symmetric to 1e-15 and positive on every level, and AMG-CG converges on the stopping system in 10 iterations (corrector 0: 10 against 406), agreeing with IC-CG to 4e-9; read-only accessors Amg::coarse_interchanges, level_operator, level_prolongator, cycle_at, coarse_solve. With the default switched on a scratch copy no registered hash moves (kepsilon_channel and cavity-coupled, the only baseline cases with an AMG, never interchange), T no longer stops at 2951, and its run differs from ADR 0363 H1 from step 2917 on. Seven mutations caught. Partial by Rule I: the check L4 missed (the Laplacian's coarsest LU interchanges at step 0, harmless to the order) and was corrected by amendment 1. Open: switching the default (maintainer; recommended).

title: Studio preview of a case with [mesh.adapt] shows the adapted mesh
acceptance: The Studio mesh preview of a case with [mesh.adapt] shows the mesh the run solves on (the adapted mesh of Simulation::new, with its cell count and mesh hash), and preview_g1's g1_g7_shipped_cases_preview_the_solvers_mesh compares cases/cavity/adapt_re100.toml with Simulation::new like every other case, without the base-mesh exception added on 2026-11-13.
note: From the gate 4 fix (ADR 0262 addendum, 2026-11-13). ADR 0377, 2026-11-12: the Studio preview of a case with [mesh.adapt] builds the mesh Simulation::new sets the run up on (the base lattice, 576 cells for cases/cavity/adapt_re100.toml, with the solver's numbering and hash), then runs the run's adaptive loop (rcfd_api::sim::adapted_mesh, the first step's loop with a cancellation poll before each solve) and shows its final mesh, the mesh the run solves on after its first step (2799 cells, mesh hash 05bb8beae5da57da, equal bit for bit to Simulation::new plus one step); the Mesh side gives its cells and mesh hash and the loop's cost (3 solves of 576, 1,269 and 2,799 cells, 97 + 122 + 188 iterations, about 2.5 s); a case the run refuses is shown unadapted with the reason. g1_g7_shipped_cases_preview_the_solvers_mesh compares the adaptive case with Simulation::new like every other case, without the 2026-11-13 exception (the file is again its text before gate 4). A newer request stops the loop at the next solve (D2: the thread ended at 0.29 of a full build); no other case's preview, run, store or hash changes (E1, all rcfd-studio tests, baseline_hashes, the F-342 and F-476 tests pass unedited). Five mutations each failed their tests, M4 only after a corrected script (ADR 0377 amendment 2), hence partial by Rule I. Open: ADR 0377 Q1 (Simulation::new keeps the base lattice), Q2, Q4 (a solve in progress is not interrupted).

title: Field store of a run with [mesh.adapt] writes the adapted mesh
acceptance: A run of cases/cavity/adapt_re100.toml with output.store_interval set writes a readable field store whose mesh is the adapted mesh (2799 cells for the shipped case) with no warning, and sf2_every_shipped_case_writes_a_readable_store runs that case through the store like the other ten without the skip added on 2026-11-13.
note: From the gate 4 fix (ADR 0262 addendum, 2026-11-13). DONE pending acceptance (ADR 0373, 2026-11-12): runctl::drive opens the field store of a run whose [mesh.adapt] loop is pending after its first step, on the mesh the run solves on (or at the end on the base lattice when no step is taken, as before); every other run opens it where it did. cases/cavity/adapt_re100.toml with output.store_interval = 20 writes a readable store of the adapted mesh (2799 cells, the run's mesh hash, one snapshot at step 188) with no warning; sf2_every_shipped_case_writes_a_readable_store runs it without the 2026-11-13 skip (11 of 11; its count assertion 10 -> 11, ADR 0373 Q1); the store bytes of the ten other shipped cases equal main's (20 hashes), the existing store tests and baseline_hashes pass unedited; four mutations each failed their tests.

title: Elasticity multigrid on quadratic tetrahedra: a smoother that brings Tet10 within twice the Hex8 count
acceptance: Every limit not stated here is registered in the ADR before the run. With the geometric aggregation of ADR 0370 (ElasticAmgSettings::quadratic()), a registered opt-in smoother setting for quadratic elements (more block Gauss-Seidel sweeps or a Chebyshev smoother, derived before the run) such that on the Tet10 cantilever of slenderness 20 of ADR 0305 CG with one V-cycle reaches 1e-8 in at most 30 iterations with operator complexity <= 1.5 and the setup and solve time recorded beside ADR 0370's (31 iterations, 3.1 s); a test on a graded or anisotropic Tet10 box where pass 2's restriction to the candidates changes the aggregates (ADR 0370 mutation M5); every count and bit of ADR 0305 and ADR 0370 with their settings unchanged.
note: From ADR 0370 questions 1 and 2 (with a graded or anisotropic Tet10 mesh on which mutation M5 changes the aggregates), recommendation taken on the maintainer's standing instruction of 2026-11-11. ADR 0375, 2026-11-13: rcfd_linalg::amg_elastic::ElasticAmgSettings::quadratic_smoothed() (opt-in; quadratic() with QUADRATIC_SWEEPS = 2 forward block Gauss-Seidel sweeps before and 2 backward after the coarse correction, so the cycle stays symmetric; the count derived from ADR 0370's measured rate of 0.46 per iteration with a C/(C + nu) V-cycle model, estimate 22). On the Tet10 cantilever of slenderness 20 (121 680 unknowns) CG with one V-cycle reaches 1e-8 in 23 iterations (limit 30; quadratic() 31 in the same run), operator complexity 1.4762 (the setup is that of quadratic()), setup 0.86 s against 0.83 s, solve 3.56 s against 2.84 s (ADR 0370: 3.1 s): fewer iterations, more time. On two graded Tet10 boxes (x-graded 1.25 per cell; graded 1.2, 1.3, 1.4 in x, y, z) restricting pass 2 to the candidates changes 16 and 46 aggregates, so ADR 0370's mutation M5 is now caught; on the uniform box it changes none. Library change: 14 lines inserted in amg_elastic.rs, nothing else; counts and bits of ADR 0305 and ADR 0370 unchanged (hashes against main, ADR 0370 counts 27 and 31 measured again, baseline hashes pass). Six mutations, all caught. Done by the registered rule; acceptance is the maintainer's call.

title: Wave-solver drive with returning waves at the sampled section
acceptance: A drive built from two sampled sections of a duct field that holds both directions reproduces the entering wave's modal amplitudes at the inlet within 1 percent and ignores the returning one to 1 percent; a single section with a returning wave is reported by a measured residual.
note: From ADR 0372 question 1, recommendation taken on the maintainer's standing instruction of 2026-11-11. DONE pending acceptance, ADR 0378, 2026-11-12. Library only. Built: rcfd-post `wave_drive.rs` `SurfaceDrive::from_sections` (two or more sampled rcfd-surface-series sections, each read by the F-452 `from_series` with its own faces and clock; per harmonic and mode the entering and returning waves split over the planes with the closed-form kz by `split_axial`; refused when the separation, |sin(kz d)| or tanh(alpha d), is below 0.05 for any mode; `SplitDrive` plays back the entering wave only and reports the returning amplitudes, separations, reflection ratio and split residual) and `SurfaceDrive::entering_residual` (a single-section drive measured against a second sampled section); the F-452 off-plane refusal now names the farthest face (ADR 0372 question 2). Registered checks, all met at the first run, no amendment: the F-452 channel field with a returning wave of each component (reflection factors 0.5, 0.4, 0.6), sampled on 24 wall-clustered faces at x = -0.02 m and 20 uniform faces at x = -0.05 m on different clocks; on 64 cells across the entering amplitudes at the inlet agree with the closed form within 8.8e-4, 3.5e-3 and 2.3e-3 (limit 1e-2), the returning wave found at the inlet is at most 1.7e-5 of it (limit 1e-2) and 1.9e-14 of it is left in the drive; the split drive equals the closed-form entering wave within 1.6e-13 and its run equals the closed-form-driven run within 5.7e-15; the single-section drive of the same field is off by the reflection factor exactly and its residual against the second section, 0.526 and 0.888, equals the closed form within 1.4e-15 (5e-14 for an entering field only); three sections agree with two within 6.8e-15; four refusals located. Six mutations caught (waves swapped, wrong reference plane, split skipped, separation test removed, carry dropped from the residual, first off-plane face named). Limits: hard-walled duct, medium at rest; the single-section residual needs a second section (one section of pressure cannot be split); only the two-dimensional channel was run; no case key or CLI (F-451).

title: Overset: a second-order own-part pressure gradient of the ring cells under the prescribed fringe flux
acceptance: An opt-in of FringeFlux::PrescribedOwnGradient whose ring cells take a pressure gradient of second order from the calculated cells of their own part (exact for a linear pressure, no fringe value); with it, on TG_L of ADR 0219 moving with the quadratic donor interpolation, the largest error of the calculated background cells within two cells of the background fringe is at most 1.2 times that of the default coupling at levels 1 and 2, the largest error over the calculated and fringe cells at most 1.2 times, continuity and the outflow balance hold to 1e-9 in every step, the checks of ADR 0347 (UA, UA2, U1) hold, and without the opt-in every result is bit-identical.
note: From ADR 0376 question 2; low priority.

title: Axial velocity in the surface-series format for a one-section split
acceptance: An rcfd-surface-series file carrying the axial velocity with the pressure lets a drive built from one section split the entering and returning waves of a duct field within 1 percent of the closed form; files without velocity read and drive bit-identically as before.
note: From ADR 0378 question 1. NEEDS THE USER: it changes the rcfd-surface-series format. Size M.

title: A check that sees fixed against sliding patches of the co-simulation smoothing
acceptance: A [cosim] case whose initial wall displacement has a component along a fixed patch gives a different mesh when that patch is declared sliding than when it is declared fixed (the mutation MU5 of ADR 0380 is caught), and the points of the fixed patch do not move (0 bits); without the table every case hash is unchanged.
note: DONE (ADR 0381, 2026-11-13; registered before the test). A [cosim] case whose initial wall displacement is tangential to xmax (case 8x8x2 of 0.4x0.4x0.1 m, dy = 5e-3 sin(pi y/W)) gives a different mesh when xmax is declared sliding than when it is fixed (168 points differ, largest dy on xmax 4.316e-4 m, closed form 4.3e-4), the 27 points of the fixed xmax do not move (0 bits), a sliding xmax keeps its x (0), and an x-only displacement cannot tell them apart (0 bits, the old set-up). The mutation MU5 of ADR 0380 is caught on the first run, as are two more (every other patch fixed; the initial displacement reduced to x). No library line changed; baseline_hashes and case_hashes_w48u pass unedited.

title: Second-order immersed forcing: the single-corrector mode by a linearisation of the whole step
acceptance: The period-two growth of DFG 2D-2 on M2 with build_second_order_bounded and one PISO corrector (ADR 0374: stop at step 34 at dt 1e-3, runs at 5e-4 and 2.5e-4) is measured by a registered finite-difference linearisation of the whole step (velocity and pressure) about the state of an early step, whose dominant eigenvalue is real and below -1 at dt 1e-3 and of magnitude below 1 at dt 5e-4 and with two correctors, with its mode at the first fluid cells; or the part of the step that carries the growth is identified by a registered measurement.
note: From ADR 0374 question 3, recommendation taken on the maintainer's standing instruction of 2026-11-11. ADR 0374 narrowed the stop (the time step, the body, a period-two oscillation, two correctors damp it); the frozen pressure-lag map did not separate the settings.

title: Pressure-lag estimate at an immersed body
acceptance: The pressure-lag estimate of ADR 0073 for DFG 2D-2 on M2 with the first-order immersed forcing and one corrector at dt 1e-3 (ADR 0374: 1.13 to 1.30 for a run that runs, the mode in a solid cell at the surface) is explained by a registered measurement (the solid cells, the start and the tolerance of the pressure solve), and either the estimate leaves out what is not a fluid mode, opt-in or with the defaults bit-identical, so that it is below one for that run and above one for a setting that stops, or the limitation is documented with its numbers.
note: From ADR 0374 question 4, recommendation taken on the maintainer's standing instruction of 2026-11-11.

title: Hex20 face loads through the model path
acceptance: Every limit not stated here is registered in the ADR before the run. Load::Traction and Load::Pressure on surface sets of Hex20 faces give through nodal_load_vector the per-node forces of hex20::pressure_loads and hex20::traction_loads bit for bit; SolidMesh::face_area and face_area_vector of an 8-node face equal hex20::face_area and the 3 x 3 Gauss area vector within 1e-15 relative (no panic); every load vector and area of Tri3, Quad4 and Tri6 faces is bit-identical to before; the baseline hashes are unchanged.
note: ADR 0383, 2026-11-13: Load::Pressure and Load::Traction on Hex20 faces go through nodal_load_vector, and SolidMesh::face_area and face_area_vector take 8-node faces (8-node arms in loads::face_shape_functions, loads::face_rule and SolidMesh::face_tangents delegating to hex20). Met: per-node forces equal hex20::pressure_loads and traction_loads bit for bit on flat and curved meshes (24 of 24 sets), face_area and face_area_vector equal hex20::face_area and the 3 x 3 Gauss vector exactly (84 faces), Tri3, Quad4 and Tri6 loads and areas bit-identical to a transcription of the previous code (checked also on the previous code), total force 2e-16, baseline hashes unchanged; five mutations caught. The L3 refusal row of si_hex20 (ADR 0292) stays as an ignored record, L1 and L2 continue in l1_to_l2_face_loads_and_uniaxial_tension_after_landed (the maintainer's si_scaffold decision of 2026-11-13 applied to si_hex20 by the lead). Uniform pressure and traction only; a position-dependent traction stays on hex20's per-node forces.

title: Hex20 cantilever with the beam-theory support and the bore stress on a refined mesh
acceptance: Every limit not stated here is registered in the ADR before the run. Cantilever L/h = 20, nu = 0.3, one Hex20 through the thickness and 10 along, with the support of beam theory at the root (u_x = 0 on the root face, u_y and u_z fixed on its neutral line), registered before the run: tip deflection within 1 percent of P L^3/(3 E I) (1 + 3 E I/(kappa G A L^2)), the full clamp recorded beside it. Thick cylinder b/a = 2, plane strain, Hex20 with the radial element count derived in the registration from the second-order rate of ADR 0292's diagnostic: bore hoop stress within 1 percent and bore displacement within 0.2 percent of Lame.
note: From ADR 0292's two known misses (cantilever 1.8 percent with the full clamp, bore hoop stress 1.17 percent on 4 x 8 elements). Size S.

title: Modal analysis on the transformation: linear constraints, rigid sets and supports in the modal analysis
acceptance: Every limit not stated here is registered in the ADR before the run. modal_analysis of a model with linear constraints, rigid sets or elastic supports reduces K and M by the transformation of ADR 0296 (T^T K T, T^T M T; zero right-hand sides only, a non-zero value refused naming the constraint) and expands the modes by T. A model with prescribed displacements only gives the bits of today's modal analysis. A bar (nu = 0) on an end spring k has its first axial frequency from the closed-form transcendental equation within 0.5 percent at 20 elements; the modes are M-orthonormal within 1e-10 and every constraint row holds on each expanded mode within 1e-12; a model held only by springs uses the automatic shift when a rigid motion is free.
note: ADR 0384, 2026-11-13: modal_analysis of a model with linear constraints, rigid sets or elastic supports reduces K (with the supports) and M by the transformation of ADR 0296 (T^T K T, T^T M T, the reference points without mass of their own) and expands each mode by T (rcfd_fem::mpc::modal_analysis_mpc, which also returns the reduced matrices and the modes over the reference unknowns; modal_analysis_with dispatches on mpc::uses_transformation). Non-zero values are refused naming the row ("constraint 3 (Linear): value 1e-3; a modal analysis takes zero values only"). Prescribed-only models keep the bits (P1 bit-equal; the clamp written as Linear constraints gives bit-equal eigenvalues). Bar (nu = 0) on an end spring at 20 elements: 2.4e-5 from z tan z = kL/(EA) (limit 0.5 percent), 5.5e-14 from the discrete closed form; rigid end of the fixed-free bar 2.6e-4 from c/(4L), 1e-14 discrete; skew rollers at 30 degrees against the axis-aligned block: eigenvalues 9e-16, modes 2e-11; M-orthonormality 9e-16; every constraint row on every expanded mode 1.5e-16; threads 1 and 8 bit-equal. Default shift Shift::Auto on the transformation path: a bar held only by axial springs is shifted and reports rigid_free; its three zero modes are at 2.07e-6 of the first flexible frequency against a registered 1e-6 (known miss: they are fixed by the residual times the shift, 2e-13 of the shift). A collinear rigid set is refused naming its massless reference rotation. Seven mutations caught, one (all models on the transformation) survives as predicted. si_mpc N4 (the modal refusal of ADR 0296) stays as an ignored record (the maintainer's si_scaffold decision of 2026-11-13 applied by the lead); the si_scaffold R11 modal row was retired by the maintainer's pattern. Follow-up F-488 (the zero-mode measure and the explicit-shift report).

title: Overset: a consistent cell pressure gradient in the geometry corrections
acceptance: OversetSolver::set_geometry_corrections takes the cell pressure gradient of the momentum predictor and of the velocity correction from the least-squares gradients of the corrections (or another gradient exact for linear fields on B3d), with the defaults bit-identical: the Taylor-Green vortex with an axial velocity of ADR 0382 on B3 and B3d with the component moving as in ADR 0255 has an error of the calculated and fringe cells on B3d at most twice that on B3 with the default and the quadratic donor interpolation, continuity within 1e-9 at every step, ADR 0367's linear shear and uniform flow within their limits, and a run of the warped background alone that names the share of the warped background in the remainder.
note: From ADR 0382 questions 1 and 2, recommendation taken on the maintainer's standing instruction of 2026-11-11. Size M.

title: Zero modes on the transformation: the eigenvalue measure against the shift and the explicit-shift report
acceptance: Every limit not stated here is registered in the ADR before the run. For a body held only by springs (ADR 0384's KF and a free block with one spring), the zero modes found with the automatic shift satisfy |lambda_i| <= 1e-9 sigma and their number equals the number of free rigid motions counted from the springs, the linear rows and the rigid sets; with a shift given by the caller, rigid_free is reported by the zero-shift factor test and agrees with the automatic case on every model of ADR 0384.
note: From ADR 0384 question 1, recommendation taken on the maintainer's standing instruction of 2026-11-11. Size S.
